A source-matched native image, four-class N03 fairness, N04 session/MRU forwarding and N05 journal debt remain open.

proofs.title: Outbound NNTP TLS phase ordering and no protocol downgrade
proofs.statement: fn-fc-offers-and-credentials-wait-for-tls-and-login: for a connection in the phase fn-owner-feed-dial-open installs (greeting, or handshake-owed for implicit TLS) whose peer record requires a protected channel (STARTTLS or implicit TLS, or a credential whose profile did not permit clear text), and for EVERY sequence of socket reads and TLS reports fed to the two functions the host calls -- fn-fc-step (host/owner-host.lisp:1591, in fn-owner-feed-reply-chunk, called by host/native/feed-service.lisp:256) and fn-fc-after-tls (owner-host.lisp:1496, in fn-owner-feed-tls-established, feed-service.lisp:194) -- the kinds the host acts on satisfy fn-fc-gate-okp, a property written over observations only: no MODE, no ready and no delivered reply (so, through the :feed-conn install at owner-host.lisp:1454 that fn-feed-offer's natp conn test waits on, no IHAVE, CHECK or TAKETHIS) before a line coded 382 was answered :tls, a TLS report was accepted after it, and, when the record carries a credential, a line coded 281 was read; and no AUTHINFO USER or PASS before the 382 and the TLS report (implicit TLS starts past the 382). A clear transport with a credential and no clear-text permission therefore never sends it and never goes live. fn-fc-starttls-refusal-closes-before-the-credential: in the STARTTLS phase, a complete line whose code is not 382 (RFC 4642 2.2.1's 502 or 580) is :refused -- the host records the peer-local loss and closes (feed-service.lisp:391-395) -- the connection is closed, and the observations of any later reads and TLS reports on it contain no command, handshake or offer, so nothing falls back to clear text. fn does not read CAPABILITIES before STARTTLS; the peer's answer to STARTTLS is the advertisement the machine acts on. Trusted, not proved: that the host reports TLS up only after fnn-tls-connect verified the chain against the record's anchor and the server name (OpenSSL; tests/test_native_tls_transport.py's wrong-anchor and wrong-hostname witnesses), and that the socket carries the rendered bytes. Covered scope: one connection incarnation's phase machine; the composition with owner-feed's offer (fn-feed-offer and fn-feed-send need a natp fn-feed-conn, set only at :ready and cleared by fn-feed-lost) is read from the definitions, not proved here.
proofs.pending_subject: The image gate (plan T9): the matrix's V0-TRANSIT-TLS-AB/BA and V0-TRANSIT-TLS-WRONG-ANCHOR rows measured on a frozen image, two nodes on one box, including a kill -9 of the sender mid-transfer and exactly one copy after restart. OpenSSL chain and hostname behavior remains trusted integration evidence, not an ACL2 proof.
proofs.progress_note: T9c, 2026-09-22: the two keystones above over the functions the host calls, with tests/acl2/feed-connection-teeth-tests.lisp as the teeth book -- a reachable non-degenerate witness per keystone (a connection built from a decoded profile and driven through a real peer's replies, STARTTLS and implicit), and one must-fail per hypothesis under the keystone's own hints, each preceded by the keystone itself through the same macro so that no must-fail passes on a broken hint. The earlier status text named fn-fc-step theorems that did not exist; these replace them. Status stays in-progress until an image measures the matrix rows.

proofs.title: Principal-bound inbound peer role selection
proofs.statement: fn-auth-step-binds-a-peer-role-only-by-a-principal-login: for any session and any wire event, if fn-auth-step leaves a peer role on a connection that had none, then the connection was well-formed, not handshaking, unauthenticated and on a channel its policy accepts (so protected-only without TLS never binds, which is also fn-auth-step-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls, PRF-031), the event was an AUTHINFO PASS line with one token that checks against the cached name's stored verifier, the subject installed is that credential's principal, the role is fn-auth-principal-match of the principal under the configuration pinned into the connection, and the role is principal-derived (fn-auth-principal-rolep). fn-auth-principal-match is the one peer whose record, read back through fn-cfg-peer-find, says (:principal HEX) and which is the only auth-principal row naming HEX; zero rows (mismatch) or two (duplicate) give nil. fn-auth-step-principal-login-binds-exactly-the-unique-match: on a well-formed, non-handshaking, unbound, unauthenticated reader whose channel the policy accepts, a command line inside the 510-octet bound that tokenizes to AUTHINFO PASS <one token>, after a USER, with a checking secret, is answered 281, installs the principal and leaves exactly the match as the role -- a peer for one match, a still-authenticated reader for a mismatch or a duplicate, and the 281 the same in every case. fn-auth-step-starttls-clears-a-principal-role: whenever a step enters the TLS handshake (a hold that is not an XREDEEM redemption hold, fn-auth-redeem-waitp; that hold is PRF-164's fn-auth-step-redeem-hold-keeps-the-role), the new session has no subject, no cached name and no principal-derived role, and keeps the old role exactly when it was not principal-derived (a source-address peer stays a peer). fn-ocfg-open-begins-unbound: every open fn-ocfg-open accepts installs, at the identifier it allocated, a reader with no role, subject, cached name, TLS layer or handshake, whatever the owner's other connections did, so a reconnect begins unbound. Covered scope: one step of fn-auth-step, and the OPEN transition of fn-ocfg-open; the fold over a whole read is OB-AUTH-FOLD's. That the check refuses a wrong secret is A-CRYPTO and is witnessed, not proved. The subjects are what the host calls: fn-auth-step through books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk reaches through fn-own-read and fn-served-step, and fn-ocfg-open at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open.
proofs.progress_note: Lane t9b-role, 2026-09-22 (plan T9, row PRF-049): the four events above are the keystones; tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp keystones 8 to 10 and tests/acl2/owner-config-tests.lisp carry a reachable witness each (a real enrolled credential, a replayed peer table with one principal peer beside a source-address peer, a duplicate table, a table with no principal row, and a reconnect through fn-ocfg-read and fn-ocfg-open) and one must-fail per hypothesis, generated by a macro that first admits the full statement from the keystone, with a refuting value evaluated beside each; tools/teeth_check.py does not expand those macros. The same lane repaired fn-auth-bind-principal-peer: it bound on the auth-principal row count alone, so a row group carrying an auth-principal row that denotes a source-address record (admissible through a :set-peer delta; the teeth's shadow table) was bound, was not principal-derived, and survived STARTTLS; it now binds only fn-auth-principal-match, which reads the record back. Status stays in-progress until the image gate: a native reconnect on a deployed image, which is root's.

proofs.title: Mandatory hybrid authored-source profile binding
proofs.statement: The host-called fn-hsig-authorize-at, at the version fn-hsig-source-version names (version 1 for an authored source of at most 65535 octets, the u16 length's width; version 2 above, up to the u32's 4294967295), authorizes only a canonical Ed25519-and-ML-DSA-65 profile with exact fixed component widths and two verified primitive observations; each version's domain-separated, length-delimited signing preimage contains the principal, ordered enrolled key set and exact authored source octets. Across both versions equal preimages determine the same version, principal, keys and source (fn-hsig-signed-preimage-at-injective), no v1 preimage equals any v2 preimage (fn-hsig-v1-v2-preimages-disjoint), and on a v1 source the versioned preimage and authorization are the v1 functions (fn-hsig-preimage-at-v1-source-is-v1-preimage-by-definition, fn-hsig-authorize-at-v1-source-is-authorize-by-definition), so every v1 signature keeps its bytes.
proofs.progress_note: host/native/signatures.lisp calls fn-hsig-host-authorize, whose body calls fn-hsig-authorize. The framing keystones prove that equal valid subject bodies, and equal tagged signing preimages, determine the same principal, ordered Ed25519/ML-DSA-65 key set and exact authored source. Projection witnesses are non-degenerate and each theorem has one must-fail event per hypothesis. Reachable tests cover both-valid, each bad component, absent ML-DSA, unknown/unsupported ML-DSA, stripping, component order/profile confusion, source changes and enrolled-key changes. Native component evidence covers libsodium Ed25519 and OpenSSL 3.6.4 ML-DSA-65. These are byte-framing results, not cryptographic injectivity: primitive security, RNG, ABI and library correctness remain trusted assumptions; key custody, recovery authority and durable article/verdict composition remain open. The byte-framing injectivity book and its hypothesis counterexamples certified on hbox in certify-20260921T181329Z-2345431; the complete selected closure source digests match the integrated source. This does not certify live author submission or either signature primitive. Bounds P4 (2026-09-25, D27): the v1 source bound is the u16's 65535, not the article constant, and carrier v2 (item 1 = 2, tag fn-authored-source-hybrid-v2, u32 length) signs sources above it; the host calls fn-hsig-authorize-at and fn-hsig-signed-preimage-at through fn-hsig-host-authorize and fn-hsig-host-preimage (host/hybrid-signature-host.lisp) with fn-hsig-source-version. The two -by-definition events are the v1 correspondence, not keystones; the keystones are the per-version injectivity, the cross-version disjointness and the versioned injectivity, each with one must-fail per hypothesis in its test book. Certified with every dependent in certify-20260925T025612Z-3717718; native and verifier results in planning/evidence/bounds-p4-2026-09-25.md. Signed-path (2026-09-25): every source a carrier version admits (fn-hsig-subject-at-p) is within the kind-4 composite's authored-source bound, which is the v2 carrier's u32 width, so the Store never refuses a signable source by a data cap. The native signature copy (host/native/crypto.lisp fnn-crypto-octets) read the preimage list by ELT, quadratic in the source (99.6% of a 215 KB signed POST, 99.9% of signing); it is one pass now: signing 200 KiB 145.29 s to under 5 s, the signed POST 47.45 s to 0.76 s (unsigned 0.34 s).

proofs.title: Authoritative mixed Store history and atomic identity acceptance
proofs.statement: The host-called owner publication path writes one ordered Store-event stream whose journal sequence is independent of burned allocator transaction IDs; a bound kind-4 article and historical verdict commit atomically against the exact earlier enrolled key snapshot, recovery reconstructs the same historical verdict without current-key recomputation, and expected prepublication refusal consumes its reservation while indeterminate or structural faults remain fenced.
proofs.pending_subject: The carried journal sequence is preserved by initial, prepare, I/O, refusal, abort, finish and recovery transitions, but its invariant has not been joined to every actual owner publication path or the physical publication/recovery cuts. Prove the kind-4 snapshot/article/verdict binding over the host-called completion and recovery paths. The raw witness establishes condition routing and reservation cleanup only; it does not prove filesystem durability or cryptographic primitive correctness.
proofs.progress_note: Source integration carries journal sequence separately from allocation frontier, uses one native prepared-publication helper for article, retention and identity events, and replays enrolled kind-3 plus bound kind-4 history. The phase-aware relation fn-sn-identity-sequencep and fn-sn-finish-preserves-identity-sequence cover every completion arm. The selected kind-4 schema-1 codec now carries exact authored source and its ACL2-derived identity separately from the embedded received-carrier article; the replay snapshot binder checks carrier projection, enrolled ordered keys, both signature components' shape and the recorded principal. ACL2 constructor/codec tests exercise source and keyset substitutions. The native caller now verifies both primitives before asking ACL2 to construct this event. Combined saved-image acceptance/reopen evidence, reader HDR projection, host/physical recovery refinement and key succession remain open; structural replay checks do not prove native primitive correctness.

proofs.title: Outbound AUTHINFO phase ordering and secret custody
proofs.statement: WHEN: fn-fc-offers-and-credentials-wait-for-tls-and-login (PRF-047's keystone) says the AUTHINFO lines are sent only after the 382 and the TLS report, and that the feed makes no MODE, no ready and no offer until a 281 is read, on every sequence of reads and TLS reports fed to fn-fc-step and fn-fc-after-tls; a credential on a clear transport without the profile's explicit permission is never sent. REFUSAL: fn-fc-refused-login-closes-without-an-offer: in either login phase, a complete line whose code is not 281 (and, answering USER, not 381) is :refused, which fn-owner-feed-connection-result-kind (owner-host.lisp:1566) reports as :connection-refused and feed-service.lisp:391-395 answers with the peer-local loss and a close; the connection is closed and nothing fed to it afterwards produces a command, a handshake or an offer. WHAT: fn-fc-auth-user-command-sends-the-configured-name-alone and fn-fc-auth-pass-command-sends-the-configured-secret-alone: on a state whose name (secret) is an fn-fap-tokenp true list, the renderer the host calls (owner-host.lisp:1505, 1605, 1610) returns exactly the prefix, the token and CRLF, one line, so a credential cannot carry a second command; fn-fc-decoded-profile-renders-verbatim-in-every-state composes it with what the host does, with no hypothesis: the profile bytes go through fn-fap-decode (feed-service.lisp:172), the decoded fields are installed by fn-fc-initial-auth-state (owner-host.lisp:1484), and in every state any sequence of reads and TLS reports reaches, the USER and PASS lines are the prefix, the decoded field and CRLF. Not proved here: that the profile file is owner-only and bounded (feed-service.lisp:161-168, native integration evidence), the secrecy of the secret on the wire beyond the TLS ordering above, and the loss-to-requeue composition of fn-feed-lost.
proofs.pending_subject: The image gate (plan T9): the matrix's V0-TRANSIT-AUTHINFO-AB/BA and V0-TRANSIT-AUTHINFO-WRONG rows measured on a frozen image. Filesystem ownership and mode checks on the profile remain native integration evidence; the loss-to-requeue composition is PRF-029/K5's (T9a).
proofs.progress_note: T9c, 2026-09-22: events are the five theorems above; the teeth book is tests/acl2/feed-connection-teeth-tests.lisp (for the unconditional composition, the must-fail is the false neighbour: the same claim over a name and secret that did not come through fn-fap-decode, refuted by a name carrying CRLF and a second command). fn-fap-decode-yields-two-renderable-tokens and fn-fap-decode-refusal-yields-no-credential in books/feed-auth-profile.lisp are the decode facts the composition uses. Status stays in-progress until an image measures the matrix rows.

proofs.title: NEWNEWS exactly filters durable acceptance stamps and reads no payload
proofs.statement: fn-nntp-newnews-scan-is-the-acceptance-filter equates the one-pass served scan with an independent quadratic specification that searches later-accepted articles for the nearest natural stamp, proving soundness and completeness of the conservative legacy horizon and wildmat scope. fn-nntp-newnews-scan-reads-no-payload proves erasing all article payload octets leaves the answer unchanged; fn-nntp-newnews-scan-lines-at-most-candidates bounds the output by matching available articles; fn-nntp-newnews-lines-are-clean proves every line is safe to render. fn-nntp-step-dispatches-newnews-to-the-newnews-response is the subject equation for the host-called dispatcher; fn-nntp-newnews-response-preserves-session and fn-nntp-effects-newnews-response carry the response through the served effect path. Covered scope: one reader session on a pinned committed archive, with a natural schema-1 acceptance stamp or the conservative schema-0 horizon. One command costs O(A*Gprime) for A committed articles and Gprime matched groups, reads no payload and emits at most C lines for C candidates. The true-time no-miss claim for legacy articles assumes A-CLOCK and is outside this theorem.
proofs.note: At this source, green_check finds books/nntp-newnews green at its exact include closure in certify-20260923T232942Z-484654, its test book green in certify-20260924T005919Z-653679, books/nntp-invariants green in certify-20260923T232820Z-480447, and books/nntp-effects green in certify-20260923T232942Z-484654; none has moved dependencies. These are archived certification records, not a current native image qualification. The earlier T2b affected-closure run is certify-20260923T170842Z-2026382; native served-reader validation remains separate.

proofs.title: The operator's post is injected as a served POST is, and its retry is the stored article
proofs.statement: fn-own-operator-submission-is-an-injection-of-the-payload: if fn-own-operator-submit-result answers :submitted, fn-own-operator-submit queues exactly one control submission whose decision is injected, carries the Message-ID and newsgroup list the command named, and whose octets are a re-injection of the submitted octets by the owner's injecting agent (fn-inj-reinjectionp: the agent's Path line, an Injection-Date, the agent's Injection-Info, optionally the generated Message-ID and Date lines, then the submitted octets unchanged); fn-own-operator-decision-is-an-injection-of-the-payload states the same of the decision for any configuration, clock and node. fn-own-operator-submit-without-a-clock-refuses-and-changes-nothing: with no clock observation, or one without a wall time, the result is :refused and the owner is unchanged (D10-a). fn-own-operator-retry-resubmits-the-stored-injection: if fn-inj-decide injected the octets under one clock with that Message-ID and the node holds exactly those injected octets under it, then under any later usable clock the decision is those stored octets, so the store answers the Message-ID's duplicate rather than a conflict. All three rest on fn-inj-injected-article-is-a-reinjection-of-its-source (books/injection-invariants.lisp): every article fn-inj-decide injects is a re-injection of its source by its configured agent, for every clock reading. Covered scope: the owner's decision and its queue entry; the store attempt that follows is the served POST's, and the duplicate decision the store answers is fn-pb-existing-action (books/poster-bytes.lisp, host-called since D25), which refines fn-sn-existing-action (fn-pb-action-over-refines-the-byte-identity-decision; its exact outcome is stated in books/poster-bytes-invariants.lisp); a single theorem composing this operator retry through the host-called Store attempt is still open. The subject is what the host calls: fn-own-operator-submit through the (:operator-submit ...) event, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-operator-submit steps and host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-control-submit-serialized calls for `fn operator CONFIG post`. After the records flip (flip-L8-2, 2026-09-27) the node holds the stored article's HANDLE, so the decision takes STORED, the stored octets or :absent (fn-own-operator-decision CFG CLOCK STORED MSGID GROUPS OCTETS; the event (:operator-submit MSGID GROUPS OCTETS STORED)); the retry keystone's hypothesis is STORED = the first injection, and at the host's entry, fn-own-operator-retry-at-the-entry-is-the-stored-injection (books/owner-served-invariants.lisp): when the node holds MSGID's article and ALPHA of it (the bytes under its handle through the arena, fn-own-operator-stored-octets, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-operator-submit calls) is the injection the octets got under an earlier clock, the decision at the owner's clock is that stored injection.
proofs.progress_note: Lane T13-conform, 2026-09-22, from the INN lab's finding 1 (operator post fed INN an article with no Path; 437). Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-operator-tests.lisp builds the lab's own operator article through a real owner (configure, observe, submit, take, the store events, the completion) and asserts the queued octets byte for byte against the Path, Injection-Date and Injection-Info lines the lab's served POST carried; one must-fail per hypothesis with a refuting value beside it (the retry keystone through a macro that first admits the full statement). The native tests that run it on an image (tests/test_native_control.py) have not run: no image carries this yet.

proofs.title: An injected article's From is an RFC 5322 mailbox-list (RFC 5536 3.1.2)
proofs.statement: fn-mbx-mailbox-list-names-an-address: every value fn-mbx-mailbox-listp accepts contains an "@" octet, the addr-spec every mailbox carries. fn-inj-injected-proto-article-has-a-mailbox-list-from: whenever fn-inj-decide injects, the From field of the parsed proto-article is accepted by fn-mbx-mailbox-listp and names an address, so `From: yue` (answered 240 and served on 2026-09-22) is refused :from-invalid with `441 posting failed; From is not a valid mailbox list`. fn-mbx-mailbox-listp is RFC 5322 section 3.4's mailbox-list under RFC 5536 sections 2.1 and 2.2 (no obsolete syntax but obs-phrase, US-ASCII), bounded by the header block before either of its two passes, and reads nothing through the Lisp reader. Covered scope: soundness in the one direction stated (accepted implies an address); that the recognizer accepts every conformant mailbox-list is not a theorem and is witnessed across the grammar's productions. The subject is fn-inj-decide, which books/nntp-post.lisp fn-nntp-post-step calls on the served POST path (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk through fn-own-read) and books/owner.lisp fn-own-operator-decision calls on the operator's.
proofs.progress_note: Lane T13-conform, 2026-09-22, from the agents run's `From: yue`. Teeth in tests/acl2/injection-tests.lisp: the INN lab's POSTed article (its injected octets are what innd received) and `From: yue` refused :from-invalid; accepted and refused values across the productions; one must-fail per hypothesis. The v0 matrix row V0-POST-FROM-MAILBOX measures it on a node; no image carries it yet.

proofs.title: A relayed article changes in Path and Xref only, once, at acceptance (RFC 5537 3.6, 3.7)
proofs.statement: Over fn-peer-relayed-octets, the octets this node stores, serves and feeds on for an article a peer transferred: fn-peer-relayed-octets-change-only-path-and-xref -- removing every Path and Xref field (with its continuation lines) from what arrived and from what is stored leaves the same octets, so every other header field in order, the blank line and the body are byte-identical; fn-peer-relayed-octets-are-idempotent -- a second pass by the same node changes nothing; fn-peer-relayed-octets-carry-no-xref -- no Xref field is stored; fn-peer-relayed-octets-name-this-node-in-every-path -- when the node has a <path-identity>, every Path field of what is stored begins with it and "!" (RFC 5537 3.6 step 7, 3.7 step 6; the 3.2.1 diagnostic follows it). None has a hypothesis but the last, whose one is the identity. Each is the article-level keystone of books/path-update.lisp (fn-pu-relay-article-changes-only-path-and-xref, -is-idempotent, -leaves-no-xref, -names-the-agent-in-every-path), proved by one induction each over a walk of the raw header lines whose re-read of its own output is exact. fn-peer-injection-arguments-payload-unfolds: the payload the transfer stages for fn-node-prepare is fn-peer-relayed-octets of the received octets. Covered scope: the octets; what a reader receives is those octets (fn-durable-completion-installs-exact-pending-article, PRF-002), and the served rendering's dot-stuffing is the wire books'. An article with no Path field gets none (RFC 5537 3.7 step 1's rejection of it is open). The subjects are what the host calls: fn-peer-relayed-octets at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-take, which fills fn-owner-submit-octets, the octets host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-drain-one digests and stores; and fn-peer-injection-arguments at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide, whose staged payload the drain compares with them before the store attempt. fn-peer-relayed-octets-keep-the-received-path-tail (2026-09-24; keystone fn-pu-relay-article-keeps-the-received-path-tail, books/path-update-tail.lisp): when the node has a <path-identity>, the content of each stored Path field line, read by fn-pu-path-contents with the walk's own line classification, is the received content with <identity>!<diagnostic>! in front, or unchanged when it already begins with <identity>!; so the update prepends and the received Path is the tail. Covered scope: the first physical line of each Path field; folded continuation lines are copied and not read.
proofs.progress_note: Lane T13-conform, 2026-09-22, from the INN lab's findings 2 and 3 (fn served INN's Path without itself, and INN's Xref). Decided at acceptance, not at serving time: specs/peering.md 2.3 carries the argument. Teeth in tests/acl2/peer-inbound-tests.lisp, last section: innfeed's own TAKETHIS octets become the stored article byte for byte (Path fnA.hbox.test!!inn.hbox.test!..., no Xref), through the transfer to the durable article, with the parser's view of the result; .MISMATCH. for a peer expecting another identity; a Path line the update would push past 998 octets refused :oversize; one must-fail per hypothesis (and, for the three statements with none, the stronger statement refuted by the lab's value). The INN lab rows V0-INN-SERVING-AGENT and V0-INN-OPERATOR-POST measure it on a node; no image carries it yet.

proofs.title: A served POST's Injection-Info names the node's path-identity
proofs.statement: fn-oag-post-config-agent-is-the-path-identity: when the replayed configuration's path-identity policy is set, the posting configuration fn-oag-post-config installs (called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-post-config, which fn-owner-recover and fn-owner-reconfigure-complete install with fn-own-configure) has that identity's octets as its agent; unset, the agent is fn.example.invalid. fn-oag-open-pins-the-owner-config: a connection fn-ocfg-open opens (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open) at an identifier no connection already holds pins the owner's installed configuration; fn-oag-configured-open-pins-the-path-identity composes the two. fn-oag-served-post-names-the-pinned-agent: for any socket read fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix performs (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk), if the connection's served state satisfies fn-served-connp, the submission the read hands the owner, when it is an injected article, carries the Injection-Info line generated from the agent the connection pinned; the chain runs through fn-served-step, fn-served-feed, fn-served-dispatch, fn-auth-step, fn-peer-step and fn-nntp-post-step to fn-inj-injected-article-names-the-configured-agent over fn-inj-decide. Covered scope: the served POST path; the fn-served-connp premise is the served invariant the owner does not carry (the premise PRF-006 records for fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix), and no value is known on which the conclusion fails without it. fn.toml's [posting] agent is refused by run (fn-native-config-unsupported-key), so the path-identity policy is the only agent.
proofs.progress_note: Lane t6b-profile, 2026-09-22: the served-POST keystone is proved over the host-called fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix under the fn-served-connp premise; tests/acl2/owner-agent-tests.lisp carries a reachable witness built as the host builds it (a replayed history with the policy set path-identity delta, fn-oag-post-config, fn-ocfg-open, one POST read through fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix whose queued article says Injection-Info: hbox.ember.software) and a must-fail per hypothesis, with a refuting value for the identity and freshness hypotheses and none known for the served premise. The image measurement is tests/test_native_profile.py and V0-NODE-PROFILE.

proofs.title: The native service log says what the reply says, one line per event
proofs.statement: fn-olog-served-post-line-says-accepted-iff-durable: the line host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-outcome renders for a served submission begins with the word accepted exactly when fn-own-outcome-completion of the host's word is :durable, the completion fn-own-outcome renders into the 240; a host word alone never makes it say accepted. fn-olog-control-post-line-says-the-control-result: the control line's first word is the word of fn-own-control-outcome-result, the value the control reply carries. fn-olog-served-post-line-is-one-line, fn-olog-control-post-line-is-one-line and fn-olog-connection-line-is-one-line: no line contains CR or LF, whatever octets the Message-ID, agent or peer name held. fn-olog-staging-cleanup-line-is-one-line: the line host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-staging-cleanup renders for an error fnn-publish's best-effort staging cleanup swallowed after the record is durable contains no CR or LF, whatever the stage path or the OS error text held; that the host writes it exactly once per swallowed error is measured by the NNTP probe's record-stage-unlinked EIO row, not proved. Covered scope: the rendered octets; that host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-log writes them and one LF to the file run opened append-only is measured by tests/test_native_profile.py, not proved. bp-app-refusal-line-says-refused-iff-refused: the BP application receiver's line for a transfer it did not accept (host/native/bp-app.lisp fnn-bpapp-deliver, through host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-refusal-log) begins with refused exactly when the receiver answered :refused or :clock-unusable, so a busy owner reads deferred and an unknown word uncertain; fn-olog-bp-app-refusal-line-is-one-line: that line holds no CR or LF, and it carries the application planner's reason field. Covered scope: the rendered octets; that host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-log writes them and one LF to the file run opened append-only is measured by tests/test_native_profile.py, not proved.
proofs.progress_note: Lane t6b-profile, 2026-09-22: the keystones have no hypotheses; tests/acl2/owner-log-tests.lisp evaluates each renderer on a real injected decision and a real control decision, and its must-fails name the weaker statements a host-word log would satisfy (the line echoes the host word; the control line uses the served classification) with the refuting owner evaluated beside each.

proofs.title: Bounded canonical BPv7 status-report payload codec
proofs.statement: For every fn-bpn-reportp payload, fn-bpn-report-decode of fn-bpn-report-encode returns that report and no trailing octets (fn-bpn-report-decode-of-encode); valid reports encode in at most 1194 octets (fn-bpn-report-encode-length-bound), below the decoder 4096-octet preflight, and every accepted input re-encodes byte-for-byte (fn-bpn-report-accepted-input-is-canonical). This covers RFC 9171 section 6.1.1 whole and fragment payloads, four assertions, optional requested times, and local reason codes 0 to 11. Reports are remote observations only; node-machine generation, correlation, consumption and release authority are outside this codec claim.
proofs.note: D1a codec source and its tests have ACL2 certification, including a maximal-profile witness and rejected malformed/noncanonical vectors. No native node path calls this codec yet. These component theorems are therefore not credited as requirement keystone events under the actual-caller rule; D1b/D2 generation and consumption remain open. The evidence records the component claims without implying a served implementation.

proofs.title: TCPCL final acknowledgement follows the durable delivery disposition
proofs.statement: The exact native fn-tcl-host-drive caller emits final END ACKs only immediately before matching :bundle-received events; at each such event, the ordered held messages satisfy fn-tcl-held-final-ackp. The host-called fn-tcl-delivery-plan then releases that ACK only for (:accepted path-or-nil), replaces it with XFER_REFUSE for definitive (:refused reason), and withholds it for (:uncertain reason). The source-level proof does not establish the physical FNBS barrier, raw Lisp execution, or socket delivery.
proofs.progress_note: ACL2 8.7 certified the exact host-drive event order, ordered held-list projection and conditional delivery plan. Reachable witnesses cover coalesced prior-transfer partial ACK/refusal, two completed bundles in one read, and missing-held/path-type counterexamples. Native source executes the selected message list; combined-image A2 callback runtime remains pending.

proofs.title: BP persisted age anchors are compared only within a durable boot domain
proofs.statement: The host-called fn-bpnf-clock-domain-plan returns :same only when a valid saved FNBS kind-6 frame decodes to the exact canonical current Linux boot ID; a different boot fences regardless of the numeric monotonic reading, and a missing marker with legacy obligations fences rather than renewing or expiring them. The 82-byte marker roundtrip and served guards are certified. The host's boot-ID observation, physical barriers, and combined-image caller still require native evidence, and cross-boot reanchoring remains open.
proofs.progress_note: The exact startup planner and canonical kind-6 marker are ACL2-owned, guard verified, and focused-book certified. Concrete witnesses include same-boot restart, both directions of incomparable new-boot uptime, legacy outbound and received rows, malformed marker, invalid observed ID, and a crash in the publisher link window. Native combined-image and physical clock/barrier evidence remain pending. A mismatched or legacy domain is an explicit lifecycle fence, not completed reboot recovery.

proofs.title: Native authored carrier receives the local NNTP injection trace without changing signed source
proofs.statement: For any nonnil result of the exact ACL2 fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets called by host/native/hybrid-control.lisp, fn-hsig-injected-carrier-retains-exact-signed-source proves the authenticated authored source is a suffix of the received octets, and fn-hsig-injected-carrier-is-a-news-injection proves the received octets satisfy the ordinary fn-inj-reinjectionp grammar for the rendered portable carrier, configured agent and projected Message-ID. The native event constructor accepts only the same injected bytes. This is an ACL2 byte-projection claim under a successful injection decision; it does not prove cryptographic primitives, filesystem durability, or peer I/O.
proofs.progress_note: The source-matched ACL2 book/test and dependent Store tests passed on hbox. The positive fixture constructs a real schema-1 injected event and replays its exact source; closed injection and pathless carrier witnesses fail the conclusions when the successful-injection premise is removed. The combined native two-owner peering/restart test awaits the shared image.

proofs.title: Exact-source topic metadata candidate is bounded and canonical
proofs.statement: The native topic-inspect-carrier command passes only the exact source returned after hybrid-carrier verification to fn-th-host-inspect-source. Successful inspection binds to exactly one FN-Topic field in that parsed source and its canonical raw physical lines. Every valid root, control, or report constructor encodes within 1,531 binary octets and 39 items; decoding its encoding recovers the constructor. The canonical folded field renderer emits lines of at most 85 octets. Accepted decoder bytes are canonical. This establishes no topic anchor or admission.
proofs.progress_note: ACL2 8.7 certified the codec, general constructor bound/inverse, host-called authored raw-line binding, canonical folded-field line bound, and max-profile/negative tests at exact digests on hbox. The full-envelope native saved-image max-profile gate remains pending; no topic admission claim is made.

proofs.title: Consumer projection equals the completed Store prefix through publication and crash replay
proofs.statement: Under fn-csi-full-relationp, the actual decoded Store dispatcher fn-snrt-step preserves the phase-aware relation for every event (fn-csi-store-step-preserves-full-relation). The relation equates the carried consumer projection with strict replay of the completed dense Store prefix, checks a linked unfinished candidate before finish, erases the process projection on crash, and reconstructs it from physical records on recovery. Induction over fn-snrt-run yields arbitrary finite mixed traces; a corrupted carried projection refutes the premise in the test book. This component covers logical Store transitions and admissible crash images, not a host-observed syscall refinement or served consumer call.
proofs.progress_note: The logical Store invariant and test roots are certified in scope. Native image 1d26e01f separately witnesses local-owner poll, advancing ACK/reopen, selected packing and fenced clone cursor recovery. Those tests do not prove syscall refinement or the consumer-owned transaction/ACK/reply join; general remote policy and two-store composition remain open. The current topic/consumer composition now certifies the actual :prepare-topic consumer-relation arm and a reachable bootstrap/register, topic admin/anchor/report, observed-reopen trace with ACK unchanged; the hbox source-matched scope is in planning/evidence/consumer-topic-store-trace-2026-09-24.md. This adds no served-path or physical durability claim.

proofs.title: Topic candidate author and root declaration bind to verified historical context
proofs.statement: The native topic inspector calls the ACL2 selector with exact source, principal and ordered keys returned by hybrid verification. A selected root is marked controller-matched only when its declared controller equals that principal and its declared keyset ID equals the ACL2 subject identity of the canonical principal/key snapshot. Reports obtain their author reference from that same verified context, not metadata or From. For a retained schema-1 event the historical selector first requires the T10 exact-source/carrier/keyring-snapshot binding; no topic admission or succession decision follows.
proofs.progress_note: The selector and accepted-event wrapper plus matching/mismatching principal, changed-key, From, relay and unbound historical event witnesses certify on hbox at the lane source. A source-matched saved-image CLI run and integrated reverse closure remain pending. The native command keeps generic candidate output and explicitly reports admission=unestablished.

proofs.title: Pinned group buckets and OVER ranges refine the committed archive
proofs.statement: For a projection-consistent accepted archive, fn-gidx-listgroup-command-of-build equates indexed LISTGROUP with the archive command. For an accepted archive, maintained bucket and trie correspondence, and an OVER or XOVER keyword, fn-nntp-carried-over-range-equals-archive-command equates the actual pinned archive dispatcher with the original response for every one-argument token; invalid ranges and untagged indexes fall through. fn-gidx-number-article-of-build proves that a bucket entry resolves through the trie to the same first article as the archive scan, including the identifier and number availability gates. For ARTICLE, HEAD, BODY and STAT and every argument list, fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned-msgid-arms-are-the-scan equates the same pinned dispatcher with the scanning archive dispatcher under the trie correspondence and no withdrawal hit (fn-nntp-number-withdrawn-p and fn-nntp-msgid-withdrawn-p false: a withdrawn number or Message-ID answers 423/430 withdrawn, PRF-084). fn-own-read reaches that dispatcher through served dispatch; fn-own-relation and fn-served-connp maintain the pins across view refresh, open, feed and read. On a peer connection, fn-pix-history-hasp-is-peer-history-hasp equates the IHAVE/CHECK history test the host's carried read runs (one fn-midx-lookup in the owner view's trie when the session node holds the list the trie is keyed to) with the fn-peer-history-hasp scan for every Message-ID, under fn-node-statep and the trie correspondence; fn-oix-ocfg-step-keeps-view-indexed carries that correspondence over every configured-owner event. fn-pgc-peer-arm-is-peer-step-pinned equates the peer arm the carried read runs, which evaluates no fn-node-statep, with fn-peer-step-pinned under fn-peer-sessionp, a named peer and the trie correspondence. The claim excludes arbitrary tagged indexes, unindexed HDR/GROUP/NEXT/LAST/NEWNEWS, disk indexing, and elapsed-time performance.
proofs.progress_note: Scoped ACL2 certification and called-owner sparse/historical LISTGROUP witnesses are recorded in the group-bucket evidence. Indexed OVER/XOVER resolve selected-group bucket entries through the pinned trie; the called pinned dispatcher equality has direct reachable and malformed-state premise teeth, with redundant range, tag, bound and session assumptions removed. HDR remains on the archive fold. The native OVER/XOVER socket driver is prepared but has not run on a source-matched image; combined-image qualification and full dependent closure at integrated source remain open.

proofs.title: Experimental root-only topic admission is grounded in historical authorship and finite local policy
proofs.statement: The experimental root-only Store path selects prior T10-bound exact source and snapshot, checks installed local administrator, roster, same-topic parents and finite quota, and completes only a matching topic event. Fresh version-2 root anchors bind the exact earlier immutable administrator-install event ID and generation; historical version-1 anchors retain ID-only replay semantics and cannot be freshly staged. The owner-called report selector returns :replayed-historical only for selected earlier exact source and retained admission, without another Store event. Topic completion advances the exact Store sequence/transaction and slot-12 projection while preserving article acceptance. Observed reopen separately validates topic replay; deriving that validity for every modeled crash image from a maintained live Store relation remains open. Physical publication is not yet qualified (no native v1-to-v2 migration: fresh deploys at 6.6.0).
proofs.progress_note: Scoped v2 local proposal, Store fresh-v1 refusal, canonical event/prefix and mixed-source vector roots passed at exact bytes. Historical v1 meaning is retained. The dual-image native migration test is retired (no migrations: fresh deploys at 6.6.0, lane config-and-legacy); the full affected closure remains open. The maintained topic/crash relation is under separate active proof work and is not supplied by the interim BP/byte reopen premise.

proofs.title: Local consumer status reports the scoped committed journal distance
proofs.statement: The experimental local-owner command `consumer status CONTROL ID` reports the registered consumer ACK, committed journal frontier and their event-distance from fixed committed Store projections after the same local principal, query-version and view-version scope checks used by position and poll. The diagnostic leaves owner state unchanged. For the exact host-called kind-9 FNCT codec, decoding an encoded accepted reply returns its ACK, frontier and gap when ACK and frontier are uint32 values, ACK is no greater than frontier, and gap equals frontier minus ACK; decoding an encoded refused, uncertain or fault reply returns that status with empty fields under the constrained frame-digest shape. This target remains in progress because the subsequent topic/index composition requires its own native qualification. The codec theorem does not prove concrete hash security, native filesystem recovery or article unreadness/application processing; Store recovery authority remains PRF-064. EXTENSION (lane friend-blockers, 2026-09-27, the stranger rehearsal's stops): PKT-709: fn-ncl-cli-plan answers (:help) for `help` (the host prints fn-ncl-usage-text for help, no words and every usage refusal); the register retry moved to books/consumer-reason.lisp fn-ncr-cli-after (PRF-263, lane friend-blockers-2: only an unbootstrapped or unnamed refusal retries).
proofs.progress_note: The ACL2 local status codec, owner scope decision and native-control host test passed the scoped status/index run. The general accepted and nonaccepted kind-9 codec roundtrips and their isolating teeth certified in the selected hbox book/test roots at the exact new source bytes; these are proof-only changes to the executable codec. The earlier e160442f image passed unknown-consumer refusal, read-only status, advancing ACK and recovered status checks. The joined topic/index source has scoped certification but has not yet run on a matching saved image. The diagnostic does not assert application processing or discharge.

proofs.title: Operator-local hybrid key lifecycle preserves per-principal authority and historical verdicts
proofs.statement: The host-called local enrollment and revocation constructors require the next durable keyring generation; new hybrid-author requests use only the named principal's newest recognized enrollment, leaving unrelated principals active, while identity replay retains earlier snapshots and accepted verdicts byte-exact across rotation and revocation.
proofs.progress_note: The per-principal selector, next-generation event constructors and versioned tombstone are implemented. Completed kind-3 Store-node theorems equate the post-finish selector to identity replay and preserve historical verdicts; successful recovery theorems equate the carried selector and verdicts to replay of recovered durable records. A reachable Store trace commits A1 and a kind-4 verdict, then B2, A3 rotation and A4 tombstone, checking maintained node/file and identity-sequence relations and observed reopen. Selected crash cuts before and after B2 publication distinguish absent from durable enrollment. The host calls the selector under the serialized owner. The frozen 863c2141 production image passed three targeted native lifecycle/carrier tests on scratch Stores with OpenSSL 3.5.8. A global crash-phase relation for every lifecycle trace, incoming signed-carrier authority caller, and cost/index correspondence for a large snapshot history remain open. Local permission does not define portable succession or retroactive signature invalidation.

proofs.title: The POST outcome at the wire keeps its three outcomes and names its refusal
proofs.statement: fn-own-consumed-completion-is-240-or-uncertain: over fn-own-outcome (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-outcome), once a completion has been consumed into the ledger after the connection's submission was taken, the reply is the 240 for the host word :durable and the uncertain `441 ... do not repost' for every other word, so a durable record is never answered as a refusal. fn-post-outcome-store-refusal-kinds-are-distinct and fn-post-outcome-store-refusal-is-not-uncertain: over fn-nntp-post-outcome, each Store refusal kind (duplicate, conflict, malformed, unaffordable, storage-failed, unnamed) is its own 441 line and none is the uncertain line. D25, over fn-own-outcome with the word fn-pb-existing-action returns (books/poster-bytes.lisp; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt), keyed on the poster's source recovered by the injection inverse fn-inj-source-of (books/injection.lisp; fn-inj-source-of-inverts-the-injection: every injected article gives back its source exactly, at every clock reading, in all four generated-field cases): fn-pb-a-resend-at-any-clock-is-answered-already-stored, the held article is a source injected at clock A and the submission is that source injected at clock B under the same Message-ID and groups, with the Date present or absent, and the reply is `441 posting failed; this article is already stored here' while no completion has been consumed; fn-pb-a-changed-source-is-answered-conflict, any other source under that Message-ID (one changed authored byte, an authored Date changed or removed) is answered the conflict line; fn-pb-an-existing-action-writes-nothing, whatever fn-pb-existing-action answers, the outcome leaves the owner's Store, its feeds and its outcome records as they were. RFC 5537 section 3.5 item 11 over fn-inj-decide, one theorem per case: fn-inj-no-injection-date-when-date-and-message-id-are-supplied (the injected article is the Path line, the Injection-Info line and the source, at every clock reading), fn-inj-injection-date-is-the-clock-otherwise, and fn-inj-a-supplied-injection-date-is-never-replaced (a local acceptance policy refuses such a proto-article).
proofs.note: Lane p2-wire, from the campaign's W1/W2/W3 (planning/evidence/campaign-1a9dd747-2026-09-24.md). The refusal kind is relayed by the host from the ACL2 step that refused (fn-pb-existing-action since D25, fn-owner-prepare, fn-store-publication-admissibility, fn-owner-known-abort); the capacity comparison against max-transactions is still a host computation. The durable word of a POST commit is fn-ccar-own-finish's (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission), equal to fn-own-finish by fn-ccar-own-finish-is-own-finish. The refusal words are a local policy choice pending ember's decision. D25 (lanes d25-dup-conflict, then d25-injection-inverse): the duplicate-versus-conflict decision is fn-pb-existing-action; since lane d25-injection-inverse its subject is the poster's source through the injection inverse, not a projection that drops named fields, so no scope limit on an opening Date remains for records of injection recipe v2. The provenance of generated fields is carried by the injected block itself (recipe v2: Path, then Injection-Date, generated Message-ID, generated Date, then Injection-Info closing the block); no Store record field was added. Recipe v1 records are read under v1 only where unambiguous (fn-inj-source-of-a-v1-record) and otherwise compared octet for octet (fn-inj-source-of-an-ambiguous-v1-record). A relayed article, or one another agent injected, is compared octet for octet, so a transit copy whose Path differs is again a conflict (as before D25). The supplied-Injection-Date refusal is a local acceptance policy, not an RFC requirement. It refines fn-sn-existing-action (fn-pb-action-over-refines-the-byte-identity-decision).
proofs.progress_note: Lane log-recovery-2 (2026-09-27, PKT-838): tests/campaign/native_nntp_post_probe.py (the per-file POST cuts at the wire) was deleted with the per-file layout; tests.test_native_commit_log's test_every_post_log_cut_is_old_or_new_and_the_node_goes_on checks each served log cut at the wire. A-HOST dropped from this row's assumptions (lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G3-9, 2026-09-27): no theorem of the row takes fn-assume-host-report or fn-assume-host-events (books/assumptions.lisp) as a hypothesis, so the citation was decorative (AGENTS.md: the theorems that use a named assumption mention it). The host's honest I/O remains the trust boundary these theorems sit inside, not a hypothesis of them.

proofs.title: Group names are the RFC 5536 section 3.1.4 grammar and reserved names are never created
proofs.statement: fn-record-group-namep-is-the-rfc-5536-grammar: the recognizer every host site applies admits exactly an ASCII string of 1 to 128 octets (local bound) whose octets are an RFC 5536 section 3.1.4 <newsgroup-name>; four rejection theorems name a forbidden octet, a leading dot, an empty component and a trailing dot. fn-native-admin-plan-refuses-a-reserved-group-create: a well-formed `group create NAME` whose NAME is reserved (first component "example" or the name "poster", ASCII case folded) is refused :reserved-group-name and carries no configuration delta; the subject is fn-native-admin-plan, which host/native-admin-host.lisp:7 calls. fn-native-operator-run-refuses-a-reserved-init-group: an `init` naming a reserved group in any position is never an accepted plan; the subject is fn-native-operator-run, which host/native-operator-host.lisp:19 calls, and host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-dispatch-plan exits on a non-accepted plan before any store observation. fn-native-admin-group-name-creatablep-is-the-rfc-5536-rule: a creatable name is a valid group name whose case-folded octets are not "example", do not begin "example.", and are not "poster". Covered scope: the operator and admin command paths; the initial configuration record's refusal in fn-cfg-host-initial-octets (program mode) is witnessed, not proved. fn-native-admin-plan-create-ignores-special-purpose: for every creatable name, including RFC 5536 section 3.1.4's specific-purpose names (fn-native-admin-group-name-special-purposep: a first or only component "to" or "control", any component "all" or "ctl", exactly "junk", case folded), a well-formed `group create NAME` plans exactly the accepted :create-group of the typed name with no capacity, rows or policy, so no plan field derives from the special-purpose class.
proofs.progress_note: Lanes group-name-validity (grammar, 2026-09-24) and group-names-2 (reserved names, 2026-09-24). Teeth: records-shape-tests has the grammar witnesses and seven must-fails; native-admin-tests and native-operator-tests have the reserved witnesses (example, example.test, Example.a, EXAMPLE.test, poster, POSTER, Poster refused; fn.example, examples.test, poster.x, fn.poster accepted; retire of example.test accepted) and one must-fail per hypothesis. fn-record-group-namep-bounds-length-by-definition is the local bound by definition and is not cited. Lane defaults-precise (2026-09-24): specific-purpose recognizer and the local-agreement theorem; teeth in native-admin-tests (15 special witnesses, 12 near misses, the plan witness over five special names and one ordinary, one must-fail per hypothesis). persvati run-20260924T230642Z-0e1b.

proofs.title: RETIRED (D34, lane migration-removal): Offline store-profile upgrade: the operator's fields (format 8), only non-shrinking upgrades, every gate monotone, old or new at every crash cut
proofs.statement: The store profile is the operator's (D27): format fn-store-8, twelve fields validated by fn-bs-profile-validp (1 <= T <= 2^32-1; R <= H; R at least every Store event kind's publication ceiling; R, A, G and the group-name bound within their codec ceilings; 1 <= K <= T; each namespace count in 1..2^32-1), with a format-7 tuple run under its translation fn-bs-profile-of. fn-bs-profile-validp-codecs-accept: every field of the profile a store runs under is within its codec, and when admitted R covers every kind. fn-profile-upgradep OLD NEW holds when OLD is admitted, NEW is a valid profile, NEW is not OLD, and none of the twelve fields is smaller; fn-profile-upgrade-format-7-to-8: a format-7 tuple upgrades to its translation with every kind's budget unchanged, and the verb with no field writes exactly that. Monotone gates, over the functions the host calls at open and publication: fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-txn-observation (fn-profile-txn-observation with the profile's max_transactions, host/native/io.lisp fnn-transaction-files), fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-replay-bound (fn-profile-replay-within-boundp with max_history_octets, per record from fnn-durable-records), fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-publication-admissibility (fn-bs-publication-admissiblep, fnn-publish) and fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-verdict (fn-sbud-verdict: the count gate and the history-octet gate, fn-sbud-verdict-is-the-count-and-history-admissibility). Replay takes no profile argument, so an admitted store replays to the same state. fn-profile-upgrade-verdict-writes-only-upgrades: an :upgrade verdict of the function fnn-command-upgrade-profile calls (through fn-store-profile-upgrade-verdict) carries octets that decode to the requested profile, an upgrade of the store's (under A-CRYPTO, fn-bs-config-decode-of-encode, now over every valid profile); fn-profile-upgrade-budget-after-reopen: the next open's budget is the requested profile's. fn-bs-profile-program-crash-is-old-or-new: for the byte program fnn-upgrade-profile-write runs, from a store with nothing pending, every crash image of every cut of the successful run names the old inode with its old content or the new inode with exactly the staged octets; -crash-budget-is-old-or-new gives the old or the new budget. Covered scope: the successful run and its crash images; syscall error arms are classified by the host and witnessed natively, not modelled. The owner's history gate uses a carried record-octet sum equal to the kernel's when the cache is a prefix sum (fn-sbud-bytes-used-is-kernel-sum); the host resets it at profile install and relies on committed records growing append-only within one owner process, which is stated, not proved.
proofs.progress_note: Retired 2026-09-26 by D34 (fresh deploys, no migrations): its subject was removed with it (the offline upgrade relation fn-profile-upgradep, fn-profile-upgrade-verdict and P-PROFILE, books/store-profile-upgrade.lisp and books/byte-store-profile-program.lisp). What now covers the property: a deploy is a reinstall plus store import (PRF-205); the store has one format (books/store-profile-open.lisp fn-spo-config-open-store-format-is-exactly-a-foreign-frame). The id is kept.

proofs.title: Transaction-prefix reclaim keeps the reconstructed history, over the functions the reclaim and the next open call
proofs.statement: Let NAMES be the transaction namespace the reclaim observed, LOWER the selected pack's boundary (fn-ccp-framed-boundary, the value fn-ccp-coverage-framed returns to host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-pack-lower-bound), and GONE any subset of fn-bs-pack-reclaim-plan NAMES MAXIMUM LOWER (the names fnn-pack-prefix-reclaim unlinks; every process-death image of its program deletes such a subset). fn-ccp-reclaim-keeps-namespace-observation: if fn-profile-txn-observation NAMES MAXIMUM LOWER (the open gate host/native/io.lisp fnn-transaction-files calls through fn-store-txn-observation-selected) is valid, then on NAMES without GONE it is valid and equals the old observation with exactly GONE's pairs left out. fn-ccp-covered-deletion-keeps-reconstruction: when fn-ccp-observe-framed (the body of host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-checkpoint-compaction-observe, called by fnn-pack-recover-records inside fnn-recover) answers :ok on an observation, it answers identically on any sub-observation that leaves out only pairs below the pack boundary. fn-ccp-reclaim-preserves-reconstructed-history composes the two over the host's read of each issued pair: if the open before the reclaim reconstructed its history, the open after the reclaim (at any cut) observes a valid namespace and hands the generic replay the identical record list. fn-ccp-complete-observation-reconstructs-its-records: for a complete contiguous observation from 0 at least as long as the boundary, that list is exactly the records read, which is what the same open handed replay before any pack existed. Hypotheses: the pre-reclaim open succeeded (the reclaim command runs only after its own fnn-open-live-store), LOWER is the selected pack's boundary, and the bytes of every surviving name are unchanged (for the uncovered suffix, fn-bs-selected-reclaim-crash-preserves-suffix-payload in the byte model; the reclaim program writes no file content). Replay is a function of the record list, the frontier and the configuration records, and the reclaim program touches neither the frontier nor config.json, so GROUP counts and watermarks, ARTICLE by number and by Message-ID, HDR, retention pins and every other replayed fact are unchanged; that last step is by definition, not a theorem. One owner: fn-bs-pack-reclaim-plan reads fn-profile-txn-observation (no inline bound), and fn-ccp-profile-upgrade-keeps-reclaim-plan gives its monotonicity under an offline profile upgrade.
proofs.progress_note: Retired 2026-09-27 (lane flip-cleanup, 2026-09-27; design 2026-09-27 storage-log section 9 row 5, log-recovery's section 6 continuation): its subject was deleted with the pack layer. A format-9 store has no transaction namespace and no packs: `store compact` publishes a state checkpoint with the log rotated and drops the covered segments (host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-command-compact). books/checkpoint-compaction-preservation.lisp, books/byte-store-compaction-correspondence.lisp and books/store-compact-verb.lisp and their tests are gone, with the host wrappers (host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-checkpoint-compaction-observe/-coverage, fn-store-compact-decide), which no native line had called since the native pack verbs went (PKT-838). What covers the property now: the drop preserves the open's history (PRF-270, fn-lg-segment-drop-preserves-the-open). The two operator keystones (`store compact` is exactly the compact action) moved to PRF-270. Before: Lane m5-compaction (2026-09-24). Certified on persvati (run-20260924T213519Z-7956, manifest certify-20260924T213534Z-827010, ACL2 8.7, every book under 4 s) and on hbox with the w28 toolchain. Teeth: a reachable five-event store (record, undertaking, release, identity, enrollment) whose open before, after losing covered names 1 and 3, and after the whole plan reconstructs the same five records; concrete counterexamples and a must-fail for each composition hypothesis (a suffix gap; losing the newest suffix name, which the gate accepts and which silently drops record 4; a plan computed above the pack boundary, same loss; a conflicting surviving covered file, refused before and accepted after). Native, developer image of this branch on hbox: six operator POSTs around a selected pack, then reclaim and every reclaim cut (each covered unlink occurrence and the directory barrier); GROUP, ARTICLE by number and by Message-ID, HDR Subject and store retention are identical, the suffix files byte-identical, and the next POST gets high+1. Open: the byte model states survival for the uncovered suffix only, not old-or-absent for a covered name; guards of the framed observe stay unverified (the Store-event decoder chain); one pack holds at most 4096 events and 4 MiB, so the exact-history pack cannot compact an arbitrarily large store; no operator entry reaches reclaim (developer `checkpoint` verb only). Lane m5-compact-verb (2026-09-24): the operator entry `operator CONFIG store compact` (fn-cverb-decide decides pack+select+reclaim+retire, resume, or a named refusal; the host carries out exactly those steps). fn-cverb-pack-fits-the-profile-budget: when the decision packs, every file present plus the pack the host seals from the same records fits the profile's aggregate bound (field 3); fn-cverb-pack-decision-capture-succeeds: a pack decision on an exact event history below a uint32 frontier is never refused by the capture; the operator argv reaches :compact exactly for `store compact` (two native-operator theorems). The 4 MiB pack is kept as the compaction unit (refused by name above it; the 4096-event limit never binds, fn-cverb-profile-count-within-pack-events). Native on images of 5181e0ea: the ten CHECKPOINT_CUTS (now including the two retire cuts) pass through the developer checkpoint verbs and the operator verb, 20/20; the production image compacts, rereads every article identically and posts at high+1. Finding 3 of m5-compaction is not detectable from the open's observation: the frontier is reserved before the record, so a lost newest file equals an abandoned reservation (fn-cverb-open-history-gate-admits-a-lost-suffix); a post-commit witness is a decision for ember. Lane bounds-p1-profile (2026-09-25): fn-cverb-profile-count-within-pack-events is renamed fn-cverb-preset-count-within-pack-events and holds for the presets only; under an operator profile with max_transactions above 4096 (the D27 default is 2^32-1) the 4096-event pack limit can refuse compaction by name (:exceeds-compaction-unit) until chained packs (P5).

proofs.title: LIST COUNTS is the archive's exact count from the pinned buckets; a Message-ID retrieval's number names the same article
proofs.statement: For a projection archive and the group buckets the owner carries (the build of its articles), fn-gidx-list-counts-command-is-the-archive-fold equates the served LIST COUNTS reply, read from the pinned buckets, with the archive fold fn-nntp-list-counts-command, for every argument list; fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned-list-counts states it at the pinned dispatcher; fn-nntp-group-count-is-listgroup-length makes the count field the length of LISTGROUP's number list for the group, with no hypothesis; fn-gidx-counts-work-of-build-bound bounds the reply's bucket work by G*B + M for G distinct listed groups, B buckets and M memberships (linear per group in B plus its own entries, each visited a constant number of passes; an empty group adds one lookup in the next-number table). For ARTICLE, HEAD, BODY and STAT with a Message-ID the number is fn-nntp-msgid-local-number: the article's available number in the selected group, else 0 (RFC 3977 section 6.2.1.2); under fn-statep (fresh local numbers) fn-nntp-msgid-number-retrieves-the-same-article shows a positive number, sent back as any number token reading as it, retrieves the same article in the same group, the section's second-ARTICLE clause. fn-served-step-list-counts-is-the-archive-counts and fn-served-step-msgid-retrieval-carries-the-local-number carry both to fn-served-step, which fn-own-read runs (fn-own-read-is-served-step-on-pinned-prefix; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk), under the trie and bucket relations fn-own-relation carries and one framed command line. Excluded: HDR/XHDR/GROUP/NEXT/LAST, which still fold the archive; elapsed-time performance.

proofs.title: D23 relay trust: carriage, authorship and release authority are separate questions over the functions bp-node calls
proofs.statement: fn-bpaj-carried-source-decision CFG P G SOURCE (books/bp-session-admission.lisp) is the one decision for a delivered bundle: :direct when SOURCE is the delivering neighbour P's own enrolled EID; :carried P A when P's boundary has a (P "bp-boundary-carries" SOURCE 0) row and A is the unique boundary directly enrolled with transport-bp SOURCE; else refused with :generation, :source-not-carried or :carried-source-unenrolled. fn-bpaj-carried-decision-is-the-authors-direct-decision: a carried decision names an author whose own delivery of SOURCE at the same generation is decided :direct under A. fn-bpaj-carried-request-is-judged-as-the-authors-direct-request: for a carried view and a view identical except that its CL ingress names A at the same generation, fn-bpah-request-trustedp (host/bp-native-app-host.lisp, called by host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-request-result) answers the same and fn-bpaj-transit-plan (called by fn-owner-app-plan-install) returns the same plan. fn-bpaj-unlisted-carried-request-is-refused: when P's boundary has neither a transport-bp nor a carries row for SOURCE, the request check does not trust the view and the plan is (:refused :no-principal). fn-bpaj-carried-unenrolled-request-is-refused: for a CL ingress at the current generation of a well-formed configuration whose neighbour carries SOURCE while no row enrols SOURCE as a transport-bp EID, the decision is (:refused :carried-source-unenrolled), the request check does not trust it and the plan is refused. Release authority (books/bp-release-authority.lisp, host-called as fn-bpah-receipt-release-record through fn-owner-bp-receipt-release-record by fnn-bpnode-receipt-result, which publishes only the record it returns): fn-bpah-unauthorized-issuer-releases-nothing: for a bare (unsigned) receipt whose issuer is neither the delivering neighbour's own enrolled EID nor on its (NAME "bp-boundary-releases-for" EID 0) list, the host's gate fn-bpah-receipt-gatep is false and the release record is nil. fn-bpah-carrier-without-release-row-releases-nothing: the same for a bare receipt when the neighbour's boundary has no transport-bp and no releases-for row for the issuer, with no hypothesis about its carries rows. fn-bpah-released-receipt-names-exactly-its-obligation: a non-nil record implies the receipt is authorized (a signed receipt by fn-bpah-receipt-signature-verifiedp, a bare one by fn-bpah-release-issuer-authorizedp), the work the receipt's work id finds is outstanding and satisfies fn-bp-authorized-receiptp, the record's work id is that work's, and fn-bprl-apply-journal-record admits it. fn-bpah-receipt-naming-other-terms-releases-nothing: a receipt whose work id finds no outstanding work, or whose subject, policy or terms differ from that work's, gives nil. Signed receipts (books/bp-signed-receipt.lisp frame; preimage fn-bpsr-signed-preimage, the article scheme's fn-hsig-subject-body under the tag fn-bp-receipt-hybrid-v1 over the requester EID and the exact receipt ADU; host observations by fnn-hsig-observe-raw, the verdict fn-hsig-authorize; A-CRYPTO): fn-bpah-signed-receipt-releases-through-any-carrier: for a signed receipt of the delivered shape whose signature verifies under the issuer's own enrollment at this node (the unique boundary directly enrolled for the issuer EID names the principal in a bp-boundary-receipt-signer row, and this Store's current keyring snapshot for the principal gives the keys), the release record is fn-bprl-receipt-auto-record of the carried ADU with authorization equal to fn-bpah-receipt-names-obligationp; no hypothesis mentions the delivering neighbour's rows. fn-bpah-unverified-signed-receipt-releases-nothing: a signed receipt whose signature does not verify gives a false gate and a nil record whoever delivered it. fn-bpah-receipt-signature-needs-both-observations: verification implies both primitive observations are :verified and the signer row is the issuer's own. fn-bpah-trusted-bare-receipt-releases: for a bare receipt the gate trusts on a carrier without require-signed-receipts, the record is the workflow's answer with authorization equal to the obligation check (a listed relay's forgery naming the exact obligation releases: the delegation profile). fn-bpah-required-signature-refuses-bare-receipts: under (NAME "bp-boundary-require-signed-receipts" "yes" 0) on the delivering neighbour a bare receipt gives a false gate and a nil record. fn-bpah-request-trust-ignores-release-rows and fn-bpaj-source-decision-ignores-release-rows: two configurations at one generation, equally well-formed, that agree after dropping releases-for rows make the same source decision and trust the same requests.
proofs.progress_note: Lane d23-issuer-authority (2026-09-24): receipts release only under the release list and the exact obligation; certified on hbox w28 run-20260924T231033Z-cfaf (manifest certify-20260924T231054Z-2148356, 94 books, the affected sets of bp-session-admission and native-admin) and run-20260924T232022Z-575d (certify-20260924T232040Z-2181356, 20 books, bp-release-authority and native-admin after the cost fix; every book under 10 s). Lab: planning/evidence/d23-issuer-authority-2026-09-24.md. Lane d23-bp-carrier (2026-09-24). Certified on hbox with the w28 toolchain: run-20260924T222039Z-5919 (manifest certify-20260924T222100Z-2041510, 85 books, the affected set of bp-session-admission, native-admin and native-operator, every book under 9 s); bp-session-admission and its tests in certify-20260924T221731Z-2038126. Lab: through dtn7-rs with one and two relays the request is accepted under the author's enrollment and the receipt is accepted at home (planning/evidence/d23-bp-carrier-2026-09-24.md). The bp-boundary verb takes `carries EID ...'; its rows ride the :set-peer delta, the configuration record round-trips and replay recovers them (ground witness in native-admin-tests). Teeth: one must-fail per hypothesis of each theorem and reachable witnesses in bp-transit-join-tests (a relay carrying dtn://b/ with dtnB enrolled plans the same :submit under dtnB), bp-session-admission-tests and bp-app-handoff-tests (a relayed receipt). Open: bp-node serve's own forwarding still expects the application peer as its TCPCL neighbour (a routing choice, not this rule); verification of a signed article against the author's enrollment is the posting path's.

proofs.title: M5 committed-history boundary: no reachable history is refused, a lost suffix containing an acknowledged or resolved record is refused by name, and a required store refuses an absent marker
proofs.statement: Over the host-called decisions fn-hm-after-commit (what the marker holds after the record of SEQUENCE: the FNSM kind-3 frame of SEQUENCE+1, host/native/io.lisp fnn-mark-committed) and fn-hm-open-verdict (the open's check, io.lisp fnn-check-history-marker called by fnn-recover with the reconstructed record count), and the history step fn-hm-step: burned reservations, uncertain publications that did or did not survive, and commits whose marker program crashed at any cut, with a crash table in which the marker is old before the rename, old or new after it, and new after the root barrier. fn-hm-run-keeps-every-open-admitted: from an admitted state, every such history with its count within uint32 is admitted. fn-hm-open-refuses-a-lost-acknowledged-record: after a commit whose marker program completed at a natural count C, followed by any history within uint32, an open that observes K <= C records is (:refused :history-short-of-marker M), where M is the marker's count. fn-hm-decode-of-encode: the marker codec round-trips every uint32. D31 (books/store-history-required.lisp), over the host-called decisions fn-hmr-open-verdict and fn-hmr-catch-up (io.lisp fnn-check-history-marker, the catch-up written by fnn-recover through fnn-mark-committed) and fn-hmr-upgrade-verdict (io.lisp fnn-command-upgrade-profile), and the history step fn-hmr-step over (D marker A profile live): burns, uncertain publications, commits in a live process crashed at any marker cut or finished (A covers the record), opens whose catch-up crashed at any cut or completed (live only then), resolutions of a held record in a live process (A covers it), and migrations whose profile crash image is old or new. fn-hmr-step-preserves-the-invariant (the model lemma the next rests on; not a registry event): the open admits, A <= M, and a live process's marker counts D. fn-hmr-open-refuses-below-every-answered-record: after any history from an invariant state, an open observing K < A records (K natural) is (:refused :history-short-of-marker M). fn-hmr-required-store-never-admits-an-absent-marker: from a required profile, after any history, an absent marker at any natural count is (:refused :marker-missing). fn-hmr-requirement-follows-a-covering-marker: a step that makes an unmarked profile required is a migration in a live process over a marker counting D, and leaves the marker. fn-hmr-legacy-store-migrates-by-the-two-step: from an unmarked store no process holds, two steps reach required only as an open (the catch-up) then a migration, over the covering marker.
proofs.progress_note: Retired 2026-09-27 (lane log-recovery-2, PKT-838; design 2026-09-27 storage-log section 9 row 3): its subject was deleted with the per-file layout. A format-9 store has no committed-history marker (M := D: the log's last complete entry is the committed history, design section 3.4); fnn-mark-committed, fnn-check-history-marker, books/store-history-marker.lisp and books/store-history-required.lisp and their tests are gone, and every image refuses a format-8 store at the profile's open (books/store-profile-open.lisp fn-spo-open-of-a-format-8-profile-refuses-by-name). What covers the property now: the log's scan and recovery (P-LOG-RECOVER, books/store-log-segments.lisp, PRF-270) -- a lost acknowledged record cannot exist because the acknowledgement follows the batch's barrier. Before: Lane m5-history-lifetimes (2026-09-24). Certified on persvati (run-20260924T230612Z-64bc, manifest certify-20260924T230629Z-1648710, ACL2 8.7 w25, book 2.5 s, tests 2.2 s; at 72d40647, run-20260924T232158Z-fa11, manifest certify-20260924T232218Z-1792716, book 2.6 s, tests 2.3 s). Teeth: a reachable seven-step history (commit, burn, commit crashed after rename with the old marker, surviving uncertain record, commit, burn, lost uncertain) that is admitted, refuses a lost newest record by name, and admits the same history after further burns. For every hypothesis of both keystones, a concrete instance where the others hold and the conclusion is false. Open: the crash table is not a program of the fn-bs byte model; an absent marker is admitted; an unacknowledged survivor above the marker is not covered.

proofs.title: The native request is the workflow's request for exactly that work, over the plan bp-obligation request executes
proofs.statement: fn-bprq-plan S WORK ATTEMPT FN-ARENA (books/bp-request-plan.lisp), called by host/workflow-host.lisp fn-workflow-request-plan, which host/native/bp-obligation.lisp fnn-bpo-request-publish calls, returns nil or (:request ATTEMPT-RECORD OUTCOME KEY ADU DESTINATION RETRY). fn-bprq-plan-is-the-works-request: whenever it returns a plan, the attempt record is an :attempt naming exactly WORK and ATTEMPT, KEY (the FNBS job key the host enqueues under) is (WORK ATTEMPT generation) with the attempt's generation, ADU decodes exactly (fn-bpa-decode-exact) to fn-bpa-make-request over the work WORK holds in the image reached by publishing RETRY (if any), the attempt and its durable outcome (fn-bprq-published-state), with the article field the octets fn-arena-payload reads from the payload arena under that work's committed node article's handle, which is a sealed handle (natp, below fn-arena-count; the records flip, PKT-RT-1: the arena is only read, and the ADU never carries the handle), that request is fn-bpa-requestp with work id WORK, and DESTINATION is that work's peer EID. Hypothesis: the plan exists. The published image is the host's: fn-bpiw-apply on these records is fn-bprl-apply-journal-record (reachable witness in the test book, not a general theorem). ION is an adapter: fn-bpiw-attempt-record-is-the-generic-attempt (test book) equates the ION constructor with fn-bprq-attempt-record, which host/workflow-host.lisp fn-workflow-ion-attempt-record now calls. Not claimed: that the image's work fields equal those before the attempt (they are stated over the published image), any transport or receipt property, or recovery of a fenced attempt.

Certified on hbox, w28 ACL2 8.7, 2 jobs: run-20260924T230759Z-4d2f (manifest certify-20260924T230813Z-2144048, bp-request-plan 7.6 s, tests 1.9 s) at the source of commit 41799aaf; the first run (certify-20260924T230223Z-2118502) certified the plan before the retry-request clause.
