proofs.title: A control article is filed only in control.<verb>, or refused, over the filing plan every ingress calls
proofs.statement: fn-ctl-control-article-is-filed-only-in-control: for every received octet string that fn-ctl-classify-octets classifies (:control VERB ARGS), fn-pa-filing-plan RECEIVED GROUPS DOMAIN (books/peer-authored-accept.lisp; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-control-filing calls it and host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit calls that first, for served POST, bound submission, NNTP transit and BP transit, and host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-hybrid-control-author calls fn-owner-control-filing itself for the local signed-author path) either files the article in exactly one group, its filing group fn-ctl-filing-group VERB, which is "control" or begins "control." and is a member of DOMAIN, or refuses it :control-not-filed; the ingress's own GROUPS (the names its Newsgroups field gave) are never the answer unless they are that group. fn-ctl-classify-reads-only-the-control-field: inserting any field F whose name is neither control nor supersedes anywhere in a field list leaves fn-ctl-classify-fields unchanged. fn-ctl-cmsg-subject-is-ordinary: an article whose parsed fields have no Control field is filed in GROUPS unchanged by fn-pa-filing-plan, whatever its Subject, Newsgroups or Also-Control. Covered scope: the filing decision; the host's use of the filed groups is a transcribed stub test (tests/native_peer_authored_accept_raw.lisp) and the native cases of the evidence file. A signed control article is filed the same way (the :control-signed refusal was removed 2026-09-25 by lane control-c3 when the signed record binding came to name the filing group; PRF-084).
proofs.progress_note: Lane control-c1 (2026-09-25), packet C1 of planning/design-2026-09-25-control-messages.md. Teeth in tests/acl2/control-tests.lisp: reachable witnesses (a cancel naming fn.test with control.cancel configured is filed in control.cancel; without it, refused; a cmsg Subject article and a .ctl/Also-Control article keep fn.test), must-fail per hypothesis (an ordinary article is filed outside control; a Control field or a Supersedes field inserted changes the classification; a signed control article is not filed). 2026-09-25 (control-c3): the signed record binding names the filing group, so a signed control article is filed; fn-ctl-unsigned-control-filing-by-definition became fn-ctl-control-filing-by-definition without its carrier hypothesis.

proofs.title: A held bundle is offered only to the routed hop, over the step the host calls; unrouted bundles stay held and are reported; the decision is deterministic in the table
proofs.statement: fn-bpnp-step-offers-only-the-routed-hop: for a routed :session event (:session PEER S t MRU OBS (:via HOP ANNOUNCED TABLE)) to fn-bpnp-step (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-foundation-step, from host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-forward-session), a :persist-attempt effect is for the row the arrival-order scan chose, and fn-bprt-next-hop of that row's own destination EID text over TABLE and live set (HOP) is HOP, the route fn-bprt-hop-route is a member of TABLE whose pattern matches the destination and whose boundary is HOP, and ANNOUNCED is the octets of that route's enrolled EID. fn-bpnp-step-unrouted-bundle-stays-held-and-is-reported: if the issued operation is not uncertain, no row the table routes to HOP is ready, the scan over every held row is ready and no route in TABLE matches that row's destination, the step's only effect is (:forward-no-route ARRIVAL HOP :no-route) and the held list is unchanged. fn-bprt-next-hop-deterministic-in-the-table: two tables whose routes matching DEST are the same set give DEST the same answer. fn-bprt-next-hop-names-a-live-matching-route: a boundary answer is the boundary of a live matching route in the table. Covered scope: the 7-field routed :session arm and the :resume arm with VIA scan only the rows the table routes to HOP (PRF-103); a :session open or :resume without VIA offers nothing; LIVE is the single session's hop.
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-routing (2026-09-25). Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-route-tests.lisp: a reachable witness (the bp-node-forward-retry fixture's held transit to dtn://bp-dest/, routed to relay, proposes the attempt) and must-fail cases for an unlisted hop, a wrong announced EID, a prefix route to another boundary, the route present (no report), and tables whose matching sets differ.

proofs.title: Bounds join: an article the profile admits is a record it publishes; the group-name ceiling is the label width; a refused operator article names the profile bound
proofs.statement: fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record (books/byte-store-frame.lisp): under a profile a store runs under (fn-bs-profile-admittedp), every record whose payload is at most the article field A and whose group count is at most G encodes (fn-record-encode) to at most the record field R; it rests on fn-record-encode-length-bound and the validity relation R >= fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling A G (:max-record-octets-below-the-article-record in fn-bs-profile-validp, which the host calls through fn-bs-profile-init-verdict, host/store-host.lisp:385, fn-profile-upgrade-verdict, :429, and fn-bs-profile-admittedp at install, host/owner-host.lisp:219). The format-7 translation takes G and the group name at the codec ceilings and R as the larger of H/T and the article record of (A, G). fn-cfg-labelp-of-record-group-name (books/config.lisp): every group name the record codec admits is a configuration label, the one statement relating *fn-record-max-group-name* and *fn-cfg-max-label*. fn-native-control-refusal-status-is-a-refusal (books/native-control.lisp): the control word for a refused operator submission (:article-exceeds-profile-bound for the injection reason :oversize, else :refused) is in the FNCT reply vocabulary and of class refused; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-control-submit-serialized calls it through fn-native-control-host-refusal-status. Covered scope: record encodings under a valid profile; the frame :blob width (131,072) and the owner's per-octet recursion at take are not covered.
proofs.progress_note: Lane bounds-join (2026-09-25). Teeth in tests/acl2/byte-store-frame-tests.lisp: a tight witness (R equal to the article record of its (A, G)); one refusal by name per argument of the relation; a concrete counterexample per hypothesis (a non-profile reads R = 0 while an empty record encodes to 70 octets; 196,609 payload octets in one group; six 256-octet groups at A). config-tests: a 256-octet group name is a 256-octet label; a 257-octet string is not a label. native-control-tests: the named status survives the sealed reply and exits 1; :uncertain and :fault are not refusals.

proofs.title: BP journal rotation: recovery from a selected held-row checkpoint equals recovery over the whole history, and every publication cut leaves one authority
proofs.statement: fn-bpnr-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover (restated for N16-F1, lane bp-n16-prod): for every authority plan0 that is not damaged, whose ordered received-final rows replay :ready, the projection ck1 of that replay (a checkpoint), E the epoch field of the recovery event over plan0 and the rows, and the file of the checkpoint the rotation publishes, fn-bpnr-rotation-checkpoint ck1 E (operation frontier (E . 0), the rotation's own id; what fn-bpnp-rotate-step's effect carries and host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-publish-generation writes): fn-bpnr-recover-auto-event (the event fnn-bps-open passes to fn-bpnp-step) over that file with no later rows names epoch E + 1 with the old replay at frontier (E . 0) and row count 0, so no operation after the reopen reuses the rotation's id; over later rows that start after (E . 0) it equals the event over plan0 and the concatenated rows with field 5 set to the later rows' count. fn-bpnr-rotation-crash-recovers-old-or-new: at every phase of the publication driver fn-bpnr-publish-action/-step/-outcome (followed by fnn-bps-publish-generation) and for either outcome of an atomic rename, the visible selection file is the old or the new one, before the rename may have been issued it is the old one, and under the new one recovery with no rows is the reopen event above. fn-bpnp-rotate-step-proposes-only-own-projection: a proposal carries fn-bpnr-rotation-checkpoint of the state's own projection, from a quiescent state, and its file exists. fn-bpnr-retirement-cut-keeps-open-view: when the root's selection file selects G and no other name the open reads is retired, the open's view (selection plan, selected directory, the other names) after any prefix of fn-bpnr-retire-ops (the removal program host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-retire-generations runs step by step: older generation directories and killed rotations' staged selections) equals the view before it; fn-bpnr-retired-names-never-the-selected-directory. fn-bpnr-checkpoint-decode-of-octets: every file fn-bpnr-checkpoint-octets writes decodes to its checkpoint. Covered scope: one atomically renamed kind-19 file; the chunked kinds 19 plus a manifest kind, the :quiesce event and the empty new-generation premise are not modelled; the removal model is a name-to-entry alist, not K0's byte store; the codec runs on octet lists (no D27 concrete twin); a killed rotation's unselected new-generation directory is kept (never reused). Natural rotation (lane bp-rotation, 2026-09-27; books/bp-node-rotation-due.lisp): host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bps-rotate-when-due, called at the open of bp-node serve and dispatch (fnn-bps-open-node), drives fn-bpnrd-due-rotation-event's answer. fn-bpnrd-due-rotation-event-by-definition: it answers (:rotate G CK) exactly when the profile is a profile 3, the recovered generation's record count has reached its rotation threshold and the state is quiescent, with G above the selected generation and CK the checkpoint of the open's recovery event (the event `bp-node checkpoint` drives). fn-bpnrd-due-rotation-preserves-recovery: when the open drove the host's recovery event (fn-bpnr-recover-auto-event over ROWS0 and a non-damaged PLAN0 whose replay is :ready, with a clock-domain decision appended), the machine state is at that event's epoch E, and fn-bpnp-rotate-step proposes the due event's publication, the published checkpoint read back at the machine's depth budget recovers with no later rows epoch E + 1 with the old replay at frontier (E . 0) and row count 0, and over later rows that start after (E . 0) the event over PLAN0 and the concatenated rows with field 5 set to their count. The state/epoch premise is a hypothesis (the recovery arm's installation of the epoch is not restated). The publication and retirement programs are the operator rotation's, so the crash and retirement keystones above cover every cut of it. In-serve rotation (lane bp-retention-leftovers): host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bps-serve-rotate-when-due asks fn-bpnrd-serve-rotation-due-p between sessions (threshold reached at a safe point: nothing issued, no pending image, no outbound session), recovers in place under the locks the serve holds (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-reopen-in-place), drives the open-time decision's rotation and reopens in place. KEYSTONE fn-bpnrd-rotation-keeps-every-held-family: for every state the machine rotates from, a proposed publication's file reopens (no rows) :ready with exactly that state's held rows, handoffs and arrival frontier at frontier (E . 0).

Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-node-counterexamples-tests: the positive trace through fn-bpnp-step, must-fails for a damaged plan0, absent octets and an unready prefix (recovery keystone) and a visible new file before the rename (crash keystone). Certified in hbox runs run-20260925T044146Z-230d, run-20260925T050214Z-702e and run-20260925T051528Z-15c2. Lane bp-rotation (2026-09-27, F7): natural rotation by a profile threshold at a node verb's open; teeth in tests/acl2/bp-node-rotation-due-tests (reachable witness over N16's real rows through fn-bpnp-step with a clock-domain decision; must-fails for later rows at the rotation's id, and corrupted-state witnesses for the publication and epoch premises); tests/test_bp_fragment_node_native's rotation test runs on production and developer images with no developer cut.

proofs.title: Open from an exact-state Store checkpoint equals the full open
proofs.statement: fn-sn-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover: for every configuration history, frontier, record prefix P and suffix Q, (fn-sco-open (fn-sco-capture configs P) configs frontier Q) equals (fn-cpo-open-observed configs frontier (append P Q)), with no hypothesis; fn-sco-open is what the host calls at open when a checkpoint verified (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint) and fn-cpo-open-observed is the full open (fn-store-sn-recover). Built from one append lemma per fold of fn-cpo-open-observed: fn-cpr-loop-append (configuration and node fold, paused at the prefix end), fn-replay-identity-append, fn-cpe-projection-replay-append, fn-th-prefix-project-append, fn-cei-build-append; the history recognizer runs over the carried record list. fn-sco-extend-of-capture: the next checkpoint is the extension. fn-sco-capture-of-later-configs: a configuration whose txid is above every covered record does not change the capture. fn-scc-decode-segments-of-segments: the FNSC segments decode to the value, for every tree whose program and record count fit the u64 header fields. fn-bs-scp-program-crash-is-old-or-new: at every cut of the publish program the checkpoint name is the old file, absent, or the new octets. fn-bs-read-ranges-concatenate: consecutive range reads concatenate under A-HOST-EXCLUSIVE-READ. Owner (2026-09-25, lane owner-checkpoint-open): fn-owner-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover, with no hypothesis: the owner fn-ock-recover-extended installs from (fn-sco-extend (fn-sco-capture configs P) configs Q) is the owner fn-ock-recover-full installs from the full open of P ++ Q (the composition fn-orec-recover-installs-ocl-relation is stated over: the Store open, the configuration replay, fn-own-start's archive, views, trie and ledger, fn-own-configure, fn-ocfg-make) or :fault on both; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-extended calls fn-ock-recover-extended on both paths (fn-owner-recover-from-checkpoint over the decoded checkpoint and the suffix, fn-owner-recover over the empty capture and the whole history, fn-ock-recover-from-empty-capture-is-full). fn-ock-recover-installs-ocl-relation carries fn-ocl-relation and fn-scar-view-indexedp to what is installed on either path. Publication: fn-ock-next-checkpoint-is-the-capture (hypothesis: an admitted history, which has no must-fail) and fn-ock-published-checkpoint-opens-to-the-full-open: what the owner publishes is the capture of its whole history and opens, over any later records, to the full open; fn-ock-not-due-keeps-the-checkpoint-open: until fn-ock-publication-duep (twice the suffix reaches K) the durable checkpoint is the one a restart selects. Replay carries the node invariant: fn-cpr-apply-event-preserves-cnode-statep (no hypothesis beyond non-refusal) and fn-cpr-loop-preserves-cnode-statep; fn-cpr-apply-event and fn-cpr-loop test a refusal by NIL on the executable path. Recovery-lag policy (2026-09-26, lane checkpoint-pipeline-5, PKT-583 (b), gpt-6's review section 2): fn-ock-publication-next (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-sco-due) decides :due, :idle, :blocked, :inflight or :coalesce; fn-ock-one-publication-in-flight: while one publication is in flight (the count it captured) the decision is never :due and the rule's observation is the one coalesced request; fn-ock-publication-next-decides-by-the-rule: with nothing in flight it is fn-ock-publication-duep at the frontier given unless a recorded deferral blocks; fn-ock-finish-binds-the-captured-prefix: the next checkpoint's sequence is the count the capture was handed (fn-owner-sco-publication-done records it as the durable S, never the count at the finish); fn-ock-fast-path-within-k-by-definition: K is the fast path's threshold at fn-sco-select, the full replay past it (the honest fallback; not a guaranteed maximum suffix). RECORDS FLIP (lanes checkpoint-arena, checkpoint-arena-2, 2026-09-27; books/store-checkpoint-arena.lisp, -load.lisp, -writer.lisp): the file carries the ARENA run first (the canonical payloads, batched, framed and chained like every run), then the four tables of the capture of the CANONICAL rows. fn-intern-events-is-intern-at (no hypothesis) and fn-intern-events-arena-is-payloads (the intern not refused, the arena a true list): the open's intern is the counter intern fn-scka-intern-at and its arena the canonical payloads. fn-scka-load-of-written-file: a plan whose segments are the arena run of PS followed by the tables' runs of the capture of RECORDS loads (fn-scka-load: fn-scka-open-run, the host's fn-scka-seal-n calls, which are one loop by fn-scka-seal-n-compose, fn-scka-finish) to those tables with the arena exactly PS. fn-scka-recover-from-checkpoint-is-full-recover (hypothesis: the whole history interns): from the capture of a prefix's canonical rows and its canonical arena, the recover over the suffix is the full recover of the whole history from the emptied arena, extension and arena; fn-scka-recover-rows-rii-is-recover-rows: the composition the host runs (fn-intern-events, then fn-rii-sco-extend) is that recover. fn-scka-write-run-is-run-segments (hypothesis: the batches sum to the payload count): the octets of the host's arena-run steps (fn-scka-write-step) are the run segments of the live rows' canonical payloads, for any buffer contents. fn-scka-next-checkpoint-is-capture: the owner's next checkpoint (its base extended over the canonical rows of the rows after it, handles from the base's payload count) is the capture of the canonical rows of all of them.
proofs.progress_note: Open items: K0 coverage of the publish program's :root rename and :root fsync (fn-bs-k0-step-inputp admits neither; the profile program has the same gap); the whole-file statement over the host's range loop; the publication keystone's history hypothesis has no must-fail (the identity fold's fault is absorbing); the pack, compaction and export verbs still re-encode the covered prefix's octets after a checkpoint open (fn-store-sco-prefix-octets; the owner's open no longer does, checkpoint-arena-2) and the Store open and the owner open each replay the suffix.

proofs.title: Control authority requires a verified principal and a covering grant; a withdrawal record is decided once and serves no view that holds its cancel
proofs.statement: fn-ctl-authorize-requires-verified-verdict: an :execute from fn-ctl-authorize VERDICT VERB GROUPS ROWS (books/control-authority.lisp) has verdict token :verified with a 32-octet principal. fn-ctl-authorize-requires-a-covering-grant: under :execute, for every GROUP of GROUPS, fn-ctl-covering-row is a member of ROWS whose principal is the verified one, whose verb is VERB and whose namespace pattern covers GROUP. fn-cfg-grant-control-admissible-iff: fn-cfg-delta-reason admits (fn-cfg-grant-control NS P VERB) iff NS is a namespace pattern, P 64 lowercase hex characters and VERB is cancel. fn-ctl-revoke-changes-decisions-not-records: when every cancel entry's txid is below the first appended configuration record's, fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals ENTRIES (append CONFIGS MORE) equals fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals ENTRIES CONFIGS. fn-ctl-cancel-executes-only-for-author-or-authority: a withdrawing fn-ctl-withdrawal-effect W T-GROUPS T-VERDICT means the target's verdict names W's principal, or W's scope is nonempty and covers every one of the nonempty T-GROUPS. fn-ctl-target-is-never-visible-beside-its-cancel: an article targeted by a record of WS whose cause is among ARTICLES and whose effect withdraws is not in fn-ctl-visible-articles ARTICLES WS VERDICTS. fn-ctl-pinned-view-keeps-its-archive: a record whose cause is absent from ARTICLES leaves the visible articles unchanged. fn-ctl-visible-is-arrival-order-independent: (T C . REST) and (C T . REST) serve the same articles. fn-hsig-signed-control-record-lists-its-filing-group: fn-hsig-carried-record-metadatap SOURCE RECEIVED RECORD (books/hybrid-store.lisp; a conjunct of the schema-1 and carried replay bindings replay's identity step calls, and required by the native constructor fn-hsig-authorized-carried-submission-event-base that host/native/hybrid-control.lisp and host/native/owner.lisp reach) with SOURCE classified (:control VERB ARGS) implies the record lists exactly (fn-ctl-filing-group VERB). fn-hsig-malformed-control-binds-no-record: a source classified :malformed binds no record. fn-ctl-visible-add-is-visible and fn-ctl-visible-extend-is-visible (books/control-visible.lisp): when the carried list equals fn-ctl-visible-articles OLD WS VERDICTS, the incremental list after one new article (resp. a batch DELTA) equals fn-ctl-visible-articles of (A . OLD) (resp. (append DELTA OLD)); an ordinary article costs one pass over WS, an executed cancel one pass over the visible list. fn-ctl-refresh-visible-is-visible (books/control-visible.lisp; called by fn-own-refresh, books/owner.lisp, which every owner step at an idle store runs): when the carried visible list equals fn-ctl-visible-articles OLD WS OLD-VERDICTS and NEW has distinct Message-IDs, fn-ctl-refresh-visible NEW OLD OLD-VISIBLE WS2 OLD-VERDICTS VERDICTS equals fn-ctl-visible-articles NEW WS2 VERDICTS, WS2 being fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals NEW OLD WS VERDICTS RECORDS CONFIGS (the records fn-ctl-withdrawal-plan decides for each cancel or superseding article the refresh first publishes, under fn-ctl-config-at of that article's own acceptance-record txid in the Store records RECORDS over the configuration journal CONFIGS). fn-ctl-articles-withdrawals-is-the-journal: the rebuild the refresh runs at a discontinuity (start, reopen) equals fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals over the archive's entries (TXID CAUSE VERDICT TARGET). fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals-is-the-journal (called by fn-own-refresh with the Store's records and fn-sn-config-history): when the carried records are the journal of the old archive under the old Store records R0, verdicts V0 and configuration journal C0, every withdrawing article of the old archive has its acceptance record in R0, the verdicts grew by at most one pair for a Message-ID outside the old archive, and the configuration records appended since carry txids above every old entry, the refresh's records over the grown inputs are the journal of the new archive under them: the live decision is recovery's. fn-ctl-withdrawal-plan-record-is-bound: a record names its cause, its target (a cancel argument or a Supersedes field, fn-ctl-article-target), the verified principal, the principal's cancel grants and the generation. fn-ctl-visible-state-statep: the visible state of an acceptance state is one. Supporting (not registry events; teeth are the owner tests' relation witnesses): fn-own-refresh-preserves-relation and fn-own-conn-serves-a-projection (books/owner-invariants.lisp), the restated K1 holds after every refresh; the committed view's archive is fn-ctl-visible-state of its prefix under the records and verdicts it carries, and a connection's archive is that prefix's state with a subsequence of its articles. Covered scope: the served view and every connection pinned after a withdrawing article's refresh, records decided at each article's own txid live and at recovery alike, Supersedes under the cancel's rules. Served answers (control-c3e; subject fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned, books/nntp.lisp, reached from fn-own-read through fn-served-step and fn-served-dispatch; the control pin is the fourth slot of the group pin, the owner connection's fn-own-conn-control set from fn-own-view-control at open and advance): fn-nntp-423-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-holder, when the pin's withdrawn list is fn-ctl-withdrawn-articles RAW WS VERDICTS, a `423 withdrawn' answer names an article of RAW holding the number that the view does not serve and the pinned archive holds nothing at that number; fn-nntp-withdrawn-holder-answers-423-withdrawn, the converse for ARTICLE/HEAD/BODY/STAT with one number argument and a selected group; fn-nntp-430-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-article and fn-nntp-withdrawn-article-answers-430-withdrawn, the same by Message-ID under the pinned trie's correspondence with the archive; fn-nntp-hdr-fn-control-is-the-status, `HDR :fn-control <msgid>' answers one line whose item is fn-ctl-control-item of fn-ctl-control-status (the kernel, over the trie by fn-ctl-served-status-is-control-status) of the article with that Message-ID, served or withdrawn, or 430, or 503 when the item would not be a clean field; fn-nntp-hdr-fn-control-executed-means-withdrawn, an executed status names a target RAW holds and the view does not serve, withdrawn by the record the article caused. fn-own-read-archive-command-is-the-pinned-dispatcher (books/owner-control-read.lisp; host line host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk): one read framing one archive command line answers that dispatcher's reply over the connection's archive, trie, buckets and control pin whenever the reply offers no article; fn-own-related-conn-control: under fn-own-relation a connection's control pin has W = fn-ctl-withdrawn-articles of its pinned prefix under the pinned records and its archive serves that prefix's visible list (fn-own-control-okp in fn-own-conn-okp; the view carries W = fn-ctl-subseq-diff of its raw and visible lists, refreshed by fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawn). Kernel (books/control-served.lisp): fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawn-is-withdrawn (now for any RAW), fn-ctl-number-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-holder, fn-ctl-msgid-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-article, fn-ctl-executed-status-means-withdrawn, fn-ctl-owed-status-means-not-held. Not covered: the owner-level lift has no teeth book yet (no reachable owner witness nor must-fail per hypothesis for fn-own-read-archive-command-is-the-pinned-dispatcher); the owner relation does not carry the journal equality nor the configuration-txid fact it rests on (records appended later have larger txids); the txid lookup walks the Store records (no Message-ID-to-txid index); a view with an empty group index pins no control, so it answers the plain 423/430 (a view serving no article). PKT-575 (PRF-256): fn-ctl-cancel-executes-only-for-author-or-authority gains the disjunct `the record's principal is :node` (the operator's withdrawal). After the records flip (flip-L8-2) the refresh reads a withdrawing article's target and Cancel-Key entries from its row's control fact in the Store's history (fn-ctl-article-plan; fn-hf-control-of-held-facts-of and fn-ctl-control-of-fields: the fact is the readers over the row's bytes), and fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals-is-the-journal's hypotheses are: the carried records are the journal of the old archive, the verdicts grew by at most one pair for a Message-ID outside it, no configuration record was appended or every appended one comes after every entry, and the history grew by the new article's rows only (fn-ctl-history-grows-by-p); records made before their target arrived are resolved to its locks by the refresh (fn-ctl-resolve-tlocks), as recovery reads them. After the records flip an archive article's payload position is an arena handle: the served HDR :fn-control reply (fn-nntp-control-hdr-response, books/nntp.lisp) reads the withdrawing article's octets through the arena (fn-nntp-article-bytes) and hands them to the kernel (fn-ctl-control-status C CBYTES ..., books/control-served.lisp; lane matrix-reds, PKT-850: before, the kernel parsed the handle and every executed withdrawal answered `none'); fn-nntp-hdr-fn-control-status-is-the-model-status (KEYSTONE, no hypothesis): that status and the item's target are the pre-flip kernel's over the article's octet model fn-nntp-article-alpha. Teeth over a flipped archive in tests/acl2/nntp-control-tests.lisp (handles 0 and 1; an empty arena answers `none').
proofs.progress_note: Lane control-c2c3 (2026-09-25), packets C2 and C3 of planning/design-2026-09-25-control-messages.md under D29. Teeth in tests/acl2/control-authority-tests.lisp: per keystone a reachable witness asserting antecedent and conclusion, and per hypothesis a removal witness (the carried verdict; the cross-post outside the grant; the wrong principal; the revoke before the cancel; the view pinned before the cancel; the early cancel). The two reconfiguration headlines (fn-ocl-no-reader-observes-a-half-change, fn-ocl-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation) are universally quantified over delta lists and were recertified with the new slot and kinds. Open: the served view (K1 restated over fn-ctl-visible-articles at fn-own-refresh), signed control filing, the host's commit-time call, Supersedes. Lane control-c3 (2026-09-25): the signed record binding names the filing group (the :control-signed refusal is gone, signed cancels can be verified), and the visible list has an incremental form with its correspondence keystones. Still open: the owner wiring (fn-own-refresh carrying the visible list, K1 restated), the host's commit-time and recovery calls, 430/423, HDR :fn-control, Supersedes, fn_verify. Lane control-c3d (2026-09-25): records decided at each withdrawing article's own Store txid, live and at recovery (the journal keystones); Supersedes; the config-owner-live rules scoped (15.1 s to 7.6 s); the reader kernel for 423/430 withdrawn and HDR :fn-control with no caller yet; fn_verify's withdrawal report. Open: the served wiring of the reader kernel, the owner relation carrying the journal equality, the two-node native cases.

proofs.title: Owed receipts leave from bp-node serve: the contact offers exactly the queued receipt job on its route
proofs.statement: fn-bpnp-receipt-contact-offers-the-queued-job: over the called fn-bpnp-step on (:base E), where E is fn-bpnp-receipt-contact-event of the node state and the peer (the event host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-send-receipts asks for after each fnn-bpnode-queue-outboxes in bp-node serve), for a well-formed base, a non-nil event and a journal token below *fn-bpn-machine-max-records*, the one effect persists the :attempting record of the first :queued job for that peer and the pending success effect is that job's :cl-send with its route, peer, key and wire. fn-bpnp-receipt-contact-event-needs-a-queued-job: the event is non-nil exactly when the peer is an EID, nothing is issued, no delivery is uncertain, the base is neither fenced nor pending and a :queued job for the peer exists. fn-bpnp-uncertain-receipt-transfer-keeps-the-job-owed and fn-bpnp-receipt-reoffer-after-uncertain (spec 4.3.2): an uncertain base transfer is connection-local; over the called fn-bpnp-step it proposes only the durable :requeued :uncertain record, keeps the job :attempting until that is durable, fences nothing and emits no release, receipt-prepare or :forwarded; once durable the job is :queued again with its own identity and the receipt contact event opens for its peer again. Only an uncertain publication fences. Covered scope: the decision, the offer and the uncertain transfer's outcome; a connect that produces no socket reads :failed and requeues the same way. The host's exit scope (serve and dispatch continue; bp-contact tick answers exit 3) is host reporting over these effects. Open: 'offered once per contact' is not an ACL2 statement over the host loop (fnn-bpc-drive-contact stops at the first transfer or outcome that is not :accepted and the durable :attempting record takes the job out of :queued; the latter is witnessed in the test book, not proved over a driver).

proofs.title: The running owner's status report is the offline report of the same state, and its pages join to it
proofs.statement: fn-nls-live-report-is-the-offline-report: for every KIND (status, pins, peers, obligations), profile, configured owner OC and observation, when the carried octet sum CACHE is valid for the records of OC's Store (fn-sbud-octets-cache-validp) and no connection is open (no pin in fn-ocfg-pins), (fn-nls-live-report kind profile oc cache obs) equals (fn-nls-offline-report kind profile (fn-own-store (fn-ocfg-owner oc)) (fn-ocfg-config oc) obs); the owner reaches fn-nls-live-report through fn-native-live-status-host-answer (host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status-answer), once per request and the offline command reaches fn-nls-offline-report through fn-native-live-status-host-offline (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-live-report). fn-nls-client-step-of-owner-reply: for every octet REPORT whose length is a uint32 and every client prefix ACC of it (with, past the first page, the report's total and digest), the client's step on the owner's page from (len ACC) is :done REPORT, or :next with the strictly longer prefix of one more chunk; fnn-control-live-status folds pages through fn-nls-client-step. fn-nls-page-of-buffer-is-reply: for every REPORT and OFFSET, (fn-nls-page (fn-nls-buffer report) offset) equals (fn-nls-reply report offset), with no hypothesis; fn-nls-buffer is the report as one string with its frame digest and fn-nls-page answers a substring of it (the D27 twin of the page). fn-nls-client-step-of-owner-page: the client-step keystone with the same hypotheses over the page the owner answers, (fn-nls-page (fn-nls-buffer report) (len acc)). fn-nls-cached-buffer-of-put: for a positive offset, the buffer the owner looks up for KIND after storing BUFFER for KIND is BUFFER; fn-native-live-status-host-answer renders anew at offset 0 and otherwise pages from the stored buffer. fn-nls-nat-is-the-decimal-digits: for every natural N, (fn-nls-nat N), which renders every number of the report, is a nonempty run of decimal digits whose value under fn-nntp-decimal-value is N. Supporting: fn-nls-reply-decode-of-encode, fn-nls-request-decode-of-encode, fn-nls-open-of-seal. fn-nls-report-of-query-kind-is-query-report: for every administrative plan, the status-path report of the kind fn-native-admin-result-report-kind names -- the kind host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-execute-admin passes to fnn-operator-status-once for an accepted `peer list' or `control list', live (fn-nls-live-report) or offline (fn-nls-offline-report) -- is fn-nls-query-report of the plan over the same configuration (fn-native-admin-query-report, or books/account-list.lisp fn-acct-kinds-list-report for `account list'), so `control list' renders the authority rows (fn-cfg-authorities), `peer list' the peers and `account list' the accounts slot; supporting: fn-native-admin-control-report-empty-iff-no-rows (the listing is empty only over no grant row). Covered scope: the rows are rendered, not parsed back (qual-e747dbcc A3).
proofs.progress_note: Answering changes no state by signature (the host wrappers return one value and no state), not by a theorem. The multi-page join trusts the frame digest to name one report (A-CRYPTO): a report that changes between pages restarts the join, at most 8 times. The owner pages from a string buffer rendered once per request (fn-nls-page); the renderer and the FNLS frames are still octet lists (their D27 twin is open). The open= line names each process's own open, the offline orphan listing is the reader's own observation, and the checkpoint-file line is each answering process's lstat at the request. The words (the history-marker word, checkpoint-file, open-cost) are tests, not theorems; the live and offline reports share them through fn-nls-report.

proofs.title: A recognized Store event's kind and fields are read by shape on the commit the host calls
proofs.statement: On every Store event (fn-store-event-p), fn-evc-field-by-shape at 0, 1 and 2 equals fn-store-event-sequence, -txid and -generation, and fn-evc-class-by-shape names exactly the recognizer that holds (fn-record-p, fn-store-retention-event-p, fn-stxe-p, fn-stxk-p, fn-stxa-p, fn-cpe-eventp, fn-th-topic-eventp); each reading is O(1) and looks at the head and at most ten conses (books/store-events-carried.lisp, ten keystones, :rule-classes nil). The carried accessors fn-evc-* are the references in the logic and these readings in execution, guard fn-store-event-p, which a history record carries under fn-sn-statep (fn-ccar-seek-finds-a-store-event). The commit the host calls reads the completion record through them: fn-ccar-own-finish-is-own-finish (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission) and fn-ccar-ocfg-complete-is-ocfg-step-complete, fn-ccar-ocfg-complete equal to fn-ocfg-step of (:complete) for every configured owner with no hypothesis (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish, the completion of identity, retention, consumer and topic events: the signed POST). The feed intent's Path is parsed once at take and carried: fn-icar-submission-targets equals fn-own-submission-targets under fn-icar-carryp (host fn-owner-submission-intent and fn-owner-submission-resolution).
proofs.progress_note: Open: the identity prepare (host fn-owner-prepare-identity) still goes through the unverified fn-ocfg-step and fn-sn-prepare-identity, whose fn-sf-prepare-record replays the whole appended history (fn-sf-history-recoverablep); the article path's correspondence (fn-spc-related-candidate-is-recoverable) has no identity analog yet. fn-replay-apply-record and fn-replay-identity-step still recognize the composite and decode its record on the gate and again on the finish. UPDATED 2026-09-26 (PRF-144, lane signed-history-index): the identity prepare no longer replays the appended history; fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity stages through fn-spc-stage-record and equals fn-sn-prepare-identity under fn-snt-relation. RECORDS FLIP (2026-09-27, flip-L1): the class-by-shape readings are over the RETAINED vocabulary: an article row is fn-held-p and an accepted statement row fn-hstxa-p (fn-evc-class-by-shape-is-fn-held-p, -is-fn-hstxa-p); the wire kinds fn-record-p and fn-stxa-p are the codec domain (fn-wire-event-p) and never a retained event. A-HOST dropped from this row's assumptions (lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G3-9, 2026-09-27): no theorem of the row takes fn-assume-host-report or fn-assume-host-events (books/assumptions.lisp) as a hypothesis, so the citation was decorative (AGENTS.md: the theorems that use a named assumption mention it). The host's honest I/O remains the trust boundary these theorems sit inside, not a hypothesis of them.

proofs.title: The octet buffer abstracts to the octet list
proofs.statement: fn-octets (books/octets-stobj.lisp) is an abstract stobj whose logical value is the octet list and whose executable is a resizable (unsigned-byte 8) array with a fill count. The abstraction relation fn-octets$corr (the array's first FILL cells read in order are the list, the fill count is within the array, the concrete object is well formed) is established by the creator (create-fn-octets{correspondence}) and preserved by every export, and every export's executable step equals the list operation on the abstraction under the export's guard: fn-octets-get{correspondence} is nth, fn-octets-put{correspondence} is update-nth, fn-octets-append-octet{correspondence} is append of one octet (through the array's doubling resize), fn-octets-list{correspondence} is the list read tail-recursively, fn-octets-from-list{correspondence} is the list written; each with the guard theorem and the logical preservation ACL2 requires. The derived readers a codec twin reads the buffer with are their take/nthcdr terms over the logical value, under the hypothesis that the value is a true list, which every buffer value is: fn-oct-slice-list-is-take-nthcdr, fn-oct-prefix-equalp-is-list-prefixp (a prefix test against the list-model shape fn-inj-strip has, not take, which pads with nil past the end), fn-oct-suffix-equalp-is-equal. Every executable function is guard-verified. The host fills the array from the byte vector of a socket read in raw Lisp (host/native/io.lisp fnn-octets-fill: reserve, one replace, the count; A-HOST) and calls the buffer entries with the live stobj (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt). Bulk exports (lane octets-bulk, 2026-09-27): fn-octets-append-back{correspondence} is the octet-by-octet back copy fn-oct-back-copy (each appended octet the one OFF back when it is appended, so a run longer than OFF repeats, as an LZ match) executed as one reservation and one forward array loop; fn-octets-get-word{correspondence} is fn-oct-word-at (K octets as a little-endian natural; seven unrolled reads at K = 7); fn-octets-append-word{correspondence} is append of fn-oct-word-octets (a fixnum loop below 2^56, the octet-list write above); fn-oct-word-octets-of-word-at is the round trip that makes a word copy between two buffers the copy of the octets (a defabsstobj export cannot name a second buffer).

Since 2026-09-25 (pbb-d32) the buffer twin reads a recipe v3 record (D32, a supplied Path): the source is a description (K A B) of buffer positions, st[K..A) then st[B..) with the AGENT! insertion cut out, found by the index Path scan (fn-pbb-path-scan-is-inj-path-scan, fn-pbb-unsplice-at-is-inj-unsplice, fn-pbb-source-index-is-inj-source-of) and compared in place (fn-pbb-range-match-is-equal-of-append, fn-pbb-desc-equalp-is-equal); the agent of a v3 record is read from its block (fn-pbb-block-agent-is-pb-block-agent, fn-pbb-path-agent-is-pb-path-agent). proofs.title: Frame blobs have per-schema widths; the control socket carries an article up to the profile's A
proofs.statement: D27, packets PKT-008/009. The frame field grammar (books/frame-fields) has a spec form (:blob . W), 1 <= W <= 2^32-1, beside :blob (131 072, the node's own fields); fn-frame-field-parse-of-octets-wide-blob (books/frame-invariants) is its round trip, and fn-frame-fields-octets-within-width: a record whose values satisfy SPECS encodes to at most (fn-frame-specs-width SPECS) octets, which is the journal encoders' guard bound (books/frame-journal, with the FNWF and FNRJ tables proved within their payload caps). The FNCT request's article field is (:blob . *fn-record-max-payload*) and its group-list field the encoded list at the record's group ceiling (books/native-control). KEYSTONE fn-native-control-request-within-profile-frame: for naturals A and G, every request encoding (fn-native-control-request-encode, which the client calls through fn-native-control-host-request-encode in host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-submit) whose article is at most A octets and whose group list has at most G names is at most (fn-nctrl-max-frame-for A G) octets; fn-native-control-request-within-read-bound gives the same under fn-nctrl-read-bound-for, the bound the owner reads a control connection under (host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-handle-client, computed once at fnn-control-start from the carried profile's A and G through fn-owner-control-profile-bounds and fn-native-control-host-read-bound, or fn-native-hybrid-control-host-read-bound = fn-nhctrl-read-bound-for when hybrid control is built in, which covers both, fn-nhctrl-read-bound-covers-both). The owner's injection decision then refuses an article past A as article-exceeds-profile-bound (PRF-016's boundary). Covered scope: the request encoder and the read bound; the frame decoder's cons walk and the ACL2 octet lists at runtime are D27's representation work, not this target. The FNRJ request-context blobs (a Store record and a request ADU at 131 072), the app journal's record count and aggregates, and the history pre-check figures (PKT-011) are open. EXTENSION (lane downstream-requests, 2026-09-27; Mini/DREGG's PKT-codex-003): the local signed-author request (books/native-hybrid-control.lisp, kind 5, `hybrid-author`) carried only a v1 source (at most 65,535 octets, *fn-hsig-v1-max-source*), so a v2 source that the served POST accepts was refused on the control socket. Its source field is now (:blob . *fn-nhctrl-max-source*), the frame's u32 payload less the other four fields (4,294,963,388; fn-nhctrl-max-payload-is-the-frame-width), and fn-nhctrl-author-request-covers-every-storable-article: *fn-article-max-octets* < *fn-nhctrl-max-source*. The read bound no longer reads the codec width: fn-nhctrl-read-bound-for A G = max(fn-nctrl-read-bound-for A G, 42 + the widest key request, fn-nhctrl-author-frame-for A = 42 + 3,907 + min(A, max-source)). KEYSTONE fn-native-hybrid-control-author-request-within-read-bound: (implies (and (natp a) (<= (len source) a) (not (equal request :bad))) (<= (len request) (fn-nhctrl-read-bound-for a g))) for request = (fn-native-hybrid-control-author-encode generation source ed ml path), which host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-command-hybrid-author calls through fn-native-hybrid-control-host-author-encode; the owner's bound is computed at host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-start through fn-native-hybrid-control-host-read-bound. Teeth: tests/acl2/native-hybrid-control-tests.lisp (a 65,536-octet source round-trips; a 300,000-octet source at A = 300,000, G = 0 is formed, within the hybrid bound and past the ordinary one, and decodes to itself; the hypothesis-removal witness at A = 1,000). Native: tests/test_native_hybrid_author.py test_v2_source_through_hybrid_author (191,283 octets accepted, its resend DUPLICATE, served with its acceptance-time verdict; a carrier past A refused ARTICLE-EXCEEDS-PROFILE-BOUND). That case found the route injecting under the codec's payload bound (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-live-post-config was fn-owner-post-config at *fn-record-max-payload*), so a carrier past A passed injection and the owner's admission (fn-own-control-decision, :control-invalid) refused it with no name; fn-owner-live-post-config is now the owner's installed configuration (fn-own-config: the profile's A and header limits), so the carrier arm's :oversize is the named word.
proofs.progress_note: Certified: runs 22ae (538 passed) and 2f56 (exit 0) on persvati, e8e4 on hbox (image closure, 198 passed); native operator post of 131 073 and 290 000 octets under A = 300 000 accepted, 300 001 refused by name (planning/evidence/bounds-blob-2026-09-25.md). Open: the FNRJ receipt blobs and app-journal counts (PKT-010 remainder), the pre-reservation figures (PKT-011, blocked by fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-verdict, PRF-072), and the octet lists at runtime on this path (D27 representation).

proofs.title: Content reclamation removes only unheld payload bytes and every history decision reads the same afterwards
proofs.statement: fn-rcl-reclaimable-is-no-obligation-names-it: (fn-rcl-reclaimable rule now h verdicts article) (the standing verdict fn-rcl-standing-verdict, which reads no payload; the tombstone test is the caller's on the octets it holds: the record's own payload in fn-rclp-rewrites-p, the arena in fn-rcl-verdict-in, the payload in the octet model fn-rcl-verdict, fn-rcl-verdict-reclaimable-by-definition) equals: rule not keep-forever and a rule, the rule permits the article's stamp at now, no authorship verdict other than :absent (fn-rcl-verdict-heldp), and no obligation of (fn-rcl-obligations h) -- reader pin, consumer cursor, undelivered feed to a live peer, BP obligation -- names the article; no hypothesis. fn-rcl-reclaim-never-touches-a-held-article: if an obligation names the article or the rule is keep-forever, fn-rcl-reclaim-if-permitted is the identity. fn-rcl-reclaim-keeps-the-duplicate-history: fn-acceptedp of every Message-ID is unchanged, no hypothesis. fn-rcl-reclaim-keeps-every-binding and fn-rcl-reclaim-keeps-the-numbering: groups, memberships, pin, stamp, per-group next numbers, next txid and pending unchanged; every other article unchanged. fn-rcl-reclaim-preserves-statep: under fn-statep. fn-rcl-prepare-commutes-with-reclaim: under fn-statep, fn-accept-prepare after reclaiming equals reclaiming after fn-accept-prepare. fn-rcl-existing-action-after-reclaim: for an article M present and not already a tombstone, the D25 verdict fn-rcl-action-over (the host entry fn-store-existing-action is it over alpha, fn-store-existing-action-is-the-verdict-over-alpha) for every Message-ID, submission and groups is unchanged, or SHA-256 collides on the compared pair, or the submission names another agent under which the removed payload gives back a source. fn-rcl-config-rule-after-retention-set: under fn-rcl-rulep, the rule read after fn-cfg-apply of fn-rcl-rule-deltas is the rule, on any prior value. fn-nntp-reclaimed-article-answers-reclaimed: fn-nntp-article-response on an article with a usable identifier and a tombstone payload answers 423 (number or current) or 430 (Message-ID) article reclaimed. fn-rclb-same-articlep-is-rcl-same-articlep: under fn-octets-p (the buffer's recognizer), the buffer comparison fn-rclb-same-articlep, which the native owner's buffer verdict fn-pidx-existing-action makes (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action-buffer, fn-owner-prepare-buffer), equals the list comparison fn-rcl-same-articlep; the list sites call fn-store-existing-action (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare, fn-owner-existing-action; host/store-node-host.lisp prepare and fn-store-sn-existing-action). The store-shaped twins fn-rcl-existing-action and fn-rclb-existing-action, which compared with the held handle, were retired (PKT-860, entry-guards-2). fn-nntp-over-by-msgid-answers-reclaimed: for a Message-ID token naming a held tombstone, fn-nntp-over-response (called by fn-nntp-archive-command) answers 430 article reclaimed; fn-nntp-over-current-answers-reclaimed: with a selected group and a current article that is a tombstone, 423 article reclaimed. fn-nov-lines-indexed-skip-a-reclaimed-article (subject of fn-nntp-over-range-indexed, the pinned OVER/XOVER range) and fn-nov-lines-skip-a-reclaimed-article (unpinned): the lines over NUMBERS equal the lines over NUMBERS without a tombstoned article's number. fn-nntp-newnews-scan-lists-only-live-articles: every Message-ID fn-nntp-newnews-scan lists is that of an article that is not a tombstone; no other hypothesis. fn-rcl-store-holders-hold-behind-a-lagging-consumer: while a registered consumer's acknowledgement is below the committed frontier, no article numbered (n >= 1) in a served group is reclaimable under fn-rcl-store-holders, for every rule, clock and verdict list. fn-rcl-absent-verdict-contributes-nothing: when fn-stx-verdict-of-octets of a payload under any keyring is :absent, fn-stx-delta of that payload is nil under every keyring, so an :absent verdict holds nothing; with fn-sn-finish-records-the-acceptance-verdict (the recorded verdict is fn-stx-verdict-of-octets of the payload) and fn-rcl-tombstone-contributes-nothing (fn-stx-delta of any payload satisfying fn-rcl-tombstonep is nil under every keyring), reclaiming such an article leaves the statement index every later open derives unchanged. fn-rcl-tombstone-refused-at-carrier-form: every payload satisfying fn-rcl-tombstonep gets (:refused :article) from fn-pa-carrier-form, which the host calls as fn-owner-peer-carrier-form (host/owner-host.lisp) in host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit before any Store call, on every served ingress (POST, IHAVE, TAKETHIS, peer and BP transit, bound submissions); no other hypothesis. Its keystone lemma fn-rca-nul-first-octet-is-not-an-article: an octet string whose first octet is 0 does not parse (fn-article-parse), no other hypothesis. Not covered: the developer image's store post (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-post), which prepares a raw payload file without an article check. PKT-844 (lane bp-retention-leftovers): each article is in exactly one retention class, fn-rcl-class-in (books/store-reclaim-holders.lisp): :reclaimed (tombstone), :signed (an authorship verdict other than :absent names it: every kind-4 composite, served key statements among them), :reclaimable, :held (a holder), :kept (the rule keeps it). KEYSTONE fn-rcl-store-classes-partition-the-articles: reclaimable + reclaimed + held (fn-rcl-store-counts) + signed + kept (fn-rcl-store-classes) = the Store's article count, the articles=N of the same status report (host: books/native-live-status.lisp fn-nls-reclaim-words, `signed=N kept=N'). fn-rcl-signed-article-is-never-reclaimable: a signed article is not reclaimable under any rule, clock or holders.
proofs.progress_note: Open: the durable `store reclaim` byte program and its `--dry-run` verb in books/native-operator (design B, reclaim through the compaction pack: planning/evidence/reclaim-host-2026-09-25.md); the reclaimed record's own replay step; holders: the consumer reading is conservative (a lagging consumer holds every article), feed state and FNBS rows are not read, reader pins have no durable form (offline reclaim needs none); the retention charge released with the payload; articles with a verdict other than :absent are held; the buffer's source digest slices the two ranges of the D32 description into one list on the resend-of-a-reclaimed-article path (a two-range buffer digest reader would remove it); native N=5,000 run and cut campaign (SCN-048). audit-fixes rcl (2026-09-27): since the acceptance flip the reclaim counts (status's reclaim line, the reclaim verbs' reports) read each article's HANDLE as its octets, so reclaimable-octets and freed-octets were 0 and a tombstoned article counted reclaimable again. fn-rcl-store-counts now takes the arena (host: fn-native-live-status-host-offline/-answer, fn-store-reclaim-decide(-stream), fn-store-log-reclaim-decide-stream pass the live fn-arena) and reads lengths and the tombstone head through it; KEYSTONE fn-rcl-store-counts-is-the-model-over-alpha: the counts are fn-rcl-summary / fn-rcl-held-count over ALPHA of the Store's articles (tests/acl2/store-reclaim-holders-tests.lisp).

proofs.title: A supplied Path is prefixed in place and the injection inverse still recovers the exact source
proofs.statement: Over fn-inj-decide (books/injection.lisp), which books/nntp-post.lisp fn-nntp-post-step calls for a served POST and books/owner.lisp fn-own-operator-decision for the operator's post: fn-inj-source-of-inverts-the-injection, every injected article gives back its source exactly under fn-inj-source-of, at every clock reading, in all four generated-field cases, with or without a supplied Path (recipe v3); its keystone for the Path case is fn-inj-unsplice-of-a-splice (books/injection-path.lisp): inserting AGENT! where the source's Path content begins and removing it gives back the source, because fn-inj-path-scan-of-a-kept-prefix shows the scan reads nothing at or past the offset it returns. fn-inj-injected-octets-are-the-block-and-the-prefixed-source: with a Path supplied the injected octets are the v2 block without its Path line followed by the source with AGENT! inserted at fn-inj-path-offset; fn-inj-injected-article-retains-the-source-octets now holds under the hypothesis that no Path was supplied. RFC 5537 section 3.5 item 11 twins: fn-inj-no-injection-date-when-date-and-message-id-are-supplied-with-a-path and fn-inj-injection-date-is-the-clock-otherwise-with-a-path. D25 over v3 (books/poster-bytes-invariants.lisp, fn-pb-existing-action the host calls): fn-pb-path-agent-of-an-injection reads the agent from a v3 block's Injection-Info line, so fn-pb-one-source-at-two-clocks-is-one-article and fn-pb-two-sources-are-two-articles cover a supplied Path: a resend at any clock is already stored here, a changed supplied Path is the conflict.

proofs.title: A bound login's accepted signed article carries its bound principal; the policy off changes nothing
proofs.statement: Over fn-lb-owner-gate (books/login-binding.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-login-gate calls for host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-served before the transit attempt, composed with fn-pa-current-plan, which that attempt calls next: fn-lb-bound-login-accepted-signed-article-carries-its-principal, when the owner's live configuration sets posting-policy bound-logins, the in-flight submission's login is bound to principal P, the gate passes and the plan answers :ok, the plan's principal (the one its verified verdict names) is P. fn-lb-bound-login-unsigned-article-is-refused and fn-lb-bound-login-other-principal-is-refused: under the policy a bound login's article with no FN-Authorship carrier is (:refused :login-unsigned LOGIN), and one whose carrier names another principal is (:refused :login-not-bound LOGIN). fn-lb-policy-off-never-refuses and fn-lb-unbound-login-never-refuses: without the policy, or for a login with no binding (an unauthenticated connection's login is nil), the gate passes and the host continues into the attempt it made before. fn-lb-verdict-names-the-login: every verdict names the in-flight login. The policy the gate reads is the value set last: fn-cfg-set-policy-sets-the-policy (books/config-invariants.lisp), over fn-cfg-apply-delta, after a :set-policy delta for a slot the policy read for that slot is the value set, so `policy set posting-policy open` turns the gate off (before 2026-09-25 the first value set stayed in force).

proofs.statement: fn-osb-install-serves-the-profile-bound: for an admitted Store profile, fn-osb-install -- which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-profile calls from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-install on every run path, the developer owner run included -- answers :installed and leaves an owner whose fn-own-body-limit, the bound every later connection's wire reads, is the profile's max-article-octets A; fn-osb-install-keeps-the-posting-configuration: the posting bit, agent and served groups are unchanged; fn-osb-install-keeps-configp: a well-formed posting configuration stays one. fn-olog-served-refusal-lines-one-per-441: the lines host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk leaves for a socket read are exactly one per 441 reply in the effects the client is sent, each one line beginning refused; fn-olog-post-refusal-reason-names-the-sent-reason: each injection reason fn-post-refusal-line names reads back from its reply as itself. fn-olog-control-refusal-line-says-refused-iff-submit-refused: the line fn-owner-operator-submit leaves says refused exactly when fn-own-operator-submit-result is :refused (no hypothesis). fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word-restart-unless-no-owner: the credential verb's answer, fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word, which host/native/auth-admin.lisp fnn-native-auth-admin-result-code calls, is restart-required exactly when the writer-lock observation taken after the durable change is neither :free nor :absent and the running owner did not answer :accepted or :uncertain to the binding reload (PKT-221, PRF-175; a password change never asks, so for it this is the old statement). Covered scope: that the host observes the lock after the durable write, writes each line and one LF, and that the developer init routes its words through fn-nop-developer-init is measured by the native tests, not proved. fn-profile-format-7-store-needs-upgrade: fn-profile-needs-upgrade-verdict, which host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-needs-upgrade calls for `operator CONFIG store needs-upgrade', is by definition the no-argument upgrade-profile verdict's (one owner), and is :needs-upgrade for every admitted format-7 store. fn-profile-rollback-sound-iff-records-within: fn-profile-rollback-verdict, which fnn-command-rollback-check calls with the kept config.json's decoded profile, the store's own config.json profile and the committed transaction files' octet lengths, says :sound exactly when the kept profile is admitted, does not drop the store's history-marker requirement (fn-profile-rollback-drops-markerp), and every length is within fn-profile-rollback-record-bound (R for format 8, H/T for format 7). fn-profile-rollback-keeps-a-required-marker: when the store's profile requires the committed-history marker and the verdict is :sound, the kept profile requires it too; the kept format-7 config.json over a migrated store is refused as history-marker-required-dropped (qual-e747dbcc U1). Covered scope: that the older image's open reads records under that bound is the bounds-join record's statement about that image, not proved.

proofs.title: Opaque carriage stays within the boundary's budget over the owner-carried projection, and a present carrier's refusal has exactly one of four classes
proofs.statement: Over the constructor the host calls for the carried arm (fn-pcb-carried-event, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-peer-carried-relay-event): given the projection fn-pcb-usage of the committed records at the event's release evidence, committing whatever it returns keeps the history admitted (fn-pcb-carried-event-keeps-history-admitted), and across any admitted history the carried charge through the boundary is at most its charge budget and the count at most its count budget (fn-pcb-carried-history-within-budget); with no budget nothing is carried (fn-pcb-admission-without-a-budget-admits-nothing, fn-pcb-no-budget-history-carries-nothing) and each exhaustion is refused by its own name. The owner's cache read at the evidence equals the projection whenever it is the fold of a prefix of the committed records (fn-pcb-carried-usage-is-the-projection) and stays so (fn-pcb-extended-cache-is-valid, fn-pcb-cache-valid-after-commit). The operator's budget rows read back exactly after the extension delta (fn-pcb-peer-budget-after-extend-delta). For a present carrier not carried and not accepted under both primitive observations, fn-pcb-refusal-class is one of no-local-binding, unsupported-profile, signature-failed and malformed (fn-pcb-present-carrier-not-accepted-has-a-class); an absent carrier has none.

proofs.title: Queued base jobs are offered only to their routed hop, each at most once per contact; the routed session scans only routed rows and the ungated forms offer nothing
proofs.statement: Host subject since PRF-120: the host asks fn-bpnj-contact-next (books/bp-node-job-offer.lisp; host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bpc-drive-contact before every offer of a base contact, for bp-service run/resume, bp-obligation request, bp-contact tick and bp-node serve, and fnn-bpnode-send-receipts) and drives its event through fn-bpnj-step (fnn-bps-foundation-step); the named theorems fn-bpnj-contact-next-offer-shape (the offer is the key of fn-bpnj-select's job) and fn-bpnj-step-delegates-every-other-event (fn-bpnj-step is fn-bpnp-step on every event but the three new arms) connect the theorems below, stated over fn-bpnp-contact-next and fn-bpnp-step, to the host-called functions. fn-bpnp-contact-offer-is-the-routed-hop: when fn-bpnp-contact-next (formerly asked directly by fnn-bpc-drive-contact) answers an offer with routing (:table TABLE) in force, fn-bpnp-step on its event (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-foundation-step), for a well-formed base and a journal token below its bound, persists exactly the :attempting record of the peer's first queued job, the :cl-send it owes carries that job's durable route, and that route is the one fn-bprt-send-decision names over TABLE: the contact port of the boundary fn-bprt-next-hop chooses for the destination among the boundaries with a contact; the EID the host passes as the expected TCPCL peer is the decision's. fn-bpnp-contact-holds-an-unrouted-job: with no route matching the destination the driver never offers. fn-bpnp-contact-offers-each-job-at-most-once: along any sequence of states the host consults it at, threading OFFERED, the keys one contact offers are distinct and none was offered before. fn-bpnp-contact-closes-only-when-nothing-owed-remains: with the peer an EID, nothing issued, no delivery uncertain, the base neither fenced nor pending and a queued job for the peer, a close means that job's key is in OFFERED; fn-bpn-apply-record-keeps-forwarded: no lifecycle record returns a :forwarded job to :queued, so a job queued again after its offer had a transfer that was not accepted. fn-bpnp-step-session-offer-is-the-scan-choice (restated) and fn-bpnp-routed-rows-skip-an-unrouted-row: a routed :session proposes the row the arrival-order scan chooses among the held rows the table routes to its hop, so an unrouted older row never blocks a younger routed one; a :session open or :resume without VIA offers nothing. Covered scope: queue-time routing is host-driven through fn-bprt-job-route and a job is not queued without a route; a table change after queueing holds the job (:route-changed) and a durable re-route record is open; verbs without a Store keep the queued address; the contact host is loopback.

proofs.title: XPAT on the served reader step: the arm is fn-nntp-xpat-response, comma alternatives OR, the label is listed; the POST boundary's refusal text is ACL2's
proofs.statement: Over fn-nntp-step-pinned (books/nntp.lisp), which fn-nntp-post-step-pinned calls for every non-POST command on the served path (fn-served-step, fn-served-dispatch, fn-auth-step-pinned; host/native/owner.lisp through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk): fn-nntp-step-pinned-xpat-is-the-xpat-response, for an open, well-formed, projected session and a command line within the preflight whose keyword is XPAT, the step's result is fn-nntp-xpat-response over the line's arguments (the pinned dispatcher adds no XPAT arm). fn-nntp-xpat-alternation-is-or: appending non-negated wildmat alternatives q to a pattern list p ORs them in the matcher the XPAT arm calls (fn-nntp-xpat-matchesp), over every header content; RFC 2980 section 2.9's join of additional arguments into one pattern is kept. fn-auth-capability-lines-advertise-xpat: the served CAPABILITIES block (fn-auth-capability-lines-for-peer) lists XPAT for every configuration. Over fn-sbud-post-boundary-refusal (books/store-budget-naming.lisp), which host/native/io.lisp fnn-validate-post-boundary calls: fn-sbud-post-boundary-refusal-is-nil-exactly-when-admitted, the rendered refusal is NIL exactly when fn-sbud-post-boundary admits, with fn-sbud-post-boundary-refusals-are-distinct (two different words, one of them a boundary word, never share a text) and fn-sbud-post-boundary-refusal-is-a-printable-line; the host keeps no text table.

proofs.title: Records of the old schemas decode and re-encode identically under the u64 record codec
proofs.statement: fn-record-v1-bytes-decode-identically: for all octets, if the pre-P6 decoder (fn-record-v1-decode-exact, books/records-schema-v1.lisp, the text of books/records.lisp at e366c633) accepts them, then (fn-record-decode-exact-impl octets) equals (fn-record-v1-decode-exact octets); fn-record-v1-bytes-are-their-translation: under the same hypothesis the new encoder writes the decoded record back to exactly those octets. The host reaches fn-record-decode-exact-impl through fn-store-event-decode-exact (host/store-host.lisp fn-store-decode-records, called by fn-store-sn-recover) and the seam attachment (books/records-attach.lisp), so an old store opens to the records the old image read and nothing is rewritten. Built on fn-cbor-decode-prechecked-wide-extends-narrow and the restated record keystones fn-record-impl-round-trip and fn-record-impl-accepted-input-is-canonical (now over u64 fields and schema 2). Record ceiling (the fix of the lane's first cut, which raised the overhead a profile's R must hold to 1 111 octets and so refused a saved format-8 profile with R = 17 138 486): fn-record-impl-encode-narrow-length-bound: a record that is not fn-record-widep (sequence, txid, generation, charge and a natural stamp all at most 2^32 - 1) encodes to at most fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling of its payload length and group count, the 1 083-octet overhead the profile relation reads; the seam exports it as fn-record-encode-narrow-length-bound, and any record, wide or not, is within fn-record-wide-encoded-octets-ceiling (1 111). fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record gains the hypothesis that the record is not wide (every record was narrow before P6; the width of the producers is stated, not proved, and a wide record past R is refused at the publish gate, host/store-host.lisp fn-store-publication-admissibility). fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-stays-valid (books/byte-store-profile-v1.lisp): every VALUES the relation of dev 56eb33ee admitted (fn-bs-profile-v1-invalid-reason, frozen, the ceiling written out at 1 083) is admitted by fn-bs-profile-admittedp, which host/store-host.lisp fn-store-profile-admittedp calls, and fn-bs-profile-of VALUES is VALUES; its relation half is fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-is-valid.
proofs.progress_note: Certified with teeth; the theorem is over the implementation the seam attaches, not over the constrained seam function; the open corollary over fn-store-sn-recover is by congruence of the program-mode host map and is not an ACL2 event. Format 10 (lane format-bump-10, 2026-09-28): books/byte-store-profile-v1.lisp and its tests were deleted with format 9 (D34: every format-10 profile is written by a format-10 init or import under the current relation; the frozen pre-P6 relation and the PKT-467 window describe profiles no format-10 store holds); the events and paths that named them are removed from this row.

proofs.title: The subject identity reads the octet buffer in place, through the digest seam
proofs.statement: books/subject-id-buffer.lisp: fn-sidb-subject-id is fn-id-subject of fn-frame-digest-buffer over the subject preimage's fixed head (fn-id-subject-prefix of the buffer's length) and the buffer, and fn-sidb-subject-id-is-id-subject-of-payload (the keystone) says it is fn-id-subject-of-payload of the buffer's octets, with no hypothesis: the identity is stated against the constrained digest (A-CRYPTO), not a named algorithm, and books/frame-digest-buffer.lisp attaches the buffer form to fn-blake3-of-prefixed-buffer-any (BLAKE3 since store format 10, lane blake3-digest; SHA-256's books/sha256-buffer.lisp before, now deleted). fn-blake3-of-prefixed-buffer-is-blake3 (books/blake3-stobj.lisp) is the buffer BLAKE3 equal to fn-blake3 of the appended list on every prefix and every value. fn-sidb-subject-id-bounded (guard t, guard-verified, fn-sidb-subject-id-bounded-unfolds) is the entry: host/native/io.lisp fnn-subject-id-buffer calls it under fnn-metadata-buffer, which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt calls for the served POST after fnn-octets-fill, so no octet list of the payload is built for its identity.
