proofs.title: The checkpoint open and publication cost: one Store open, a count-carrying file, linear list checks, the publication off the owner mutex
proofs.statement: fn-sco-store-open-of-extended-capture: over the capture of any prefix P extended over any Q (P = NIL is the full path), the open fn-sco-store-open computes is (fn-cpo-open-observed configs frontier (append P Q)), and when it is :ok its configuration fold is (fn-cpr-replay configs (append P Q)); host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-extended calls fn-sco-store-open on both paths (fn-store-sn-recover over the empty capture, fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint over the decoded checkpoint) and tests the kind, which is fn-sn-open-okp by fn-sco-finalize-okp-is-kind-ok. fn-ock-install-of-store-open-by-definition: fn-ock-install over that pair is fn-ock-recover-extended of E, so PRF-083's owner keystone holds of host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-from-store-open (native owner.lisp fnn-owner-recover-core), with no second extension. fn-sco-thaw-of-freeze: for every checkpoint of the right shape, thawing the file's value (the count in the record slot, the records read back out of the event index) gives the value; fn-sco-freeze-of-capture-carries-the-count: a capture of at most 2^32 records is written with its count; fn-ock-published-segments-decode-to-the-checkpoint composes it with the FNSC round trip under the codec's tree and width hypotheses (host fn-store-sco-decode thaws; fn-store-sco-publish-octets and fn-ock-publication freeze). fn-ock-publication-is-the-capture-at-the-capture-point (hypothesis: an admitted history): the publication the owner runs outside its mutex over the values captured under it (fn-owner-sco-capture, native fnn-owner-publish-captured) is the capture of the captured history. The linear :exec paths equal the unchanged :logic definitions with no hypothesis: fn-ks-distinctp-is-nodupp, fn-ks-subsetp-is-subset-logic, fn-no-duplicatesp-is-ks-nodupp, fn-subsetp-is-ks-subset-logic, fn-article-listp-is-shape-and-distinct-msgids, fn-node-binding-listp-is-shape-and-distinct, fn-retain-no-duplicatesp-is-no-duplicatesp; fn-cnode-statep reaches them through fn-node-statep in fn-sco-cpr-resume, fn-sco-cpr-finish and fn-sco-finalize-from.
proofs.progress_note: Open: the Store state still holds the record list (fn-sf-records; a commit appends to it, store-files.lisp), so the kernel does not yet carry a count; fn-node-articles-have-archive-bindingsp and fn-articles-freshp are still quadratic in the whole-node recognizer; the covered prefix's octets are still re-encoded for fnn-open-live-store's callers; two hypotheses have no must-fail (the :ok hypothesis of the Store open's replay conjunct and the admitted-history hypothesis of the publication keystone) and the 2^32 bound of fn-sco-freeze-of-capture-carries-the-count has no reachable counterexample. Lane checkpoint-pipeline (2026-09-26): the schema-2 freeze/thaw and the list publication went with schema 3 (D34); their theorems are removed from this target's events (fn-sco-thaw-of-freeze, fn-sco-freeze-of-capture-carries-the-count, fn-ock-published-segments-decode-to-the-checkpoint, fn-ock-publication-is-the-capture-at-the-capture-point, fn-sco-thaw-checked-accepts-own-publication); the schema-3 file's round trip is PRF-199.

proofs.title: Key succession and revocation over the acceptance plan: the owner's key-statement executor, the :revoked token and its replay binding
proofs.statement: Over fn-pa-current-plan (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-peer-carrier-plan, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit), which now takes TRANSITP and has a fifth outcome :revoked: while a principal's newest snapshot is its tombstone no plan for it is :ok on any path (fn-pa-no-ok-plan-for-a-revoked-principal, fn-pa-revocation-leaves-no-ok-plan), and on NNTP transit a carrier under keys once enrolled is :revoked at the tombstone's generation, elsewhere refused :local-enrollment (fn-pa-revoked-principal-on-transit-is-revoked-at-its-tombstone); fn-pa-revoked-event exists only with both primitive observations verified and is the composite replay's revoked branch admits at those snapshots (fn-pa-revoked-event-binds-the-arm-and-both-observations), and replay admits a :revoked composite exactly when its generation names a tombstone of that principal (fn-osp-replay-admits-a-revoked-composite-exactly-at-its-tombstone), leaving the keyring unchanged, as the carried composite does (fn-osp-*-composite-keeps-the-keyring). Over the key-statement executor fn-ks-plan / fn-ks-execute (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-plan / -event, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement after a :verified kind-4 commit): a statement acts only on its own stored :verified verdict with a keys grant covering its groups (C2's fn-ctl-authorize), so a :carried or :revoked statement never changes a keyring; the verdict's generation was the principal's current enrollment and a succession's old key is that enrollment's; the PoP is a D09 signature by the new keys over the statement's Message-ID and old key with both observations verified; after the succession's kind-3 event the new keys are selected and any other key set, the old one included, is refused :local-enrollment; after a revocation's no plan is :ok. The executor runs after every durable kind-4 composite that carries a statement, :carried and :revoked included, once the statement's own barrier returned (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-statement-committed; PRF-310), and a Store refusal of the key change leaves the article accepted and is reported as such (transit detail :key-change-refused; log line `key-statement ... refused`). The crash cut between the statement's commit and its change's is a model crash point: the open's recovery (fn-ks-recover; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement-recover over the newest record, through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-pending) reaches from the cut exactly the uninterrupted acceptance under the recovery's rows and observations (fn-ks-recover-completes-the-cut) and, after an acceptance that acted, changes nothing under any rows or observations (fn-ks-recover-after-an-acting-acceptance-changes-nothing); executing a statement whose change is already the newest snapshot yields nothing (fn-ks-execute-is-idempotent). The verb keys is grantable (fn-cfg-grant-control-admissible-iff over *fn-cfg-control-verbs* = (cancel keys)). The rendered item for :revoked begins `r`, never `v` (fn-stx-verified-item-first-octet-names-the-token), and token code 5 round-trips. The next generation is ACL2's (fn-hl-next-generation; control kinds 7 and 8). Evidence is never rewritten: a kind-3 completion keeps every stored verdict (fn-hls-finish-snapshot-keeps-historical-verdicts, existing) and a kind-4 one conses its own (fn-hls-finish-kind4-verdicts, existing).
proofs.progress_note: Open: no native run (no image was built on hbox for these bytes); a crash between the statement's kind-4 commit and the executor's kind-3 commit leaves the statement accepted and unexecuted (no model crash point, no recovery re-run); a refused kind-3 commit surfaces as the transit attempt's refusal after its kind-4 committed; fn_verify.py does not render :revoked; the served path (NNTP POST, BP transit) never reports :revoked by design (TRANSITP nil). A-HOST dropped from this row's assumptions (lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G3-9, 2026-09-27): no theorem of the row takes fn-assume-host-report or fn-assume-host-events (books/assumptions.lisp) as a hypothesis, so the citation was decorative (AGENTS.md: the theorems that use a named assumption mention it). The host's honest I/O remains the trust boundary these theorems sit inside, not a hypothesis of them.

proofs.title: Invitation binding: accept enrols only a bound invitation; confirm consumes a pending invitation this node issued exactly once and enrols only the acceptance that consumed it
proofs.statement: fn-pinv-accept-step-enrols-only-a-bound-invitation: a (:enrol EVENT) from fn-pinv-accept-step SEQ TXID GEN RECEIVED OBSERVED-ML ED ML SNAPSHOTS (books/peer-invite.lisp; called by host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-accept) has EVENT = fn-hl-enroll-event at fn-hl-next-generation SNAPSHOTS of the carrier's principal P and key set K, P not already enrolled with K, and fn-pinv-bound-document-p: fn-hsig-authorize-at over the carrier decoded from RECEIVED and the two primitive observations, the body has the invitation kind line and names P, the Ed25519 and the ML-DSA-65 key of K (fn-pinv-body-names-p, a line of the body), and fn-prin-genesis-bindsp P (Ed25519 || ML-DSA-65) TOKEN. fn-pinv-issue-plan-records-the-signed-invitation: an :issue delta is fn-cfg-issue-invitation of the body's nonce, the verified principal and the invitation's authored-source identity, the nonce keying no row. fn-pinv-confirm-consumes-only-a-pending-named-invitation: a (:consume DELTA) from fn-pinv-confirm-plan (called by fnn-pinv-owner-confirm) has a bound acceptance, the row its nonce keys pending, naming the body's Inviter-Principal and Invitation-Source-Id, and DELTA = fn-cfg-consume-invitation of the nonce, the acceptor and the acceptance's source identity. fn-pinv-confirm-step-enrols-only-the-consuming-acceptance: an (:enrol EVENT) from fn-pinv-confirm-step (called by fnn-pinv-owner-enrol-confirmed) has a bound acceptance, the row consumed (state 1) by exactly its principal and source identity, P not enrolled with K, and EVENT the kind-3 enrolment of P and K. fn-pinv-consumed-stays-consumed-across-replay: a consumed invitation stays consumed through fn-config-replay-loop; fn-pinv-consumed-refuses-consumption: fn-cfg-delta-reason refuses every :consume-invitation of it; fn-pinv-consumption-consumes. fn-pinv-confirm-after-its-consumption-enrols: after the consuming delta is applied (the crash point before the kind-3 record) the same acceptance's plan is :enrol; fn-pinv-confirm-step-never-enrols-twice. Covered scope: the owner's three steps and the configuration admission and replay; the peer record is still `peer add`; the crypto primitives are A-CRYPTO.

proofs.title: The NEWNEWS pull feed advances its cursor past a round only when every listed Message-ID drew 235, 435 or 437 from the local node, and a crash mid-round recovers the cursor that round asked with
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/native/pull-service.lisp calls (fn-pull-begin, fn-pull-step through fn-pull-step-pair, fn-pull-close, fn-pull-replay over fn-pull-journal-scan): closing a round moves the cursor only if the round ran to its end and every Message-ID its NEWNEWS listed has a 235, 435 or 437 answer, the new instant being the peer's DATE less one second (fn-pull-close-advances-only-past-a-fully-answered-round; per id fn-pull-unanswered-id-holds-the-cursor); an answer is recorded only by a local reply and is that reply's own code for the article in hand (fn-pull-step-answers-only-from-the-local-node); no step changes the round's cursor or journals anything (fn-pull-step-keeps-the-cursor-and-journals-nothing) and every NEWNEWS it sends names the round's cursor instant (fn-pull-step-newnews-names-the-cursor); if the FNPL journal replays to the owner's cursor, it replays after the begin, after any events and after the close to that cut's cursor (fn-pull-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut), so the round begun after a crash asks the dead round's instant (fn-pull-recovery-asks-the-dead-rounds-newnews). The schedule starts only a due, idle peer and spaces rounds by the operator's interval (fn-sched-pull-due-is-due-and-idle, fn-sched-pull-started-is-not-due, fn-sched-pull-finished-waits-its-interval). That the peer lists again what it listed for the same instant is RFC 3977 7.4's NEWNEWS semantics, not proved. Restated 2026-09-26 by PRF-165 (PKT-213): the cursor carries PENDING (per-id consecutive 430 counts) and fn-pull-close-advances-only-past-a-fully-answered-round / fn-pull-unanswered-id-holds-the-cursor now admit an id the peer answered 430 for BOUND consecutive complete rounds; PRF-165 states them.
proofs.progress_note: Native (hbox, SCN-058): a second fn node, INN 2.7.4 nnrpd and a SIGKILL mid-round then the same NEWNEWS all pass. Open: the pull client has no TLS arm (a TLS transport is not pulled); a remote 430 for a listed id holds the cursor until the peer stops listing it; the cursor lives in <store>/pull/*.fnpl (FNFD envelope and phase machine), not a Store transaction record. proofs.title: The operator's configuration is ACL2's: [alerts]/[ops] rows, the rendered configuration, missions and their store profiles, the SIGHUP log reopen, and file-first on the bound commit route
proofs.statement: fn-native-config-show-round-trip: for every configuration C that fn-native-config-show-wfp admits, fn-native-config-load -- the loader fn-native-operator-run (host/native-operator-host.lisp:19) reads fn.toml through -- of fn-native-config-show-octets C, the text `operator CONFIG show' prints and a mission writes, is (:accepted C); the [alerts] and [ops] rows are part of C. fn-native-config-load-renderable: every configuration fn-native-config-load accepts satisfies fn-native-config-show-wfp (the parser's values are parsed-shaped and each field's normalization keeps its bound), so fn-native-config-show carries no run-time check; with the round trip, fn-native-config-loaded-show-round-trip: the rendering of every loaded configuration loads back as itself. fn-native-mission-profiles-valid and fn-native-mission-store-opens-with-its-profile: for each of small-community, relay and archive, the mission's profile request resolves to an admitted profile, and the frame `init' writes for it (fn-bs-config-frame-for-profile, host/store-host.lisp fn-store-metadata-config-frame) decodes at every later open to exactly that profile (under A-CRYPTO through fn-bs-config-decode-of-encode). fn-native-operator-run-init-under-a-mission: under a configuration naming a mission, an accepted init plan's profile is the mission's request. fn-olr-reopen-iff-requested: fn-olr-decide, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-log-reopen answers host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-maybe-reopen-log with, reopens exactly when a log path is configured and a SIGHUP arrived since the last one handled, and every counted request is then handled. fn-obc-commit-only-after-filing: fn-obc-commit-gate, which fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission asks (through fn-owner-bound-commit-gate) before any commit callback, answers :commit only when fn-pa-filing-plan files the article in exactly the committed groups; with C1's keystone a control article then commits only in its filing group (fn-obc-control-commits-only-in-its-filing-group). Covered scope: that the host calls the callback only on :commit, and swaps the log descriptor under the log mutex, is host code measured natively, not proved.

proofs.title: BP outbound fragmentation: every fragment the send plan answers fits the peer's Transfer MRU, reassembles exactly to the parent's payload with no data cap, and restores the parent
proofs.statement: The subject is fn-bpfs-plan WIRE MRU (books/bp-fragment-send.lisp, logic mode, guard-verified), which host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-send-effect calls after SESS_INIT with the session's negotiated Transfer MTU (fn-tcl-negotiated-transfer-mtu). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-fit-mru: when the plan answers (:fragments W1 ... Wn), every Wi is at most MRU octets (the chunk is MRU minus 8 minus the encoded length of the empty fragment at the largest offset; fn-bpfs-fragment-length-bound over fn-bpfs-fragment-primary-length-shift and the payload block's exact length). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-reassemble-exactly: the decoded views of the Wi draw the decoded parent's payload exactly on the reassembly canvas fn-bpf-canvas at the parent's ADU offset (0 for a whole parent, its own offset for a fragment parent) and all carry the parent's total, for every payload length and fragment count (no data cap). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-restore-parent: every Wi decodes to a bundle with the parent's extension blocks and ADU key and the fragment flag, and a whole parent's fragment primary unfragments to the parent's primary. fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-reassemble-within-caps: for a whole parent of at most *fn-bpf-max-length* (65538) octets cut into at most *fn-bpf-max-fragments* (64) pieces, the receiver's executable reassembler fn-bpf-reassemble answers (:ok payload). Covered scope: the sender's base-job send path (bp-service run and the bp-node send of queued jobs through fnn-bps-send-effect); held-transit forwarding (the :session arm's MRU wait) does not fragment; the receiver's reassembler and held-row recognizers keep the 65538 x 64 caps; one job attempt covers all fragments (no per-fragment custody records); the plan runs on octet lists (no D27 concrete twin).

proofs.title: Peering composed: the confirm's one configuration record consumes the invitation and configures the peer; a declined key statement is decided at reopen under the configuration in force at its txid; the admission verdict names its class
proofs.statement: fn-pinv-confirm-record-configures-the-issued-invitations-peer: a (:configure DELTAS) from fn-pinv-confirm-record-plan RECEIVED INVITATION OBS ED ML INVITATIONS SNAPSHOTS PEERS (books/peer-invite.lisp; host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-confirm calls it through fn-pinv-host-confirm-record-plan) has fn-pinv-confirm-plan :consume, the row pending, the invitation of kind invitation whose authored-source identity is the row's, the confirmed peer fn-cfg-peerp with auth (:principal ACCEPTOR) and a name no peer of PEERS has, and DELTAS = (consume-delta, fn-cfg-set-peer-delta peer). fn-pinv-confirm-record-fold-consumes-and-configures: over fn-cfg-apply V GEN STAMP DELTAS (the fold fn-cfg-apply-record runs when the owner completes the publication) the invitation row is consumed by exactly this acceptor and acceptance source identity, the peers table holds exactly the peer's rows under its name, and (not enrolled) the next confirm plan is :enrol. fn-ks-reopen-is-blind-to-later-configuration and fn-ks-a-decline-replays-as-a-decline: fn-ks-recover-recorded (the open's recovery; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement-recover with AT-OPEN, rows from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-rows = fn-ks-statement-rows with AT-OPEN; no policy switch) decides the pending statement under fn-ctl-config-at its own txid, so configuration records later than the statement change nothing, and a statement whose plan declined is left as the acceptance left it. fn-ks-recorded-recovery-completes-the-cut: when every configuration record precedes the txid and the journal replays, the recorded recovery of the cut is the uninterrupted acceptance under the live grants. fn-pcb-admission-verdict-names-its-class: the verdict is one of :unsigned :carried :malformed :cryptographically-invalid :unenrolled :unsupported-profile :verified; :verified iff the plan is :ok under both verified observations; :carried iff the D23 arm; a present carrier is never :unsigned. Not covered: pull over TLS (packet 8), the observation determinism the decline theorem assumes (A-CRYPTO), fn-pcb-admission-verdict has no host caller yet (its classes are the transit refusal detail's plus :carried/:verified).

proofs.title: A resend of an accepted source after its withdrawal or reclamation is answered from the Store (duplicate or conflict), never prepared as a fresh acceptance, and is served a 441 line
proofs.statement: Over the decision the host calls at POST (fn-rclb-existing-action, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action-buffer from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt; fn-rcl-existing-action, fn-owner-existing-action from fnn-owner-attempt-transit): for a string Message-ID held in the Store's article list, both answer :duplicate or :conflict after fn-sn-finish of that Store, whatever the completed record (fn-vj-a-completion-keeps-a-held-message-id-answered; a cancel that withdraws the target is accepted by such a completion, and the owner's carried commit is fn-sn-finish by fn-ccar-sn-finish-is-sn-finish), and for any Store whose article list is fn-rcl-reclaim-state of an acceptance state holding it (fn-vj-reclamation-keeps-a-held-message-id-answered); while the resend is the connection's in-flight submission with no completion consumed, fn-own-outcome renders the duplicate or the conflict 441 line for it (fn-vj-a-held-message-id-is-answered-441). The host returns the word before fnn-advance-frontier and fn-owner-prepare-buffer, so no number is allocated (host control flow, observed natively, not a theorem). The same source being :duplicate rather than :conflict after reclamation is fn-rcl-existing-action-after-reclaim with its SHA-256 collision disjuncts. proofs.title: The record producers the node runs stay inside the widths the profile admits, discharging the width hypothesis of fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record
proofs.statement: fn-sn-prepare-stages-a-narrow-article-record (books/record-width-producers.lisp): if CHARGE is at most 2^32 - 1 and fn-sn-prepare stages the record fn-sn-article-record builds (the result is not the input state), that record is not fn-record-widep: sequence, txid and generation are within u32 because the file machine stages only the reserved txid (frontier - 1), generation = txid and sequence = the committed count, and every file state holds a u32 frontier with strictly increasing committed txids below it (fn-sf-prepare-record-stages-u32-coordinates, fn-sn-prepare-stages-u32-coordinates); the stamp is below 2^32 by fn-record-stamp-of-observation (fn-sn-article-record-stamp-and-charge). The charge premise is discharged by the charge gate: fn-sbud-post-boundary answers :ok only for a u32 charge (fn-sbud-post-boundary-admits-a-u32-charge), and fn-post-admitted-article-record-is-within-r composes the boundary verdict :ok under PROFILE, the producer and the prepare into the conclusion of fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record: the staged record encodes within the profile's R, so the publish gate's record check (host/store-host.lisp fn-store-publication-admissibility, asserted by host/native/io.lisp fnn-publish) never refuses it. The BP ingress producer: fn-bpi-staged-record-is-narrow (policy charge u32 by fn-bpi-policy-p). Host calls: host/store-node-host.lisp and host/owner-host.lisp call fn-sn-article-record and then the prepare (fn-spc-prepare, equal to fn-sn-prepare by fn-spc-prepare-equals-specification-under-relation; fn-pcar-sbud-prepare, equal to fn-sbud-prepare by fn-pcar-sbud-prepare-is-sbud-prepare), after the boundary (host/native/io.lisp fnn-post-boundary; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-post-boundary); the boundary and the prepare are separate host calls, so the composition is over the host's order, stated, not one ACL2 function. Not covered: the signed composite (kind 4) and the peer-carried event producers, which carry their own R check (fn-owner-signed-event-boundary). Packet 1 (decided): the history gate charges an article its own figure, fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling of its payload length and group count (fn-sbud-article-figure, books/store-budget-article.lisp). fn-sbud-article-verdict-keeps-history: if fn-sbud-article-verdict-at PROFILE USED BYTES-USED PL GC is :admissible and RECORD is narrow with at most PL payload octets and GC groups, then fn-profile-replay-within-boundp PROFILE (+ BYTES-USED (len (fn-record-encode RECORD))): the bound the next open checks per file (host/native/io.lisp fnn-durable-records through host/store-host.lisp fn-store-profile-replay-within-bound). Host: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict (native store post, before reservation). fn-sbud-prepare-under-article-budget-keeps-history: a fn-sbud-prepare that staged under fn-sbud-article-budget-for PROFILE BYTES-USED RECORD kept the history within H; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer pass that budget with the owner's carried committed octets (fn-owner-record-octets) to fn-pcar-sbud-prepare (= fn-sbud-prepare). fn-post-admitted-article-keeps-history composes the store-post sequence with PRF-123's keystone. fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-article-verdict: an upgrade keeps every article verdict (the figure does not read the profile).

proofs.title: One authored source, one identity: the host's tombstone-aware duplicate verdict keys on the poster's source at every clock, before and after reclamation
proofs.statement: The subject was fn-rcl-existing-action (books/store-reclaim.lisp; retired, PKT-860: see RECORDS FLIP below for the subject now), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action and fn-owner-prepare call, and fn-owner-existing-action-buffer through fn-rclb-existing-action (fn-rclb-same-articlep-is-rcl-same-articlep); host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt reaches them for the served POST and the operator post. fn-sr-an-injection-is-not-a-tombstone: no fn-inj-decide decision's octets are a tombstone (injected octets open with Path or Injection-, a refusal has none). fn-sr-a-retry-is-already-stored: the held payload is source S injected at clock A under Message-ID M and groups G; S injected at clock B under M and G is :duplicate. fn-sr-a-changed-source-is-a-conflict: a different source S2 under M is :conflict for any groups and clocks. fn-sr-the-tombstone-keeps-the-source: fn-rcl-tombstone-of of an injection is a tombstone whose source digest is SHA-256 of S, whose agent is the configured one and whose octet digest is SHA-256 of the injected octets. fn-sr-a-retry-after-reclaim-is-already-stored and fn-sr-a-changed-source-after-reclaim-is-a-conflict: the same two verdicts against the tombstone, the second up to a SHA-256 collision on the two sources (fn-rcl-collisionp, about 2^128 work, assumed not proved). The tombstone theorems are unreachable-in-composition until a program writes tombstones (store reclaim is not implemented). fn-sr-a-signed-retry-is-already-stored (PKT-166): the hybrid-author route's stored octets fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets, held at clock A, recomputed at any clock B under the same Message-ID and groups, are :duplicate; host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-hybrid-control-author asks fn-owner-existing-action before it commits. RECORDS FLIP (flip-books-residue, 2026-09-27): the held payload is an arena handle; the subject is fn-store-existing-action (books/store-intern.lisp), which the host calls after flip-L6 at fn-owner-existing-action, fn-owner-prepare and host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-existing-action, and at fn-owner-existing-action-buffer through fn-pidx-existing-action (fn-pidx-existing-action-is-store-existing-action); the held-payload hypothesis reads the bytes under the held handle through the arena the verdict reads (fn-handle-bytes). The pre-flip statements over fn-rcl-existing-action equated a handle with octets and were vacuous on a flipped Store.

proofs.title: The reader's search scope: the served XPAT reply over a range is XHDR's lines for exactly the served, matching numbers in it, and a withdrawn number is never a hit
proofs.statement: Over fn-nntp-step-pinned (books/nntp.lisp), which the served path reaches for every non-POST reader command (host/native/owner.lisp through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk, fn-served-step, fn-served-dispatch, fn-auth-step-pinned, fn-nntp-post-step-pinned): fn-nntp-step-pinned-xpat-range-is-the-scope, for an open, well-formed, projected session with a selected group and a command line within the preflight whose keyword is XPAT, whose field is a header name or metadata item, whose second argument is a range and whose joined pattern parses, the step's result is fn-nntp-multi of the 221 initial line and fn-nntp-hdr-lines-for-numbers of the field over fn-nss-hits of the range's numbers in the served archive. fn-nss-hits-are-the-scope: a number is in that set iff it is positive, within the range's bounds, the group's served archive holds an available article at it, the field renders, and fn-nntp-xpat-matchesp accepts the rendered field. fn-nss-withdrawn-number-is-never-a-hit: a token the pinned step answers 423 withdrawn for (fn-nntp-number-withdrawn-p) never names a hit, for any field, pattern or number list.

proofs.title: Local-owner consumer poll and ack: a page is a read whose continuation never passes an unreturned matching event; ack writes only a forward in-scope declaration within the frontier, idempotently
proofs.statement: Subjects are the functions the host calls: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll calls fn-col-poll and fn-owner-consumer-local-ack calls fn-col-ack (books/consumer-owner-local), from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-consumer-local-serialized. fn-col-poll-scan-page-contract: for any event window, a :scan answer's continuation p is a natural with position <= p <= max(position, frontier) and p <= position + budget; an empty page's scanned prefix contains no group-matching article event and, when budget > 0 and position < frontier, p > position; a nonempty page's event is the window's event at p - 1 - position, it matches, and no earlier event in the window matches. fn-col-poll-is-the-index-window-scan-unfolds equates fn-col-poll's :poll answer with that selector over the carried index window (fn-col-poll-index-window), the continuation written into the owner-pinned scope cursor; fn-col-poll-is-a-page-or-a-refusal: it answers :poll or :refused, never a Store write proposal; fn-col-scope-entry-position-is-natural discharges the contract's natp premise. fn-col-ack-is-the-kernel-ack-unfolds equates fn-col-ack with fn-cp-ack under the pinned local principal, query version 1 and view 0. fn-cp-ack-writes-only-a-forward-declaration-in-scope: a :write is exactly (:ack cursor), in the recorded scope, not below the recorded position (nfix) and not equal to it, within the committed frontier; an in-scope equal position within the frontier is the :no-op. fn-cp-ack-after-its-commit-is-a-no-op: after fn-cp-apply of that ack, the same ack is a :no-op. Not claimed: that an acked position was served by a poll (an ack is a declaration), an unavailable gap (no native content reclamation reaches this profile), or independence of the byte and cursor ceilings.

proofs.title: A ready base job is never starved by an older held or offered job on its contact, a transport result settles only its own attempt, a report or receipt is sent only by the durable record of its accepted transfer, and an encoder refusal settles its pending record
proofs.statement: fn-bpnj-step (books/bp-node-job-offer.lisp) is the step host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-foundation-step calls; it equals fn-bpnp-step on every event but three (fn-bpnj-step-delegates-every-other-event). fn-bpnj-contact-next, asked before every base offer (fnn-bpc-drive-contact; fnn-bpnode-send-receipts), answers an offer while any queued job for the peer is ready (fn-bpnj-contact-offers-while-a-ready-job-remains), and the offer's event persists exactly that job's :attempting record with the :cl-send of its durable route (fn-bpnj-contact-offer-starts-the-ready-job). A transfer result names its attempt token: another token settles nothing (fn-bpnj-stale-job-result-settles-nothing), the current one proposes :finished for :accepted and :requeued otherwise (fn-bpnj-named-result-is-the-transport-outcome), and :forwarded is reported only at the durable answer to a pending :finished record of an :attempting job (fn-bpnj-step-forwarded-needs-a-durable-finished-record), so a queued report intent or job is not a sent one. A :refused answer settles the pending record (fn-bpnj-encoder-refusal-settles-the-pending-record). The new arms keep the guard premises and the lifecycle invariant (fn-bpnj-step-preserves-guard-premises, fn-bpnj-new-arms-preserve-the-lifecycle-invariant). Under A-BP-CONTACT the host's first ask is an offer and the contact offers a ready job within its prefix of keys at or ahead of it (fn-bpnj-contact-offers-a-ready-job-under-a-bp-contact). Covered scope: base FNBS jobs (requests, receipts, status reports); the held-bundle forwarding path (kind 8) keeps its own session scan and stale-callback handling (fn-bpnp-forward-result-*). Not covered: token monotonicity across every served event and restart; freedom of :finished proposals on non-base events.

proofs.title: Pull over TLS as the node's own principal: the feed's protected preamble gates the pull round, a clear credential without the loopback-lab exception is refused before any dial, and the cursor's cut theorem transfers
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/native/pull-service.lisp fnn-pull-round calls (fn-pull-plan-profile-path, fn-pull-session-begin through fn-pull-session-begin-pair, fn-pull-session-step through fn-pull-session-step-pair, fn-pull-session-close-effects, fn-pull-session-close; books/peer-pull-session.lisp) and the plans host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-pull-plans reads (fn-pull-plans, now carrying the transport security and the outbound credential policy). fn-pull-session-credentials-wait-for-tls-and-login: for a plan whose fn-pull-plan-verdict is :tls, the feed-connection observations of the session driven by ANY host events (fn-pull-session-obs, which is fn-fc-drive of the session's initial machine over the events it fed: fn-pull-session-obs-is-the-machine-over-its-trace) satisfy fn-fc-gate-okp from the start stage -- PRF-051's fn-fc-offers-and-credentials-wait-for-tls-and-login instantiated, not restated: no AUTHINFO before a 382 and the host's verified-TLS report, no :ready (the only transition that sends DATE and lets the round step) before a 281 when a credential is carried. fn-pull-session-refuses-a-clear-credential-without-the-lab-exception: a clear transport with a credential, without both the profile's explicit clear-text permission and a loopback host literal, has verdict :refused-clear-credential, no profile path (the secret is not read), begin effects exactly the cursor's journal record and (:close) (no :dial), a session that answers every later event with nothing, and a close equal to the cursor fn-pull-begin asks with. fn-pull-begin-ready-is-the-round-after-the-greeting: the round a session enters at :ready is the round fn-pull-begin reaches on a 200/201 greeting, sending the same DATE; fn-pull-begin-ready-cursor-fields. fn-pull-session-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut: PRF-100's fn-pull-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut (statement unchanged) transferred to the session: after the begin, after any events (the TLS preamble included) and after the close records, the FNPL journal replays to that cut's cursor. Trusted, not proved (A-HOST, as PRF-051): the host reports (:tls-up) only after fnn-tls-connect verified the chain against the plan's trust anchor and the plan's server name; the loopback-lab exception is a local policy for the lab, never a general secure-peering claim.

proofs.title: BP fragment reassembly without a family-size ceiling: the executed reassembler equals the uncapped index-wise reference on every input, in work linear in the octets received, and the node's family query and selector run it
proofs.statement: The subject is fn-bpfw-reassemble FS TOTAL (books/bp-fragment-sweep.lisp, logic mode, guard t, guard-verified): a merge sort of the fragments by offset, then one tail-recursive sweep over positions 0..TOTAL-1 keeping only the suffixes of the extents covering each position, then the reference's outcome scan. The node's fn-bpnf-fragment-query (books/bp-node-fragment-family.lisp) calls it; fn-bpnf-family-plan calls the query; fn-bpnf-family-next, which host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-fragment-progress calls through fnn-core, selects the family, and the host then steps (:family arrival observation) through fnn-bps-foundation-step. fn-bpfw-reassemble-is-spec: for every FS and TOTAL, fn-bpfw-reassemble equals fn-bpfw-spec, the reference fn-bpf-reassemble's own definition with *fn-bpf-max-length* (65538) and *fn-bpf-max-fragments* (64) removed from its input recognizer (fn-bpfw-inputsp: well-formed fragments, a positive total, one total for all). fn-bpf-reassemble-is-capped-spec: fn-bpf-reassemble equals fn-bpfw-spec when TOTAL <= 65538 and (len FS) <= 64, and (:invalid :bounds) otherwise. fn-bpfw-exact-canvas-reassembles: under fn-bpfw-inputsp, a family whose index-wise canvas is an octet list reassembles to (:ok canvas). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-reassemble-uncapped: for the sender's plan fn-bpfs-plan of a whole parent answering :fragments, fn-bpfw-reassemble of the fragments' views answers (:ok payload) for every payload length and fragment count. fn-bpnf-fragment-query-is-reference (restated): the node query equals fn-bpfw-spec over the family's cells. fn-bpnf-family-next-memo-is-aux: the executed selector (the :exec branch of fn-bpnf-family-next), which plans each family at most once per call, equals the per-member selector (anchor included) under its invariant, established with an empty tried list at the call. Scope: the reassembler has no data ceiling, but a family is still bounded upstream by the held-image cap *fn-bpnf-max-held-image*, the bundle decoder's 1 MiB input, the ADU record's 65538 octets and the machine's slots and octet budget (P5 of planning/design-2026-09-25-bounds.md); the representation is octet lists (no D27 concrete twin); the merge in the sort recurses to the fragment count. Jobs (books/bp-node-fragment-jobs.lisp): fn-bpnf-family-jobs-agreep HELD says every active fragment row carries exactly the reassembly job (job state (:dispatch-pending), no dispatch record, no next hop, no kind-8 attempt). fn-bpnf-family-apply-conserves-jobs: under it, a :ready kind-18 application (the one rule live completion and replay call) consumes only rows whose one job was reassembly, installs a whole row carrying (:dispatch-pending), and the new held list satisfies the relation. fn-bpnp-step-family-events-keep-jobs-agreeing: fn-bpnp-step (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-foundation-step) on (:family A OBS) and on (:persist-result EPOCH OP RESULT) while a kind-18 operation is issued preserves the relation through every wrapper of the served step. Established by the empty held list of a cold start (fn-bpnf-family-jobs-agree-when-empty); preservation over recovery replay and over the dispatch, forward, delivery and deletion arms is not proved (open).

Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-fragment-sweep-tests (a 70000-octet ADU in 100 fragments, out of order and overlapping, every outcome against the spec, one witness per hypothesis of fn-bpfw-exact-canvas-reassembles) and tests/acl2/bp-fragment-send-tests (the 100-fragment and 70000-octet plans the capped reference refuses; a must-fail per hypothesis). Native: tests/test_bp_fragment_node_native test_seventy_fragments_across_a_kill_reassemble_once. See the record for the manifest and native SHAs.

proofs.title: `store reclaim` rewrites only unheld legacy article records to their tombstones, converges, and frees exactly the octets admission counts
proofs.statement: Subject: the per-record rewrite fn-rclp-event (host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-log-reclaim-event, called per record by host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-log-reclaim-steps) under the context fn-rclp-ctx (fn-store-reclaim-context); fn-rclp-events is its map over the history (books/store-log-reclaim.lisp fn-lgr-rewrites-are-the-events), and PRF-271 (fn-lgr-decide-checkpoints-the-rewrite) makes it the history the log's checkpoint holds. fn-rclp-events-keep-the-summary-shape: fn-cc-octet-event-listp of the rewrite equals fn-cc-octet-event-listp of the history, for every sequence, lower and upper, no hypothesis. fn-rclp-event-decodes-to-the-tombstoned-record: a rewritten event decodes to the record with every field equal but the payload, which is fn-rcl-tombstone-of the old payload, and the charge, which is the history unit *fn-rclp-history-unit* (1). fn-rclp-rewritten-charge-is-the-history-unit: the charge a rewritten event carries into the ledger is the history unit, an unrewritten event carries its own; fn-rclp-freed-charge-account sums the released charge over the list. fn-rclp-events-never-touch-a-held-article: if the I-th event's record's article is named by an obligation of fn-rcl-obligations h, or its verdict needs its payload (fn-rcl-verdict-heldp), or the rule is keep-forever, the I-th event is byte-identical. fn-rclp-events-keep-every-other-kind: an event that does not decode as a legacy record (accepted-statement composites and every other kind) is byte-identical. fn-rclp-a-reclaimed-event-stays-reclaimed: a rewritten event is not rewritten again under any context; fn-rclp-events-idempotent under the same context. fn-rclp-freed-is-the-admission-count: for a rewritten event the fn-store-event-encode lengths the admission gate sums (fn-sbud-record-octets) fall by exactly the event's length less its replacement's; fn-rclp-freed-octets-account sums it over the list. The operator keystones: `store reclaim` and `store reclaim --dry-run` are exactly the :reclaim and :reclaim-dry-run native actions.

proofs.title: The operator's health verdict: eight states, each decided by the status report's sources, one line and one exit code each
proofs.statement: Over fn-nh-verdict (books/native-health.lisp), which fn-nh-offline-report, fn-nh-fenced-report and fn-nh-live-report render and host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-health-host-offline, fn-native-health-host-fenced and fn-native-live-status-host-answer call (host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-health-report; host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status-answer): fn-nh-verdict-states, the verdict has eight outcomes in *fn-nh-states* order, each :held, :clear or :unobserved exactly as the report's sources decide: fenced from the host's fence observation; exhausted from the headroom at the transaction-id or ledger codec ceiling; unqualified-profile from fn-bs-profile-validp and the development profile; space-pressure from free headroom below the operator's [alerts] headroom_min_percent on transactions, history octets or retention charge, when not exhausted; no-route from held :forward obligations with an empty fn-bprt-table; stranded-transfer from feed entries dropped at their retry bound; unavailable-peer from feeds with pending work and no connection; receipt-debt from held :forward obligations; a source not observed is :unobserved. fn-nh-exit-code-decodes: the exit code names the first held state (fn-nh-code-state) and is 0 exactly when no state is held or unobserved. fn-nh-report-exit-of-render: the code the host returns, read back from the rendered octets by fn-nh-report-exit (fn-native-health-host-exit, fnn-operator-execute-health), is the verdict's code for every verdict of at most eight outcomes. fn-nh-first-held-monotone: a verdict holding every state another holds has a first held state no later. fn-nh-pressedp-monotone: more use or a higher threshold never clears pressure. fn-nh-live-report-is-the-store-report: with the carried octet sum valid, the owner's report is the verdict over its Store's own committed octets, configuration and feed table. fn-nh-fence-of-route: an uncertain control-socket route is always fenced; otherwise the clone fence and the lock decide. EXTENSION (lane friend-blockers, 2026-09-27, the stranger rehearsal's stops): PKT-711: fn-nh-feed-unavailablep also holds a feed with an entry the peer deferred (queued with an attempt counted); KEYSTONE fn-nh-deferring-peer-is-held: health holds unavailable-peer while any peer defers this node's articles (`deferred=N`).
proofs.progress_note: See planning/evidence/operator-health-2026-09-25.md for the farm manifest and the native cases.

proofs.title: Every record a producer can stage is within the profile's R at any sequence, transaction ID, generation and stamp width, and the frontier frame carries u64 with every format-2 frame read unchanged
proofs.statement: fn-record-encode-producer-length-bound (books/records-seam.lisp, the seam constraint discharged by fn-record-impl-encode-producer-length-bound in books/records-canonicality.lisp and by both attachments): if a record's charge is at most 2^32 - 1, its encoding is at most fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling of its payload length and group count -- the 1 083-octet ceiling every saved profile's R was checked against -- whatever the width of its sequence, transaction ID, generation and stamp (the ceiling counts five-octet heads for the schema octet, the group count, the Message-ID, the three metadata strings and every group name, which encode at least 17 octets shorter; four eight-octet heads need 16). fn-bs-profile-admits-every-producer-record (books/record-width-producers.lisp): under an admitted profile such a record within A and G encodes within R, with no narrowness premise (PRF-086's fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record is the narrow case). fn-sn-prepare-stages-an-article-record-within-its-ceiling: a record fn-sn-prepare stages from fn-sn-article-record with a u32 charge is within the ceiling of its own payload and groups; fn-bpi-staged-record-fits-the-producer-ceiling: the same for the BP ingress producer (policy charge u32). fn-sbud-article-verdict-keeps-history-at-producer-width and fn-sbud-prepare-under-article-budget-keeps-history-at-producer-width (books/store-budget-article.lisp): an article admitted by the article verdict (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict) or staged under the served budget (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare -> fn-sbud-article-budget-for) keeps the committed history within H at any producer width. Frontier format 3 (books/byte-store-frame.lisp): fn-bs-frontier-impl-round-trip over every n <= 2^64 - 1 (the host's fn-store-metadata-frontier-frame/-decode through the scan seam's attachment), and fn-bs-frontier-decode-extends-format-2: every octet string the frozen format-2 reader fn-bs-frontier-v2-decode accepts, the format-3 reader fn-bs-frontier-decode-impl reads to the same transaction ID, so every saved frontier file opens unchanged. The allocator's successor fn-bs-frontier-next still stops at 2^32 - 1: the file machine (fn-sf-statep), the observed open (fn-sn-open-observed), the checkpoint (fn-checkpointp, fn-checkpoint-restore) and its TREE naturals (fn-cpc-treep) and the consumer candidate bound read u32, which is PKT-244.
proofs.progress_note: Certified with teeth (persvati, w25, 2 jobs, 300 s): run-20260926T010201Z-edf7 (certify-20260926T010233Z-3422722: 562 of 565 passed; the three reds were this lane's test books, fixed in 9104f415) and run-20260926T011811Z-b295 (certify-20260926T011837Z-3569115: those three passed). Native served-POST gate on the a9ed4dc2 developer image (SCN-072). The allocator past 2^32 - 1 and the stamp past 2106 wait on PKT-244.

proofs.title: The operator walk: no store is a refusal (exit 6) before any open, a MODE STREAM refusal stops the dial, and a snapshot rollback's loss is counted
proofs.statement: Over fn-native-operator-store-outcome (books/native-operator.lisp), which host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-store-outcome calls through fn-native-operator-host-store-outcome on every accepted plan before fnn-operator-dispatch-plan executes it: fn-native-operator-absent-store-is-refused, an accepted plan whose native action opens a store (fn-native-operator-result-needs-storep), over an observation that found none of *fn-nop-store-markers* beside the configured root, is refused with reason :no-store, exit code 6 (*fn-nop-no-store-exit*) and native action :none, so no open is attempted and the outcome is never the fault code 4; fn-native-operator-store-outcome-passes-a-present-store, with any marker observed or a plan that needs no store the plan passes unchanged. Over fn-fc-step, fn-fc-streaming-refusal-p and fn-fc-dial-allowedp (books/feed-connection.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-feed-reply-chunk and fn-owner-feed-has-queued call (host/native/feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-reply-step, fnn-feed-dial-plan): fn-fc-mode-stream-refusal-stops-the-dial, a complete peer line other than 203, 500 or 501 in the :mode phase (RFC 4644 section 2.3; since PRF-207, 500 and 501 are the IHAVE fallback, the old form a must-fail in tests/acl2/feed-connection-tests.lisp) is a refusal that closes the connection, is classified as a streaming refusal, and once the owner records the peer with :mode-stream-refused the dial is not allowed for that peer whatever it has queued; fn-fc-dial-allowedp-of-put-other, other peers keep their dial. Over fn-native-operator-snapshot-loss: fn-native-operator-snapshot-loss-counts-the-suffix, :loses exactly when the first list is an element-wise prefix of the second, and the count is the number of elements after it. Until 2026-09-26 the host handed it (sequence . file length) descriptors, which is not a history comparison (gpt-6's answers section 7); the verb's history claim is PRF-141, over exact committed records, and this lemma is the list-level function PRF-141's fold equals.
proofs.progress_note: Part 2 (the bp-node health verdict over the BP node's report, PKT-174's default) is not done; see planning/evidence/operator-walk-2026-09-26.md, PKT-264.

proofs.title: Admission keeps the maintenance reservation (one release record) and maintenance's temporary space is checked against the disk
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-smr-verdict-at (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-publication-verdict, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-preflight-publication for every non-article Store record: retention, identity, consumer and topic events, BP admission's included; and host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-publication-verdict), fn-smr-article-budget-for (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer, the served POST and BP transit prepares, handed to fn-pcar-sbud-prepare), fn-smr-article-verdict-at (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict, the developer store post). The reservation fn-smr-roomp profile used bytes is (fn-sbud-verdict-at profile :release used bytes) = :admissible. fn-smr-admission-keeps-the-reserve: if fn-smr-verdict-at admits a record of kind K /= :release at (used, bytes) and octets is a natural at most K's publication ceiling, fn-smr-roomp holds at (used+1, bytes+octets). fn-smr-prepare-keeps-the-reserve: if fn-sbud-prepare with budget fn-smr-article-budget-for (profile, the prepare's committed count, bytes, record) changed the configured owner and the record is narrow, fn-smr-roomp holds at (count+1, bytes + len (fn-record-encode record)) and the history is within H. fn-smr-article-verdict-keeps-the-reserve: the same for fn-smr-article-verdict-at and a narrow record within the asked counts. fn-smr-reserve-admits-the-release: where the reservation holds, fn-smr-verdict-at admits :release. fn-smr-admission-is-within-the-profile: every admission passes fn-sbud-verdict-at. fn-smr-roomp-antitone-in-octets and fn-smr-roomp-is-within-the-bound. fn-smr-admitted-profile-starts-reserved: an admitted profile holds the reservation at (0, 0). fn-smr-profile-upgrade-keeps-the-reserve. The disk half (lane log-leftovers): KEYSTONE fn-scka-publication-setup-plans-within-the-disk: the setup of every state checkpoint publication, called before anything is allocated (books/store-checkpoint-arena-writer.lisp fn-scka-publication-setup; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-sco-prepare for the owner's automatic, `store compact' and `store reclaim' checkpoints through host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-publish-captured, and host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sco-publish-setup offline), unless the capture is unencodable, answers (:plan ESTIMATE) exactly when ESTIMATE is within the budget, the observed free octets are a natural, and ESTIMATE is within them less the maintenance reservation (fn-ockp-space: free less fn-smr-reserve-octets), where ESTIMATE is the arena run's ALEN plus the length of the table file the pipeline writes (fn-sct-file-octets of the setup's tables, any S); otherwise it defers by name and nothing is written. Scope: ALEN is fn-scka-run-octets of the payload lengths; its equality with the length fn-scka-write-run writes is not proved; the free-octet observation is the host's statvfs, an environmental fact not modelled.
proofs.progress_note: Trimmed 2026-09-27 (lane flip-cleanup, 2026-09-27): the disk half (fn-cverb-pack-fits-the-disk, fn-rclp-pack-fits-the-disk: a pack fits the observed free octets) was deleted with the pack layer. Keystone for the state checkpoint's space check (the checkpoint compaction and reclaim publish): fn-scka-publication-setup-plans-within-the-disk (lane log-leftovers, 2026-09-27; admitted in the persvati REPL with its teeth in tests/acl2/store-checkpoint-arena-tests.lisp). Open: the arena run's octet estimate is not proved equal to what the writer writes. Before: Lane reclaim-lifecycle-2 (2026-09-26). Open: the free-octet observation is the host's statvfs, an environmental fact not modelled (a concurrent writer can take the space between the observation and the write; the write then fails before the selection, which the pack publication cuts cover). The BP namespace's own reservation is the FNBS debt cover (books/bp-node-debt.lisp), not restated here. Every book under 10 s.

proofs.title: A relay takes custody only over an admitted channel: a bundle whose channel admission was refused is refused at reception with the admission's reason, before any FNBS step
proofs.statement: host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-receive calls fn-bpaj-admitted-receive-event (books/bp-channel-ingress.lisp) with the admission answer of fnn-bps-tcpcl-admission (fn-owner-bp-tcpcl-ingress, i.e. fn-bpaj-tcpcl-ingress-result over the live owner configuration) and hands fnn-bps-foundation-step only its :ready answer. fn-bpaj-refused-channel-takes-no-custody: when the admission answer is not :admitted, the answer is exactly (:refused REASON) with the admission's own reason (fn-bpaj-channel-refusal-reason) and is not :ready, so no kind-5 custody row is proposed and hence no forwarding job, :attempting record, fragment family or owed receipt follows from that bundle. fn-bpaj-admitted-channel-receives-under-its-ingress: an admitted channel's answer is fn-bpnf-receive-wire-event under the admitted ingress, whose principal is the policy's selection (fn-bpaj-admitted-ingress-binds-announcement-and-selection). D23 (planning/decisions.md), mandate section 4 'Offline forwarding'; retires PKT-170.

proofs.title: The payload arena abstracts to the list of sealed payloads; a sealed handle is immutable and never reused; commit and open establish the same relation with the history
proofs.statement: fn-arena (books/payload-arena.lisp) is an abstract stobj whose logical value is the list of sealed payloads, oldest first (fn-arn-payload-listp), and whose executable is one resizable (unsigned-byte 8) array holding every payload back to back with an offset and a size per handle. The abstraction relation fn-arena$corr (the concrete object well formed, the fill and the count within their arrays, every handle's range below the fill, and the slices in handle order the logical list) is established by the creator and preserved by every export (the {correspondence}, {preserved} and {guard-thm} obligations, stated as defabsstobj-missing-events prints them and proved before the defabsstobj). fn-arena-seal-buffer{correspondence}: copying the octet buffer's cells in place at the fill and recording the range as the next handle corresponds to append of the buffer's value, an export taking a second stobj. KEYSTONES: fn-arena-seal-keeps-sealed and fn-arena-seals-keep-sealed say a handle that is a natural below the count reads the same octets after one seal and after any sequence of seals; fn-arena-seal-new-handle and fn-arena-seal-count say a seal's new handle is the old count, denotes the sealed octets, and the count grows by one (no hypothesis). fn-arn-store-corr (the arena is the history's payloads oldest first, fn-arn-payloads-of over fn-sf-records' commit order) is kept by a commit's seal (fn-arn-store-corr-of-commit) and established by an open's seals from the empty arena (fn-arn-store-corr-of-open, no hypothesis). Every executable function is guard-verified. No host entry calls the arena yet: the record's payload field must become a handle first (planning/evidence/rep-wave-d-2026-09-25.md section 3), so the subject is the base of that program, not a served path.
proofs.progress_note: Lane rep-wave-d (2026-09-25): the arena and its theorems certified on persvati (run-20260926T002605Z-febf, 1.17 s and 0.77 s at two jobs). The host join (the seal at the served POST's finish, the handle in the record) is the model change of the record's payload field, a coordinated freeze the record's section 3 lays out; until it lands the served path holds the list and no representation improvement is claimed. Lane records-freeze (2026-09-27, PRF-221): the byte array is now books/payload-arena-bytes.lisp under the name fn-arena-bytes (fn-arena$c, fn-arena$corr and every obligation unchanged in proof; the correspondence event of this row is fn-arena-bytes-seal-buffer{correspondence}), and fn-arena (books/payload-arena.lisp) is the attachable generic over the same logical side whose keystones this row names; both certified at the current digest by run-20260927T025909Z-155a. A-HOST dropped from this row's assumptions (lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G3-9, 2026-09-27): no theorem of the row takes fn-assume-host-report or fn-assume-host-events (books/assumptions.lisp) as a hypothesis, so the citation was decorative (AGENTS.md: the theorems that use a named assumption mention it). The host's honest I/O remains the trust boundary these theorems sit inside, not a hypothesis of them.

proofs.title: A BP verb's run class is ACL2's, with one exit code per class; a BP node's held rows and held octets are the operator's profile, a saved profile opens, and replay past the profile is refused by name, never truncated
proofs.statement: Part 1 (books/bp-run-class.lisp, books/bp-node-run-class.lisp). The host records evidence with fn-bprc-note: the reason of each (:forward-refused W A G REASON) effect through fn-bprc-effect-evidence (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-drive-effects, :process scope), each TCPCL session's outcome and fence flag through fn-bprc-session-evidence (host/native/bp.lisp fnn-bp-exit-code, fnn-bp-session-word), each publication classification through fn-bprc-publication-evidence, and the article verdicts its tally counted through fn-bprc-with-articles; it renders fn-bprc-run-exit-code (fnn-bps-exit-code, fnn-bp-exit-code, the bp-node serve result) and, for every fnn-store-indeterminate, the fenced code (fnn-bp-verb). fn-bprc-exit-code-separates-the-classes: the five classes :accepted 0, :refused 1, :fenced 3, :interrupted 6, :not-connected 7 answer five codes. fn-bprc-fence-is-never-masked: once :fenced is recorded, whatever was recorded before or after, the class is :fenced. fn-bprc-connection-local-never-fences: from the empty record, words among :failed, :uncertain, :refused, :accepted and nil never make the class :fenced. fn-bprc-uncertain-article-fences. fn-bpnrc-job-result-class-is-the-transport-class: under PRF-120's hypotheses (fn-bpnj-named-result-is-the-transport-outcome), the class of the effects of the durable answer to a named job result is fn-bprc-transfer-class of its outcome: :accepted, :refused, :interrupted for :uncertain, :not-connected otherwise. Part 2 (books/bp-node-profile.lisp, books/bp-node-profile-replay.lisp). fnn-bps-open reads bp-node-profile through fn-bpnpf-read and opens the machine with fn-bpnf-initial-state under its rows and octets. fn-bpnpf-read-of-octets: for every profile fn-bpnpf-validp admits (each field a machine limit, 1..2^24), the file's octets read back as exactly that profile. fn-bpnpf-valid-profile-opens: every valid profile opens a machine whose max-jobs and max-octets are the profile's. fn-bpnpf-write-never-lowers: bp-node profile publishes only a profile that raises or keeps every field. fn-bpnpf-replay-past-the-profile-is-refused: after any prefix that replays :ready to a held list the profile has filled, a well-formed received row makes fn-bpnf-family-replay-rows-aux over the whole journal answer (:fault :held-beyond-profile). Scope: the ADU, bundle-decoder and held-image ceilings are still constants (PKT-276); the Store profile's max-bp-rows is not read; the class does not yet separate expiry, no-route, busy delivery or a clock-domain change (PKT-276).
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-lifecycle-3 (2026-09-26, wave 2), PKT-276. Teeth: tests/acl2/bp-run-class-tests (the five codes; a must-fail per hypothesis of the separation; the fence among mixed evidence; the class of each outcome over the reachable attempting state of PRF-120's teeth, the stale attempt and the pending state as hypothesis removals), tests/acl2/bp-node-host-tests (the mixed article/session cases), tests/acl2/bp-node-profile-tests (the 128-row profile round trip, a zero-row and a 2^24+1-row profile, a configuration-less open, a lowering write refused, replay of two durable kind-5 rows under one row of profile answering :held-beyond-profile and under two :ready). Native: the six BP modules' expectations and SCN-067 under a 128-row profile; see the record.

proofs.title: The BP receiver binds a signed article its Store committed and never submits it a second time: the first durable commit is the only submission, and the verdict the delivery is bound to is the receiving Store's own
proofs.statement: host/bp-receipt-journal-host.lisp fn-bprj-request-action calls fn-bpaj-dispatch-fast (books/bp-native-app-fast.lisp) over the owner's bound Store for host/native/bp-app.lisp fnn-bpapp-action, before every step of fnn-bpapp-accept-locked; host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-plan-install and fn-owner-app-record call the lookup it uses, fn-bpaj-transit-record-lookup-fast. A signed article is committed as a kind-4 composite (fn-stxa-p) carrying the article record and the receiving Store's kind-2 verdict; the Store binding now reads a history's article records (fn-bpr-article-records, books/bp-receipt.lisp: a plain record, or the record a composite carries, as replay installs it). Both keystones are stated over the Store the host dispatches over (books/owner-store-indexed.lisp, fn-osi-live-store: the Store of the owner host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-extended installs, after any sequence of the owners the host installs), with no index premise: fn-osi-live-owner-store-is-indexed (PRF-144) discharges it; the -under-index lemmas of books/bp-signed-binding.lisp are the refinement layer. fn-bpaj-dispatch-never-resubmits-a-stored-article: when the live Store's article records contain an article record whose Message-ID is the one the dispatcher reads (fn-bpaj-dispatch-msgid: the relaying agent's check for a transit intent), the dispatcher does not answer (:submit). fn-bpaj-dispatch-binds-the-stores-own-record: a (:bind RECORD) answer names an article record for that Message-ID, accepted by the receiver's Store check, that is the article record of an event of the Store's own history, and when that event is a signed composite the composite binds its verdict to exactly RECORD (fn-stxa-bindsp). The request carries no verdict. Cites PRF-128 (the channel is admitted first), PRF-127 (relaying keeps the authored source), PRF-117 (the D23 source decision) and PRF-026 (a kind-4 completion records its verdict); D23, D25. Retires PKT-247.
proofs.progress_note: CHANGED 2026-09-26 (PRF-144, lanes signed-history-index and signed-history-index-2): the dispatcher's lookups read the Store's Message-ID index; the keystones are stated over the live owner's Store, where the index relation is a theorem (fn-osi-live-owner-store-is-indexed), not a hypothesis.

proofs.title: Relaying cannot change who wrote an article: the stored transit projection keeps fn-hc-authored-source on the NNTP and BP routes
proofs.statement: fn-rs-authored-source-is-the-walk (books/relay-source.lisp): for every octet list the parser accepts, fn-hc-authored-source of the parsed article equals fn-rs-source-walk (the reserved-field line walk) of fn-pu-strip of the octets, so the authored source is a function of the octets with Path and Xref stripped. fn-rs-relaying-keeps-the-authored-source (books/relay-source-routes.lisp): when the parser accepts both OCTETS and fn-peer-relayed-octets CFG PEER OCTETS, their authored sources are equal (with fn-peer-relayed-octets-change-only-path-and-xref). fn-rs-a-transfer-is-wanted-only-if-both-parse: fn-peer-decide-transfer answers :want only when both parse. fn-rs-a-wanted-transfer-keeps-the-authored-source: on :want, the payload fn-peer-injection-arguments stages (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-take through fn-peer-transfer) parses and has the received article's authored source. fn-rs-a-bp-transit-keeps-the-authored-source: when fn-bpaj-transit-plan (host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-plan-install) answers :submit, the request's article and fn-bpaj-transit-stored-octets both parse and have the same authored source. proofs.title: The state checkpoint's octets, written in batches through the octet buffer, are the program the tables codec specifies: the frame-level writer facts (re-targeted to schema 3 by lane checkpoint-pipeline)
proofs.statement: books/owner-checkpoint-writer.lisp (the definitions and step-level twins, split from owner-checkpoint-pipeline by checkpoint-pipeline-5; the loop keystone stays there). The writer the host calls per step (fn-ockp-step -> fn-ockp-batch -> fn-ockp-encode-batch -> fn-sct-renc, called from host/native/io.lisp fnn-checkpoint-write-steps by both entries) writes forward into the buffer: fn-sct-renc-is-program: (implies (true-listp fn-octets) (equal (fn-sct-renc x cand mtrie n table k fn-octets) (append fn-octets (fn-sct-program x cand mtrie n table) (fn-scc-repeat (nfix k) *fn-scc-op-cons*)))); fn-ockp-encode-batch-is-rows-program: the batch of B rows appends fn-sct-rows-program of those rows; fn-ockp-chunks-of-append-cut: fn-scc-chunks of P ++ Q is the full chunks the cut of P emits then the chunks of the residue with Q behind it (the residue invariant of the batched cut); fn-ockp-frames-of-append: the frames of appended chunk lists chain through fn-ockp-chain-end. proofs.title: A BP node's ADU octets and bundle octets are the operator's profile, the held image's bound is its held octets, and the ADU, bundle and held-image codecs are widths that never cap below a profile
proofs.statement: books/bp-node-profile.lisp: profile 2 is (ROWS OCTETS ADU BUNDLE), each a machine limit (1..2^24). fnn-bps-open reads bp-node-profile through fn-bpnpf-profile-read. fn-bpnpf-profile-read-of-octets: every valid profile 2 written by fn-bpnpf-profile-octets reads back as exactly itself. fn-bpnpf-profile-read-of-format-1: a format-1 frame of a valid (ROWS OCTETS) reads as (ROWS OCTETS 65538 1048576), and no file is the default. fn-bpnpf-profile-read-is-valid. fn-bpnpf-profile-write-never-lowers: a write bp-node profile publishes (fn-bpnpf-profile-write-octets) reads back as written and raises or keeps each of the four fields. books/bp-node-profile-admission.lisp: host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-receive calls fn-bpnpf-admitted-receive-event with the profile in force. fn-bpnpf-admission-within-profile-is-the-channel-answer: with a valid profile, a wire within the bundle octets and (if :ready) a bundle whose ADU (a fragment's total ADU length) is within the ADU octets, the answer is fn-bpaj-admitted-receive-event's (PRF-128). fn-bpnpf-admission-ready-is-within-profile: a :ready answer has a valid profile, a wire within its bundle octets, an ADU within its ADU octets, and is the channel answer. fn-bpnpf-admission-refuses-beyond-the-profile: on an admitted channel, a wire past the bundle octets is (:refused :bundle-beyond-profile) and a :ready bundle whose ADU is past the ADU octets is (:refused :adu-beyond-profile). fn-bpnpf-profile-within-codec-widths: every profile field is within its codec's width (*fn-bpa-max-octets*, *fn-bpb-max-data*, *fn-bpb-max-input*, *fn-bpnf-max-held-image* = 2^24; *fn-bpn-lifecycle-max-payload* = 2^24 + 3072). books/bp-node-profile-replay.lisp: fn-bpnpf-replay-past-the-octets-is-refused: after any prefix replaying :ready, a well-formed received row whose image does not fit the profile's held octets beside the held rows makes fn-bpnf-family-replay-rows-aux over the whole journal (:fault :held-beyond-profile). books/bp-adu.lisp: the ADU's fields are record items (fn-record-item-encode: the generic CBOR bytes at or below 65,535 octets), the article width is *fn-bpa-max-article* = 2^24 - 2106, and fn-bpa-round-trip and fn-bpa-encoding-bound hold at that width (their statements unchanged). books/bp-limits.lisp: fn-bpn-limits-compose-at-the-codec-widths replaces fn-bpn-limits-compose. fn-bpfw-reassemble-is-spec (PRF-121) is unchanged. Scope: the sender machine's job image stays the plain :blob (131,072); decoding a held family image at replay is one step linear in its octets, not a resumable quantum (PKT-294). Profile 3 (lane bp-rotation, 2026-09-27): (ROWS OCTETS ADU BUNDLE ROTATE), ROTATE the rotation threshold (a machine limit, which may be lowered). fnn-bps-read-profile reads through fn-bpnpf-node-profile-read; the machine and the admission read its base (fn-bpnpf-node-profile-base). fn-bpnpf-node-profile-read-of-octets: every valid profile 3 written by fn-bpnpf-node-profile-octets reads back as itself. fn-bpnpf-node-profile-read-of-older: whatever fn-bpnpf-profile-read admits (formats 1 and 2, no file) reads with the default threshold 4,096. fn-bpnpf-node-profile-read-is-valid, fn-bpnpf-node-profile-base-is-a-profile. fn-bpnpf-node-profile-write-never-lowers: a write bp-node profile publishes (fn-bpnpf-node-profile-write-octets) reads back as written and raises or keeps each held and codec field.

proofs.title: The schema-3 tables read from the octet buffer are what the list reader gives: the buffer load of the host's plan is fn-sct-decode-file of the frames' octets, on any input, and the ref codec's stack machine by index is the list machine (re-targeted to schema 3 by lane checkpoint-pipeline)
proofs.statement: books/store-checkpoint-tables-reader.lisp. fn-sct-load (the host-called entry: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sco-decode, called by host/native/io.lisp fnn-state-checkpoint-load at the store's open) is the list reader on the frames' octets: fn-sct-load-is-decode-file: (implies (and (fn-octets-p fn-octets) (fn-sccr-planp plan (if (consp plan) (fn-sccr-at 1 (car plan)) 0) fn-octets)) (equal (fn-sct-load plan fn-octets) (fn-sct-decode-file (fn-sccr-plan-segments plan fn-octets)))), with the same verdict on corrupt input. fn-sctr-run-is-run: the ref codec's machine by index over cells [i, end) is fn-sct-run over that slice; fn-sctr-step-is-step likewise; fn-sctr-run-decode-is-run-decode: a run over the plan is the list run over its frames' octets (through the unchanged chain check fn-sccr-join, fn-sccr-join-is-join). fn-sccr-admitted-within-bounds (kept): a segment ACL2 admits has the extent the codec sizes it, within both bounds; fn-sccr-admit-segment refuses another schema by name (:schema). The same property as the schema-2 fn-sccr-decode-plan-is-decode-segments and fn-sccr-decode-of-plan (the buffer decode is the list decode; with PRF-199 the decode of the writer's file is the value).

proofs.title: A re-signed carrier of an accepted signed source is a D25 conflict at the signed control route; only the saved artifact is already stored
proofs.statement: The subject was fn-rcl-existing-action (books/store-reclaim.lisp; retired, PKT-860: see RECORDS FLIP below for the subject now), which host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-hybrid-control-author asks through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action on the octets fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets computes, before it commits. fn-sr-a-re-signed-carrier-is-a-conflict (books/consumer-artifact-retry): the held payload under Message-ID M is fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets of source S, principal P, keys K and signatures S1 at clock A; the same S, P and K with signatures S2 different from S1, at any clock B and for any groups, both plans naming M, is :conflict. It instantiates fn-sr-a-changed-source-is-a-conflict (PRF-117) through fn-cra-a-re-signed-carrier-is-other-octets: two rendered carriers (fn-hc-render-at-most) of one source, principal and key set with different signatures are different octets (folding inserts only octets outside the base64 alphabet, base64 round-trips, and the canonical carrier decodes to exactly its signatures, fn-hc-decode-at-of-encode-at). The same artifact resent is :duplicate by fn-sr-a-signed-retry-is-already-stored (PRF-117, cited, not restated). Together they are the fn side of CNS-003: a client that resends its saved artifact gets D25's duplicate; one that re-signs gets a conflict. Not claimed: that the two Message-ID and the two nonempty-octet hypotheses are necessary (they are the instantiated keystone's; no conclusion-failing witness exists at the fixture and the weakened theorem is not proved), anything about the Python consumer (an external client), or that a revoked author's resend reaches D25 (the enrolment check refuses it first; PKT-322). RECORDS FLIP (flip-books-residue, 2026-09-27): the held payload is an arena handle; the subject is fn-store-existing-action (books/store-intern.lisp), which the host calls after flip-L6 at fn-owner-existing-action, fn-owner-prepare and host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-existing-action, and at fn-owner-existing-action-buffer through fn-pidx-existing-action (fn-pidx-existing-action-is-store-existing-action); the held-payload hypothesis reads the bytes under the held handle through the arena the verdict reads (fn-handle-bytes). The pre-flip statements over fn-rcl-existing-action equated a handle with octets and were vacuous on a flipped Store.

proofs.statement: fn-ks-accepted-statement-finishes-under-its-admission-context: when every record of the admission journal CONFIGS is at or before the statement EVENT's txid, CONFIGS replays (fn-config-replay RESERVED CEILING CONFIGS is not :fault), and every record of MORE is later than the txid, fn-ks-recover-recorded (fn-ks-cut RECORDS SNAPSHOTS EVENT) (append CONFIGS MORE) OBSERVED ED ML SEQUENCE TXID STORE-GENERATION equals fn-ks-accept RECORDS SNAPSHOTS EVENT under the authorities of CONFIGS' replay (the live grants the acceptance read). Subject fn-ks-recover-recorded, the open's recovery: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement-recover -> fnn-owner-key-statement with AT-OPEN, rows host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-rows = fn-ks-statement-rows (books/key-statements.lisp). proofs.title: One BP arrival's fragment selection reads the held rows' primary blocks and re-encodes and plans only rows whose family holds its offset-zero fragment, answering what the reference selector answers
proofs.statement: books/bp-node-fragment-step.lisp: host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-fragment-progress (called after every accepted arrival by fnn-bps-receive and at open by fnn-bps-open) calls fn-bpnf-family-next, whose :exec (guard verified in books/bp-node-fragment-guards.lisp) is (fn-bpnf-family-select st (fn-bpnf-held-list st) observation nil (fn-bpnf-zero-family-keys (fn-bpnf-held-list st))). fn-bpnf-zero-family-keys collects, from each row's primary block alone, the family key (principal, ADU key, coherence key) of every candidate row (fn-bpnf-fragment-candidatep: primary block, fragment flag, not deleted, not consumed; fn-bpnf-active-fragment-is-candidate) at offset zero. fn-bpnf-family-select-is-aux: for HELD a subset of the held list, TRIED a list of family keys every active held row of which has a plan that is not ready (fn-bpnf-family-keys-not-readyp, true of nil), and ZERO those offset-zero keys, the select equals fn-bpnf-family-next-aux, the reference selector (the anchor included); with fn-bpnf-family-next-memo-is-aux both equal the memo it replaces. fn-bpnf-family-without-zero-key-is-not-ready: a held active row whose family key has no offset-zero candidate has a plan that is not ready (from fn-bpnf-family-without-offset-zero-is-not-ready, PRF-134). Work, counted over the select's own control flow: fn-bpnf-family-select-plans-bound: the rows the select re-encodes (fn-bpnf-active-fragmentp, whose fn-bpnf-heldp re-encodes the bundle) and plans (fn-bpnf-family-plan-at, whose reassembly is linear in the family's octets, PRF-121) are at most the candidate rows whose family key is in ZERO; fn-bpnf-family-select-steps-bound: a call that plans no row makes at most |held| * (1 + |zero| + |tried|) header steps (one visit and the key comparisons of its two membership tests per row). So an arrival into a family whose offset-zero fragment is not held re-encodes no held row. Scope: the maintained relation is the call's own (TRIED, established empty at each host call and preserved by each step of the walk); nothing is carried across calls. A family whose offset-zero fragment is held is planned on every call until it is complete (its plan is linear in its octets): a family arriving in offset order costs its octets per arrival (PKT-308). The session's post-arrival scans ask every held row the same kind of question: books/bp-app-handoff.lisp fn-bpah-local-pendingp (per row in fn-bpah-select-oldest-at and -uncertain-at, host fnn-bpnode-dispatch-pending) and books/bp-report-observe.lisp fn-bpn-report-observe-held (per row in fn-bpn-report-observe-next, host fnn-bpnode-observe-reports) now have an :exec (mbe, guard verified; their :logic bodies and every statement about them unchanged) that reads the row's primary block first: fn-bpnf-held-nonfragment-headerp and fn-bpnf-held-administrative-headerp (books/bp-node-foundation.lisp). fn-bpah-local-pendingp-has-a-nonfragment-header and fn-bpn-report-observe-held-needs-an-administrative-header state why the prefilter refuses only rows the definition refuses (with fn-bpnf-heldp-primary-blockp: a held row's primary block is a block), so a fragment row costs those scans its header, not a re-encoding. The expiry scan books/bp-report-deletion.lisp fn-bpn-report-find-expired-held (host fnn-bpnode-delete-expired, after every session) asked fn-bpnf-heldp twice per row (fn-bpn-report-held-delete-pendingp and fn-bpah-held-expiry); its :exec asks first fn-bpah-held-expiry-header (books/bp-app-handoff-time.lisp: the same clock decision read from the primary block and the anchor), and fn-bpah-held-expiry-header-of-held equates it with fn-bpah-held-expiry on every held row, so a live row costs the scan its header. The receive step's own per-row work (fn-bpnf-held-octets walks each held wire's length, fn-bpnf-find-held compares keys) is outside these theorems.
