proofs.title: RETIRED (D34, lane migration-removal): store rollback-check --snapshot: an earlier state of this history exactly when the snapshot's committed records are this store's first records, compared octet for octet, and the count is the records after them
proofs.statement: books/native-operator.lisp. host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-rollback-snapshot acquires both stores read-only under their shared writer locks (fnn-acquire; a store an owner holds is refused, never read unlocked) and holds both while it reads each committed history as the open reads it (fnn-rollback-history: fnn-durable-records from the selected pack's lower bound, the pack's records through *fnn-pack-recover-callback*, i.e. fn-store-checkpoint-compaction-observe, then the suffix files; fnn-check-history-marker over the count) and calls fn-native-operator-history-start, then fn-native-operator-history-step once per snapshot record with the store's record at the same position (CUR-PRESENT nil past the store's end), then fn-native-operator-history-verdict with the store's record count (through the fn-native-operator-host-history-* wrappers). Both theorems are stated over that composition, V = (fn-native-operator-history-verdict (fn-nop-history-run (fn-native-operator-history-start) snap cur) (len cur)), fn-nop-history-run being the host's loop. KEYSTONE fn-native-operator-history-loss-is-ancestry: (and (iff (equal (car V) :loses) (equal (append snap (nthcdr (len snap) cur)) cur)) (implies (equal (append snap (nthcdr (len snap) cur)) cur) (equal (cadr V) (len (nthcdr (len snap) cur))))): the verb answers :loses exactly when the store's history is the snapshot's records followed by more records, and the count is the number of those records; otherwise (:refused :snapshot-not-a-prefix). fn-native-operator-history-loss-is-snapshot-loss: V equals fn-native-operator-snapshot-loss (PRF-130's list-level function). Events are exact record octets: no sequence number, length or file size is compared, as a filter or as a count, and no collision assumption is used. Every executable function is guard-verified (guard t). What it does not say: that the host's loop makes exactly these calls (host code, source-checked by tests/test_native_rollback_history.py); anything about the configuration history, which a restore also replaces; that the snapshot is the newest earlier state; or freshness (a store-local comparison is not an anti-rollback witness, mandate 5.6).
proofs.progress_note: Retired 2026-09-26 by D34 (fresh deploys, no migrations): its subject was removed with it (store rollback-check --snapshot, fn-native-operator-history-*, fn-native-operator-snapshot-loss). What now covers the property: a deploy is a reinstall plus store import (PRF-205); the store has one format (books/store-profile-open.lisp fn-spo-config-open-store-format-is-exactly-a-foreign-frame). The id is kept.

proofs.title: The owner's admission and a BP contact's job selection cost what the request costs: the contact's selection is one traversal of the job list, equal to the two lookup scans (part 2, certified); the Store's maintained record count and octets (part 1) are held for a continuation
proofs.statement: Part 2. fn-bpnj-contact-next (books/bp-node-job-offer.lisp; host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bpc-drive-contact and host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-send-receipts call it before every offer) reads the gate, then traverses the job list once (fn-bpnj-scan), and equals the former two-scan answer over fn-bpnj-select and fn-bpnj-held on every state (fn-bpnj-contact-next-is-the-two-scan-selection), so PRF-120's theorems keep their statements; the scan's ready and held components are the lookup scans' from any examined prefix (fn-bpnj-scan-finds-the-selected-job, fn-bpnj-scan-finds-the-held-job), and under the machine's key uniqueness (fn-bpn-job-listp, the jobs field of fn-bpn-machine-statep) every job is its own entry, so the one confirming lookup succeeds at once (fn-bpnj-unique-keys-make-every-job-its-own-entry). proofs.title: The Store's capacity is a resource vector maintained by every admission: a release per open undertaking and the maintenance release stay admissible, and every admitted history of mixed record kinds is within H and T
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-cvec-verdict-at (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-publication-verdict, every served non-article Store record, BP admission's retention included; host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-publication-verdict), fn-cvec-article-budget-for (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer, the served POST and BP transit, handed to fn-pcar-sbud-prepare), fn-cvec-article-verdict-at (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict), fn-cvec-debt-extend (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-record-debt, the carried (K . DEBT)), fn-cvec-config-generations (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-cfg-native-admin-authorize, handed to fn-native-admin-publication-authorize). The vector fn-cvec-roomp profile used bytes debt is fn-smr-roomp at (used+debt, bytes+debt*R), R the release ceiling 4096: the profile's gate admits debt+1 release records in turn. DEBT is the history's open undertakings (fn-cvec-record-debt: +1 per :undertake, -1 per :release), equal to the carried cache when valid (fn-cvec-debt-extend-is-the-record-debt) and moving as the ledger's :forward pins do (fn-cvec-admit-forward-adds-one-debt, fn-cvec-release-forward-removes-one-debt). Established at init (fn-cvec-admitted-profile-starts-held); preserved by every admitted non-release record with the debt its own undertaking adds (fn-cvec-admission-keeps-the-vector), by a release against an open debt (fn-cvec-release-keeps-the-vector), by the served article prepare (fn-cvec-prepare-keeps-the-vector) and the developer article verdict (fn-cvec-article-verdict-keeps-the-vector, and at any producer width with a u32 charge fn-cvec-article-verdict-keeps-the-vector-at-producer-width), by a reclaim (fn-cvec-roomp-antitone-in-octets) and a profile upgrade (fn-cvec-profile-upgrade-keeps-the-vector). fn-cvec-roomp-discharges-every-debt: where it holds, the j-th release (j <= debt) is admitted after j releases of at most R octets. The composed statement fn-cvec-admitted-history-keeps-the-vector / -from-init: a history of mixed record kinds each admitted at its prefix by the gate of its kind (fn-cvec-history-admittedp; an article within its figure under a u32 charge, PRF-126; every other kind within its publication ceiling, a premise its producer's codec discharges; a release only against an open debt) leaves the vector holding at the committed count, the actual committed record octets fn-sbud-record-octets and the history's debt, and is within H (fn-profile-replay-within-boundp) and below T. With no debt the vector and the gate are PRF-129's except for :undertake (fn-cvec-roomp-without-debt-is-the-reserve, fn-cvec-verdict-without-debt-is-the-reserve-gate). The charge component is pre-paid (fn-cvec-release-never-raises-the-charge). fn-cvec-config-publication-keeps-the-release-generation: a configuration record other than the retention rule is accepted only below max-config-generations.
proofs.progress_note: Lane capacity-vector (2026-09-26). The disk component is an environmental assumption (the observed free octets are not owned; a failed write is refused or uncertain, never torn). The history-level equality of the record debt with the ledger's :forward pin count is proved per transition, not over replay. Producers outside PRF-123/126 (the signed composite, peer-carried records) meet their kind's ceiling by their codec, a premise here. RECORDS FLIP (2026-09-27, flip-L1): the vector's per-record octet measure is fn-sbud-row-octets (what the row stores) in fn-cvec-record-admittedp, fn-cvec-history-admittedp and fn-cvec-record-keeps-the-vector, so it stays the measure fn-sbud-record-octets sums; on a wire event it is the encoding (fn-sbud-row-octets-of-wire-row). RESTATED (flip-L1-3): the article arm asked fn-record-p of a history row, which no retained article satisfies (fn-cvec-wire-record-is-no-article-row: a wire record is never a row of kind :article), so every history holding an article was unadmitted. fn-cvec-record-admittedp's article arm now asks fn-held-p and the article verdict at the row's facts octets (fn-cvec-row-payload-length, the wire record's payload length the intern copies) and its groups; fn-cvec-record-keeps-the-vector goes through fn-cvec-article-verdict-keeps-the-vector-for-a-held-row (the row stores its payload length, within the figure charged). tests/acl2/store-capacity-vector-tests.lisp admits a history holding the POST's row (fn-intern-row-at) and refuses the row past the figure.

proofs.title: A friend's invitation configures the inviter at the invitee: the accept's one configuration record sets the inviter peer from the invitation's signed address before the enrolment, and a crash between the two resumes as the enrolment without a second record
proofs.statement: fn-pinv-accept-record-configures-the-verified-inviter: a (:configure DELTAS) from fn-pinv-accept-record-plan RECEIVED OBS ED ML SNAPSHOTS PEERS (books/peer-invite.lisp; host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-accept calls it through host/peer-invite-host.lisp fn-pinv-host-accept-record-plan) has the invitation bound (fn-pinv-bound-document-p: the carrier verifies under the key set its body names and the inviter is its genesis principal), the inviter not enrolled with those keys in SNAPSHOTS, an Inviter-Port that is a port, the peer fn-pinv-inviter-peer (named and path-identified by Inviter-Path, transport (:nntp 1 Inviter-Host Inviter-Port (:clear)), inbound Groups, no outbound half) fn-cfg-peerp with auth (:principal INVITER-HEX), no row of PEERS under its name, and DELTAS = (fn-cfg-set-peer-delta peer). fn-pinv-accept-record-fold-configures-the-inviter: over fn-cfg-apply V GEN STAMP DELTAS (the fold fn-cfg-apply-record runs when the owner completes the publication) the peers table holds exactly the peer's rows under its name, and the accept record plan over the folded peers table is the accept plan, which is :enrol (the crash point after the record resumes as the enrolment, never a second record). Not covered: TLS words and the outbound half (the operator's peer add of the same name), the signature primitives (A-CRYPTO), that the address the inviter signed is reachable.

proofs.title: The limits of a public reader port as the host calls them: admission bounded by the total and per-address rows in force, a step budget per quantum that waits and never refuses, the none anonymous policy gating every reader and posting command 480, and no limit or reconfiguration dropping a connection
proofs.statement: books/public-exposure.lisp. The host calls: fn-exp-open through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-exposure-open from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-serve-client at every accept (it admits or refuses and opens the owner connection in the same call, over fn-ocfg-open / fn-ocfg-open-peer with the pinned AUTHINFO configuration fn-exp-pinned-acfg); fn-exp-charge through fn-owner-exposure-charge from fnn-owner-exposure-wait before every served step; fn-exp-observe through fn-owner-exposure-observe inside fn-owner-chunk after every served step, as books/public-exposure-reply.lisp's fn-exp-observe-effects over the step's effects (fn-exp-observe-effects-unfolds: it is fn-exp-observe of fn-served-reply-octets of the effects, so every fn-exp-observe theorem here is about the host's call; its executable reads the reply's two facts, answered and the 481 count, by one constant-stack scan of the effects with no copy of the reply: fn-exp-481-scan-counts-the-481-replies, fn-exp-effects-scan-is-the-reply-scan, fn-exp-observe-effects-is-the-observation-of-the-reply; exposure-reply-size, PKT-481: fn-exp-481-count's per-octet recursion over a 2 MiB reply had exhausted the control stack and stopped the owner); fn-exp-idle through fn-owner-exposure-idle on every receive timeout; fn-exp-release in the serve loop's unwind; fn-exp-health-lines through host/native-live-status-host.lisp for `health'. The limits are fn-exp-limits over the LIVE configuration value (rows written by `policy set', books/native-admin.lisp :set-exposure / :set-policy), the owner's bound (a run's is *fn-exp-owner-connection-bound*, PRF-211), ACL2's reading of the bound listener (fn-exp-address-publicp) and `[auth] required'. KEYSTONES: fn-exp-open-admits-within-the-limits-in-force (an open that returns an id happened only with the owner below the total, leaves the address at most one higher, and, for an address outside the trusted range (PRF-211), happened only with the address below its per-address limit in force and leaves it within that limit); fn-exp-open-never-exceeds-a-limit-in-force (no open carries an address outside the trusted range past max(before, limit): a lowered limit closes nothing and admits nothing more); fn-exp-charge-bounds-steps-per-quantum (under a positive steps row a step proceeds only below the budget and leaves the address's count for the quantum within it; exhaustion is (:defer MS), never a close: fn-exp-charge-waits-and-never-closes); fn-exp-anonymous-none-gates-every-restricted-command (under the none policy the pinned configuration requires authentication, and for any session carrying it with no subject every restricted command -- POST included -- is 480, no submission, session unchanged: composed with books/nntp-auth.lisp's fn-auth-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed); fn-exp-limits-never-drop-a-connection (for any limits, open, charge, observe and idle keep every registered connection; only release removes); fn-exp-idle-closes-only-silence and fn-exp-observe-closes-only-on-a-failed-login (the only two closes the book asks for). NOT covered: that the pinned configuration IS the session's (fn-auth-open-session and served.lisp's fn-served-peer-and-reader-open-under-the-same-policy state it; no composed theorem over fn-ocfg-open is proved here); that the host's loop makes exactly these calls (source, and the native campaign tests/test_native_public_exposure.py); a read-only anonymous level and a public-groups level (need an nntp-auth change, 281 dependent books: deferred, PKT-405); TLS renegotiation and handshake cost (OpenSSL, host trust); what happens behind a reverse proxy (every client one address).

proofs.title: The implicit-TLS listener is offered only beside its certificate and runs the STARTTLS session after the handshake; the operator's inspect answer is the store's lookup
proofs.statement: Over fn-served-dispatch (books/served.lisp), which books/owner.lisp fn-own-read-step calls for the host's fn-owner-tls-established, on the connection fn-served-open-group-indexed makes, which fn-own-open calls for the host's fn-owner-open (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-serve-client, implicit mode, after SSL_accept): fn-served-implicit-tls-is-the-starttls-session, under a well-formed policy (fn-auth-configp) with TLS available, STARTTLS on the opened connection emits the (:starttls) handshake effect, and the connection after the (:tls-established) event alone equals the connection after STARTTLS and then that event; fn-served-implicit-tls-session-is-protected, the event emits nothing, records the TLS layer and owes no handshake. Over fn-native-operator-result-run-implicit-tls-port (books/native-operator.lisp), which host/native/operator-live.lisp (`run') reads through fn-native-operator-host-result-run-implicit-tls-port to decide whether fnn-owner-run binds the second listener: fn-native-operator-implicit-tls-listener-needs-its-certificate, a port is offered only for an accepted run plan that is not --once, with certificate and key octets present, in 1..65535 and not the plaintext port. Over fn-native-operator-inspect-report, which host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-execute-inspect calls with fnn-bridge-lookup-found-p's boolean: fn-native-operator-inspect-report-is-the-lookup, exit 0 and :accepted exactly when the store binds the Message-ID, exit 1 and :absent otherwise, and the printed line is the verdict's. proofs.title: A chain of packs reconstructs the history: contiguous digest-linked links compose one prefix, compaction extends it over the uncovered suffix, the open over the walked chain answers the history, reclaim and publication cuts keep it
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/checkpoint-host.lisp calls for host/native/checkpoint.lisp (fnn-pack-walk, fnn-pack-extend-chain, fnn-pack-recover-records, fnn-pack-retire-older-generations): fn-ccc-links-okp-composes-a-prefix (a walked chain is BOUNDARY exact Store events from sequence 0 under the newest frontier); fn-ccc-capture-extends-the-chain (fn-ccc-capture-link from the chain's boundary, frontier, generation and digest yields a link that, consed on, is again a chain whose records are a prefix of the history and strictly longer; the old chain is its tail); fn-ccc-capture-link-succeeds (it succeeds on a valid suffix); fn-ccc-chain-reconstructs-the-history (fn-ccc-observe-chain over the decoded chain and an observation holding, for every sequence from some N at or below the chain's boundary to the end of H, the record H holds there answers (:ok H frontier) when the chain's records are a prefix of H and the suffix is valid: no reclaimed file is needed, and the served view replays exactly these records); fn-ccc-reclaim-preserves-reconstructed-history (PRF-073 over a chain); fn-ccc-retire-plan-keeps-the-chain; fn-ccc-publication-crash-walks-old-or-new-chain (under the marker-old-or-complete-candidate and files-kept facts of the pack program, the walk reads the old chain or the new link on it); fn-ccc-links-count-within-boundary (walk fuel T suffices); fn-cverb-pack-decision-capture-succeeds restated over the chain capture. Joined with the reclamation work (pack-chain-join, 2026-09-26): fn-rclp-reclaiming-pack-is-a-first-link (books/store-reclaim-pack.lisp; when fn-rclp-decide answers :reclaim, the summary it hands host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-pack-publish-generation is, through fn-ccc-link-of-summary, a valid first link with no predecessor whose boundary is the selected chain's coverage and the whole committed history); the compact verb's temporary-space figure is the next link's (fn-cverb-pack-fits-the-disk, PRF-129). The between-links cut (pack-chain-link, lane pack-chain-cut): fn-ccc-chain-program is fnn-pack-extend-chain's link as a program (:publish, :select, then the cut); fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-walks-the-extended-chain (at the Nth cut the state is the selection's, from the lemma fn-ccc-chain-cut-state-is-previous-state that a :cut leaves the preceding step's state; the marker names link N and the walk from it reads links N..1 on the chain selected before, when the host's chain names each predecessor, its generations are distinct and its entries are the host's triples); fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-reopens-to-the-history (the reopen there answers the history under fn-ccc-chain-reconstructs-the-history's hypotheses over that chain).
proofs.progress_note: Retired 2026-09-27 (lane flip-cleanup, 2026-09-27; design 2026-09-27 storage-log section 9 row 5, log-recovery's section 6 continuation): its subject was deleted with the pack layer: the pack chain (books/checkpoint-pack-chain.lisp) and its host wrappers (host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-checkpoint-chain-*) had no native caller since PKT-838 deleted fnn-pack-walk and the pack verbs; the books and tests are gone. What covers the property now: the record log's open over its segments and the checkpoint (PRF-270). Before: Lane bounds-p5 (2026-09-25). Open: the link codec round trip is executed, not proved; the crash keystone is stated under the pack program's two facts, not composed with fn-cpp-crash-selects-old-authority-or-complete-candidate by a theorem. Lane pack-chain-cut (2026-09-26, PKT-459): the between-links cut pack-chain-link is a model program cut (fn-ccc-chain-program) with its K0-shaped state theorem and its crash keystones (fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-walks-the-extended-chain, fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-reopens-to-the-history); the chain's links-okp at the cut is a hypothesis, not composed from the per-link captures (PKT-460).

proofs.title: A control article is offered to every peer whose outbound wildmat matches its Newsgroups names or its filing group, and an ordinary article's feed scope is unchanged
proofs.statement: fn-own-submission-offers-a-control-article-under-its-newsgroups-and-filing-group: for an owner O with a submission in flight whose octets classify :control (fn-own-feed-control-of, equal to fn-ctl-classify-octets whenever the article parses: fn-own-feed-control-of-is-the-filing-classification), a peer NAME of the feed table (fn-own-feed-tablep, fn-own-feed-entry-of) with an outbound half whose wildmat matches a group of the article's Newsgroups (fn-own-feed-groups-of) or its filing group (fn-ctl-filing-group of the verb), whose path-identity the Path does not name, which is not the origin and whose queue does not hold the Message-ID, is a member of fn-own-submission-targets O (books/owner-feed-subject.lisp; the host's intent calls it through fn-icar-submission-targets, equal to it, at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-submission-intent, and the durable enqueue fn-own-feed-durable through fn-own-outcome, fn-own-control-outcome and fn-own-transit-outcome). fn-own-submission-target-of-a-control-article-is-in-its-scope: every target of a control article matches its base groups, its Newsgroups names or its filing group. fn-own-sub-feed-groups-of-an-ordinary-article: a submission whose octets do not classify :control has exactly its base groups. Not covered: the pull side (NEWNEWS serves by the filed group), the receiving node's acceptance of the cancel (PRF-097/C3's), RFC 5537 section 5.3's advice that a cancel's Newsgroups equal its target's (the author's, not checked).

proofs.title: The operator's `keys redecide MSGID` decides a stored key statement as a new acceptance under the grants in force at its own txid, repeats nothing at the next open, and is refused by name for a Message-ID that names no stored statement or a statement already acted; and the transit refusal class the owner prints is the seven-class admission verdict's refusal arm
proofs.statement: Subject fn-ks-redecide / fn-ks-redecide-plan / fn-ks-redecide-event (books/key-statements.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-redecide-find/-plan/-event compute over the owner's Store records, keyring snapshots and live authorities rows, called by host/native/keys.lisp fnn-keys-owner-redecide under the owner mutex (control request 12, `operator CONFIG keys redecide MSGID`). (1) fn-ks-redecide-decides-under-the-configuration-at-its-own-txid: when every record of the journal CONFIGS is at or before TXID and CONFIGS replays, the redecide under the replay's authorities (the live rows the host passes) equals the redecide under fn-ks-redecide-rows TXID CONFIGS (fn-ctl-config-at the redecide's own txid). (2) fn-ks-reopen-after-a-redecide (no hypotheses): the open's recorded recovery fn-ks-recover-recorded of the redecided state, under any journal and any coordinates, is the redecided state when the redecide committed a kind-3 change and the recovery of the unchanged state otherwise, so PRF-124 and PRF-140 carry over. (3) fn-ks-redecide-of-no-stored-statement-is-refused-by-name and fn-ks-redecide-of-an-acted-statement-is-refused-by-name: the plan is (:refused :not-a-key-statement) / (:refused :already-acted) and the state is unchanged. (4) fn-ks-redecide-of-an-unacted-statement-is-its-acceptance-decision: for a stored statement that has not acted, the plan and kind-3 event are fn-ks-plan and fn-ks-execute of it, so the PRF-098 keystones over them apply. (5) fn-ks-a-redecide-that-acted-is-refused-the-second-time: after a redecide that acted, when the statement's verdict generation precedes the keyring's next generation, the same MSGID is refused :already-acted under any grants. The record is the kind-3 change itself at the redecide's coordinates (no re-filed composite, no new record kind, no cut). Teeth: tests/acl2/key-statements-tests.lisp section PRF-166 (decline, later grant, redecide at a later txid; one must-fail per hypothesis; the generation hypothesis's removal is a CORRUPTED-STATE witness). Not covered: live rows = replay of fn-sn-config-history is the owner's maintained relation (P6/PRF-028 (certified again at the current digest since c7072ddc: served-path-scale's manifest certify-20260926T123813Z-1816946 covers its thirteen theorems), not proved here; the host-to-model link of fnn-keys-owner-redecide is by construction (it calls the named functions), as PRF-098. (6) fn-pcb-admission-verdict-refusal-arms-are-the-refusal-class (books/peer-carriage.lisp, PKT-240, no hypotheses): fn-pcb-verdict-refusal-class of fn-pcb-admission-verdict equals fn-pcb-refusal-class on every input; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-refusal-class, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-transit-class inside fnn-owner-attempt-transit, computes the former. Witnesses for all seven verdicts in tests/acl2/peer-carriage-tests.lisp.

proofs.title: The consumer count is the operator's profile field 9: the served registration refuses exactly past it and the table stays within it
proofs.statement: The consumer registration the owner serves (fn-cp-register-within, called by books/consumer-owner-local.lisp fn-col-register from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-register with MAX = fn-store-profile-max-consumers of the carried profile, host/store-host.lisp) is (:refused :max-consumers) iff fn-cp-register answers :write and the table already holds (nfix MAX) entries, and is fn-cp-register's answer otherwise (fn-cp-register-within-refuses-exactly-past-the-operator-bound, no hypothesis). proofs.title: One fn-wide outcome classification and one ACL2 code map: every native command exits code(classify(f, x)), the seven classes' codes are disjoint and fixed, a fence is the only 3 in every family, NO-STORE and the clock-undecided decode are refusals, and CONFLICT is a refusal that keeps every earlier FNCT octet
proofs.statement: books/outcome-class.lisp: *fn-outcome-codes* maps :accepted 0, :refused 1, :fenced 3, :fault 4, :usage 5, :interrupted 6, :not-connected 7; fn-outcome-code reads it. fn-outcome-code-separates-the-classes: distinct classes have distinct codes. fn-outcome-code-table-by-definition: the seven codes are (0 1 3 4 5 6 7). fn-outcome-code-is-fenced-iff-fenced: over classes, the code is 3 exactly for :fenced. Families: host conditions (fn-outcome-of-host-condition, called by host/native/io.lisp fnn-exit-code-for; the +fnn-exit-*+ constants are fn-outcome-code of their classes): fn-outcome-host-condition-fences-iff-indeterminate. Control (fn-native-control-status-exit-code, called by the operator post and hybrid clients): fn-native-control-exit-is-fenced-iff-uncertain; topic control fn-thlc-outcome-class. BP (fn-bprc-exit-code is fn-outcome-code; host fnn-bp-exit-code, fnn-bps-exit-code, fnn-tcl-exit-code): fn-bprc-run-exit-code-is-fenced-iff-fenced; bp decode (fnn-command-bp-decode renders fn-bprc-decode-exit-code): fn-bprc-decode-never-fences, the clock-undecided verdict exits 1. CONFLICT (PKT-246): :conflict appended to *fn-nctrl-statuses*; fn-native-control-conflict-is-a-refusal: for an owner control result in the admitted range, the completion status (fn-native-control-completion-status, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission for the operator post and hybrid-author) is :conflict only for an owner refusal of D25's :conflict word, it classes :refused and exits 1, and any other word passes the result through; fn-nctrl-conflict-keeps-every-earlier-octet: each status of *fn-nctrl-statuses-before-conflict* is sealed exactly as the enumeration before :conflict seals it. The round trip of :conflict and the older decoder's :bad are executed witnesses (the seal's digest is A-CRYPTO's constrained function in proofs).

proofs.title: A signed POST's identity prepare and a signed-entry lookup cost what the request costs, not what the history holds: the prepare stages without replaying the appended history, and the BP receiver's Message-ID lookups read a maintained index
proofs.statement: Part 2, the incremental identity prepare. host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-identity (called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-identity-commit for every signed POST's kind-4 composite and every keyring snapshot) installs fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity, whose store step fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity stages through fn-spc-stage-record: the specification's candidate predicate without fn-sf-history-recoverablep over (append records (list event)) (O(N*L) per signed POST, PKT-223). fn-spc-related-identity-candidate-is-recoverable (books/store-prepare-correspondence.lisp): in a :reserved state satisfying fn-snt-relation, a candidate the prepare's gate has applied to the live node (consp (fn-replay-apply-record node event)) leaves the appended history recoverable at the frontier (by fn-snt-deferred-preparation-outcome). KEYSTONES fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity-is-sn-prepare-identity-under-relation: (fn-snt-relation s) implies (fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity s event) = (fn-sn-prepare-identity s event); fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity-is-ocfg-step-under-relation: (fn-own-relation (fn-ocfg-owner oc)) implies (fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity oc event) = (fn-ocfg-step oc (list :store (list :prepare-identity event))). The premise is the article prepare's (fn-opc-prepare-equals-owner-event-under-relation): fn-own-relation conjoins fn-snt-relation, established at observed open and preserved by the owner transition family. They replace the hypothesis-free equalities of carry-kind, which held only because the function replayed. Cites PRF-117 (the D23 source decision) and fn-sr-a-signed-retry-is-already-stored (a signed retry is the D25 duplicate) unchanged: the verdict the prepare stages is the specification's. Part 1, the Message-ID index. The Store's derived event index (fn-sn-event-index, books/consumer-event-index.lisp) is a pair: the sequence trie and a Message-ID trie from each Message-ID to the article records the history commits under it (a plain record, or the record a kind-4 composite carries, decoded once when added: fn-cei-event-article), in history order. fn-cei-put extends both halves, so fn-sn-io's record-directory append (the one transition that grows the history) maintains it and every open's fn-cei-build establishes it. proofs.title: An invitation code redeems at most one account, once, across a crash: the accounts slot keeps a redeemed row the same row, the redeem plan stages only an admitted delta and resumes as already redeemed, and a redeemed account's credential is in the connection's snapshot
proofs.statement: Over the configuration the owner replays at open (fn-config-replay-loop; the records fn-owner-reconfigure-complete publishes through fn-ocl-publish), a code's redeemed row in the tenth slot (books/config.lisp fn-cfg-accounts) is the same row, or that row's tombstone once an account delete names its login, after every later acceptable record (fn-acct-bound-row-succeeds-across-replay; per admitted delta list fn-acct-bound-row-succeeds; restated by lane public-node-2 from the row's equality, which account delete falsifies), and fn-cfg-delta-reason refuses a redeem of a redeemed digest unless it carries exactly that row (fn-acct-redeemed-refuses-another-redeem). The redeem plan fn-acct-redeem-plan (books/accounts.lisp; a pure function of the configuration value, the stamp, the code, the login, the password, the host's salt observation and whether the snapshot already names the login) plans :redeem only of a delta the configuration admits at every generation and ledger, which redeems the code under that login with the verifier fn-authsec-enrol computes (fn-acct-redeem-plan-is-admitted-and-redeems); after that delta is applied the same code, login and password plan (:already-redeemed) under any later stamp, salt and snapshot (fn-acct-redeem-plan-after-its-redeem-is-already-redeemed: the crash after the publication's root barrier and before the reply); another login is (:refused :account-redeemed) (fn-acct-redeem-plan-refuses-another-login); an unknown code plans neither (fn-acct-redeem-plan-of-an-unknown-code-stages-nothing). The row keeps the verifier as text and fn-acct-text-verifier-of-verifier-text is the representation's round trip. The connection's credential snapshot fn-auth-config-with-accounts (books/nntp-auth.lisp; host-called through books/owner-config.lisp fn-ocfg-open from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open, and fn-ocfg-open-peer from fn-owner-open-peer) is a configuration, keeps the operator's credential for a login auth.toml names, and otherwise finds the redeemed row's credential (the login's local principal fn-acct-local-principal, the row's verifier, posting); composed with fn-auth-step-principal-login-binds-exactly-the-unique-match (cited) a redeemed account's 281 installs exactly that principal. The wire (friends-accounts-2), over fn-auth-step-pinned (the dispatcher books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch calls, reached by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk through fn-own-read, and by the owner's re-entry fn-owner-account-outcome, host/native-admin-host.lisp, through fn-ocfg-read-step): XREDEEM before a TLS layer on a protected-only listener answers 483 and changes nothing (fn-auth-step-pinned-xredeem-before-tls-is-483); after 381, XREDEEM PASS PASSWORD answers nothing and holds the session (handshakingp, so the served fold stops) with exactly the cached code, login and password and no subject (fn-auth-step-pinned-xredeem-pass-holds-for-the-owner; a hold binds nobody and keeps the role, fn-auth-step-redeem-hold-keeps-the-role); a holding session answers the owner's (:account-outcome WORD) 281 exactly when WORD is :bound, else 482, and leaves the hold (fn-auth-step-pinned-redeem-outcome-answers-the-word). The owner's plan (host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-acct-host-owner-redeem-stage, run by host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-account-redeem under the owner mutex inside fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked) is fn-acct-redeem-bounded-plan over the live configuration: where fn-acct-redeem-plan redeems, it redeems exactly while the credential table is under the profile's max-credentials, else (:refused :account-credential-bound) (fn-acct-redeem-bounded-plan-refuses-exactly-past-the-operator-bound); the word fn-acct-redeem-word is :bound only for a resume or a :redeem whose publication answered :accepted, i.e. after fn-owner-reconfigure-complete installed the durable record (fn-acct-redeem-word-is-bound-only-after-a-durable-redeem); an unknown code stages nothing and is refused (fn-acct-redeem-word-of-an-unknown-code-is-refused); after its redeem is published the same request is (:already-redeemed) and :bound under any later stamp, salt, snapshot, count and bound (fn-acct-redeem-bounded-plan-after-its-redeem-is-bound: the crash cut FN_ACCOUNT_TEST_STOP_AFTER_PUBLISH). Not covered: the lift of the wire keystones through fn-served-step's fold to fn-own-read (the fold's stop on handshakingp is books/served.lisp's, cited); that a guessed code finds no row is the crypto seam's preimage resistance (A-CRYPTO); P6's publication theorems are PRF-028 (certified again at the current digest since c7072ddc: served-path-scale's manifest certify-20260926T123813Z-1816946 covers its thirteen theorems). EXTENSION (lanes public-node-2 and -3, 2026-09-27): `fn operator CONFIG account delete LOGIN` (books/native-admin.lisp, host host/native-admin-host.lisp) stages config delta code 27 (:account-delete), which tombstones the login's redeemed rows (mark 7: digest and login kept, verifier dropped) and withdraws nothing (fn-acct-delete-apply-unfolds). KEYSTONE fn-acct-delete-is-admitted-exactly-when-held-and-unobligated: admitted exactly when the login is well formed, held, and no signing binding, moderator role or consumer binding names it. KEYSTONE fn-acct-delete-keeps-the-login-taken. KEYSTONE fn-auth-config-with-accounts-after-an-account-delete-offers-only-the-operators-credential: every later snapshot offers only auth.toml's credential under that login.

proofs.title: The cheaper committed-history marker programs PKT-079 and PKT-143 allow are refused by the contract they would refine: the deferred marker leaves A <= M <= D, and an unfenced or in-place marker is refused by the byte model's discipline and its crash images
proofs.statement: Over the history model of books/store-history-required.lisp (the host-called decisions fn-hmr-open-verdict and fn-hmr-catch-up, host/native/io.lisp fnn-check-history-marker and fnn-recover's catch-up; the marker written by fnn-mark-committed at host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-publish-prepared) and the byte programs of books/byte-store-marker-program.lisp (fnn-mark-committed's syscalls): fn-hmr-deferred-commit is the step in which a live process answers success for record COUNT while the marker still counts COUNT (the marker of commit n renamed under commit n+1's reservation, the brief's shared later barrier). fn-hmr-deferred-commit-leaves-the-invariant: from any state satisfying fn-hmr-invp with a live process, the step leaves a state that does not satisfy it (A = COUNT+1 > M = COUNT). fn-hmr-deferred-commit-admits-a-lost-answered-record: from the same state, K = COUNT is below the answered prefix and (fn-hmr-open-verdict profile marker K) is (:admitted :marked K): the negation of fn-hmr-open-refuses-below-every-answered-record's conclusion, so a lost newest record that a client holds a 240 for is admitted by the next open. fn-hmr-deferred-commit-is-not-caught-up: D31 case (2) does not cover it, the catch-up over the shortened history writes nothing. The byte candidates fn-bs-marker-unfenced-program (the stage's fsync folded into the record's staging barrier: a fence drains one inode, so the marker's stage is unfenced) and fn-bs-marker-in-place-program (one overwrite of committed-history.json and one fsync) are refused executably: the model's discipline D1 (fn-bs-links-only-fencedp) rejects the first and D2 (fn-bs-never-overwrites-authorityp) the second, and on the K5 fixture a crash image of each (a garbled unit of the pending write, fn-bs-tear-write) holds a marker that is neither the old nor the new one: the open of a store that lost nothing refuses it, :history-short-of-marker 23 or :marker-damaged, so fn-bs-marker-crash-after-barrier-is-new and fn-bs-marker-crash-open-stays-admitted are false of them. fn-bs-marker-program stays the served program; its cost is seven barriers per commit, measured in the record; the one sound sharing (the next reservation renamed under the marker's root barrier before the acknowledgement) is a file-kernel and K0 change, PKT-441.
proofs.progress_note: Retired 2026-09-27 (lane log-recovery-2, PKT-838; design section 9 row 3): the marker programs it compared (books/byte-store-marker-candidates.lisp, books/byte-store-marker-program.lisp, books/store-history-required.lisp) were deleted with the per-file layout; a format-9 store has no marker (M := D). Before: Lane publish-program (2026-09-26, dev 17ff24aa). Certified on persvati (ACL2 8.7 w25 acl2-literal, 2 jobs, 300 s): run-20260926T102908Z-0df7, manifest certify-20260926T102932Z-378295, the book passed and the test book failed on a wrong witness (one garble selector for an eleven-unit write: the fixture's unit is 4 octets); run-20260926T103449Z-fa4d, manifest certify-20260926T103516Z-444060, the repaired test book passed; no book over 10 s. Teeth: a reachable history (open, one acknowledged commit, the deferred commit) asserting every hypothesis and conclusion of the three theorems, beside the served step at the same point (invariant kept, the open refused); the live hypothesis removed (a state that is not live: the identity step, the invariant kept, K not below A, a marker behind the history caught up); the invariant removed as corrupted-state witnesses (a marker above the history: the deferred step lands on the invariant and the open at K refuses; a marker behind: caught up). The byte refutations are ground images on the K5 fixture (byte-store-k0-marker-tests' pair): admissible choices, the observation neither old nor new, the open's refusal by name, and the served program's image at the same cut for contrast. Not claimed: a general theorem over the unfenced program's crash images (the ground counterexample refutes the universal claims); any program of the served path changed; the sound sharing (PKT-441).

proofs.title: Pull liveness: a peer's 430 for a listed id is an answer of the class unavailable; the round goes on, the id holds the cursor for at most BOUND consecutive complete rounds and is dropped, logged, exactly at the bound; the counts are durable in FNPL
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/native/pull-service.lisp fnn-pull-round calls (fn-pull-session-step through fn-pull-session-step-pair, fn-pull-session-close, fn-pull-session-close-effects; books/peer-pull-session.lisp) and fnn-pull-journal-open / fnn-pull-journal-append call (fn-pull-journal-scan with its committed offset, fn-pull-records-replay, fn-pull-cursor-envelope; books/peer-pull.lisp). A peer's 430 to the round's ARTICLE for a listed id is an answer of the class unavailable: the round records the id, reopens the local transit connection (:reopen-local) and goes on with the remaining ids. fn-pull-session-step-marks-unavailable-only-on-the-peers-reply: a host step that changes the unavailable ids is a (:remote . octets) event after the preamble, in phase :article, and adds exactly the article in hand. fn-pull-session-close-advances-only-past-a-fully-answered-round (PRF-100's keystone restated; its conclusion strengthened per id, not weakened): if the host's close moves the advance count, the round is :done, every listed id drew 235/435/437 from the local node OR was answered 430 by the peer in this round with its consecutive count reaching the bound, the new instant is the peer's DATE less the overlap, and PENDING is nil; fn-pull-close-advances-past-all-answered-when-nothing-is-unavailable keeps PRF-100's conclusion verbatim for a round with nothing unavailable, and the old form is a must-fail witness in tests/acl2/peer-pull-tests.lisp. fn-pull-session-unavailable-id-is-retried-below-the-bound: an id unavailable with 1 + its count below the bound leaves the instant and advance count where they were (so the peer lists it again: RFC 3977 7.4, not proved) and a complete round journals its count as exactly one more; fn-pull-session-complete-round-past-the-bound-advances: a complete round in which every unavailable id reached the bound advances and clears PENDING, the log naming each id whose count reached the bound in that round (dropped exactly at the bound, never before). fn-pull-records-replay-is-the-replay: the records the open scans back from a journal of cursor appends (one :pull-unavailable frame per PENDING entry, then the committing :pull-cursor frame) fold to exactly fn-pull-replay's cursor, so fn-pull-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut (PRF-100, cited, its statement over the four-field cursor) holds of the on-disk journal; fn-pull-records-replay-ignores-an-uncommitted-tail: unavailable records whose cursor record never became durable change nothing (and the scan truncates them). BOUND is the peer row pull-unavailable-rounds (`peer pull NAME SECONDS ROUNDS`), else the local policy *fn-pull-default-unavailable-rounds* = 5: a work bound on re-listing, not a data cap. Trusted, not proved: that the peer lists again what it listed for the same instant (RFC 3977 7.4).

The host's honest I/O remains the trust boundary these theorems sit inside, not a hypothesis of them.

proofs.title: The two-node consumer exchange: the receiving node's stored event keeps the carrier's authored source and both signatures, and the served poll report is the event's exact encoding or a named :oversize refusal
proofs.statement: (a) The subject is fn-pa-authorized-event, which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit's :ok arm calls through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-peer-carried-event for NNTP and BP transit and served POSTs. fn-osp-authorized-event-keeps-the-carried-source-and-signatures (books/owner-signed-post): whenever it forms an event, fn-pa-carrier-form of the received octets is :ok; the event's authored source is exactly the carrier's source (nth 1); its article record is exactly fn-record-encode of the record over the received octets (so the stored projection holds the carrier); and fn-hsig-authorize-at holds of the carrier's source version, principal, keys, source and signatures (nth 4) with the host's primitive observations: the two signatures the verdict authorized are the carrier's. The hop-local Path may differ between nodes; the source and signatures may not. (c) The subject is fn-col-poll-report (books/consumer-owner-local), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll serves. fn-col-poll-report-fits-or-refuses-by-name (books/consumer-owner-local-progress): a non-page or empty page is fn-col-poll's answer unchanged; a page whose encoded report satisfies fn-ncl-poll-event-bytesp is (:poll cursor report) with the event's exact encoding (fn-col-poll-report-octets: fn-stxa-encode, or fn-rcon-record-encode-impl for a legacy record); a page whose report is octets longer than *fn-stxa-max-octets* is (:refused :oversize). fn-col-poll-report-is-a-page-or-a-refusal: never a write, so an oversize article leaves the position unchanged. (b) PKT-256's CORRUPTED-state witness for fn-cp-ack-writes-only-a-forward-declaration-in-scope's frontier premise and (d) PKT-262's witness (a consumer registered after an article polls it first: intended) are teeth in tests/acl2/consumer-owner-local-progress-tests. Not claimed: that the :oversize antecedent is witnessed concretely (it needs a report above 4,294,966,940 octets, reachable only for a profile whose record bound R exceeds *fn-stxa-max-octets*; PKT-467); an explicit skip past an oversize article (PKT-466); anything about the Python consumer (an external client whose lock, resend and correlation are its own bookkeeping under CNS-003); BP carriage (PKT-333 phase 2).

proofs.title: A login's signing binding is a row of the configuration the owner publishes live: at start and on `principal bind|unbind' the configuration binds every login as the credential file does, an open session is decided under the table its connection pinned, a connection opened after the publication under the published table, and the verb says `applied' only after the owner published
proofs.statement: Subject fn-lb-ocfg-gate (books/login-binding-live.lisp), called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-login-gate from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-served; fn-lb-sync-plan, called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-login-bindings-plan from host/native/auth.lisp fnn-native-auth-publish-bindings (at start in fnn-native-auth-install and on control request 14 in host/native/login-bindings.lisp), whose delta lists are staged by fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas and published by fn-owner-reconfigure-complete (fn-ocl-publish) through fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked. (1) By definition (fn-lb-ocfg-gate-unfolds, not cited) the host's verdict is fn-lb-owner-gate (PRF of books/login-binding.lisp; its keystones apply) with the policy of the live configuration and the binding table of the in-flight submission's connection pin. (2) The delta (books/config.lisp :login-binding, code 17, rows (LOGIN PRINCIPAL-HEX "" 2) of the accounts slot): fn-lb-binding-delta-binds-the-login binds exactly the given principal (nil unbinds), fn-lb-binding-delta-keeps-other-logins leaves every other login, fn-lb-binding-delta-is-admitted is admitted against every configuration for a bindable login and a 32-octet principal. (3) fn-lb-sync-binds-file-logins-as-the-file-does-and-keeps-account-bindings: when the plan is :ok, applying its deltas binds every login as the credential file's table does, except a redeemed account the file does not name, whose binding stays as the configuration holds it (PRF-388); fn-lb-pairs-deltas-set-exactly-their-logins is the fold; fn-lb-pairs-deltas-ignore-the-record-coordinates lets the host's records of at most 64 deltas compose. (4) fn-lb-a-publication-keeps-every-open-connections-table (no hypotheses): staging and publishing any change leaves every connection's pinned table; fn-lb-an-open-session-is-decided-under-its-pinned-table: over any owner trace that does not re-pin the connection, the gate decides its submission under the table pinned before the trace. (5) fn-lb-a-connection-opened-after-a-publication-is-bound-anew: with nothing staged, a durable publication of the binding deltas (the owner's history relation before, fn-ocl-config-historyp; no stale pin at the fresh identifier after, which fn-ocfg-statep implies) and a connection opened next, that connection's table binds every login the deltas name as the file does and every other as before. (6) fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word-applied-only-when-published (fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word-restart-unless-no-owner, restated with the owner's answer, stays its PRF's): `applied' only when the lock was not seen free or absent and the owner answered :accepted. Teeth: tests/acl2/login-binding-live-tests.lisp (a witness per keystone asserting every antecedent; one must-fail per hypothesis; the gate witness is login-binding-tests' constructed owner, the publication witness config-owner-live-tests' replayed ground owner) and tests/acl2/native-auth-admin-tests.lisp. Not covered: that the owner's live configuration is its history's replay across every publication (the maintained relation; PRF-028 (certified again at the current digest since c7072ddc: served-path-scale's manifest certify-20260926T123813Z-1816946 covers its thirteen theorems); the host's reading of the credential file (bounded transport, as before).

proofs.title: A relay serves every admitted BP neighbour at once: bp-node serve binds one listener per transport-bp boundary row that admits a session and a session on a bound listener is admitted under exactly that row; held transit is dispatched to the neighbour the route table names for its own destination and one pass offers a held row on at most one session
proofs.statement: Over the functions the host calls. LISTENERS (host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-command-bp-node binds fn-bpaj-listener-ports through host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-bp-listener-ports, then fnn-accept-any-loop; each session's admission is fn-bpaj-session-principal inside fn-bpaj-tcpcl-ingress-result, host fn-owner-bp-tcpcl-ingress): fn-bpaj-listener-session-is-admitted-under-its-row: for PORT in (fn-bpaj-listener-ports CFG) and an EID ANNOUNCED, the session principal on (:tcp4 127.0.0.1 PORT 127.0.0.1) is (:admitted NAME GEN) for the listener's boundary NAME when ANNOUNCED is NAME's unique transport-bp EID, else (:refused :eid-mismatch): never :ambiguous-peer or :no-trust-profile. fn-bpaj-admitted-session-arrives-on-a-bound-listener: an admitted session on a positive port arrived on a port in the set. fn-bpaj-listener-ports-are-distinct. DISPATCH (fnn-bpnode-dispatch-one's :progress event with fn-bpnp-host-routes = (:table TABLE), through fn-bpnj-step to fn-bpnp-step and fn-bpnp-progress-step): fn-bpnp-progress-dispatch-names-the-routed-hop: when the step proposes :persist-dispatch, the record applies (:ready), its peer (written into the row's next-hop slot 11 by fn-bpnp-dispatched-held) is an EID, and its text is the EID of the route fn-bprt-outbound-choice selects for the named row's own destination (a :hop; the route is a live matching one by the carried fn-bprt-next-hop-names-a-live-matching-route); fn-bpnp-table-route-peer-is-the-routed-hop. FORWARDING (fnn-bpnode-forward-contact opens one fnn-bpnode-forward-session per entry of fn-bpnp-forward-plan; the routed :session event's fn-bpnp-routed-start runs fn-bpnp-forward-scan): fn-bpnp-forward-plan-has-one-session-per-peer; fn-bpnp-forward-plan-offers-a-row-on-one-session: two plan entries whose sessions' scans select the same held row are the same entry. The single-peer routes form is the one-row instance for a node with no route rows (fn-bpnp-host-routes).
proofs.progress_note: A-HOST dropped from this row's assumptions (lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G3-9, 2026-09-27): no theorem of the row takes fn-assume-host-report or fn-assume-host-events (books/assumptions.lisp) as a hypothesis, so the citation was decorative (AGENTS.md: the theorems that use a named assumption mention it). proofs.title: The open's freshness and archive-binding checks, the admission's identity test and the refresh's group index run in one pass, each equal to its unchanged logical definition
proofs.statement: Four linear executions of whole-state checks, each equal to the unchanged :logic definition. fn-articles-freshp-is-one-pass (books/acceptance.lisp, no hypothesis): (fn-fr-freshp articles) = (fn-articles-freshp articles); fn-fr-freshp folds the articles once with a hash set of the memberships seen, checking each article against the earlier ones (disjointness is symmetric: fn-fr-disjointp-commutes), and is the :exec branch of fn-articles-freshp. fn-node-articles-have-archive-bindingsp-is-indexed (books/node.lisp, no hypothesis): (fn-nab-articles-boundp a b p) = (fn-node-articles-have-archive-bindingsp a b p); the bindings and pins are indexed once in two hash tables, the first element with a key kept (the linear searches' answer), and it is the :exec branch. Both run inside fn-statep and fn-node-statep, which the host reaches at every Store open through fn-sco-store-open's fn-sco-finalize-from test (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-extended; fn-sn-open-observed's tests are carried), at every reader open through fn-nntp-projectionp and fn-own-reader-context's fn-peer-open-session (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open -> fn-ocfg-open -> fn-own-open), and at each BP acceptance check (fn-bpi-node-record-committedp). fn-retain-known-id-scanp-is-known-idp (books/retention.lisp, no hypothesis, iff): fn-retain-admissiblep's :exec walks the pins and releases for the identity instead of consing their identity lists; reached from fn-node-prepare on every POST and every replayed acceptance. fn-gidx-refresh-is-build (books/owner.lisp; hypothesis: the old index is (fn-gidx-build old-articles) or NIL, which fn-own-view-okp carries): (fn-gidx-refresh buckets old new) = (fn-gidx-build new); fn-own-refresh installs it, so a refresh after one acceptance puts the new article's entries into the old index instead of rebuilding it; fn-own-refresh-preserves-relation (books/owner-invariants.lisp) holds unchanged. The executed functions reach none of fn-all-article-memberships, fn-memberships-conflictsp, fn-pair-memberp, fn-node-find-binding, fn-retain-find-id, fn-retain-obligation-ids or member-equal (asserted over the callee closure in the test book).
proofs.progress_note: Lane served-path-scale (2026-09-26). Teeth in tests/acl2/open-one-pass-tests.lisp: a reachable twelve-article node (fn-node-prepare/fn-node-complete) on which each executed check and its quadratic reference agree; CORRUPTED states (a membership shared eleven and six articles apart, a released pin, a dropped binding, a wrong-subject binding or pin placed before and after the good one) on which both refuse or both accept; the group-index keystone's reachable extension witness, a stale-index counterexample and a must-fail without its hypothesis; the admission's known and fresh identities.

proofs.title: A friend whose keys succeeded since genesis is peered under its current keys: a peering document binds a principal this node's keyring holds only by its current enrolment (the genesis identity otherwise), and the confirm of a current acceptor completes at its consumption; `peer list' shows the carriage budget an older reader still parses past; the transit log names the admission verdict beside the class; `account list' names a binding row
proofs.statement: Subject fn-pinv-document (books/peer-invite.lisp) under the owner's keyring (fn-owner-hybrid-snapshots), reached through fn-pinv-issue-plan, fn-pinv-accept-record-plan / fn-pinv-accept-step and fn-pinv-confirm-record-plan / fn-pinv-confirm-step, which host/peer-invite-host.lisp wraps for host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-issue, fnn-pinv-owner-accept, fnn-pinv-owner-confirm and fnn-pinv-owner-enrol-confirmed. (1) fn-pinv-document-binds-a-known-principal-only-at-its-current-keys: when the keyring has a generation for P (fn-hl-current-for-principal), a document that passes is signed by exactly P's current enrolment (a superseded key set is refused `not-current-keys`, a revoked P `revoked`). (2) fn-pinv-document-of-a-current-enrolment-is-accepted: every other check passing and P's current enrolment the carrier's key set, the document is (:ok SOURCE P K) with no genesis condition; a never-succeeded principal enrolled at its genesis keys is the instance. (3) fn-pinv-document-of-an-unknown-principal-is-the-genesis-decision: a principal with no generation is decided exactly as under the empty keyring (the genesis identity, `genesis`). (4) fn-pinv-an-enrolling-accept-is-the-clis-plan: whenever the owner's accept step enrols, the accept plan under the empty keyring (the accepting CLI's fn-pinv-acceptance-source) is the owner's. (5) fn-pinv-confirm-step-current-only-for-the-consuming-current-acceptor and fn-pinv-confirm-of-a-current-acceptor-completes-at-its-consumption: the confirm step answers (:current), enrolling nothing, only for a bound acceptance whose row this acceptance consumed and whose principal is current at its keys, and does so right after that consumption. (6) books/native-admin-peer-budget.lisp, the report fn-native-admin-query-report (host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-native-admin-host-query-report, `peer list`) and fn-nls-report (:peers) serve: fn-native-admin-peer-budget-decode-reads-the-configured-budget, fn-native-admin-peer-extra-decode-reads-past-the-budget (over clean rows the older reader reads the same values and leaves the budget words), fn-native-admin-peer-budget-row-octets-extends-the-older-line. (7) fn-pcb-transit-refusal-detail-is-the-class-and-the-verdict (no hypotheses; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-refusal-class from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-transit-class) with books/owner-log.lisp fn-olog-detail-fields (by definition, not cited): the transit log's `detail=CLASS verdict=VERDICT`. (8) fn-acct-list-word-is-pending-only-for-a-pending-row (books/account-list.lisp, served by books/native-live-status.lisp for `account list`). Not claimed: that the keyring's succession is honest (a key statement's admission, PRF-098); an invitation from a succession-era inviter unknown to the invitee (it is refused `genesis`: no succession chain travels with the document); the POST reply naming a refused key change (PKT-473).

proofs.title: A control reply that cannot carry its value refuses by name: profile validation refuses a record bound the consumer poll reply cannot carry, and the live-status reply names a report its u32 total cannot say
proofs.statement: (a) PKT-467, the coordinator's ruling (D27: profile validation, representation and format evolution agree). The subject is fn-bs-profile-validp / fn-bs-profile-admittedp (books/byte-store-frame), which host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-upgrade-profile reaches through fn-hmr-upgrade-verdict / fn-profile-upgrade-verdict and `init` through host/store-host.lisp fn-store-profile-init-verdict (fn-bs-profile-init-verdict); every open through fn-store-profile-admittedp. fn-bs-profile-invalid-reason answers :max-record-octets-above-the-poll-reply when R exceeds *fn-stxa-max-octets* (4,294,966,940: the Store frame's u32 less the kind-6 poll reply's 9 header and 346 cursor octets, the inequality fn-ncl-poll-event-bytesp checks). fn-bs-profile-valid-record-fits-a-poll-reply: for any value, fn-bs-profile-max-record-octets is at most *fn-stxa-max-octets*, and every payload fn-bs-publication-admissiblep admits (the gate host/store-host.lisp fn-store-publication-admissibility asserts for host/native/io.lisp fnn-publish) is within it. fn-col-poll-report-of-an-admitted-payload-fits (books/consumer-owner-local-progress): a page whose event encoding is such an admitted payload is served by fn-col-poll-report (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll) as that page, not :oversize. fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-stays-valid (books/byte-store-profile-v1) now carries R <= *fn-stxa-max-octets*, and fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-above-the-poll-reply-is-refused-by-name says the window it excludes is refused by the new name: together they characterize which saved profiles still open. (b) The subject is fn-nls-page over fn-nls-buffer (books/native-live-status), which host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-status-host-answer answers for host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status-answer, and fn-nls-client-step, which host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status folds pages through. fn-nls-page-refuses-exactly-past-the-total-width: for an octet report and any offset, the client's step on the owner's page is (:refused :report-past-the-total-width) exactly when the report is longer than 2^32-1 octets; the refused reply's existing chunk field carries the word (no layout change). Not claimed: that the served store's events re-encode to at most R (the :oversize arm stays as the named refusal for a store holding an event past its own R; PKT-470); that a live-status report is bounded before it is rendered (the render is whole, octet lists: PKT-470, hot-path-checker's class); a concrete witness of either past-the-ceiling antecedent (each needs 2^32 octets; the hypothesis teeth are proved symbolically). (c) [retired by format 10: the saved-profile window refusal and the repair are gone with format 9; every format-10 profile satisfies the arm at its writing] PKT-471, the coordinator's decision (a named refusal at open, never translation-at-open). The subject is fn-spo-config-open (books/store-profile-open), the open host/native/io.lisp fnn-metadata-config-decode calls through host/store-host.lisp fn-store-metadata-config-open on every open (fnn-load-config from fnn-acquire: owner start, store recover, inspect, checkpoint, status, the offline health). fn-spo-open-of-a-saved-format-8-profile-opens-or-refuses-by-name: for every profile the format-8 encoder saved under the relation before PKT-467 (fn-bs-profile-v2-validp, frozen; fn-bs-profile-valid-is-v2-valid and fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-is-v2-valid include the current and the pre-P6 saved profiles), the open of its frame (fn-spo-saved-frame) is (:opened VALUES) when R <= *fn-stxa-max-octets* and (:refused :max-record-octets-above-the-poll-reply) otherwise, never (:rejected), the host's fault; the host prints ACL2's line (fn-spo-refusal-text) at exit 1. fn-spo-config-open-refuses-only-what-the-old-open-rejected: a refusal is never a frame fn-bs-config-decode decoded, so every store the open opened before opens the same. The repair is a separate verdict, fn-spo-repair-verdict, which fnn-command-upgrade-profile reaches through fnn-command-repair-profile on that refusal (fn-profile-upgradep is unchanged, so every fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-* theorem is unaffected): fn-spo-repair-admits-exactly-the-lowering-to-the-width: over any saved profile's frame the verdict writes exactly when the saved R exceeds *fn-stxa-max-octets* and the target is (:current ((4 . *fn-stxa-max-octets*))), what `store upgrade-profile --max-record-octets 4294966940` parses to, and the written frame opens as the saved profile with R lowered and every other field kept (fn-spo-repaired-keeps-every-other-field). Not claimed (PKT-486): that the repair's open under the lowered profile names a store holding a committed record above the lowered read bound (it would fault on the read bound; no such record is constructible below 4 GiB); a native crash witness of the repair path (it writes through the upgrade's byte program, fn-bs-profile-program-crash-is-old-or-new).

proofs.title: A peer's configuration rows and the checkpoint generations are data bounded by the profile or by their records: 1,024 rows is a work bound per delta, and the generation allocator refuses exactly at the profile's capacity
proofs.statement: Rows: an :add-peer-rows delta for an existing peer with keyed rows is refused by fn-cfg-delta-reason exactly when it carries more than *fn-cfg-max-rows* rows (fn-cfg-add-peer-rows-refuses-exactly-past-the-work-bound); applied, the group is the old group less the repeated rows followed by the new ones, with no bound on its length (fn-cfg-add-peer-rows-extends-the-group); any well-formed delta adds at most *fn-cfg-max-rows* rows to the peers slot and a delta list at most that times its length (fn-cfg-apply-delta-adds-at-most-the-work-bound, fn-cfg-apply-adds-at-most-the-work-bound); the deltas the host publishes for `peer carries` / `peer budget` (fn-pcb-extend-deltas, through fn-native-admin-plan-deltas-over from host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-native-admin-host-apply and fn-native-admin-host-owner-reconfigure) apply as the whole-group :set-peer extension (fn-pcb-extend-deltas-apply-as-the-extend-delta), so PRF-099's budget keystone carries. Generations: on a gap-free checkpoint namespace fn-cpp-next-generation is :exhausted exactly when CAPACITY names are retained and is the count otherwise, for CAPACITY within the uint32 width (fn-cpp-next-generation-refuses-exactly-at-the-profile-capacity); CAPACITY is max-transactions + 1 of the opened profile (host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-checkpoint-generation-capacity). RETIRED HOST ARM (lane matrix-reds, 2026-09-27): the native callers are gone (fnn-pack-publish-generation with the pack chain, PKT-838; fnn-checkpoint-publish with the generation checkpoints, whose capture could not represent the flipped node); the generation clauses are properties of the logical model only, and no native test exercises them (tests/test_native_checkpoint_generations.py deleted). Group names: the authorization the host calls for every configuration record (fn-cvec-native-admin-authorize, from host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-cfg-native-admin-authorize, host/native/admin.lisp fnn-admin-authorize, offline and in the live owner's arm) refuses :max-group-name-octets exactly when the record creates a group whose name is longer than the profile's field 7 and is otherwise the publication authorization it replaced (fn-cvec-native-admin-authorize-refuses-exactly-past-the-group-name-bound); an accepted record creates no longer name (fn-cvec-accepted-group-names-are-within-the-profile); an accepted init plan names no group longer than the field 7 of the profile it writes (fn-nop-init-plain-groups-are-within-the-profile, books/native-operator.lisp fn-nop-parse-init-plain). EXTENSION (lane friend-blockers, 2026-09-27, the stranger rehearsal's stops): PKT-708 (decided by the coordinator): KEYSTONE fn-nop-mission-init-serves-control-cancel: an accepted init under a mission serves control.cancel (fn-nop-with-cancel-group), so a reader's own cancel is filed with no group create; a plain init serves exactly its named groups.

proofs.title: `control log` and `control evidence MESSAGE-ID` print what the owner decided about withdrawing articles: the evidence's decision for a stored article is a record of the log exactly when it is a withdrawal record, in the log's own words
proofs.statement: books/control-evidence.lisp fn-cev-evidence-decision-is-in-the-log: for every RAW, VERDICTS, RECORDS, CONFIGS and MSGID, with WS equal to (fn-ctl-articles-withdrawals RAW VERDICTS RECORDS CONFIGS) (the owner's maintained relation: the carried records are the journal of the carried archive, established by fn-own-start's refresh and preserved by fn-own-refresh through fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals-is-the-journal and fn-ctl-articles-withdrawals-is-the-journal; the offline report establishes it by construction), the decision fn-cev-plan of the article fn-cev-find-article names is a member of WS iff it is a withdrawal record (fn-ctl-withdrawalp). fn-cev-decision-line-is-a-log-line: then the decision's words (fn-cev-decision-line) are "decision=" followed by the log's line for that record (fn-cev-log-line), a member of fn-cev-log-lines WS. proofs.title: A POST reads the committed count, record octets, completion debt and carriage usage without walking the history: the count is the Store's derived event index's, the three caches advance through that index, and each equals its fold under the maintained index relation
proofs.statement: Subjects, each called by host/owner-host.lisp: fn-sbud-count (books/store-budget.lisp) from fn-owner-publication-verdict, fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer (the budget fn-cvec-article-budget-for is handed), fn-owner-record-octets, fn-owner-record-debt, fn-owner-carried-usage and fn-owner-install-profile; fn-sbud-bytes-carried from fn-owner-record-octets (reached from the verdict, both prepares and fn-owner-headroom); fn-sbud-headroom-carried from fn-owner-headroom; fn-scf-debt-carried (books/store-carried-folds.lisp) from fn-owner-record-debt; fn-scf-usage-carried from fn-owner-carried-usage (fn-owner-peer-carried-relay-event). The index now counts its puts (books/consumer-event-index.lisp, index = (SEQ-TRIE MSGID-TRIE . proofs.title: The executed BP CRC-32C and exclusive-or are the bitwise definitions: fn-bpp-crc32c-scan runs a table-driven scan and fn-bpp-xor runs logxor under a mask, each proved equal to the bitwise body every codec theorem reasons about
proofs.statement: books/bp-primary.lisp. fn-bpp-xor-is-masked-logxor (hypotheses (natp a), (natp b)): (fn-bpp-xor a b k) = (logand (logxor a b) (+ -1 (expt 2 k))), the :exec body of fn-bpp-xor's mbe, for every k (a k that is not a natural gives 0 on both sides). fn-bpp-crc32c-scan-table-is-scan (hypotheses (natp crc), (fn-cbor-octet-listp xs)): (fn-bpp-crc32c-scan-table crc xs) = (fn-bpp-crc32c-scan crc xs), where fn-bpp-crc32c-scan-table, the :exec body of fn-bpp-crc32c-scan's mbe, advances the register an octet at a time by one lookup in *fn-bpp-crc32c-table* and a shift, and the logical body advances it eight bitwise register steps (fn-bpp-crc32c-octet). The table is a defconst evaluated from fn-bpp-crc32c-octet at every octet value, and fn-bpp-crc32c-table-agrees checks all 256 entries by evaluation inside the proof. Both keystones are used by the guard proofs of the mbe functions (verify-guards fn-bpp-xor, verify-guards fn-bpp-crc32c-scan), so the executed bodies are what the guard-verified host path runs. Host lines: host/bp-node-host.lisp calls fn-bpn-send (the authoring path: fn-bpb-encode, fn-bpb-block-crc, fn-bpp-crc-octets, fn-bpp-crc32c) and fn-bpb-decode (fn-bpn-host-authored-retry; the decoder's CRC check computes the same fn-bpp-crc-octets). The logical bodies of fn-bpp-xor, fn-bpp-crc32c-scan and fn-bpp-crc32c are unchanged, so every existing codec theorem (PRF-038's round trip, bp-primary-invariants' CRC width and octet facts) holds unchanged; none is restated. CRC-16 (type 1) keeps the bitwise scan over the executed exclusive-or. Scope: a CRC is a checksum, not a digest; nothing here is a claim about integrity against an adversary.

proofs.statement: fn-cat (books/catalog.lisp) is an attachable abstract stobj whose logical value is the list of held records (books/catalog-record.lisp: the wire tuple's eleven positions with the payload a natp handle into fn-arena, the byte facts, the context, the numbers and the withdrawal), oldest first, and whose executable is the indexed tables (rows by sequence, a Message-ID hash table, a (group . number) hash table, a group table of row count and next number, the octets total). fn-cat$corr states once that the count is the length, the rows below it are the list, every bound Message-ID looks up to its ascending sequences and every row's Message-ID is bound, every bound (group . number) names the first row binding it and every row's numbers are bound, every bound group maps to its row count and one past its high and every row's groups are bound, and the octets cell is the sum. The creator establishes it (create-fn-cat{correspondence}) and every export preserves it (fn-cat-commit{correspondence}: the numbers assigned one past each group's high, every table advanced without a walk; fn-cat-withdraw{correspondence} and fn-cat-redecide{correspondence}: a same-key row replacement keeps every table; fn-cat-clear{correspondence}), as defabsstobj-missing-events prints the obligations. fn-cat-intern-list-materializes: the held record the intern builds from a wire record W, materialized by handle from the arena the intern sealed, is W (alpha of intern is the identity; fn-cat-intern-is-intern-list equates the buffer intern, hypothesis-free). fn-hf-body-lines-of-is-nov-body-line-count-by-definition: the body line count column is fn-nov-body-line-count's value over fn-nntp-split-article and fn-nntp-crlf-lines. proofs.title: The committed delta equals the refresh: the view's incremental application of the one article a completion installs is fn-own-refresh's view on every projection (fn-view-apply-is-refresh); on the catalog, a commit leaves every pinned version unchanged and puts the row's article on top of the new version, and a withdrawal at version W leaves every version at or below W and removes the target from every later one
proofs.statement: The pinned view is a VERSION that a successful GROUP or LISTGROUP advances to the owner's committed view and that no other command moves (NNT-042, specs/nntp.md; gpt-6's wave-5 review section 1). PROVED over the machine the host calls (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span -> books/served-span.lisp fn-scar-ocfg-read-span -> fn-scar-dispatch = fn-served-dispatch, fn-scar-dispatch-is-served-dispatch): (1) fn-served-step-pin-is-old-or-live: after any read a served connection's pin (archive, verdicts, Message-ID trie, group buckets, control pin, pin identity) is either what it was or the live view's (fn-served-live-pin of fn-served-conn-live), and the live view is untouched, for every connection and every octet list; (2) fn-served-successful-selection-is-the-repinned-dispatch: on a GROUP/LISTGROUP line whose reply is 211 (fn-served-selectedp) the dispatch IS fn-served-dispatch-core over fn-served-repin of the connection (the fresh view with the command's own selection effects); (3) fn-served-failed-selection-keeps-the-connection: when the reply is not 211 the result connection is the input connection with only its wire framing state replaced (previous view and cursor unchanged); (4) fn-served-repin-preserves-connp: the re-pinned connection is a connection (its re-selected reader session is consistent with the live archive: fn-served-reselect keeps the group when the live view has it and sets GROUP's own cursor); (5) fn-own-read-preserves-relation / fn-own-read-step-preserves-relation restated with the two cases (the read-back fn-own-finish-read takes the pin from the served connection; the view case is fn-own-conn-okp-of-view-pin, the :advance argument); proofs.title: Completion by token and the shared transition: fn-cat-complete commits the pending PreparedCommit's row at its expected position with no history search and refuses a stale token or a mismatched expected by name; fn-sn-finish-held over the held record and its context is fn-sn-finish on the article arm; the keyring generation names the keyring; the pinned view is a version
proofs.statement: books/catalog-commit.lisp. fn-cat-complete-by-token: for a PreparedCommit PENDING (fn-pc-p), TOKEN its token and its EXPECTED the catalog count, (fn-cat-complete token pending fn-cat) commits the row (fn-cat-at expected C') = (fn-cat-assign held C), the count is expected + 1, the pending is cleared and the result is the :article delta of that row (fn-delta-of-row); fn-cat-complete-stale-refused and fn-cat-complete-expected-mismatch-refused: a token that is not the pending's, or an expected that is not the count, is refused by name and nothing changes; fn-cat-abandon-clears, fn-cat-abandon-stale-refused; fn-cat-token-of-abandoned-attempt-is-stale: a token from an abandoned attempt cannot complete the next attempt when the txids differ (the txid is consumed per attempt; the test book shows equal txids let it through). fn-sn-finish-held-is-finish (KEYSTONE, the shared transition): for a store S (fn-sn-statep), W its completing record (fn-sn-completion-record, kept as the meaning), W an article record, H a held record with (fn-held-wire h bytes(W)) = W (alpha), bytes(W) the node's pending bytes, and CTX the context of bytes(W) under S's keyring and generation, (fn-sn-finish-held s h ctx) = (fn-sn-finish s): the finish with the record supplied and the verdict and identity delta from the context, no walk of the history, no read of the bytes. fn-sn-finish-held-refuses-a-stale-context: a context whose generation is not the store's leaves the store unchanged. fn-sn-context-fixed-between-prepare-and-finish: every transition the owner and the host apply (fn-snrt-step and its arms, fn-sn-io, fn-sn-finish, fn-sn-finish-held, fn-sn-with-configuration) leaves the keyring and its generation, and fn-sn-set-keyring leaves the keyring whenever it leaves the generation; fn-sn-set-keyring-advances-the-generation is the writer's negative (unreachable-in-composition: no native host line calls it). books/catalog-delta.lisp: fn-cat-apply-delta-step-bounded (a step touches at most its quantum of rows); the delta grammar, its one-shot application and its resumable form are defined and guard-verified, and that the resumable run under any quanta equals the one-shot application is OPEN (not proved in this lane's budget; the ground check in the test book passes by computation and is not a proof); fn-view-cancel-after-target: a cancel of a row committed when the count is W withdraws it at W, a reader at version V with target < V <= W still sees it, a reader at W + 1 does not. The composite (kind 4), retention, consumer and topic arms keep fn-sn-finish over the event; the equation with fn-own-refresh's view is PRF-202.

KEYSTONE fn-auth-step-pinned-answers-500-to-a-keyword-help-does-not-list: for every AS, LINE, ARCHIVE, INDEX, VERDICTS, CONFIG, OBSERVATION and INJECTION, if (fn-auth-sessionp AS), AS is not handshaking TLS, its peer session awaits no transit article, its POST session awaits no body, its reader session is open (openp = t), (fn-nntp-command-inputp LINE), the first token of LINE is a keyword token, the arguments are within RFC 3977 section 3.1's bound, and (not (fn-nntp-served-keywordp keyword)), then (fn-auth-step-pinned AS ... (list :command LINE)) has effects (fn-auth-single AS "500 command not recognized"), no submission, and session AS. fn-auth-step-pinned is the dispatcher books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch calls for every framed command line (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-serve-client -> fn-own-read -> fn-served-step -> fn-served-feed -> fn-served-dispatch). fn-nntp-served-keywordp is membership (RFC 3977 section 3.1 case-insensitively, fn-nntp-keywordp) in *fn-nntp-served-command-table*, 28 keywords in six rows; fn-nntp-served-keywordp-unfolds writes it out as the disjunction the dispatchers test. fn-nntp-help-renders-the-served-command-table-by-definition: (fn-nntp-help SESSION) = (fn-nntp-multi SESSION "100 help text follows" (fn-nntp-help-table-lines *fn-nntp-served-command-table*)).
