proofs.statement: Over the served step the host runs (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk -> fn-served-step), a framed LIST NEWSGROUPS [wildmat] line answers fn-nntp-list-newsgroups-described over the pinned archive's groups and the descriptions of the connection's posting configuration's listing (fn-served-step-list-newsgroups-is-the-described-listing), and LIST MOTD answers fn-nntp-list-motd over that listing's message (fn-served-step-list-motd-is-the-configured-message); a description is sent when it is non-empty printable ASCII and otherwise the (no description) marker, and with no listing the reply is the marker listing of before (fn-nntp-described-lines-of-no-descs). The listing of the posting configuration books/owner-agent.lisp fn-oag-post-config builds (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-post-config; installed by fn-ocl-publish after each published record) holds, for a group G, G's description in the configuration's eleventh slot exactly when G is served and has one (fn-oag-description-of-the-listing), and the node's message lines (fn-oag-motd-of-the-listing). Over fn-cfg-apply-delta (replay and live staging), the :set-group-description delta for NAME makes NAME's description its pieces concatenated (fn-cfg-description-after-set-is-its-pieces), leaves every other name's text (fn-cfg-description-after-set-of-another-name), makes the node's message (NAME "") its lines (fn-cfg-motd-after-set-is-its-lines), and no other kind touches the slot (fn-cfg-descriptions-of-other-kinds); fn-cfg-delta-reason refuses a name that is neither "" nor a live group (:no-such-group, by definition) and admits only the delta's own printable rows (fn-cfg-admitted-description-rows-are-printable). The reader listing is not an input of the injection decision (fn-inj-decide-ignores-the-listing).

proofs.title: The process heap is the store profile's figure: an accepted figure holds every store the profile admits and fits the observed machine; a profile the machine cannot hold is refused by name
proofs.statement: RE-MEASURED (lane reservation-figure, 2026-09-27): the figure's terms are the runtime's today. STATE: fn-heap-arena-octets is the paged arena (arena-offheap stage 1): USED + one 256 KiB page + 32 octets a page, never 3 USED (a named parameter lane arena-offheap-3 replaces with its cache bound; the keystones use only fn-heap-arena-octets-monotone); 48 N of handles; 2 N (12,288 + 320 G): the measured live state a record less its payload after per-record-state (the log kernel holds a COUNT) and catalog-columns (8 to 10 KB a record posted or reopened, plus 1.3 KB for realistic Message-IDs), where 5,120 was below the measurement. OPEN: since log-open-stream (PRF-283) and rm2-format9 the open reads one log entry at a time and the full replay takes each record into a 1 MiB chunk (*fn-heap-open-chunk-octets* = *fn-srs-chunk-octets*): fn-heap-store-open-octets (profile ou on) = 2 x 16 x 2 x (chunk + R) + 2 OU (the checkpoint suffix's vectors) + 2 x 1,024 ON; the 64 OU of list copies and 16 KiB a record are gone (the scale preset's open 49,152 -> 2,655 MB). The explosion of `init --profile scale --max-transactions 1048576 --max-article-octets 4096' (reservation 41,961,201 MB) is the membership product 2 x T x 320 x G at G = 65,535 (the scale preset's, the codec ceiling): nothing but G bounds a store's memberships (the history budget charges an article its payload, books/store-budget-stored.lisp), so it is the admitted worst case, not a double count; at G = 16 the same profile's state is 35,633 MB (tests/acl2/heap-reservation-tests.lisp pins both). STATUS: books/heap-reservation.lisp fn-heap-status-decide, called by host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-print-store-line (`operator CONFIG status' and `health'), is the launcher's run reservation over the store on disk; KEYSTONE fn-heap-status-decide-is-the-launchers-run-reservation: (equal (fn-heap-status-decide profile core nursery observations observed) (fn-heap-reserve-operation-decide :run profile core nursery observations (fn-heap-reserve-run-connections bound) observed)) for every owner bound. Before, status printed connection-budget's launch figure (fnn-heap-decision, now removed): 39,519 MB where the launcher reserves 4,662 MB for the mission's top rung on 123 GiB. Figures (core 389 MB, 64 MiB nursery): small 1,924 -> 1,232 MB at its bounds, its first run 672 -> 997 MB (up: the measured record state); development 7,934 -> 7,506; scale 221,127 -> 173,021. Record: planning/evidence/reservation-figure-2026-09-27.md. RE-DERIVED (lane reservation-after-flip, 2026-09-27; supersedes the list figure below for every command): since the records flip the served state is the payload arena, so books/heap-store-figure.lisp models what a process holding a store of USED payload octets in N records needs, having opened an input of OU octets in ON records, at the collector's TRIGGER: fn-heap-store-need = DYN + 3 USED (the arena's byte array, doubling, old copy live during a resize) + 48 N (handles) + 2 N (5,120 + 320 G) (each record's retained small objects and group memberships, twice for the collector; measured 3.5-4.8 KiB and 0.25 KiB) + 2 x 16 x 2 OU + 2 x 16,384 ON (the full replay's transient: the recovery decodes the records as octet lists; measured about 54 B per octet and 34 KiB per record) + 2 x 16 x (R + 3 HDR) + 2 x fn-ock-capture-budget (the request in flight and both buffers) + 2 TRIGGER. DYN is the image's dynamic content: CORE is the image observation (FILE . DYNAMIC) (host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-image-observation), a natural CORE being the whole file as before. TRIGGER is fn-heap-nursery-trigger (d nursery) = max(8 MiB, min(cap, d/16)), which host/native/io.lisp fnn-gc-nursery-octets now calls; the figure fn-heap-store-figure-octets = fn-heap-with-nursery (the base, nursery), the least D of three candidates with D >= base + 2 trigger(D) (fn-heap-with-nursery-holds-the-trigger, for every D at least the figure). OBSERVED (the probe's (OCTETS . RECORDS) of the store's history files, transaction files counted; host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-history-observation) bounds the open's input (fn-heap-open-octets-bound, -records-bound; H and T when NIL); the state stays at H and T since a run grows the store. KEYSTONE fn-heap-store-figure-holds-every-store: (implies (and (natp d) (<= (fn-heap-store-figure-octets profile core nursery observed) d) (<= (nfix used) (nfix H)) (<= (nfix n) (nfix T)) (<= (nfix ou) (fn-heap-open-octets-bound profile observed)) (<= (nfix on) (fn-heap-open-records-bound profile observed))) (<= (fn-heap-store-need profile core used n ou on (fn-heap-nursery-trigger d nursery)) d)). fn-heap-figure-octets is the unobserved store figure; KEYSTONE fn-heap-decide-admits-every-store-the-profile-admits now concludes that store need (ou <= H, on <= T) within the decision's megabytes and those within the machine. fn-heap-operation-decide sizes EVERY command by the observation (:init by the empty store, fn-heap-operation-observation) and the offline verbs by the larger of their list copies and the store figure; KEYSTONE fn-heap-operation-decide-holds-the-store (every action; the member hypothesis removed after proving the weakened theorem). heap-reservation: the threads are 12 fixed + 2 I/O loops + 16 control clients whatever the connections (fn-heap-thread-count; host fnn-mux-thread-count calls it), the core outside the dynamic space is the core file (fn-heap-core-file); fn-heap-reserve-decide-holds-every-thread-the-node-runs drops (natp connections); init judges the first run of the empty store it makes (fn-heap-reserve-first-run-decide). The small preset: 1,662 MB at its bounds on the production image (1,736 on the image-floor core), 583 MB for the run of an empty store and 791 MB for the 1,000-post store (dev before: 824 MB for all); 925 and 1,133 MB in all with 30 threads (before 1,316). fn-heap-small-profile-run-fits-a-small-machine replaces -fits-a-small-machine (the nursery hypothesis removed after proving the weakened theorem). Record: planning/evidence/reservation-after-flip-2026-09-27.md. books/heap-figure.lisp. fn-heap-decide (profile core nursery observations) is the host-called subject: host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-decision calls it, from fnn-command-heap (the `heap -- ARGV` probe the installed packaging/fn runs before it execs the command with --dynamic-space-size MB) and fnn-heap-print-store-line (the line `operator CONFIG status` and `health` print). The figure fn-heap-figure-octets = CORE + NURSERY + 2 x 16 x (2H + R) + 2 x fn-ock-capture-budget(profile), in SBCL megabytes rounded up (fn-heap-mb-of); the machine is fn-heap-machine-octets, the least positive observation. KEYSTONE fn-heap-decide-admits-every-store-the-profile-admits: (implies (and (fn-bs-profile-admittedp profile) (equal (car d) :heap) (<= used (fn-bs-profile-max-history-octets profile)) (natp core) (natp nursery)) (and (<= (+ core nursery (* 32 (+ used used R)) (* 2 (fn-ock-capture-budget profile))) (* 2^20 (fn-heap-decision-mb d))) (<= (* 2^20 (fn-heap-decision-mb d)) (fn-heap-machine-octets observations)))) with d = (fn-heap-decide profile core nursery observations): for every history of USED octets within H (the store budget's bound, fn-sbud-verdict-at), the image, the nursery, the lists at sixteen bytes per octet with the collector's copy, and both checkpoint buffers fit the megabytes passed, which fit the machine. (natp used) was removed after proving the weakened theorem. fn-heap-decide-refuses-exactly-past-the-machine: for an admitted profile and an observed machine the decision is (:heap MB WORD MACHINE-MB) when MB x 2^20 <= machine and (:refused :machine-cannot-hold-profile MB MACHINE-MB) otherwise; fn-heap-decision-exit-code-of-a-refusal: a refusal exits 1 (outcome-class :refused). The small preset (*fn-heap-small-request*: the development base with T 16384, H 8 MiB, R 196608, G 16, K 128) is admitted and fn-heap-small-profile-fits-a-small-machine: with core <= 512 MiB and nursery <= 64 MiB it is accepted on every machine of at least 1536 MiB (OpenBSD's default datasize); (heap-figure's fn-heap-init-request and its two theorems are retired from this row, 2026-09-27: no host line calls it; init's choice is books/heap-reservation.lisp fn-heap-init-decide.) Scope: the 16 B per octet is the octet-list representation's cons (rep-wave-d section 1.2); the second history copy is the open's transient; the model states retained octets, not SBCL's allocator, and the native case measures VmHWM against it. EXTENSION (lane image-floor, HST-017): books/heap-reservation.lisp fn-heap-reserve-decide (profile core nursery observations connections), the subject host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-reservation calls from fnn-command-heap, is fn-heap-decide's decision and, when that accepts an admitted profile, the stack (fn-heap-stack-kib: the constant *fn-heap-stack-octets*, 1,024 KiB, since lane served-line-iterative made the served path's stack need independent of the article: least 142 KiB for 16 lines, 2,000,000 lines and one 4 MiB line; the per-line term 512 KiB + 40 x (floor(A/2) + 1024) is retired) and THREADS = connections + fn-native-control-max-active-clients + 12; the whole HEAP + CORE + THREADS x (STACK + 4 MiB) is refused by name (:machine-cannot-hold-threads) past the machine. KEYSTONE fn-heap-reserve-decide-holds-every-thread-the-node-runs: (implies (and (fn-bs-profile-admittedp profile) (equal (car r) :heap) (natp connections)) (and (equal (fn-heap-decision-mb r) (fn-heap-decision-mb (fn-heap-decide ...))) (<= (+ connections clients 12) threads) (<= *fn-heap-stack-octets* (* 1024 stack-kib)) (<= (+ (* 2^20 mb) (nfix core) (* threads (+ (* 1024 stack-kib) 4 MiB))) (fn-heap-machine-octets observations)))); fn-heap-reserve-decide-refuses-exactly-past-the-machine and -keeps-heap-figures-refusals. Scope: the stack constant rests on a measurement of compiled frames on SBCL 2.6.8 (served-line-iterative's record section 5; image-floor's section 4), pinned by tests/test_native_image_floor.py's stack witnesses, not a theorem about frames. INIT (PKT-582, in the shape of gpt-6's wave-5 review s.8): fn-heap-init-decide (request core nursery physical limits budget-octets sizing-octets), called by host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-init-decision (from operator.lisp fnn-operator-execute-init, which prints fn-heap-init-report-line, and from the heap probe through fnn-heap-init-request), sizes within an explicit budget: the least of the physical memory less the OS's reserve (a quarter, at least 512 MiB), each limit the process runs under (RLIMIT_DATA, RLIMIT_AS, every cgroup memory.max) and FN_INIT_BUDGET_MB. proofs.title: The reader port's connection capacity is the operator's exposure-connections row with no fixed ceiling under it, the port refuses exactly at the capacity with RFC 3977's named 400, and an address in the operator's trusted range is never refused on the per-address rule while one outside is refused exactly at its limit
proofs.statement: books/public-exposure.lisp over books/public-exposure-rows.lisp. The subject is fn-exp-open, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-exposure-open calls at every accept (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-serve-client) through fn-ocar-exp-open (equal to it under the configured owner's relation: fn-ocar-exp-open-is-exp-open-under-ocl-relation, books/owner-open-carried.lisp), over the limits fn-owner-exposure-limits reads with fn-exp-limits from the owner's LIVE configuration value and the owner's bound. A run's owner is installed with *fn-exp-owner-connection-bound* = one past the limit rows' width (books/native-operator.lisp fn-native-operator-result-run-max-connections, host/native/operator-live.lisp `run' through fnn-control-owner-run-normalized), so fn.toml's fixed 32 no longer bounds a run. fn-exp-owner-bound-exceeds-every-capacity: under fn-cfg-limits-withinp (carried by fn-cfg-valuep, preserved by every delta) the capacity fn-exp-connections-capacity (the exposure-connections row, 31 with none) is below that bound. fn-exp-limits-total-is-the-capacity: the total in force is the capacity whenever the owner's bound exceeds it. KEYSTONE fn-exp-open-refuses-exactly-at-the-capacity: under the run's bound, fn-cfg-limits-withinp and the failed-login rule not refusing the address (fn-exp-auth-refusesp), fn-exp-admit-decision is exactly (:refuse busy-400 1) when the owner holds the capacity or more, else (:refuse address-400 2) for an address outside the trusted range at its per-address limit, else :admit; fn-exp-open-refusal-is-a-400-and-opens-nothing (PRF-161) makes a refusal the named line (`400 too many connections; try again later', RFC 3977 section 5.1.1) with nothing opened. KEYSTONE fn-exp-trusted-address-is-never-refused-by-address: an address fn-exp-trusted-addressp accepts under the limits' trusted range (the `exposure-trusted' :set-policy row, parsed by fn-exp-trusted-of-word; `policy set exposure-trusted' admits only fn-exp-trusted-wordp, books/native-admin.lisp) is never given the per-address refusal. fn-exp-untrusted-address-is-refused-exactly-at-its-limit: outside the range, with the failed-login rule not refusing and the owner below the total, the decision is the per-address 400 exactly when the address holds its limit. Not proved: the CIDR parser's agreement with RFC 4632 text beyond the witnesses; the memory a capacity costs (PKT-605).

proofs.title: One admission decision, three wire forms: CHECK and TAKETHIS answer as IHAVE does, the streaming pipeline is bounded, and fn's feed falls back to IHAVE on a peer that does not stream
proofs.statement: books/peer-transit-forms.lisp over the functions the served path calls. fn-peer-check-and-ihave-answer-one-offer-decision: for one connection state and one well-formed Message-ID, the code fn-peer-command answers to IHAVE and to CHECK are fn-peer-offer-code's IHAVE and CHECK images of the same fn-peer-decide-offer decision, so CHECK's code is the RFC 4644 section 2.4 form of IHAVE's RFC 3977 section 6.3.2 code (238/335, 438/435, 431/436). fn-peer-takethis-and-ihave-answer-one-transfer-verdict: for every transfer decision and durable completion, fn-peer-transit-outcome-effects renders TAKETHIS's code as the streaming form of IHAVE's (239/235, 439/437, 436/436; 436 after TAKETHIS is fn's local policy, RFC 4644 section 2.5 names 400) and closes exactly when IHAVE's does. fn-peer-transfer-submission-differs-only-in-form-unfolds: the transfer arm hands the owner the same (peer, Message-ID, octets) whatever the form. fn-peer-step-pinned-keeps-outstanding-offers-within-the-peer-bound: no served event raises the connection's outstanding 238 count above the larger of its value and the peer record's inbound max-inflight (D27: a pipeline past the bound is 431). books/feed-connection.lisp fn-fc-mode-stream-unsupported-falls-back-to-ihave: a 500 or 501 answer to MODE STREAM (RFC 3977 section 3.2.1) makes the same connection ready with streaming off, security and credential kept, and records no stop; books/owner.lisp fn-own-feed-connect-in-ihave-form-offers-ihave, -sends-the-bare-article and fn-own-feed-connect-in-stream-form-offers-check: after a connect in the :ihave form the feed offers the IHAVE line and sends the bare article, after a streaming connect to a streaming record it offers CHECK. Not claimed: that a real peer's code means what the RFC says (the INN lab measures that), nor a CAPABILITIES-driven choice of form (RFC 4644 section 2.3 prefers CAPABILITIES; fn asks MODE STREAM).

proofs.title: Reading the schema-3 checkpoint file written for the tables of a capture gives those tables, and their value is the capture (the keystone of the one resumable pipeline; the batched loop writes that file at any batch size)
proofs.statement: books/store-checkpoint-tables.lisp. fn-sct-decode-file-of-file-is-the-capture: for c = (fn-sco-capture configs records), tables = (fn-sct-tables-of-capture c frontier revision) and progs = (fn-sct-table-programs tables (fn-sco-event-index c)): (implies (and (fn-sct-tables-treep tables) (<= (len records) (1+ *fn-cbor-max-uint*)) (fn-sct-programs-widthp progs)) (and (equal (fn-sct-decode-file (fn-sct-file-segments progs seg (len records))) (list :ok tables)) (equal (fn-sct-capture-of-tables tables) c))), for any segment size. Built from fn-sct-run-of-program (the ref codec's stack machine pushes the program's value, with a decoder table that agrees with the encoder's below the count: fn-sct-agreep-of-build, the capture's event index against the index built from the P rows), fn-sct-run-of-rows-program (a run's stack is its rows), fn-sct-decode-programs-of-table-programs (the four programs decode to the tables), fn-sct-decode-file-of-file-segments (the four runs decode to the four programs, through the codec's fn-scc-join-of-chunks) and fn-sct-capture-of-tables-of-capture (the tables of a capture mean the capture, for every configuration history and record list; the file-local reference s is the fresh P table's index, the identity on a fresh table, never assumed for a live one). With PRF-135's fn-sct-load-is-decode-file the host's load (fn-store-sco-decode) of the file gives the capture the open extends, so fn-sn-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover and fn-sco-open transfer unchanged. PROVED (checkpoint-pipeline-2): fn-ockp-run-writes-the-file, books/owner-checkpoint-pipeline.lisp: for setup = (fn-ockp-setup next frontier revision seg budget free) and tables = (fn-sct-tables-of-capture next frontier revision), (implies (and (fn-ockp-tables-encodablep tables) (true-listp fn-octets) (natp seg) (equal (mv-nth 0 (fn-ockp-run setup (fn-ockp-initial-state tables fn-octets) b seg s segment-bound file-bound fuel fn-octets)) :ok)) (equal (mv-nth 1 (fn-ockp-run ...)) (fn-sct-file-octets (fn-sct-table-programs tables (fn-sco-event-index next)) seg s))): the octets of the host's steps (fnn-checkpoint-write-steps loops on fn-ockp-step until fn-ockp-donep; fn-ockp-run is that loop in the logic, answering :fuel when the fuel ends before the four tables), at ANY batch size and ANY segment size, from ANY initial buffer contents (fn-ockp-initial-state starts the residue at the buffer's fill), are the file the tables codec specifies whenever the loop completes with :ok. From fn-ockp-run-is-the-remaining (the residue invariant: what remains of a state is the run K from the residue [W, fill) and the rows not yet encoded, framed from INDEX with the chain at PREV, then the runs after it; each step's frames are exactly the difference: fn-ockp-batch-writes-the-remaining, split on the four tables), fn-ockp-cut-frames-is-cut (the buffer's cut is the list's cut), fn-ockp-chunks-of-append-cut, fn-ockp-frames-of-append, fn-ockp-encode-batch-is-rows-program and fn-ockp-counts-are-chunk-counts. With the decode keystone above, the file the loop writes decodes to the tables and the tables mean the capture.

proofs.title: The pipeline defers by name before any allocation exactly when the file it would write exceeds the checkpoint budget or the space, naming the estimate and the bound, and the deferral blocks a retry exactly while that bound is below the estimate
proofs.statement: books/owner-checkpoint-writer.lisp (split from owner-checkpoint-pipeline by checkpoint-pipeline-5). fn-ockp-decide-defers-by-the-estimate: (implies (and (natp estimate) (natp budget)) (let ((verdict (fn-ockp-decide estimate budget free))) (and (iff (equal (car verdict) :deferred) (or (< budget estimate) (not (natp (fn-ockp-space free))) (< (fn-ockp-space free) estimate))) (implies (< budget estimate) (equal verdict (list :deferred :exceeds-budget estimate budget))) (implies (and (not (< budget estimate)) (natp (fn-ockp-space free)) (< (fn-ockp-space free) estimate)) (equal verdict (list :deferred :exceeds-space estimate (fn-ockp-space free)))) (implies (not (equal (car verdict) :deferred)) (equal verdict (list :plan estimate))) (implies (< budget estimate) (iff (fn-ock-publication-blockedp verdict later-budget later-space) (< (nfix later-budget) estimate))) (implies (and (not (< budget estimate)) (natp (fn-ockp-space free)) (< (fn-ockp-space free) estimate)) (iff (fn-ock-publication-blockedp verdict later-budget later-space) (or (not (natp later-space)) (< later-space estimate))))))). fn-ockp-space is the free octets the host observed by statvfs less fn-smr-reserve-octets (nil when unobserved: deferred by name). Called by fn-ockp-setup (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-publish-captured; host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sco-publish-setup); the blocked rule on the due path (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-sco-due). N) with G a colon-free printable group and N the article's available local number fn-nntp-article-number G (fn-xref-pairs-exact), each an entry the group index builds (fn-xref-pair-is-an-index-entry); the server of fn-oag-post-config's listing is the node's path-identity when set (fn-oag-listing-server-is-the-path-identity); LIST OVERVIEW.FMT names Xref:full on the same condition; every reply is well-formed (fn-nntp-effects-*-served) and without a server the renderers are the eight-field ones (*-without-a-server). proofs.title: `tls reload` takes the renewed certificate and key exactly when they load, match, are valid now and keep every served name, and refuses by name otherwise
proofs.statement: Subject fn-tlsr-decide (books/tls-reload.lisp), which host/tls-reload-host.lisp fn-tlsr-host-decide computes for host/native/tls-reload.lisp fnn-tls-owner-reload, the owner's handler of the FNCT kind-19 `reload` request (`operator CONFIG tls reload`); the host swaps the served SSL_CTX (fnn-tls-context-swap, under the context lock fnn-tls-accept holds across SSL_new) exactly when the decision is :accept and frees the candidate otherwise. (1) fn-tlsr-decide-accepts-exactly-loaded-matching-current-covering-material (KEYSTONE, no hypotheses): the decision accepts iff the chain loaded, the key loaded, the key matches (the three library observations), the clock is an integer with notBefore <= now < notAfter (both times parsed from the leaf's UTCTime/GeneralizedTime contents), the subjectAltName is readable, and every dNSName of the served facts is among the new ones. (2) fn-tlsr-decide-carries-the-facts-or-a-named-refusal: an accepted decision is (:accept NAMES NOT-AFTER) of the parsed facts; any other is (:refuse R) with R one of the nine named reasons the reply and the operator's line carry. Teeth: tests/acl2/tls-reload-tests.lisp (a real EC P-256 certificate's times and subjectAltName octets; the positive witness asserting every conjunct and the acceptance; per conjunct a witness where it alone fails and the decision refuses by its name; per conjunct a must-fail of the acceptance without it; the window ends; the frames' round trip and an old owner's plain refusal). Trusted, not proved: the library's parse of the certificate and its three booleans (HST-016's seam), that SSL_new takes its own SSL_CTX reference (OpenSSL 3, LibreSSL), and the host clock. proofs.statement: The configuration-only fold over CONFIGS ++ (R) is fn-cfgc-config-extend of the fold over CONFIGS (fn-cfgc-config-replay-of-one-more, from fn-cnode-replay-loop-splits-at-any-prefix); the physical fold fn-cpr-replay over CONFIGS ++ (R) and EVENTS is fn-cfgc-cpr-extend of the fold over CONFIGS and EVENTS, one fn-cpr-loop step, when both lists are true lists and every event's txid is below R's (fn-cfgc-cpr-replay-of-one-more); an observed history is below its frontier, so a record at or past the frontier is filed after every event. Hence the candidate from the open's carried folds is fn-native-admin-candidate-open-result of the appended history (fn-cfgc-candidate-open-result-is-the-replayed-candidate) and the authorization the host calls, fn-cfgc-cvec-native-admin-authorize, is EQUAL to fn-cvec-native-admin-authorize on every arm whenever the carried fold is fn-cpr-replay of the same histories and the configuration history is a true list (fn-cfgc-cvec-native-admin-authorize-is-the-replayed-authorization), so every keystone of the replaying authorization (the lock, the generation, the occupied name, the group-name bound, the candidate) carries. The carried fold is established by the open: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-extended keeps (E replayed opened) and the configuration history it folded, and fn-sco-store-open-of-extended-capture is the theorem that replayed is fn-cpr-replay of those configurations and E's records, on the full and the checkpoint open. Host: host/native/admin.lisp fnn-admin-execute -> fnn-admin-authorize-carried -> host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-cfg-native-admin-authorize-carried (NIL, and the replaying authorization, when the observed configuration history is not the open's). PKT-601 (1), config-consumer-catalog-2: the candidate open is not recomputed. fn-cfgc-candidate-open-carried decides it from OPENED, the open's own result (kept beside E and the fold), and the extended fold: when OPENED succeeded and R is at or past the frontier, the candidate is accepted exactly when the extended fold is :ok and fn-cfgc-advance-okp (the four scalar tests of fn-replay-advance-okp, equal to it on a configured node: fn-cfgc-advance-okp-is-replay-advance-okp) holds of its node; KEYSTONE fn-cfgc-candidate-open-carried-is-the-replayed-candidate: under a true configuration history, CONFIGURATION the configuration-only fold, REPLAYED the physical fold and OPENED = fn-cpo-open-observed of the same histories and frontier, it EQUALS fn-native-admin-candidate-open-result of the appended history (from store-open-bridge fn-cpo-open-observed-succeeds-exactly: over the same events and frontier, a second configuration history opens exactly when its configured replay does, fn-cfgc-cpo-open-of-other-configs); the authorization keystones carry it with the OPENED hypothesis. PKT-601 (2): fnn-admin-verify-under-lock reads the published file back; KEYSTONE fn-cfgc-readback-verified-is-the-reopen: when fn-native-admin-publication-authorize accepted RECORD, RECORD is the decode of AUTHORIZED, and fn-cfgc-readback-verdict of the readback, AUTHORIZED, GENERATION and the frontier is :verified, the open of the configuration history plus the record read back succeeds, its fold is :ok and serves GENERATION (what the retired whole-store reopen observed; fn-bs-k0v-host-rerecovery-keeps-relation-at-every-cut loses that host line). proofs.title: The BP kind-19 checkpoint read from an octet buffer by index is the list decoder: the reopen after a rotation decodes the same checkpoint and refuses the same files, in linear work
proofs.statement: books/bp-node-rotation-buffer.lisp. fn-bpnrb-selection-plan (the host-called entry: host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-selection-plan, called by fnn-bps-open, copies the selected generation file's bytes into fn-octets-bp, an abstract stobj congruent to fn-octets, one byte per octet) reads the file by index: fn-bpnrb-decode-range checks the head, reads the u64 payload length from eight cells, checks the frame trailer over the prefix (fn-frame-trailer of fn-bpnr-checkpoint-prefix of the payload cells, built once) and runs the tree decoder fn-bpnrb-dec, which carries an index (a counted run is its cells copied once, fn-bpnrb-slice-acc; a u64 is eight cells). KEYSTONE fn-bpnrb-checkpoint-decode-is-decode, hypothesis-free: (equal (fn-bpnrb-checkpoint-decode budget x) (fn-bpnr-checkpoint-decode x budget)) -- the same checkpoint on every file the list decoder takes, nil on every file it refuses, so fn-bpnr-checkpoint-decode-of-octets (PRF-081's round trip) and PRF-081's recovery keystones are about what the host executes. fn-bpnrb-selection-plan-is-selection-plan, hypothesis-free: the entry equals fn-bpnr-selection-plan over the buffer's value. fn-bpnrb-dec-is-dec: over an octet buffer, the index decoder on the cells [i, end) is fn-bpnr-dec on that slice, with the rest of the slice being the cells from the returned index. The bounded-step foundation (gpt-6's review 2026-09-26 section 2: the checkpoint pipeline's discipline for the BP checkpoint): fn-bpnrb-mstep, the recursion as an explicit machine over (position, goals, value stack); fn-bpnrb-mrun, one quantum of at most Q steps stopping once B octets are consumed, returning the exact continuation; fn-bpnrb-mrun-all-of-dec-goal (the machine run from a decode goal is fn-bpnrb-dec's result followed by the remaining goals) and fn-bpnrb-mrun-all-of-mrun (a quantum keeps the whole run: resuming from its continuation reaches the same answer; a refused quantum is a refused run). These are NOT host-called yet: the host still calls fn-bpnrb-selection-plan in one call (0.55 s at 11.4 MB); the stepped entry and its keystone are the continuation's (LANEDUMP). Every executable function is guard-verified (asserted :common-lisp-compliant in the test book). Why: the list decoder's u64 and counted reads re-established true-listp of the whole remaining input per token (fn-bpnr-read-u64, fn-bpnr-read-counted), so the reopen after a rotation was quadratic in the file (sb-sprof: 99.9 percent of samples in TRUE-LISTP, 722 s for an 11,418,801-octet file of 1,311 held rows). What it does not say: the held rows' wires remain octet lists in the checkpoint value (the replay's representation); the trailer digest is computed over a list of the prefix (the constrained fn-frame-digest has no buffer-range twin); the list decoder remains the specification and the rotation's writer (fn-bpnr-checkpoint-octets) is unchanged.

proofs.title: The catalog's number lookup at a version and its clamped range are the walks of the visible rows, under the no-number-bound-twice invariant every catalog export preserves
proofs.statement: books/catalog-number-index.lisp, over the generic fn-cat. fn-cnx-freshp (every later row's number in a group this row is numbered in is absent or larger) holds of the creator and of clear and is preserved by commit, by withdraw and redecide under their guards (fn-cnx-freshp-of-commit, -of-withdraw, -of-redecide, -of-create-and-clear, stated over fn-cat$a-* with no stobj; fn-cnx-freshp-of-cat-writers over the exports). Under it a number is bound by at most one row (fn-cnx-number-seq-unique), and KEYSTONE fn-cnx-view-seq-is-walk: fn-cnx-view-seq group n v (one probe of the (group . number) table, one row read, one visibility test) equals fn-cat-view-number-find group n count v (books/catalog-view.lisp: the walk of the rows visible at version v, newest first) for every non-nil n; KEYSTONE fn-cnx-view-range-is-walk: fn-cnx-view-range group low high v (the numbers low .. min(high, next - 1) ascending, one probe each) equals fn-cnx-walk-range group low high v, the walk per number over low .. high unclamped (a number past the group's high names no row). Hypothesis-free but for the invariant (and n non-nil for the lookup).
proofs.planning_note: Lane index-stobjs (wave 5, 2026-09-26). The subjects are not host-called: the served machine still reads the lists (fn-gidx number trie, fn-midx trie, the archive walk for ARTICLE by number) until catalog-slice's step 7b threads fn-cat through the retrieval arms; these are the lookups 7b is asked to call (LANEDUMP request). proofs.title: A contact's drain reads each job once from a per-peer cursor and answers exactly what the head-restarting scan answers
proofs.statement: fn-bpnjc-contact-next (books/bp-node-job-cursor.lisp; host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bpc-drive-contact before every base offer, and fnn-bpnode-send-receipts in host/native/bp-node.lisp) reads the job list from the cursor (F C HELD) the host threads between asks. fn-bpnjc-contact-next-is-the-head-scan (keystone): under fn-bpnjc-contact-relp (unique job keys; no job ahead of C ready on this contact; HELD the first held job ahead of C; every offered key ahead of C) its answer equals fn-bpnj-contact-next's, so PRF-120 and PRF-079 describe it. The relation is established at the contact's opening from the peer's frontier (fn-bpnjc-open-establishes-the-relation; fn-bpnjc-frontierp: every job ahead of F is another peer's or :forwarded/:expired), kept by each offer for the next ask (fn-bpnjc-offer-keeps-the-relation) and by an evolution of the jobs ahead of the cursor between asks (fn-bpnjc-evolution-keeps-the-relation; fn-bpnjc-offered-record-evolves: a lifecycle record naming an offered key, or a :queued append, is one). fn-bpnjc-drain-is-the-head-drain (keystone): along a contact's asks, threading OFFERED and the cursor, with the jobs evolving between asks (fn-bpnjc-evolving-p), the answers are the head scan's, ask for ask. fn-bpnjc-drain-visits-are-linear (keystone, work): the positions all asks examine plus the start are at most the length of the last job list asked at; an offer advances at least one (fn-bpnjc-ask-position-bounds). The frontier: fn-bpnjc-contact-close advances it over settled jobs and keeps every peer's (fn-bpnjc-close-keeps-the-frontiers); every lifecycle record keeps every frontier (fn-bpnjc-lifecycle-record-keeps-the-frontier). Covered scope: base job offers. Not covered: that every served event changes the base jobs only by fn-bpn-apply-record (the drain takes the evolution as a hypothesis); the machine's own per-offer work (find-job, replace-job) stays linear in the job's position (PKT-653).
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-cursors (Opus, 2026-09-27). Measured on hbox (tools/bench/bp-drain-bench.lisp): records examined per drain 2,002,000 -> 1,000 at 1,000 ready jobs and 200,020,000 -> 10,000 at 10,000; see the record for walls. Not done: PKT-653 (machine per-offer work linear in position), PKT-654 (4,096-record ceiling).

proofs.title: The reader opens every connection over the selection's recognised archive and Message-ID trie instead of rebuilding and re-recognising them per connection; a retention commit no longer re-runs the whole-node recogniser on the advanced node
proofs.statement: (1) The reader open. KEYSTONE fn-rdc-reset-is-served-open (books/reader-open-carried.lisp; hypothesis (fn-rdc-readyp (fn-rdc-selection archive verdicts))): (fn-rdc-reset (fn-rdc-selection archive verdicts) ll bl config observation injection acfg) = (fn-served-pin-verdicts (fn-served-open archive ll bl config observation injection acfg) verdicts). host/reader-host.lisp fn-reader-reset (native host/native/io.lisp fnn-reader-reset, once per accepted connection in fnn-serve-client) calls fn-rdc-reset over the selection fn-reader-use-store / fn-reader-use-seed recorded once per process (fn-rdc-store-selection / fn-rdc-selection, through fnn-reader-select in fnn-reader-prepare). The relation carried: fn-rdc-selection-establishes (no hypothesis beyond readiness): a ready selection's archive satisfies fn-nntp-projectionp and fn-statep and its index is (fn-midx-build (fn-state-articles archive)); fn-rdc-selection-ready-iff-projectable. The reader's archive is immutable under its shared lock (it never commits), so the selection is the establishing entry and no transition needs preservation. Refinement: fn-rdc-served-open-is-served-open (hypotheses (fn-statep archive), index = the archive's trie) over PRF-188's fn-ocar-auth-open-reader-is-auth-open-session. A reset with no ready selection is unreachable in composition (both hosts refuse before any connection) and has no separate arm. (2) The retention commit. books/replay.lisp fn-replay-apply-retention-event's test (fn-node-statep advanced) is (mbt ...), discharged under its guard by fn-replay-advance-preserves-node-statep; its logical definition is unchanged, so every theorem about it stands. Host callers: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission / fn-owner-finish (through fn-ccar-sn-finish-enabled), fn-owner-prepare-identity (fn-replay-apply-record), host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-finish, fn-store-sn-known-abort, and every replay at open.

Teeth: tests/acl2/reader-open-carried-tests.lisp: a reachable one-article archive (the reader host's seed) whose selection is ready, the carried reset equal to the reference with the greeting written, the trie and verdicts pinned and the session projected; the Store selection over owner-advance-carried-tests' committed owner store; hypothesis removal for fn-rdc-served-open-is-served-open (a wrong index with fn-statep retained; a corrupted-state archive with the index hypothesis retained) and for fn-rdc-reset-is-served-open (a refused selection); the retention mbt's lemma on the committed store's node, and its failure on a non-node (corrupted-state). proofs.title: The served path's per-line and per-octet-of-line folds run as loops: serving and posting an article uses a control stack independent of its line count and line length
proofs.statement: Four keystones, each with no hypotheses, each the :exec of an mbe whose :logic is the unchanged recursive definition, so the guard proof makes the loop the executable the host runs. fn-nntp-stuff-lines-iter-is-stuff-lines (books/nntp-session.lisp): (fn-nntp-stuff-lines-iter lines) = (fn-nntp-stuff-lines lines), the dot-stuffed CRLF block of every multi-line reply (ARTICLE, HEAD, BODY, OVER, HDR, LIST), built by a tail-recursive accumulator (fn-nntp-stuff-lines-onto) turned round once. fn-post-body-octets-iter-is-body-octets (books/nntp-post.lisp): (fn-post-body-octets-iter lines) = (fn-post-body-octets lines), the POST's article reassembled from the wire's (:article lines) event. fn-wire-list-length-onto-is-list-length (books/wire.lisp): (fn-wire-list-length-onto xs 0) = (fn-wire-list-length xs), the length fn-wire-after-line charges each article line (fn-wire-line-cost). fn-hf-crlf-count-onto-is-crlf-count (books/catalog-record.lisp, lane line-stack 2026-09-27): (fn-hf-crlf-count-onto bytes inline 0) = (fn-hf-crlf-count bytes inline), the body line count the committer's intern decides once per article (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-buffer-arena-action -> fn-owner-prepare-buffer -> fn-apc-intern-row-at -> fn-apc-held-facts-of -> fn-hf-body-lines-of); the recursion it replaced added one after its recursive call, a frame per body line, and stopped the owner on a 2,000,000-line POST at 1 MiB of stack. The recursions they replaced took one control-stack frame per article line (stuff-lines, post-body-octets) or per octet of one line (fn-inj-append inside post-body-octets, fn-wire-list-length); the profile admits a line as long as the article (fn-wire-article-line-limit), so each was a remote stop. Host chain: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk -> host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span -> fn-scar-ocfg-read-span, whose wire fold (fn-wire-feed-span -> fn-wire-feed-byte -> fn-wire-after-line) calls fn-wire-line-cost, whose served POST (fn-nntp-post-step-pinned -> fn-nntp-post-step) calls fn-post-body-octets, and whose retrievals (fn-nntp-article-response) call fn-nntp-stuff-lines. Scope: a measured constant, not a theorem about frames: the native witness posts, serves, reopens and serves articles of 2,000,000 lines and of one 4 MiB line at 1 MiB of control stack per thread on both images.
proofs.progress_note: Lane served-line-iterative (2026-09-26; image-floor packet 2, PKT-481's class, D27). Cause by persvati REPL backtrace (FN-POST-BODY-OCTETS frames to exhaustion on 3,000,000 lines) and by the native witness (one 4 MiB line: Control stack exhausted in fn-owner-chunk-span until fn-wire-list-length was a loop). Teeth: tests/acl2/served-line-iterative-tests.lisp (reachable witnesses, the composed BODY reply, served-size witnesses of 2,100,000 lines and of one 20,000,000-octet line through the compiled executables, labelled MUTATION witnesses refuted on ground instances). Lane line-stack (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27): the fourth keystone; cause read from the frames of FN_NATIVE_FAULT_BACKTRACE's stack-exhaustion report (FN-HF-CRLF-COUNT x60795 on the committer); teeth in tests/acl2/catalog-record-tests.lisp (reachable witnesses by loop and definition; 5,000,000 lines through fn-hf-body-lines-of).

proofs.title: The BP application and receipt Store checks run no whole-node or whole-Store recognizer and no history walk per request: the node recognizer is carried by the owner's relation, and the receipt hosts look the record up through the event index
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-bpaj-store-record-accepted-fast (books/bp-native-app-fast.lisp), reached per request from host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-submit and fn-owner-app-record and host/bp-receipt-journal-host.lisp fn-bprj-apply, fn-bprj-preflight and fn-bprj-request-action (native: host/native/bp-app.lisp, host/native/workflow.lisp); fn-bpaj-record-lookup-fast and fn-bpaj-bpr-accept-request-fast, now called by host/bp-receipt-host.lisp fn-bpr-host-accept and host/bp-receive-host.lisp fn-bpreq-existing-record in place of their deleted host walks. fn-bpaj-node-record-committed-carriedp is fn-bpi-node-record-committedp without its fn-node-statep conjunct; KEYSTONE fn-bpaj-node-record-committed-carriedp-is-committedp: under (fn-node-statep node) alone they are equal. fn-bpaj-store-record-accepted-fast-is-checked keeps its statement (fn-sn-statep and fn-ceis-indexedp give fast = fn-bpr-store-record-acceptedp) through fn-bpaj-sn-statep-carries-node-statep. KEYSTONE fn-osi-ocl-store-record-accepted-fast-is-checked: over the configured owner's Store (fn-owner-store = (fn-own-store (fn-ocfg-owner oc))), under fn-ocl-relation oc and fn-ceis-indexedp, the fast check is the checked one; fn-bpaj-ocl-relation-carries-sn-statep: fn-ocl-relation (established at open, kept by the ocl open/close/observe/read/advance/complete transitions) carries fn-sn-statep; fn-ceis-indexedp is PRF-144's. KEYSTONE fn-bpaj-record-lookup-fast-found-is-an-accepted-match: under fn-sn-statep and fn-ceis-indexedp, a record the indexed lookup finds has the request's article and subject (the retired host walk's predicate) and satisfies fn-bpr-store-record-acceptedp; the lookup differs from the retired walk only by refusing (two records under the article's Message-ID, or a record whose Message-ID is not the article's). Scope: the node's article and binding are still found by two pointer walks that allocate nothing (fn-find-article, fn-node-find-binding; PKT-638); the lab ingress host fn-bpi-host-prepare/-already-durablep and the BP workflow's fn-bp-statep are not changed (PKT-638).

proofs.title: A committed delta applied in bounded steps under any schedule of quanta ends where its one-shot application does: the :policy range is re-decided exactly once, row by row
proofs.statement: books/config-policy-delta.lisp (lane config-consumer-catalog-2, 2026-09-27; PKT-601 (6), discharging catalog-delta's OPEN). KEYSTONE fn-cfgp-apply-in-quanta-is-apply-delta: for a delta satisfying fn-delta-p and a natural cursor at or before the delta's range start, fn-cat-apply-in-quanta (the resumable run of fn-cat-apply-delta-step, each step re-deciding at most its quantum of rows, fn-cat-apply-delta-step-bounded) under ANY list of quanta equals fn-cat-apply-delta, the one-shot application. Its inductive form fn-cfgp-policy-in-quanta-is-the-range: for a :policy delta with natural bounds, from ANY natural cursor the run is fn-cat-recontext-range from the later of the cursor and the range start to the range end clipped to the count. Scope: the catalog alone; no host line calls fn-cat-apply-in-quanta yet (the catalog serves no path until PKT-585's steps 4 to 9); which configuration change emits a :policy delta is not decided (the held context carries a keyring generation only; the record's packet).

proofs.title: A peer named by a DNS name: the dial resolves only RFC 1123 names, each attempt, and the TLS check a transport selects is the configured name under a pinned anchor or the system's public roots
proofs.statement: books/peer-host.lisp over the functions the host calls. fn-peer-dial-target-decides-the-path (no hypothesis; host host/native/io.lisp fnn-peer-connect, called by host/native/feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-dial and host/native/pull-service.lisp fnn-pull-round): the target is exactly one of (:address A) with A the four octets fn-native-config-ipv4-address spells and the host not a name, (:resolve HOST) with HOST exactly the configured text, an RFC 1123 section 2.1 name of at most 253 octets of letters, digits, hyphen and dot and not an IPv4 literal (fn-peer-host-name-is-not-an-ipv4-literal), or (:refused :host-syntax) for anything else. fn-peer-tls-verification-selects-one-check (no hypothesis; host fnn-feed-enable-tls and the pull's (:tls NAME TRUST) effect in fnn-pull-round): the answer is :verify or :refused only; a :verify names exactly the configured server name, which is a host, sends SNI exactly when it is a DNS name (fn-peer-tls-verification-sni-is-never-a-literal, RFC 6066 section 3), and selects the system roots iff the trust is :system-roots and a pinned file iff it is a C string; a string host name with a well-formed trust is always :verify. fn-peer-tls-select-named-default (peer add, books/native-admin-peer.lisp fn-native-admin-peer-plan-base): a named host given `-` `-` is checked against its own name under the system roots; fn-peer-tls-select-numeric-host-needs-a-name-by-definition; fn-peer-tls-select-is-a-check: every selection is one fn-peer-tls-verification accepts, the roots exactly when the anchor word is `-`. The peer record admits (:tls MODE NAME :system-roots) (books/peer-config.lisp fn-cfg-peer-transportp, row n = 1), the pull plan reads it (books/peer-pull.lisp fn-pull-security-of-rows, books/peer-pull-session.lisp fn-pull-tls-securityp), and invitations carry only hosts (books/peer-invite.lisp fn-pinv-hosts-okp). Not claimed: DNS authenticity, the system bundle's trustworthiness, OpenSSL's hostname check, IPv6 peers, inbound source-address peers after renumbering. EXTENSION (lane friend-blockers, 2026-09-27, the stranger rehearsal's stops): Stop 10: `fn redeem HOST[:PORT] CODE LOGIN [--tls] [--cafile PEM]` (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-redeem) runs XREDEEM for a friend; fn-redeem-step decides each step from the reply code, fn-peer-tls-verification the TLS check, fn-redeem-text every line. KEYSTONE fn-redeem-done-only-on-281-after-the-password. EXTENSION (lane public-node-3, 2026-09-27, the OpenBSD rehearsal's finding 8): a connection that never opens or ends (host fnn-command-redeem: fnn-os-error, fnn-tls-io-error, socket and name-service errors, a close or 30 s silence in fnn-redeem-read-line) is fn-redeem-lost at its stage, and the exit code is fn-outcome-code of fn-redeem-outcome-class. KEYSTONE fn-redeem-lost-is-fenced-and-server-answers-are-not: every lost outcome is :fenced (exit 3), (:uncertain :password) exactly after the password, (:unreachable STAGE) before it; a final step outcome ((:done) or (:refused WORD)) is :accepted exactly on the 281 after the password and :refused otherwise. Not claimed: that the server did not bind the account when the connection ended after the password (it is uncertain, and said so).

proofs.title: A Store opens only on the filesystem its record names, is refused by name otherwise, and its owner's start is refused by name when it requires durable storage on a mount that observably disables it
proofs.statement: books/store-mount-identity.lisp. The record is an FNMI frame of five u16-length fields (fsid, type, mount point, source, policy); KEYSTONE fn-smid-record-decode-of-seal: the host's fnn-seal of fn-smid-record-protected, read back with ACL2's trailer over its protected prefix, decodes to the record (under fn-smid-recordp). KEYSTONE fn-smid-mountinfo-step-preserves-best-okp: the Linux mountinfo fold only ever selects a mount that contains the store root's resolved path. KEYSTONE fn-smid-recorded-store-opens-iff-same-filesystem: a store whose record was written from observation OBS (fn-smid-record-plan) opens under an observation OBS2 exactly when fn-smid-same-filesystemp holds (type and mount point equal; fsids equal where both are reported, else sources equal). KEYSTONE fn-smid-moved-mount-point-is-refused-by-name: when the root now resolves under another mount point the open answers (:refused :filesystem-changed RECORDED OBSERVED). KEYSTONE fn-smid-absent-record-is-refused: no record, no open, whatever is observed. fn-smid-open-verdict-opens-only-on-a-match. KEYSTONE fn-smid-start-refused-iff-required-and-unsafe (PKT-648): on its recorded filesystem, the owner's start is refused as :storage-not-durable exactly when the policy is 1 and fn-smid-unsafe-reason (nobarrier, barrier=0, tmpfs, ramfs) holds, else it starts. KEYSTONE fn-smid-rebound-store-opens: after rebind-filesystem under an observation, an open under it opens. fn-smid-refusal-text-is-nil-exactly-for-open / -for-start: the host prints a refusal exactly when the verdict is not (:open) / (:start). KEYSTONE fn-smid-open-decision-is-the-verdict: the host's open decision fn-smid-open-decision is fn-smid-open-verdict wherever a record is present or the root holds no config.json; KEYSTONE fn-smid-empty-root-is-refused: no record and no config.json is refused whatever is observed; KEYSTONE fn-smid-unrecorded-store-never-starts: a store with no record (made before the record) opens offline with a warning (fn-smid-unrecorded-warning) and is never started; fn-smid-refusal-text-is-nil-exactly-for-an-open-decision. Host subjects: fn-smid-open-decision and fn-smid-start-verdict (host/native/io.lisp fnn-check-filesystem-identity, from fnn-acquire and host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-install), fn-smid-mountinfo-step and fn-smid-linux-observation / fn-smid-statfs-observation (fnn-filesystem-observation), fn-smid-record-plan (fnn-record-filesystem-at-init), fn-smid-rebind-plan (fnn-command-rebind-filesystem), fn-smid-refusal-text, fn-smid-durability-warning. NOT in this target: that statfs and mountinfo report the truth (A-HOST); ZFS sync=disabled and volatile write caches (not observable); the record replacement's crash cuts as a byte-model program (PKT-671). EXTENSION (lane friend-blockers, 2026-09-27, the stranger rehearsal's stops): PKT-820: fn-smid-same-filesystemp compares type and fsid where both fsids are reported (mount point and source are not compared: the shipped systemd unit's ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths bind view shows /var/lib/fn as its own mount point), and type, mount point and source where either is unreported. KEYSTONE fn-smid-same-fsid-view-opens: a store recorded under OBS opens under OBS2 with the same type and the same nonzero fsid, whatever its mount point and source. KEYSTONE fn-smid-other-filesystem-is-refused-by-name and fn-smid-other-fsid-is-refused-by-name: another filesystem (known fsids differ) is refused (:filesystem-changed RECORDED OBSERVED). KEYSTONE fn-smid-unreported-fsid-moved-mount-is-refused-by-name: with an unreported fsid another mount point is refused. KEYSTONE fn-smid-rebind-outside-opens-inside: a rebind run outside the unit cures the unit's open. They replace fn-smid-moved-mount-point-is-refused-by-name (retired: the mount point is no longer the identity where the fsid is known).

proofs.title: A served connection's memory is named and a node refuses, by name, at start and at every live change, a connection capacity the machine cannot hold beside the store's heap figure, the core and the fixed threads; every connection fn-exp-open admits under an accepted capacity, trusted sources included, fits the machine
proofs.statement: books/connection-budget.lisp. The subjects are fn-cbud-run-decide, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-connection-budget calls once per run after recovery and before listen (host/native/mux.lisp fnn-mux-budget-install, from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-run), and fn-cbud-deltas-refusal, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas calls before any live reconfiguration is staged (native-admin, peer-invite and auth all reach it), over the host's observations (the machine: heap-figure's fn-heap-machine-octets; the core's length; the fixed threads, 12 + 2 I/O loops + the control clients; the thread control stack) and the store's profile (heap-figure's fn-heap-figure-octets is the base's heap; the profile's largest article A sizes the connection). The per-connection figure is fn-cbud-conn-octets: a heap part (the connection record, its input of two reads of the largest size a served step may read (fn-cbud-step-read-octets, called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-read-octets from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-refresh-read-octets under the owner mutex after the exposure install and after every served step; host/native/mux.lisp reads into one buffer per I/O loop of that size: 512 octets under a step rate, fn-cbud-step-read-octets-under-a-rate-by-definition, so exposure-steps-per-second keeps its meaning in octets; 4 KiB without one (the measured trade between steps and the owner mutex hold: planning/evidence/input-loop-2-2026-09-27.md), fn-cbud-step-read-octets-is-bounded; the figure holds two, fn-cbud-read-covers-the-step; lane input-loop-2), the one reply of the STATED WORKLOAD -- the largest article rendered, 2A + 1,024 -- and the parser's command line as an octet list, 32 octets per octet; the body of an article in flight is PRF-377's pool) and a native part (kernel socket buffers; the TLS session when a context is loaded); the record, kernel and TLS constants are measurements (tests/test_native_mux.py pins the resident cost). fn-cbud-bound-holds-its-connections: when the base (the store's heap figure, the core, the threads with their stacks and 4 MiB of runtime each) fits the machine, the base plus n connections at the whole per-connection figure fits for every n up to fn-cbud-bound; fn-cbud-bound-is-the-most: one more does not. The resident heap is at most the process's dynamic space, so fn-cbud-resident-octets of n connections is min(dynamic, figure + n x heap part) + the rest of the base + n x native part, and fn-cbud-limit is the larger of fn-cbud-bound and the dynamic space's bound (the whole dynamic space plus each connection's native part). KEYSTONE fn-cbud-limit-holds-its-connections: when either way holds the base (fn-cbud-base-fitsp), the resident figure of every n up to the limit is within the machine; fn-cbud-limit-is-the-most: of limit + 1 it is not. KEYSTONE fn-cbud-run-decide-holds-the-capacity: an accepted run (:hold L) has capacity <= L, L the limit, and the resident figure of capacity connections within the machine; fn-cbud-run-decide-refuses-exactly-past-the-limit: it refuses exactly when the capacity passes the limit or the base does not fit. KEYSTONE fn-cbud-admitted-connections-fit-the-machine: under PRF-211's hypotheses, when the live capacity is within the limit and the base fits, an admission (fn-exp-admit-decision = (:admit)) with nconns held leaves the resident figure of nconns + 1 within the machine; the trusted range exempts no connection from the capacity (fn-exp-open-refuses-exactly-at-the-capacity). fn-cbud-deltas-refusal-keeps-the-capacity-held: a delta list the refusal passes leaves the capacity of the applied configuration within the limit, so the maintained relation 'capacity <= held limit' (established by the run's decision) survives every live change. Lane zero-copy-commit (2026-09-28): fn-cbud-launch-decide and its theorem are gone (no caller since lane reservation-figure); the body of an article in flight left the per-connection heap part (the parser term is the command line only) for the store figure's pool of article credits, admitted by the served read (PRF-377). Not claimed: replies larger than the stated workload's (range OVER/LISTGROUP) until replies are rendered in windows (PKT-644); the measured constants as theorems; that the probe sees the live capacity (it cannot: PKT-644).

proofs.title: A restricted reader session is served the store with its excluded groups absent, and no reply can depend on what an excluded group holds
proofs.statement: books/nntp-auth.lisp fn-auth-delegate-pinned (called by fn-auth-step-pinned, which books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch calls per framed line; the carried twin books/served-carried.lisp fn-scar-auth-delegate-pinned, which host/owner-host.lisp reaches through fn-scar-ocfg-read-tls-prefix, calls the same view functions) delegates over (fn-auth-view-session, -archive, -index, -config): for a reader session whose login's rule (fn-auth-access-text over the pinned listing's fourth element) has READ text R and a projected session, the archive is fn-gac-restrict-state R (books/group-access.lisp), the index fn-gac-restrict-index R built from its articles, the session fn-gac-deselect R; otherwise each is its argument (fn-auth-view-when-unrestricted). KEYSTONES (books/group-access.lisp): fn-gac-restrict-state-is-a-projection (fn-nntp-projectionp preserved); fn-gac-restrict-index-corresponds (fn-gidx-pin-correspondencep of the rebuilt index); fn-gac-restrict-state-groups-are-readable (every group of the view is readable under R and a group of the store); fn-gac-restrict-articles-memberships-readable and fn-gac-restrict-index-withdrawn-are-readable (every article of the view and of its withdrawn list names only readable groups and memberships); fn-gac-restricted-article-is-held (the view holds Message-ID M exactly when the store holds an article M with a readable group); fn-gac-restrict-absent-groups (NO ORACLE: for a store fn-statep and any R2 admitting every group R admits, restricting to R2 then R is restricting to R). The served relation: fn-gac-deselected-consistent / fn-gac-consistent-back and fn-auth-view-consistent / -back carry fn-auth-session-consistentp and fn-gidx-pin-correspondencep into and out of the view, so fn-auth-delegate-pinned-preserves-consistentp and fn-auth-step-pinned-preserves-consistent-session hold for restricted sessions. Local policy (INN readers.conf); RFC 3977 section 4.2 wildmats.

proofs.title: A moderated group: an unapproved article is never visible in it, a moderator's approved article is, and an Approved field from anyone else is refused by name
proofs.statement: fn-cfg-set-group-moderation-sets-the-moderation (books/config-invariants.lisp, KEYSTONE): an admitted (fn-cfg-set-group-moderation NAME QUEUE ADDRESS LOGINS) (code 23, `group moderate`) applied by fn-cfg-apply-delta makes fn-cfg-group-moderation of NAME (QUEUE ADDRESS LOGINS), or nil for --off, and leaves every other group's unchanged. Over fn-post-gated-decision, the served POST's decision (books/nntp-post.lisp, called by fn-nntp-post-step; host line host/reader-host.lisp fn-reader-chunk through books/served.lisp): fn-post-unapproved-article-is-never-in-a-moderated-group (KEYSTONE): an ordinary article with no Approved field is never committed with a group whose status in the connection's configuration is moderated (it is forwarded as an RFC 5537 section 3.5.1 method-1 envelope into the queue group, or refused :moderation-unavailable); fn-post-moderator-approved-article-is-committed (KEYSTONE): with Approved and every named moderated group :approver on the connection, the decision is the injection's (committed into the moderated groups); fn-post-forged-approval-is-refused-by-name (KEYSTONE): with Approved and some named moderated group not :approver, the decision is the refusal :approval-not-moderator (441 by name). fn-mod-session-entries-approver-iff-moderator (books/moderation.lisp): on the owner-installed status list (no :approver entries), a connection's view marks group G :approver exactly when its login is one of G's moderators (books/nntp-auth.lisp fn-auth-moderation-config, called by fn-auth-delegate and fn-auth-delegate-pinned). fn-post-submission-is-the-decision-or-its-envelope with fn-mod-envelope-msgid-is-not-a-generated-id keep fn-post-distinct-injection-clocks-give-distinct-identities unconditional. Relay: fn-peer-transfer-never-stages-an-unapproved-moderated-article (books/peer-inbound-invariants.lisp, KEYSTONE) over fn-peer-transfer, the owner's transit port: a transfer that changes the node stages the article in a group moderated under the configuration only when the article carries Approved (fn-peer-decide-transfer's :unapproved-moderated refusal; RFC 5537 sections 3.6 item 6, 3.7 item 5). Queue privacy (PKT-658): fn-own-submission-targets-of-a-queue-by-definition and fn-own-feed-durable-never-enqueues-a-queue (books/owner-feed-subject.lisp, KEYSTONES) over fn-own-submission-targets and fn-own-feed-durable (host fn-owner-submission-intent and the outcomes): a submission naming a moderation queue group of the owner's posting configuration has no target and leaves the feed table unchanged; fn-auth-view-hides-the-queue-from-a-non-moderator (books/nntp-auth.lisp, KEYSTONE) over fn-auth-view-archive, the store fn-auth-delegate-pinned serves: for a projected reader connection whose login moderates none of the groups a queue serves (or has not authenticated), the view holds neither the queue group nor an article filed in it (group-access's READ rule with the queue hidden, fn-gac-readablep's :hide form; fn-mod-hidden-queues). The operator's `moderation list GROUP` (PKT-657) renders the queue's envelopes held/approved/rejected (books/control-evidence.lisp fn-cev-moderation-report; FNLS frame kind 3 code 10); The operator's verbs (PKT-657, books/moderation-verbs.lisp, host host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-moderation-plan calling fn-mvb-plan, fn-mvb-plan-unfolds): fn-mvb-approve-commits-the-held-article-approved (KEYSTONE) over fn-mvb-approve: a planned submission has LOGIN a moderator of a group the envelope queues for, the envelope held, the octets the envelope's proto-article with `Approved: LOGIN` first, fn-post-gated-decision under LOGIN's moderation view injecting them under the planned Message-ID and groups, and the operator path (fn-own-operator-decision, the (:operator-submit ...) event the host steps) injecting them too; fn-mvb-only-a-moderator-approves-or-rejects (KEYSTONE): a LOGIN that moderates no group the envelope queues for gets a refusal from approve and reject (:not-a-moderator by name when the envelope exists); fn-mvb-reject-withdraws-the-held-envelope (KEYSTONE): a planned rejection is the node's withdrawal (PRF-256) of exactly the held envelope. After the records flip the held envelope is an archive article whose payload position is an arena handle: fn-mvb-plan and fn-mvb-approve take the arena (host fn-owner-moderation-plan passes it; only read) and fn-mvb-held-article reads the envelope's octets through it (fn-nntp-article-bytes; lane matrix-reds, PKT-850: before, approve parsed the handle and answered envelope-malformed); fn-mvb-held-article-is-the-model-body-by-definition (the representation bridge; a restatement by definition, so not cited as a keystone): the held body is the body of the envelope's octet model fn-nntp-article-alpha. Teeth over a flipped archive in tests/acl2/moderation-verbs-tests.lisp (the envelope at handle 0; an empty arena refuses envelope-malformed; a pre-flip octet payload approves the same).

proofs.title: A local consumer bound to an account is served only events of a group the account reads, only with the account's credential, and otherwise exactly as the consumer poll and ack; an unbound consumer is unchanged
proofs.statement: books/consumer-bound.lisp. Subjects: fn-cbind-poll and fn-cbind-ack (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-bound-poll / -bound-ack, reached from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-consumer-local-serialized for local-control codes 7 and 8), fn-cbind-plain-poll and fn-cbind-plain-ack (fn-owner-consumer-local-poll / -ack, codes 5 and 1). The binding is the accounts slot's mark-6 row (books/config.lisp fn-cfg-consumer-bind, delta code 24) of the latest configuration; the credential check is fn-auth-checkp over fn-auth-config-with-accounts (the table AUTHINFO reads); the rule is group-access's read pattern (fn-gac-pattern / fn-gac-readablep). KEYSTONES: fn-cbind-poll-delivers-only-readable-events (a bound poll that answers a page: the consumer is bound, the password checks, the answer is fn-col-poll-report's, and the selected event's article has a group readable under the account's rule); fn-cbind-poll-is-the-consumer-poll-or-a-refusal and fn-cbind-ack-is-the-consumer-ack-or-a-refusal (every bound answer is the unbound consumer's own or a refusal, which writes nothing, so PRF-116's page-is-a-read, forward-ack-in-scope and repeated-ack-no-op guarantees hold over the delivered subsequence; an ack that is not refused had the binding, the credential and a readable query); fn-cbind-plain-poll-of-an-unbound-consumer-is-the-consumer-poll and fn-cbind-plain-ack-of-an-unbound-consumer-is-the-consumer-ack (an unbound consumer's plain answer is today's; a bound consumer's is (:refused :bound)). Local policy; no RFC requirement. RECORDS FLIP (flip-bridge, 2026-09-27): the Store retains held rows and fn-col-poll-report refuses a held article row :report, so the polls read the payload through the arena: fn-cbind-poll-over and fn-cbind-plain-poll-over (books/consumer-bound.lisp) over books/history-fold-refinement.lisp fn-col-poll-report-over carry KEYSTONES 1, 2 and 4 (fn-cbind-poll-over-delivers-only-readable-events, fn-cbind-poll-over-is-the-consumer-poll-or-a-refusal, fn-cbind-plain-poll-over-of-an-unbound-consumer-is-the-consumer-poll) and equal the arena-free polls whenever the selected event is no held row (fn-cbind-poll-over-is-poll-unless-a-held-row). Host: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll and -bound-poll still call the arena-free forms (a REQUEST to the host lane to pass the live arena); until then a bound or plain poll that selects an article answers (:refused :report). The acks read no payload and are unchanged.

proofs.title: The refused-offer memory is bounded, evicts oldest-first, and answers an offer with the refusal the parse of a remembered transfer gives
proofs.statement: books/refused-offers.lisp, books/peer-inbound.lisp, books/peer-refused-offers.lisp, books/owner.lisp. The memory (Message-ID . reason) pairs, newest first, is recorded by the owner at a transit outcome (books/owner.lisp fn-own-transit-refused under fn-own-transit-outcome, the :transit-outcome event host/owner-host.lisp steps) only for a refusal whose reason the octets decide, and the reason recorded is recomputed from the in-flight octets (fn-peer-refused-record: fn-peer-intrinsic-refusal, the arms of fn-peer-decide-transfer that read only the octets and the offered Message-ID); it is re-pinned into every peer session per read (fn-own-conn-live-session) and read by the offer arm of fn-peer-decide-offer after the history test (and its served twins fn-pix-decide-offer, fn-pgc-decide-offer). KEYSTONES: fn-rof-record-within-capacity and fn-rof-record-keeps-a-bounded-memory-bounded (D27: never longer than the operator's refused-offer-capacity, default 4096); fn-rof-record-at-capacity-evicts-the-oldest; fn-peer-decide-transfer-refuses-what-the-octets-refuse (for any node and clock, a peer with an inbound half, a well-formed Message-ID and octets within the peer's size: the transfer decision is the octets' refusal); fn-prof-run-is-sound (every Message-ID a memory built by the record step holds names a transfer of it whose octets drew exactly the remembered reason); fn-prof-offer-answer-is-the-reparse (an offer of a held, not-yet-accepted Message-ID is refused for that reason, and the remembered transfer's own decision on this node from this peer is the same refusal). Not persisted (in memory only; a restart costs one re-parse per refused article and changes no answer). A future date and a missing Path are never remembered: the first depends on the clock, the second on the operator's relay-require-path. Lane log-leftovers (2026-09-27, PKT-858): fn-peer-decide-offer-answers-the-memory holds outside the disk-slow posture (hypothesis (not (fn-peer-shed-p session))); the owner's memory built from transfers never holds the posture's entry (fn-prof-run-keeps-no-posture), so fn-prof-offer-answer-is-the-reparse is unchanged.

proofs.title: A relayed article dated beyond the operator's skew, with an unreadable date, with a malformed Path, or (when required) with no Path, is refused by name
proofs.statement: books/relay-checks.lisp and books/peer-inbound.lisp fn-peer-decide-transfer (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide calls it; the reply is fn-peer-transit-outcome-effects' 437/439 with fn-peer-reason-text). RFC 5537 section 3.6 step 2: :date-future when the Injection-Date (or, absent, the Date) read by fn-rck-date-instant (RFC 5322 section 3.3 with the section 4.3 obsolete forms) is more than fn-rck-skew seconds after the clock reading; the skew is the operator's relay-date-skew limit row, at most 86400 (fn-rck-skew-within-the-rfc; the admin word is refused above it, fn-rck-limit-valuep), 86400 without a row; without a usable clock the check does not decide and fn-peer-transfer defers :no-clock. Section 3.6 step 4: :date-syntax for a date field that is not a date-time, :path-syntax for a Path present once that is not RFC 5536 section 3.1.5's grammar (fn-rck-path-wellformedp), :no-path for a missing Path when the operator's relay-require-path is 1 (default 0: fn's own authored submissions carry no Path, PKT-674). Theorem subject: the concrete witnesses of tests/acl2/transit-hygiene-tests.lisp through fn-peer-decide-transfer and the keystone fn-peer-decide-transfer-refuses-what-the-octets-refuse (PRF-235) for the octet-decided reasons.

proofs.title: The outbound feed offers an article only to peers whose Distribution filter admits the article's Distribution
proofs.statement: books/owner-feed-subject.lisp over fn-own-submission-targets (books/owner.lisp; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-submission-intent calls fn-own-submission-intent-records, which names it, and the durable enqueue fn-own-feed-durable folds it): KEYSTONE fn-own-submission-targets-respect-the-distribution, every target's filter (fn-own-feed-dists-of, the wildmat of its outbound-distributions row, set at fn-own-feed-reconfigure, fn-own-feed-dists-of-reconfigure) admits the in-flight article's Distribution (fn-own-feed-distributions-of, RFC 5536 section 3.2.4, case-folded) under fn-own-feed-distribution-admitsp; KEYSTONE fn-own-submission-targets-keep-an-admitted-peer, the filter removes nothing else (a peer the scope decision names, whose filter admits the article and whose queue lacks the Message-ID, is a target); books/owner-feed.lisp KEYSTONE fn-own-feed-distribution-targets-member (the filter is exactly the decision). The PKT-400 keystone fn-own-submission-offers-a-control-article-under-its-newsgroups-and-filing-group gains the distribution literal. RFC 5537 section 3.6 paragraph 2; local policy: no filter feeds everything, no Distribution is world, a malformed Distribution matches no filter.

proofs.title: A cancel's authority is exactly a granted signed canceller or the poster: an unsigned cancel or Supersedes withdraws its target exactly when one of its RFC 8315 Cancel-Key entries opens one of the target's sha256 Cancel-Locks; the octets the owner stores for an account's POST carry exactly one Cancel-Lock keyed by that account under an HKDF purpose key, outside the D25 source
proofs.statement: Withdrawal (unchanged): over fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals / fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals, the record of a cause withdraws a target exactly when the cause names another target and either a verified principal P signed it or P's grants cover its groups, or no principal is verified and a Cancel-Key K of the cause has Base64(SHA-256(K)) among the target's sha256 Cancel-Locks (fn-ctl-withdrawal-authority-is-exactly-signer-or-poster; fn-ctl-verified-cause-ignores-its-keys). Stored octets: books/owner-served-invariants.lisp fn-own-sub-stored-octets CFG SUB RING (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-take; the completion gate compares the same function): for a served submission by account A (fn-own-sub-account, recorded by fn-own-finish-read from the session subject) with a key ring installed (fn-ns-ringp), unsigned and with no poster Cancel-Lock, the stored octets are `Cancel-Lock: sha256:Base64(SHA-256(K))` CRLF, then on a cancel `Cancel-Key:` with one key per retained epoch, then the injected octets unchanged, K = Base64(keyed-BLAKE3(key, hex(A) || MSGID)) with key the BLAKE3 derive_key purpose key of the current epoch (context fn/cancel-lock/v2, material the root and the node identity; HMAC-SHA256 under HKDF-SHA256 up to store format 9, RFC 8315 section 4 leaving the MAC's hash to the agent) (fn-own-stored-octets-carry-the-account-lock, fn-cl-served-payload-writes-one-account-lock). D25: the projection fn-cll-skip that books/poster-bytes.lisp reads both compared payloads through gives the injected octets for every ring and account (fn-own-stored-octets-keep-the-injected-octets, fn-cl-served-payload-projects-to-the-injected-octets, fn-cll-skip-of-the-generated-lines), so a same-source retry by any account or key epoch is :duplicate and a different source :conflict at fn-rcl-existing-action (fn-cld-a-retry-by-any-account-or-epoch-is-already-stored, fn-cld-a-changed-source-is-a-conflict-whatever-the-account). Rotation: a cancel's keys open a lock made under any retained epoch (fn-cl-ring-keys-open-every-retained-lock). Exactly the account's key opens its lock up to the stated collision (fn-cl-account-key-opens-exactly-its-lock). Derivation: distinct info labels are distinct derive_key contexts (fn-ns-purpose-inputs-separate-by-definition); the key file round-trips (fn-ns-file-parse-of-render). Not theorems: that the written line parses back as the entry (teeth on parsed stored octets); that another account's key opens nothing (a SHA-256 collision of two keyed-BLAKE3 outputs under a key the forger does not hold: about 2^-128 per chosen pair); keyed-BLAKE3 and derive_key pseudorandomness. PKT-575 (PRF-256): the plan's first arm is the node's own authority (fn-ctl-node-authorizesp: a configuration row (CAUSE TARGET REASON 1) the operator wrote), and the keystone's right side is `the node authorizes CAUSE for TARGET, or` the signer/poster condition; the effect answers :node for such a record. RECORDS FLIP (flip-books-residue, 2026-09-27): the held payload is an arena handle; the subject is fn-store-existing-action (books/store-intern.lisp), which the host calls after flip-L6 at fn-owner-existing-action, fn-owner-prepare and host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-existing-action, and at fn-owner-existing-action-buffer through fn-pidx-existing-action (fn-pidx-existing-action-is-store-existing-action); the held-payload hypothesis reads the bytes under the held handle through the arena the verdict reads (fn-handle-bytes). The pre-flip statements over fn-rcl-existing-action equated a handle with octets and were vacuous on a flipped Store. After the records flip (flip-L8-2) the target's Cancel-Lock entries are its row's control fact, carried by the record as TLOCKS (fn-ctl-w-with-tlocks) and read by fn-ctl-withdrawal-effect's key arm; the keystone is stated over the plan resolved to TLOCKS.

proofs.title: The served reader answers NEWGROUPS and LIST ACTIVE.TIMES from the configuration's creation stamps, LIST SUBSCRIPTIONS from the configured default list, LIST OVERVIEW.FMT in the compatibility form, and ARTICLE, HEAD and HDR with this node's Xref
proofs.statement: PKT-665..668 (lane reader-compat, 2026-09-27): over the pinned dispatcher the served step calls (books/nntp.lisp fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned, reached from fn-served-dispatch), fn-rcompat-reply answers, with a server name in the environment: NEWGROUPS and LIST ACTIVE.TIMES as the generic replies over the environment's facts held by the view (a name is listed exactly when the view's groups hold it and a fact dates it at or after the threshold, fn-rcompat-newgroups-names-member); the facts are the served entries' created stamps with a wall reading (fn-oag-group-facts-has-the-created-stamp, fn-oag-group-facts-are-group-facts), installed by fn-post-reader-env (fn-post-reader-env-facts); LIST SUBSCRIPTIONS 215 with the configured default list (config delta code 25) cut to the view in configured order, else the view's groups (fn-rcompat-subscription-names-member, -keep-the-configured-order); ARTICLE/HEAD the generic reply over the served representation, the stored octets with the Xref line inserted at the end of the header block and nothing else changed (fn-rcompat-served-payload-inserts-one-line, fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned-article-head-is-served), with the generic retrieval's session (fn-rcompat-retrieval-session-is-the-generic-session); HDR/XHDR Xref the value of that field (fn-rcompat-hdr-value-is-the-field-value). The served LIST OVERVIEW.FMT names Bytes:/Lines: (RFC 3977 8.4.2). Every reply is well-formed (fn-nntp-effects-rcompat-reply) and the session invariant is preserved (fn-rcompat-reply-preserves-consistent-session); without a server nothing changes (fn-rcompat-reply-without-a-server).
