proofs.title: The records freeze: the arena is an attachable generic with its byte array attached (the catalog's dependents certified once); the handle's identity, extent and lifetime over the intern; replay over the retained view equals replay over the wire view (the index fn-sn-recover recomputes and the verdicts fn-sn-finish decides, from the rows' contexts); payload identity across reclamation
proofs.statement: books/payload-arena.lisp: fn-arena is an attachable abstract stobj (defabsstobj ... :attachable t) whose logical value is the list of sealed payloads (fn-arn-payload-listp) and whose own foundation is the list-backed reference fn-arena$l; its obligations (fn-arena-count{correspondence} ... fn-arena-clear{preserved}) are proved over that foundation; the opened view, the immutability keystones (fn-arena-seal-keeps-sealed, fn-arena-seals-keep-sealed, fn-arena-seal-new-handle, fn-arena-seal-count) and the store relation (fn-arn-store-corr-of-commit, -of-open) keep their statements over the generic; the export fn-arena-seal-range (the octet buffer's cells [A, B) sealed as one payload; the byte array copies the cells with no list) with fn-arena-seal-range-is-seal-list (no hypothesis: it is fn-arena-seal-list of the slice), the interface books/catalog-load-index.lisp's fn-obi-seal-range attaches behind. books/payload-arena-bytes.lisp: fn-arena-bytes is the byte-array implementation (the concrete stobj fn-arena$c, fn-arena$corr and every obligation of PRF-118, unchanged in proof, under the names fn-arena-bytes-*{...}) with the SAME logical side (fn-arena$ap, create-fn-arena$a, the seven fn-arena$a-*). books/payload-arena-attach.lisp evaluates (attach-stobj fn-arena fn-arena-bytes) before the generic, so every book that names fn-arena (books/catalog-record.lisp and the catalog above it) executes over the byte array from the certificate it was certified with (fn-paa-smoke: the intern of a ground record into the live attached arena materializes to the record); the image includes it first. books/records-freeze.lisp, over the generic: fn-rfz-served-bytes-by-definition (the octets the served ARTICLE writes from the interned handle are the wire payload), fn-rfz-intern-extent (fn-arena-payload-len of the handle is the fn-hf-octets fact the intern decided; no hypothesis), fn-rfz-projection-bytes-by-definition (under fn-record-shapep, fn-record-encode of the materialized held record is the wire encoding). fn-rfz-contexts-okp (rows keyring generation fn-arena): every row's context is fn-held-context-of its bytes by handle under keyring and generation. KEYSTONE fn-rfz-replay-index-over-both-views: under fn-rfz-contexts-okp alone, (fn-rfz-index-of-rows rows) -- fn-stx-index-add of each row's fn-hc-delta, no bytes -- equals (fn-stx-index-of-store (fn-rfz-articles-of-rows rows fn-arena) keyring), the store's own recomputation from the bytes (the function fn-sn-recover calls over fn-stx-store of the replayed node); fn-rfz-handles-inp is the guard's requirement, not the theorem's (the weakened theorem is what is proved). KEYSTONE fn-rfz-replay-verdicts-over-both-views: under the same invariant the rows' (msgid . fn-hc-verdict) list equals the wire view's (msgid . fn-stx-verdict-of-octets of the payload under keyring and generation), the verdict fn-sn-finish decides per record. The invariant's life: fn-rfz-intern-context (the intern establishes it for the row it builds, no hypothesis), fn-rfz-handles-inp-survives-seals and fn-rfz-contexts-okp-survives-seals (any later seals keep it), KEYSTONE fn-rfz-load-establishes-contexts (fn-cat-load, the host's open from the journal or a checkpoint, establishes it for every row it commits under the keyring and generation it interns with, from a catalog in the invariant) and fn-rfz-load-from-empty-establishes-contexts. Payload identity across reclamation: fn-rfz-pinned-rows-survive-seals (under fn-rfz-handles-inp, a pinned row list materializes the same after any seals: immutable references in the view), fn-rfz-reclaim-old-view-reads-the-original (a row whose handle is below the count materializes the same after the tombstone's seal) and fn-rfz-reclaim-new-row-reads-the-tombstone (the row pointed at the count before the seal materializes to the tombstone; no hypothesis), and the versioned mapping fn-rfz-resolve with fn-rfz-resolve-before-reclaim (a reader at version V <= W, the reclaim's version, resolves the original handle), fn-rfz-resolve-after-reclaim (W < V resolves the tombstone's); both handles keep their bytes under later seals by fn-arena-seals-keep-sealed (PRF-118, cited). NOT in this target: the store state's replay over a history of held rows (fn-sn-recover over held records needs the acceptance state's payload field to be a handle: lane acceptance-payload-arena, PKT-635) and the host's calls (catalog-slice-5's step 8): no host line calls fn-cat-load or the arena yet, so the measurement of retained bytes per octet on the joined owner is that join's.

proofs.title: store import and operator init publication (P-IMPORT, P-INIT-PUB): a crash or an ambiguous rename/barrier outcome leaves no store at ROOT or the complete imported (init: complete empty) store, never replaces an unrelated destination, and recovery classifies by what it observes
proofs.statement: books/store-import-publication.lisp fn-bs-imp-program-crash-is-no-store-or-the-complete-store: for a fresh process (nothing pending), an existing parent directory, distinct STAGE and ROOT names and plan files inside the staged tree, at every pair of every run of fn-bs-imp-program under any well-formed syscall outcomes (fn-bs-imp-outcomesp: :ok or an error pair, including (errno . :issued) renames and failed barriers with torn landings) and every crash choice, ROOT's durable entry is its old one (none, or an unrelated destination untouched), or -- only when ROOT was absent -- the staged directory with every subdirectory named and every plan file named and durable with exactly its octets. fn-bs-imp-classify-by-what-is-known: fn-bs-imp-classify over the two observable names answers :no-store/:not-published only when ROOT is absent and :store-present/:publication-uncertain only when ROOT is the complete staged tree. Host: host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-store-import (through fnn-staged-publication) writes the program step for step (cuts +fnn-import-model-cuts+, renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE on Linux) and calls fn-bs-imp-classify before writing and after an error at or after the rename. operator init's plan is PRF-268's (books/store-init-log-publication.lisp fn-bs-init-log-program, the same program with the record log's plan and init's cut names from books/store-init-publication.lisp *fn-bs-init-pub-cut-names*); fn-bs-init-pub-admission (host: fnn-command-init-published, called by operator init) proceeds only when neither ROOT.init-* nor ROOT is present. Host: fnn-staged-publication is the one transcription for both. Scope: the ordinary open between staged-durable and the rename is its own program (P-RECOVER) and is modelled here as the cut import-validated; OpenBSD has no renameat2: import and init hold an exclusive flock on ROOT.lock for the whole program and re-check ROOT's absence under it before rename(2); a process ignoring the lock that creates an empty directory at ROOT in that window is the documented residual.

proofs.title: The record log's scan reads back a well-formed log exactly, and a torn append scans to the old history, the new record, or a forgery
proofs.statement: books/store-log.lisp (the storage-log design's prototype, planning/design-2026-09-27-storage-log.md section 5.2). An entry is an FNLG frame whose payload is the previous entry's trailer (32 octets, the chain) and the committed record's octets, padded with zeros to the write unit (fn-lg-entry); a log is the chained entries of a record list from a genesis trailer (fn-lg-log); the scan reads complete chained entries from the front and answers (records . aligned-end) (fn-lg-scan). fn-lg-scan-of-log-append: for (fn-frame-digestp prev) and (fn-lg-recordsp records max), the scan of (append (fn-lg-log records prev unit) x) is (append records (car (scan x from the log's last trailer))) with the log's length added to the consumed count; fn-lg-scan-of-log: alone, exactly (cons records (len log)): the frontier is the last complete entry's end. fn-lg-torn-variant-len: a torn variant of a write (fn-bs-torn-variantp, the byte model's crash of the one pending write) is no longer than the write. fn-lg-scan-of-torn-entry: for a record within max and a torn variant OBSERVED of (fn-lg-entry prev record unit), the scan of OBSERVED is (nil . 0), or (cons (list record) (len entry)), or (fn-lg-forgeryp observed prev max frame): the first slice validates as a chained frame and is not the written one, the event A-CRYPTO-TRAILER excludes (SHA-256's collision figure, about 2^-128, quoted pessimistically). fn-lg-scan-of-log-then-torn-entry: the composition over a log followed by a torn append. The shift lemma (a crash of an aligned append to a NON-EMPTY inode) and the A-CRYPTO-TRAILER corollary are lane log-core's (planning/briefs-wave5/w6-log-core.txt).

proofs.title: The header limits of one article are the operator's: the parse under a profile's limits admits exactly the headers within them and refuses the next by name, and readers parse under the ceiling so raising a limit never changes an admitted article
proofs.statement: For any limits WIDER under which OCTETS parses, fn-article-parse-under OCTETS LIMITS is that same article exactly when the input's header census (fields, physical lines, octets before the blank line, read by the parser's own line scanner) is within LIMITS, and otherwise a refusal whose code is :header-fields-limit, :header-lines-limit or :header-octets-limit (fn-article-parse-under-admits-exactly-the-limits); by instance a success is within its limits (fn-article-parse-under-within-its-limits) and a success under LIMITS is the same article under any wider limits (fn-article-parse-under-raised-limits-agree). fn-article-parse, which every reader of a stored or received article calls, is the ceiling limits' instance (fn-article-parse-is-the-ceiling-limits-by-definition). For an input the reading parser admits, fn-article-census-refusal of the census against LIMITS is NIL exactly when the parse under LIMITS admits it (and then equals the reading parse), and otherwise a limit's name while that parse refuses by a limit's name (fn-article-census-refusal-is-the-parse); fn-inj-decide (books/injection.lisp, called by the served POST through the owner's configuration, whose header limits host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-served-post-bound takes from the opened profile's fields 15 to 17, fn-bs-profile-header-limits) refuses by exactly that census refusal. The parse's work under any limits is bounded by fn-article-parse-under-work-budget (fn-article-parse-under-work-input-bound). PKT-660 (the coordinator's default): the peer transfer decision the host calls, fn-peer-decide-transfer-under (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide, with the owner's limits fn-own-config-header-limits), admits a relayed article exactly when the parse of the octets it would store (fn-peer-relayed-octets) under the limits admits them, and otherwise refuses by a limit's name (437/439) where fn-peer-decide-transfer wanted or deferred (fn-peer-decide-transfer-under-admits-exactly-the-limits), and wants only what fn-peer-decide-transfer wants (fn-peer-decide-transfer-under-wants-only-what-transfer-wants); the owner's BP transit delivery fn-own-bp-transit-submit-result submits only within the limits and is refused past them (fn-own-bp-transit-submits-only-within-the-limits, fn-own-bp-transit-refuses-past-the-limits); the owner's control delivery fn-own-control-decision (BP application and CLI articles) injects only within the limits and past them refuses by a limit's name (fn-own-control-decision-injects-only-within-the-limits, fn-own-control-decision-refuses-past-the-limits-by-name).

proofs.title: The BP application handoff's reported outcome is the application's disposition: a refused delivery is reported refused by name, never durable
proofs.statement: books/bp-handoff-report.lisp over books/bp-node-foundation.lisp. fn-bpah-persist-delivery-step's durable answer is (:delivery-answer :durable D), D the kind-7 record's disposition; fn-bpah-handoff-report (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-drive-effects prints exactly its word for every :delivery-answer that fnn-bps-foundation-step returns) is :durable exactly for an accepting disposition and :refused for a refusing one. KEYSTONE fn-bpah-handoff-report-is-application-disposition: after fn-bpah-deliver-result-step records the application's STATUS and issues kind 7 ((car e1) = :persist-delivery), the report of fn-bpah-persist-delivery-step's answer to that publication is a member of (list (fn-bpah-disposition-report STATUS) :uncertain), and with RESULT :durable and the record applying to the held list it equals (fn-bpah-disposition-report STATUS). fn-bpah-persist-delivery-reports-the-record (hypothesis-free) and fn-bpah-persist-delivery-reports-exactly state the same for the publication step alone; fn-bpah-disposition-report-durable-is-accepting: the report is :durable iff the disposition is accepting. fn-bpnf-step-deliver-result-is-step and fn-bpnf-step-persist-delivery-is-step: the foundation dispatcher fn-bpnf-step routes the host's two events (host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-dispatch-one) to these steps. Why: SCN-077's 10 MiB case printed 'BP application handoff durable' while its development-base Store (32,768-octet articles) had refused the article as oversize (PKT-630 (7)). What it does not say: that the layers above fn-bpnf-step (fn-bpnj-step, fn-bpnp-step, the fragment step) pass the answer's effects through unchanged (they do by definition, or replace a :deliver answer by (:delivery-answer :uncertain), which reports :uncertain); that STATUS is the Store's true verdict (the application layer's theorems, PRF-128/PRF-132 and the FNRJ receipt books, own that).

proofs.title: The executed BP CRC-16/X.25 is table-driven and equals the bitwise definition every bundle theorem reasons about
proofs.statement: books/bp-primary.lisp. fn-bpp-crc16-scan executes (mbe :exec) fn-bpp-crc16-scan-table: per octet, c = (logand (logxor crc x) 65535) and the next register (logand (logxor (ash c -8) (fn-bpp-crc16-table-ref (logand c 255))) 65535), the 256-entry table *fn-bpp-crc16-table* evaluated from fn-bpp-crc16-octet at every octet value by the defconst (it cannot drift). KEYSTONE fn-bpp-crc16-scan-table-is-scan: (implies (and (natp crc) (fn-cbor-octet-listp xs)) (equal (fn-bpp-crc16-scan-table crc xs) (fn-bpp-crc16-scan crc xs))), the guard proof of fn-bpp-crc16-scan. The octet step is checked at every one of the 65,536 16-bit registers by evaluation inside the proof (local fn-bpp-crc16-step-agrees), so the logical definitions, and every theorem about fn-bpp-crc16, fn-bpb-encode and the bundle codec, are unchanged. Host: every block CRC the node computes (fn-bpb-encode-block-with-crc, the decoders' checks) through fn-bpp-crc16; the reassembled whole bundle's encode in fn-bpnf-family-plan (bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-fragment-progress -> fn-bpnf-family-next, and the kind-18 publication). Why: sb-sprof over the receiver that reassembled and delivered a 1 MiB fragment family: 77 percent of CPU in fn-bpp-crc16-scan's bitwise steps (FLOOR 25.8 percent self, FN-BPP-CRC16-BIT 37 percent cumulative); a 1 MiB CRC now takes 0.06 s in the REPL. What it does not say: anything about CRC-32C (PRF-190) or the list representation of the payload (D27's by-handle encoder, PKT-630 (4)).

proofs.title: The BP application join and the receiver hold a request by reference, and every read binds exactly the live request's context
proofs.statement: books/bp-request-ref.lisp, books/bp-request-reference.lisp over books/bp-receipt.lisp, books/bp-native-app.lisp, books/bp-native-app-fast.lisp and books/bp-transit-join.lisp (PKT-646, D27, D34). The FNRJ transit intent and context the host publishes (host/bp-receipt-journal-host.lisp fn-bprj-request-transit-intent-record and fn-bprj-request-transit-context-record, called by host/native/bp-app.lisp fnn-bpapp-request-intent and fnn-bpapp-bind-context) are built by fn-bpaj-transit-intent-from-plan (host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-plan-install) and fn-bpaj-transit-context-record: the intent carries the request's reference (HEAD LENGTH DIGEST, fn-bpaj-request-ref), the relay projection's LENGTH and DIGEST and the pinned Path identities; the context carries the reference and the Store record's identity (Message-ID, txid, generation); neither carries the request ADU, the projection or the Store record. The receiver's context (books/bp-receipt.lisp fn-bpr-context-request-ref, slot 9) holds the reference, and fn-bpr-receipt-adu and the conflict rule compare references. KEYSTONE fn-bpaj-ref-request-resolves-exactly: (implies (fn-bpa-requestp request) (equal (fn-bpaj-ref-request HEAD LENGTH DIGEST (fn-bpa-request-article request)) request)); -to-the-bytes: its encoding is the request's octets. KEYSTONE fn-bpaj-transit-context-binds-the-live-request: for ctx = (fn-bpaj-transit-context-record inbound octets store-record g txid rg result), the receiver context every read binds over any record, (fn-bpr-context-from-ref record (fn-bpaj-context-ref ctx)), is (fn-bpr-context-from-request record (fn-bpaj-request octets)) and its reference is the request's; the read is fn-bpaj-apply-record (fn-bpaj-transit-context-receiver-is-existing-transition: the receiver is fn-bpr-accept-projected-ref over fn-bpaj-context-record, the Store record resolved by identity) and its fast twin (fn-bpaj-apply-record-fast-is-checked, fn-bpaj-context-record-fast-is-checked) at fn-bprj-install (every journal open, recovery included), fn-bprj-preflight and fn-bprj-apply. KEYSTONE fn-bpaj-transit-intent-pins-its-request-and-projection: an intent the builder answers names the request (fn-bpaj-intent-names-requestp) and pins the length and digest of (fn-pu-relay-article article local peer) under its own Path identities, which is the plan's stored projection. The receiver invariants (bp-receiver-store, -retention, -evolving-history) ground a context by resolving its reference over the grounding record's payload (fn-bpr-context-resolve; fn-bpr-context-resolve-of-derived-context from the keystone); their receipt conclusions now say the live request's reference is the context's. fn-bpaj-one-reference-is-one-request-or-a-digest-collision: two requests with one reference are equal or their articles differ with one length and one fn-frame-digest (A-CRYPTO, books/frame-octets; for n distinct articles the SHA-256 collision probability is at most n(n-1)/2^257). D34: the local :request-intent and :request-context-v2 kinds, their builders, the direct Store lookup and fn-owner-app-plan-install-legacy are deleted. What it does not say: that the Store keeps the record a context names (the replay refuses a context whose record is gone); that a Store record's payload IS the projection (length and digest, the collision scope above); the legacy version-1 :request-context kind still carries a request ADU (the receiver-journal model's, reached only before a journal's first intent).

proofs.title: BP fragment reassembly as a resumable step bounded in octets: any schedule of bounded steps reaches the one RFC 9171 reassembly
proofs.statement: books/bp-fragment-resume.lisp over books/bp-fragment-sweep.lisp. fn-bpfr-step runs the executed reassembler's sweep (fn-bpfw-sweep-acc) for at most QUANTUM positions and returns its state (active suffixes, queue, position, positions left, cells). KEYSTONE fn-bpfr-step-resumes (hypothesis-free): resuming the sweep from the state one step leaves equals the sweep from the state before it. KEYSTONE fn-bpfr-run-is-reassemble: for (posp quantum), steps of QUANTUM run to completion from fn-bpfr-start leave no position, and fn-bpfr-finish of the result is fn-bpfw-reassemble and fn-bpfw-spec (the uncapped reference), for every fragment list and total: complete, missing, conflicting and invalid families alike. fn-bpfr-step-is-bounded: a step consumes and emits exactly min(QUANTUM, left) positions and cells. What it does not say: that the node calls it -- the family plan (bp-node-fragment-family) still reassembles in one foundation step; carrying the state across steps, and assembling into the Store's arena by extents (PKT-585) instead of an octet list, are the integration boundary.

proofs.title: A consumer wait answers exactly the consumer's poll at the moment it returns: a refusal or an event at once, the empty page only at its deadline; it sleeps only on an empty page, and waiters are bounded by name
proofs.statement: books/consumer-wait.lisp and books/consumer-wait-codec.lisp. Subjects: fn-cwait-step and fn-cwait-admit (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-wait-step / -wait-admit, called under the owner mutex by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-consumer-local-wait for local-control codes 9 and 10, which sleeps between steps on the owner's commit signal fnn-owner-signal-commit, raised by fnn-owner-publish-prepared after each durable publication and by a stop); fn-cwait-request-encode / -decode and fn-cwait-cli-plan (host/native-control-host.lisp fn-native-control-host-consumer-request-encode / -decode / -cli-plan). The poll a step runs is fn-cwait-poll: fn-cbind-poll for a bound wait, fn-cbind-plain-poll for a plain one (PRF-234). KEYSTONES: fn-cwait-step-is-the-poll-or-a-sleep-on-an-empty-page (a step answers exactly the poll, or sleeps only on an accepted empty page before the deadline for a positive time ending at the deadline; an empty answer only at or after the deadline; every step at or after the deadline answers; a non-empty answer is never slept over); fn-cwait-run-answers-the-poll-at-its-return-point and fn-cwait-run-sleeps-only-over-empty-pages (the loop over the observed owner states: the answer is the poll of the state it returned in, an empty answer only at the deadline, and every earlier observation an empty page before the deadline); fn-cwait-admit-leaves-workers-free (an admitted wait leaves at least four of the sixteen control workers free; past the capacity of 12 a wait is refused :waiters); fn-cwait-wait-request-roundtrip and fn-cwait-bound-wait-request-roundtrip (the wire), fn-cwait-request-decode-of-another-code-is-the-consumer-decode and fn-cwait-cli-plan-of-another-command-is-the-consumer-plan (every other request and command is the consumer codec's, unchanged). Local policy; no RFC requirement. RECORDS FLIP (flip-bridge, 2026-09-27): the wait's poll over held rows reads the payload through the arena: fn-cwait-step-over (books/consumer-wait.lisp, over books/consumer-bound.lisp fn-cbind-poll-over / fn-cbind-plain-poll-over) carries KEYSTONE 1 (fn-cwait-step-over-is-the-poll-or-a-sleep-on-an-empty-page) and equals fn-cwait-step whenever the selected event is no held row (fn-cwait-step-over-is-step-unless-a-held-row). host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-wait-step still calls fn-cwait-step (REQUEST to the host lane); KEYSTONE 2 over the arena (flip-books-residue): fn-cwait-run-over-answers-the-poll-at-its-return-point and fn-cwait-run-over-sleeps-only-over-empty-pages, the loop over fn-cwait-step-over whose observations carry the payloads sealed since the previous one (a durable publication seals, then raises the commit signal): the answer is the poll over the arena as it stood at the return point, an empty answer only at the deadline, and every observation slept over an empty page before the deadline.

proofs.title: The open's replay answers its known-id and accepted tests from tries it builds as it advances, and the history recognizer reads each record's kind once, each equal to the reference; a POST's budget test reads the event index's carried count
proofs.statement: Subjects, called by the host: fn-rii-sco-extend (books/replay-identity-index.lisp) from host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-recover and fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint and host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover and fn-owner-recover-from-checkpoint; fn-rii-classified-open from host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-extended; fn-pidx-sbud-prepare (books/post-identity-index.lisp) from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer. (1) The open's replay fold carries IX, a pair of tries beside the configured node: a Message-ID trie EQUAL to fn-midx-build of the node's articles and an obligation-id trie that holds exactly the ledger's known ids for every string (fn-rii-known-okp, a guard-verified defun-sk); fn-rii-okp is the pair. fn-rii-acceptedp-is-acceptedp, fn-rii-admissiblep-is-admissiblep, fn-rii-node-prepare-is-node-prepare, fn-rii-apply-retention-event-is-apply-retention-event, fn-rii-apply-record-is-apply-record and fn-rii-cpr-apply-event-is-cpr-apply-event: under fn-rii-okp each twin equals its reference. fn-rii-ix-next-keeps-okp: the tries after a step (Message-ID trie by fn-midx-refresh; id trie kept when the ledger is unchanged or the step was a release, one id added when the step consed one pin, else rebuilt) are related to the new node, given the relation before and, for a release event, that the new node is the replay's step (fn-rii-release-step-keeps-known: a replayed release keeps what the ledger knows). fn-rii-okp-of-ix-of: the tries built from any node are related to it. KEYSTONE fn-rii-sco-cpr-prefix-is-sco-cpr-prefix: under fn-rii-okp of the starting node the carried fold equals fn-sco-cpr-prefix for every configuration and event history; fn-rii-sco-cpr-resume-is-sco-cpr-resume (no hypothesis: the resume builds the tries from the paused node); KEYSTONE fn-rii-sco-extend-is-sco-extend: (fn-rii-sco-extend c configs suffix) = (fn-sco-extend c configs suffix), no hypothesis. (2) fn-event-fields-of-rows-is-the-dispatchers (books/store-event-fields.lisp; fn-event-fields with WIREP nil, the function the pack-chain link check reads with WIREP t, PKT-721): one dispatch answers fn-store-event-p, -sequence, -txid and -generation of a retained row; fn-rii-sf-record-listp-is-sf-record-listp, fn-rii-sf-statep-is-sf-statep, fn-rii-sn-statep-is-sn-statep, fn-rii-observed-historyp-is-observed-historyp, fn-rii-sco-finalize-from-is-sco-finalize-from, fn-rii-sco-store-open-is-sco-store-open, KEYSTONE fn-rii-classified-open-is-classified-open: (fn-rii-classified-open e configs frontier) = (fn-sopc-classified-open e configs frontier), no hypothesis. (3) fn-pidx-sbud-prepare's budget test reads fn-sbud-count (the event index's carried count); fn-pidx-sbud-prepare-is-pcar-sbud-prepare gains the hypothesis fn-ceis-indexedp of the owner's Store (fn-sbud-count-is-used-by-definition), which every owner the host reaches carries (PRF-144 fn-osi-live-owner-store-is-indexed). Every function is guard-verified. Teeth: tests/acl2/replay-identity-index-tests.lisp (a mixed history: undertaking, release, two configuration records, two articles; both host paths; each identity refusal decided alike; corrupted tries holding a fake Message-ID or a fake id make the twin refuse the article the scan admits, for the step, the configured step and the fold; the release condition removed by a node that is not the release's step; the relation removed with a fake id kept), tests/acl2/post-identity-index-tests.lisp (a Store whose event index claims 100 records refuses at budget 100 where the reference stages).

proofs.title: A crash of a batch's one aligned append scans to the committed records and a prefix of the batch, or a forgery the crypto-trailer assumption excludes (T2)
proofs.statement: books/store-log-crash.lisp (design 2026-09-27-storage-log section 5.1 T2). fn-lg-tear-write-is-pieces: fn-bs-tear-write of (:write ino (* k unit) w) at unit index i equals the per-unit piece list fn-lg-pieces at offset k*unit + i*unit over (nthcdr (* i unit) w). fn-bs-crash-of-aligned-append (the shift lemma): for (posp (fn-bs-unit s)), a true-list d with (len d) = k*unit, durable content of ino = (append d z) and the pending list exactly ((:write ino (len d) w)), every crash image's content of ino is (append d (fn-lg-apply-to z (fn-lg-pieces ino 0 w sels unit))) with sels the image's selectors. fn-lg-batch-tear-is-a-prefix: for (fn-frame-digestp prev), (fn-lg-recordsp batch max), a zero region z (fn-lg-zerosp: the preallocated extent) at least as long as (fn-lg-log batch prev unit), the scan of any tear of that log over z is a prefix P of batch with consumed count (len (fn-lg-log P prev unit)) (fn-lg-prefix-verdictp), or fn-lg-forgery-in: the first damaged entry's slice validates as a chained frame that is not the written one. fn-lg-batch-crash-is-a-prefix: over the store, when the durable prefix d scans completely to COMMITTED ending on LAST, every crash image scans to COMMITTED ++ a prefix of the batch with the frontier past exactly that prefix's log (fn-lg-crash-verdictp), or the forgery. fn-lg-batch-crash-is-a-prefix-under-a-crypto-trailer: with fn-lg-platform-tears-p (each entry's observed slice is fn-assume-crash-tearp of its frame, A-CRYPTO-TRAILER) the forgery disjunct goes (fn-lg-no-forgery-under-a-crypto-trailer, from fn-assume-crash-tear-never-validates-unless-exact). The pessimistic figure is SHA-256's collision figure, about 2^-128 per chosen pair. Scope: the store's pending list is the log's one write (other inodes' pending operations are not in the hypothesis; PKT-682).

The removals of the scan-last, digest, records, extent-length and alignment hypotheses are not refuted by a ground witness (a mis-chained batch scans to COMMITTED, which satisfies the verdict) and are not removed (no weakened theorem proved).

proofs.title: The log kernel's relation R to the segment is established by P-LOG-RECOVER (T3) and preserved by P-BATCH's steps, and every crash image of a related state scans to the committed records and a prefix of the batch in flight
proofs.statement: books/store-log-kernel.lisp (design section 4). R = fn-lgk-relp: posp unit; ino in the inode table; fn-lgk-content-okp of the durable content c: c a true list and a whole number of units; the frontier f unit-aligned and within c; (fn-lg-scan (fn-bs-take f c) genesis unit max) = (committed . f) and its fn-lg-scan-last is LAST, a digest; (nthcdr f c) all zeros; the batch and the batch in flight are record lists; f plus the in-flight log's length within c; committed a true list; acked <= (len committed); and the pending list is exactly ((:write ino f (fn-lg-log inflight last unit))) when a batch is in flight, else empty. fn-lgk-append-preserves-relation: from R with nothing in flight, not faulted, the batch fitting the extent, the state after (fn-bs-write bs ino f (fn-lgk-append-octets ks unit) :ok) is related to (fn-lgk-append ks unit extent). fn-lgk-fence-preserves-relation: the state after (fn-bs-fsync-file bs ino :ok) is related to (fn-lgk-fence ks unit) (the batch committed, LAST its last trailer, the frontier past its log). fn-lgk-prepare-/finish-one-/known-abort-preserves-relation: the byte store unchanged. fn-lgk-crash-of-related-state-is-a-prefix: T2 (PRF-244) lifted to R. Establishment by P-LOG-RECOVER (T3) is open (PKT-682). books/store-log-recover.lisp (lane w6-log-core-2): fn-lg-recovered-frontier-is-the-last-complete-record (T3): for (posp unit), a true-list c whose length is a multiple of unit, the scan's consumed count f is within c and unit-aligned, and (fn-bs-take f c) scans to the same (records . f) and ends on the same trailer. fn-lgk-recover-establishes-relation: for (posp (fn-bs-unit bs)), ino in the inode table, its durable content c a true list and a whole number of units, (fn-frame-digestp genesis), no pending write of ino, and the owner obligation fn-assume-log-sole-pending-writer (a constrained function whose constraint is that no pending operation names another inode; lane w6-log-owner discharges it by functional instantiation), the store after (fn-bs-write bs ino f (fn-bs-zeros (- (len c) f)) :ok) then (fn-bs-fsync-file _ ino :ok) is R-related to (fn-lgk-recover c genesis unit max next-txid). fn-lg-scan-last-digestp: the scan ends on a digest. books/store-log-txid.lisp (lane w6-log-core-3, T5 of design section 5.1): fn-lgt-txid reads a record's txid through the codec (fn-record-decode-exact-impl); fn-lgt-okp: along committed ++ inflight ++ batch every record decodes and the txids strictly increase, each below next-txid. fn-lgt-prepare admits a record only when its txid is next-txid (else the state is unchanged); fn-lgt-recover sets next-txid to one past the largest scanned txid or the floor. fn-lgt-*-preserves-okp: prepare (checked), known-abort, append, fence, fence-failed, finish-one preserve fn-lgt-okp with no other hypothesis; fn-lgt-prepare-preserves-relation. fn-lg-txids-strictly-increase (T5): from R, fn-lgt-okp, a batch in flight, a crash image and fn-lg-platform-tears-p over the image past the frontier (A-CRYPTO-TRAILER), the kernel fn-lgt-recover of the image's content satisfies fn-lgt-okp: the durable txids strictly increase along the scan and the recovered next-txid exceeds each. Scope: the batch-in-flight case (the cuts with nothing in flight have no pending write). books/store-log-decode.lisp (lane w6-log-core-3, D27 representation boundary): fn-lg-decode, the executable scan over the segment read as a string (one header read and one range read per entry, tail-recursive, guard-verified with ec-call on the codec helpers of books/store-log.lisp), equals the logical scan with no hypothesis: fn-lg-decode-is-the-scan, (fn-lg-decode s prev unit max) = (mv (car scan) (cdr scan) (fn-lg-scan-last ...)) over (fn-lgd-octets s), the string's character codes. books/store-log-programs.lisp (lane w6-log-core-3): the log-local step language ((:write-at :segment :batch|:tail), (:fence :segment :batch|:tail), (:cut name)) and runner fn-lg-run over fn-bs-write / fn-bs-fsync-file and the kernel; the programs fn-lg-append-program (cut log-written), fn-lg-fence-program (log-fenced), fn-lg-recover-program (log-truncated, log-recovered), hosted by fnn-log-append / fnn-log-fence / fnn-log-recover. fn-lg-append-program-keeps-the-relation and fn-lg-fence-program-keeps-the-relation: from R alone every state of the run (outcomes :ok) is R-related (a refused append keeps the related state); fn-lg-append-program-appends: with nothing in flight, not faulted and the fit, the run reaches log-written at the kernel's append; fn-lg-recover-program-establishes-the-relation: the run from fn-lgt-recover of the durable content has four states and the last (log-recovered) is R-related, under the establishment's hypotheses. fn-lg-open-kernel-is-the-recovered-kernel (no hypothesis): the host's open kernel fn-lg-open-kernel (the decode of the segment string S) equals (fn-lgt-recover (fn-lgd-octets s) genesis unit max floor), the recovered kernel the recovery program's theorem names; fn-lg-append-admitsp is the admission the runner and fnn-log-append share; fn-lg-recover-tail gives the zeroing write's offset and count.

proofs.title: T1: an acknowledged member's record is read by the scan of every admissible crash image (owner batch over the record log)
proofs.statement: books/owner-batch.lisp (design 2026-09-27-storage-log sections 3.3 and 5.1 T1; D33). The batch layer (:owb ks members inflight waiting acked) sits over the log kernel fn-lgk-* (books/store-log-kernel.lisp) and the catalog's token protocol (books/catalog-commit.lisp) and changes neither; fn-owb-alignedp: the open members' records are the kernel's batch, the in-flight members' records its batch in flight, acked ++ waiting's records its committed records and (len acked) its acked count. fn-owb-acknowledged-record-survives-crash: for an aligned layer st, R at the cut (fn-lgk-relp bs (fn-owb-ks st) ino genesis max, PRF-245), a member m of (fn-owb-acked st), an admissible crash image (fn-bs-crash-imagep bs image) and, when a batch is in flight, the tear of its pending write the platform's (fn-lg-platform-tears-p over the image past the frontier, A-CRYPTO-TRAILER), m's record is a member of (car (fn-lg-scan (fn-bs-durable-content image ino) genesis (fn-bs-unit bs) max)). By fn-owb-committed-record-survives-crash (the same for any record of the kernel's committed list), fn-owb-image-scan-of-related-state (with a batch in flight every admissible image's scan satisfies fn-lg-crash-verdictp: the committed records then a prefix of the batch, store-log-crash's corollary under the crypto trailer lifted to R) and fn-owb-scan-of-related-content (with nothing in flight the durable content scans to exactly (committed . frontier), and the related store is fenced on ino). The acknowledgement discipline is the layer's: fn-owb-finish-member acknowledges only the head of WAITING, which fn-owb-fence filled from the fenced batch, so ACKED's records are a prefix of the committed records. Scope: the log's one inode and the pending list the log's one write (R's conjunct, PKT-682 item 7); a member's record is the encoded store event, supplied by the host from fn-owner-pending-octets and computed nowhere else.

proofs.title: T4: the batch of PreparedCommit tokens completes as the sequential token protocol; the batch bounds; the sole-pending-writer obligation discharged
proofs.statement: books/owner-batch.lisp (design section 3.3, 5.1 T4; D33, D27). T4 fn-owb-batch-complete-is-the-sequential-complete: two members prepared as a batch against one catalog (fn-owb-cat-prepare, the second AHEAD of the first: fn-cat-intern of the buffer's bytes, EXPECTED the count the predecessor's complete leaves) and completed in order by token (fn-owb-complete-two: fn-cat-complete each) equal the sequential protocol prepare, complete, prepare, complete (fn-cat-prepare, fn-cat-complete): the same two deltas, the same catalog, the same arena, the count advanced by two. The step fn-owb-prepare-ahead-is-the-sequential-prepare: the token minted AHEAD of n pending completes over a catalog of count c is fn-cat-prepare's token over a catalog of count c + n; the fold over a longer batch is this step repeated, and fn-owb-cat-prepare with nothing ahead is fn-cat-prepare by definition. The content: fn-cat-intern reads no catalog state. The bounds (a work bound per scheduling step, D27): fn-owb-boundedp st unit bmax omax (at most bmax open members; the open batch's log, fn-owb-batch-octets over a fixed genesis digest, at most omax octets); fn-owb-take-, -append-, -fence-, -fence-failed-, -known-abort- and -finish-member-preserves-bounds with no other hypothesis; the keystone fn-owb-batch-within-bounds: a bounded layer's open batch is within both bounds and a take beyond either leaves the layer unchanged. bmax and omax are the operator's live configuration (fn-owb-bmax, fn-owb-omax: the :set-limit slots log-batch-records and log-batch-octets of books/config.lisp; an unset slot means 64 records and the batch buffer's size), not profile fields or kernel constants. Alignment with the kernel is carried by every transition (fn-owb-*-preserves-alignment). The discharge: fn-owb-sole-pending-writer bs ino (no pending operation names another inode) holds of every R-related store (fn-owb-related-state-is-the-sole-pending-writer), and fn-owb-recover-establishes-relation is store-log-recover's fn-lgk-recover-establishes-relation (PRF-245) functionally instantiated with it for the obligation fn-assume-log-sole-pending-writer: the store after zeroing the tail past the recovered frontier and fencing the segment is R-related to fn-lgk-recover of its content. Scope: T4 is stated for two members with the step theorem carrying the fold; the duplicate-within-batch tooth (441 for a repeated Message-ID) waits on the msgid index on the catalog path (PKT-748).

proofs.title: T7: a failed barrier leaves every member uncertain and recovery holds the committed records then a prefix of the batch
proofs.statement: books/owner-batch.lisp (design section 3.3 Barrier and 5.1 T7; fsyncgate). fn-owb-uncertain-batch-recovers-to-a-prefix: for an aligned layer st with kernel ks, R at the cut (fn-lgk-relp bs ks ino genesis max), a batch in flight, the environment's admissible selection over the pending write (fn-bs-crash-choicesp choices (fn-bs-pending bs) (fn-bs-unit bs)) and the tear the platform's (fn-lg-platform-tears-p over the store the failed barrier left, past the frontier; A-CRYPTO-TRAILER): after fn-owb-fence-failed the kernel's phase is :fault, fn-owb-fault-words answers every member waiting or in flight :uncertain, fn-owb-finish-member acknowledges nothing, and the kernel recovered (fn-lgk-recover) from the durable content the failed barrier (fn-bs-fsync-file bs ino (cons :eio choices)) left holds the committed records followed by a prefix (fn-lg-prefixp) of the batch in flight. By fn-owb-fence-failed-answers-uncertain (the layer's half, for any true-list state), fn-owb-failed-fence-is-the-crash-image (when the pending list is the segment's one write, the store a failed fsync leaves is fn-bs-crash of the selection), fn-owb-failed-fence-image-is-admissible (that store is an admissible crash image, fn-bs-crash-imagep) and fn-owb-recovered-kernel-after-a-failed-fence (the kernel's half, from fn-owb-image-scan-of-related-state, PRF-253). Scope: the barrier's error path; the retry half (a member's later visibility join over the log, PRF-115) and the served fence of the store (STO-004's fn-sn machine) are the host's once the commit path moves onto the kernel (PKT-748, PKT-698).

proofs.title: The owner's scheduler bounds a control request's wait at three quanta, and a served reply rendered off the mutex in windows is the reply the served machine decided
proofs.statement: fn-osch-control-waits-at-most-the-bound (books/owner-scheduler.lisp; keystone): for every cursor C and every sequence WS of waiting-count observations in which the control class has a waiter (fn-osch-control-waitsp), the quanta of other classes picked before the first control pick, fn-osch-control-delay, is at most *fn-osch-bound* = 3; the pick is fn-osch-pick of the cursor and the counts (fn-osch-next-is-the-pick), names a slot with a waiter (fn-osch-pick-has-a-waiter) and is nil exactly when nobody waits (fn-osch-pick-nil-iff-idle); the hold/wait fold adds one hold to exactly its class (fn-osch-observe-holds) and keeps a row's buckets summing to its holds (fn-osch-row-observe-keeps-okp). fn-splan-window-is-a-prefix-of-the-reply (books/served-plan.lisp; keystone, no hypothesis on the plan): one window of W octets into the buffer, read as fn-oct-slice-list [0, len), followed by what the continuation still owes (fn-splan-remaining) is what the plan owed, len is at most W, and under :ok a window of an unfinished plan writes at least one octet. fn-splan-windows-are-the-reply (keystone): once a plan built from EFFECTS is drained to done (fn-splan-donep), the concatenation of its windows, for any W and any number of windows, is (fn-served-reply-octets effects). fn-splan-step-plan-remaining: the step's plan owes the step's reply, then the completion, the redeem reply and the exposure close. fn-splan-window-size-is-positive-until-done: the window size ACL2 hands the host before each window (the remaining octets of the effect the window starts in; a materialized effect is rendered whole) is positive exactly while the plan is not done, so the host's window loop progresses.

Host lines: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-gate-pick calls fn-osch-next at every release of the owner mutex and at every arrival at an idle owner; fnn-owner-gate-leave calls fn-osch-observe; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span returns fn-splan-step-make; fnn-owner-handle-chunk calls fn-splan-step-plan; fnn-owner-render-next calls fn-splan-window off the mutex and fnn-owner-write-plan loops it until fn-splan-donep. proofs.title: The node operator's withdrawal withdraws exactly its target, under a configuration record the operator wrote, from every view that holds its cause
proofs.statement: fn-cfg-withdraw-article-authorizes-the-cause (books/config-invariants.lisp, KEYSTONE): an admitted (fn-cfg-withdraw-article CAUSE TARGET REASON) (code 26, `article withdraw-record`) applied by fn-cfg-apply-delta makes fn-cfg-withdrawal-target of CAUSE equal TARGET and leaves every other cause's unchanged. fn-ctl-node-withdrawal-withdraws-exactly-its-target (books/control-authority.lisp, KEYSTONE): when the configuration in force at the cause's txid authorizes CAUSE for TARGET (fn-ctl-node-authorizesp), fn-ctl-withdrawal-plan makes the record (:withdrawal TARGET CAUSE :node nil GEN) whatever the cause's verdict and keys, and an article is withdrawn by it within ARTICLES exactly when it is TARGET and CAUSE is among ARTICLES (the owner refresh fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals, called by books/owner.lisp fn-own-refresh; a view pinned before the cause keeps TARGET). fn-ctl-withdrawal-authority-is-exactly-signer-or-poster and fn-ctl-cancel-executes-only-for-author-or-authority gain the node basis as a disjunct. fn-mvb-withdraw-names-exactly-its-target and fn-mvb-withdraw-makes-the-node-authorize-exactly-its-target (books/moderation-verbs.lisp, KEYSTONES) over fn-mvb-withdraw (host fn-owner-moderation-plan -> fn-mvb-plan; the host runs the named live-administration vector, then the operator submission of the cancel CAUSE): a planned withdrawal names a stored TARGET, CAUSE = <fn-withdraw. then TARGET after its <, the row's vector when no row exists (else the existing row names TARGET) and the cancel article `Control: cancel TARGET` under Message-ID CAUSE, which the operator decision (fn-own-operator-decision, the path the host submits through) injects; after the row the configuration authorizes CAUSE for exactly TARGET.

proofs.title: A sealed compressed payload denotes exactly the octets it was sealed from, whatever the encoder wrote; the ACL2 LZ4-block decoder is total, guard-verified, resumable in quanta and bounded by the recorded length
proofs.statement: books/payload-lz.lisp (brief C1 of planning/evidence/article-compression-2026-09-27.md section 6). fn-lz-run is the LZ4 block decoder over three octet buffers (abstract stobjs congruent to fn-octets: the block in cells [start, end) of fn-octets, the dictionary in fn-lz-dict, the output appended to fn-lz-out), with the dictionary as a prefix an offset may reach into; its budget B counts steps and it answers :more (resumable from the state it returns), :done, or a refusal (:truncated, :overflow, :offset, :mode). fn-lz-decode-buf decodes a whole block in one budget of 3|c| + n + 2 steps; fn-lz-decode is the same over octet lists. fn-lz-seal-form dict octets candidate answers (:lz n candidate) when the candidate decodes to exactly the octets, else (:raw octets); fn-lz-denote is the decode of an :lz form and the octets of a :raw one. KEYSTONE fn-lz-seal-form-denotes: with no hypothesis, (fn-lz-denote dict (fn-lz-seal-form dict octets candidate)) = octets: no assumption about the encoder. fn-lz-seal-form-of-literal-block / fn-lz-decode-of-literal-block: for (fn-cbor-octet-listp x), the one-sequence literal block of x decodes to (:ok x) and seals as :lz, so the :lz arm is reachable for every payload. fn-lz-run-out-len-bound: the output never exceeds (max lim (len out)); fn-lz-decode-buf-out-len-bound: at most n (D27: the only allocation is the recorded length). fn-lz-run-extends-out: for a true-list output the run only appends. Since lane octets-bulk (2026-09-27) fn-lz-copy-lits and fn-lz-copy-match keep their octet-at-a-time logic and execute through mbe as fn-lz-lits-words (seven-octet words from the block) and fn-lz-match-bulk (the dictionary part by words, the output part by one fn-lz-out-append-back); fn-lz-lits-words-is-append and fn-lz-match-bulk-is-copy-match are the equalities their guard proofs use.
proofs.progress_note: Lane codec-c1 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27): a prototype book with no host wiring. Teeth: tests/acl2/payload-lz-tests.lisp (a held-out 1993 Usenet article from usenet-20news-19997 and its liblz4-HC 9 blocks with and without a dictionary seal as :lz and denote the article; a corrupted block and a block of other octets seal as :raw and still denote it; literal blocks of 5 and 300 octets; the refusals :truncated, :offset (0 and past dict ++ out), :overflow and :short; the article's block decoded in quanta of seven steps reaches the same octets as one budget; hypothesis removal by must-fail and a ground counterexample for the octet-list and true-list hypotheses). Measured on hbox (i9-12900, one P-core) over the 9,733 held-out articles: see the record.

proofs.title: The full replay takes the history in chunks, and any chunking opens the Store one step over the whole history opens
proofs.statement: Subject, called by the host: fn-srs-step (books/store-recover-stream.lisp), whose body is the two calls host/native/io.lisp fnn-bridge-recover makes once per chunk (fnn-recover-full-replay, fnn-recover: every full-replay open, the store verbs and the owner start): fn-store-decode-records (host/store-host.lisp, which is fn-srs-decode) and the guard-verified fn-srs-intern-step with the live arena (the intern into the arena, keyring NIL and generation 0, rows accumulated newest first); the host clears the arena first and then opens over fn-srs-rows (the rows oldest first) with host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-recover-rows (flip-L6-2's open, unchanged). No :program entry updates the arena. The host closes a chunk where fn-srs-chunk-fullp says (1 MiB of record octets, a work quantum: one record is always taken first, so a record above it is a chunk by itself and nothing is refused or split for its size), converting only that chunk to octet lists. fn-srs-decode-of-append and fn-srs-intern-events-of-append: the decode and the intern (fn-intern-events, the arena threaded) of a concatenation are those of its parts. KEYSTONE fn-srs-steps-are-one-step-of-the-concatenation: for every list of chunks each a true list (fn-srs-chunksp) and any accumulator, the fold of fn-srs-step over the chunks is :bad exactly when one step over their concatenation is, and otherwise equal to it (rows and arena). fn-srs-one-step-is-the-intern-of-the-decode: one step from no rows, when not :bad, is the decode of the history interned (fn-srs-rows of it is fn-intern-events' rows, the same arena): what the one-shot open computed before the chunking. proofs.title: A local consumer command's refusal names the owner's reason on the wire, a bind of an unregistered consumer is refused by name, and the command's JSON line is ACL2's, all printable ASCII
proofs.statement: books/consumer-reason.lisp and books/consumer-owner-local.lisp. Subjects: fn-ncr-request-encode / -decode / fn-ncr-framep (host/native-control-host.lisp fn-native-control-host-consumer-reasoned-request-encode / -decode and fn-native-control-host-reasoned-framep, called by host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-consumer-local (client) and fnn-control-handle-client (owner)); fn-ncr-client-read (fn-native-control-host-consumer-client-read, fnn-control-consumer-local); fn-ncr-cli-after (fn-native-control-host-consumer-cli-after, host/native/consumer-local.lisp fnn-command-consumer-local); fn-ncr-cli-plan, fn-ncr-json-line, fn-ncr-report-summary, fn-ncr-article-json (host/native/consumer-local.lisp); fn-col-bind-refusal (host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-native-admin-host-owner-reconfigure live and fn-native-admin-host-apply offline). KEYSTONES: fn-ncr-printed-reason-is-the-decisions (for every status, the client's read of the reasoned reply the owner seals is that status and the reason's word, and a refusal that named a reason prints exactly that word); fn-ncr-request-decode-is-the-plain-decode (the kind-22 frame is decided as the kind-4 request with the same payload); fn-ncr-cli-after-retries-only-an-unbootstrapped-register; fn-col-bind-refusal-refuses-exactly-an-unregistered-bind; fn-ncr-json-object-is-ascii; fn-ncr-withdrawal-roundtrip and fn-ncr-withdrawal-report-fits-the-poll-reply (the withdrawal report's byte form, PRF-262's). fn-ncr-cli-plan-without-the-flag-by-definition: without --json the plan is the wait codec's. Local policy; no RFC requirement. The reasoned consumer request is FNCT kind 22; an old owner's plain refusal of it is resent once as kind 4 (PKT-453's pattern).

proofs.title: A consumer gets the withdrawal event, never the withdrawn content: a withdrawn article is delivered as its Message-ID, a cancel of an article of the consumer's group is delivered at its own position, and while nothing is withdrawn the page is the poll's answer
proofs.statement: books/consumer-withdrawal.lisp. Subjects: fn-cwd-page (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll and fn-owner-consumer-local-bound-poll, over the answers of fn-cbind-plain-poll-over and fn-cbind-poll-over, the polls over the live arena) and fn-cwd-wait-step-over (fn-owner-consumer-local-wait-step, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-consumer-local-wait); the scan fn-cwd-scan inside fn-cwd-poll. The withdrawal decision read is the owner's committed view's withdrawn list and withdrawal records (fn-own-view-withdrawn, fn-own-view-withdrawals; fn-ctl-msgid-withdrawn), the one NNTP's 430 withdrawn reads. KEYSTONES: fn-cwd-page-never-serves-withdrawn-content (when the poll selects an article the view withdrew, the page over any answer carrying a report is a refusal or a withdrawal report, which fn-ncr-withdrawal-decode reads as (:withdrawn MSGID)); fn-cwd-scan-delivers-a-withdrawing-cause (an event at the position, of no article of the group, whose record withdrew an article of the group, is where the scan stops, naming that article); fn-cwd-scan-withdrawal-advances (the withdrawal's next position is past the consumer's and within the frontier); fn-cwd-page-of-a-withdrawal (the page is the withdrawal at the cursor built from that position); fn-cwd-page-without-withdrawals-is-the-answer (with nothing withdrawn the page is exactly the answer, so PRF-116, PRF-177, PRF-234 and PRF-252 hold unchanged); fn-cwd-scan-is-the-poll-scan-unless-a-withdrawal; fn-cwd-page-of-a-refusal; fn-cwd-wait-step-over-is-the-page-or-a-sleep-on-an-empty-page. Pessimistic cost per poll: 16 x (R + N) comparisons (R records, N withdrawn) plus one walk of N. On dev at 2026-09-27 the view's withdrawn list is empty until lane flip-L8-2's live refresh lands. Local policy; no RFC requirement (RFC 5537 section 5.3 files a cancel in control.cancel, which is why a consumer of the target's group never selected it).

proofs.title: A format-9 store's commit goes through the record log, and any crash with a batch in flight reads back a prefix of the history that extends the committed records
proofs.statement: Subjects: the log kernel's transitions the host calls (host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-take -> fn-olr-take, fnn-log-append -> fn-lgk-append, fnn-log-fence -> fn-lgk-fence), over the state fn-olr-linkp relates to the store node's history. fn-olr-crash-reads-a-prefix-of-the-history (books/store-log-route.lisp, KEYSTONE): under fn-lgk-relp, a batch in flight, an admissible crash image (fn-bs-crash-imagep) and the link, the scan of the durable content is a prefix of the history and extends fn-lgk-committed, or the damaged entry is a forgery (A-CRYPTO-TRAILER, T2). The link is kept by every transition (fn-olr-linkp-of-recovery, -of-take, -of-append, -of-fence, -of-finish-one, -of-consume-to); fn-olr-take-is-the-prepare-at-the-owners-txid, fn-olr-take-agrees-with-the-owner, fn-olr-take-keeps-the-bounds and fn-olr-take-preserves-relation tie the take to the owner's prepare; fn-olr-consume-to-reaches-the-owner and -preserves-relation/-okp the replies after the barrier; fn-olr-sn-reserve-reaches-reserved and fn-olr-sn-order-reaches-completing (books/store-log-route-phases.lisp) the node's phases; fn-olr-sn-reserve/-order-is-the-file-route-by-definition and the owner's fn-olr-ocfg-*-is-the-file-route-by-definition name the unchanged route. Measured (pre-flip base, hbox): fsyncs per POST 7.0 -> 0.27 (NVMe) / 0.31 (tank); 200 power cuts, 0 violations (planning/evidence/commit-onto-log-2026-09-27.md). proofs.title: The record log's segments: the drop of the segments a checkpoint covers preserves the history the open replays (T8), the open's plan ignores covered leftovers, and the rotation's kernel is the recovered kernel of the new segment
proofs.statement: books/store-log-segments.lisp and books/store-log-stream.lisp. KEYSTONE fn-lgw-segment-drop-preserves-the-open: over the host's streamed fold (fn-lgw-open-chain-records / fn-lgw-open-chain-last: each segment's octets streamed by fn-lgw-run from fn-lgw-start GENESIS 1, the next genesis fn-lgc-last of the stream's kernel; host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-scan-segments runs exactly that per segment through fnn-log-stream-segment, the entry loop over fn-lgw-step), when the checkpoint's prefix is the covered segments' streamed records and the F row's genesis their last trailer, the checkpoint's records followed by the fold over the remaining segments from that genesis are the fold over every segment (fn-lgw-open-chain-is-the-chain: the fold is the model chain fn-lgs-chain-records over the segments' octets, per segment by fn-lgw-segment-is-the-scan from fn-lgw-run-is-the-open; the split is fn-lgs-chain-records-of-append; the replay of that split is the full replay by fn-sn-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover). fn-lgs-open-plan-scan-ignores-covered: at the drop's cuts (fnn-log-drop: drop-unlinked, drop-durable) the open's plan (fn-lgs-open-plan, called by fnn-recover-log) scans the same segments and refuses the same stores whatever covered segments remain. fn-lgs-rotate-is-the-recovered-kernel: the rotated kernel (fnn-log-rotate) is the kernel recovery derives from the new segment's durable zeros with the closed segment's last trailer, so R holds for the new segment by the fact that establishes it at log-recovered. fn-lgs-chain-records-of-append: the chain splits at any segment boundary. The verb: `store compact` is exactly the native :compact action (fn-native-operator-run-store-compact-is-the-compact-action, fn-native-operator-run-compact-action-is-only-store-compact; books/native-operator.lisp), whose native body is the checkpoint with the log rotated and then this drop (host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-command-compact).

Lane log-leftovers 2026-09-27: T8 restated over the streamed open (log-open-stream's fnn-log-stream-segment): the string-era fold fn-lgs-open-chain-records / -last (fn-lg-open-kernel per segment read as a string), its theorems fn-lg-segment-drop-preserves-the-open, fn-lgs-open-chain-records-of-append, fn-lgs-open-chain-is-the-chain and the string splice classifier fn-lgs-chain-broken-string-p / -at (no host caller since the stream) are deleted; the keystone is fn-lgw-segment-drop-preserves-the-open.

proofs.title: Content reclamation over the record log checkpoints exactly the per-article rewrite of the committed history

proofs.title: The owner's commit runs in three scheduled steps with its log barrier off the owner: a status or health request waits at most one quantum and never a barrier, and a batch's members are told acceptance or refusal only after its barrier, each as its own outcome
proofs.statement: fn-ocs-inspect-waits-at-most-one (books/owner-commit-steps.lisp; keystone, no hypothesis on the state or the commit's events): for every scheduler value S and every sequence WS of pick observations, each (W EVENT) with W the six waiting counts (control reader poster transit commit inspect) and EVENT what a :commit quantum picked there reports, if the :inspect class has a waiter at every pick (fn-ocs-inspect-waitsp) then the quanta of other classes picked before the first :inspect pick, fn-ocs-inspect-delay, is at most 1. The barrier is not a quantum: it is the :barrier ACTION fn-ocs-commit-step names after a START, which the committer runs with the owner released. So the wall time an :inspect request waits at the gate is at most the longest single quantum of another class; its bound's hypotheses: the store commits through the record log (format 9; on a format-8 store there is no committer and a served POST's commit is still inside its reader quantum), and no quantum of another class contains a barrier (true of the START and the COMPLETE when no feed peer is configured: a configured peer's intent flush fsyncs per member inside the START, PKT-825). fn-ocs-in-flight-admits-only-inspect-commit-and-reader: while a batch is in flight (phase :staged, :fenced or :failed) the pick is :inspect, :commit, :reader or nil -- no control-socket poster, transit or mutating control quantum runs between a batch's START and its COMPLETE; a reader runs at the reader view (PRF-288), so no read reveals an unfenced record (coordinator decision PKT-828); fn-ocs-in-flight-commit-before-reader: in flight a waiting commit step (START-NEXT, COMPLETE) is picked before any reader. fn-ocs-next-otherwise-is-ocm-next: outside a batch every non-:inspect pick is books/owner-commit-class.lisp fn-ocm-next's pick and state, so PRF-248's control bound (via fn-ocm-next-otherwise-is-osch-next) and fn-ocm-commit-waits-at-most-the-bound hold over the non-:inspect quanta; fn-ocs-inspect-pick-keeps-the-ocm. fn-ocs-complete-only-after-the-barrier: the step machine names :complete (the step that releases the members' replies) only for phase :staged and event :fenced; fn-ocs-barrier-only-from-a-start, fn-ocs-staged-only-by-a-start, fn-ocs-in-flight-until-completed. The keystone's per-pick subjects, each about fn-ocs-next itself: fn-ocs-inspect-first-when-not-last (an :inspect waits and the last pick was not an :inspect: the pick is :inspect), fn-ocs-inspect-waiting-picks-someone (an :inspect waits: the pick is not nil), fn-ocs-other-pick-clears-lasti (a pick that is neither nil nor :inspect clears LASTI). The members' replies (lane scheduler-2-rebase, onto commit-onto-log's per-member uncertain replies): fn-ocs-members-told-only-after-the-barrier (keystone; subjects the host's two calls per batch, fn-ocs-commit-step -- through fn-ocs-commit-event for the committer, directly for the inline commit fnn-owner-commit-queued-locked -- and fn-ocs-member-releases, which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-commit-complete-locked calls over each member's (WORD RENDERABLE)): if the releases for the step's action name any member :rendered (its own rendered completion: the acceptance or refusal its word decided), then the phase was :staged and the event :fenced. fn-ocs-failed-barrier-stops-telling-no-member: a staged batch whose barrier failed gets the :stop (the recovery event: the store fenced, exit 3) and no member :rendered. fn-ocs-member-rendered-only-in-a-complete (iff: :rendered exactly when the action is :complete and the word is not :uncertain), fn-ocs-member-otherwise-uncertain (every other release is :own-uncertain, :uncertain-reply or :close), fn-ocs-member-uncertain-word-told-uncertain. Scope: accepted and refused are the member's own ACL2 word and rendered reply, unchanged by the COMPLETE; after a stop a refused member of the batch is answered uncertain too (its refusal can rest on an earlier member whose record the log may not hold); a refusal that wrote nothing and names no other record (full store, malformed) is no member of the batch: it is told at its drain (PRF-354). A service stopped by the operator during a barrier answers every member with the close (host, uncertain), outside this theorem.

proofs.title: A txid reused after a crash is a fresh feed intent: the open decides a dead intent without its txid
proofs.statement: books/owner-feed-txid-reuse.lisp, host host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-feed-reconcile (every intent resolved before the owner serves): fn-own-feed-intent-reconcile-kind-reads-no-txid (the open decides a dead FNFD intent from its Message-ID, identity and evidence, never its txid) and KEYSTONE fn-own-feed-intent-reuse-is-a-fresh-intent (with no pending intent of that key, a new intent naming a reused txid and its resolution restore the pending set exactly). So the log's derived next txid (the PostgreSQL rule: a txid handed out and never logged is reused after a crash) needs no floor at the feed journals' intents (PKT-COL-8, option ii). Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-feed-txid-reuse-tests.lisp. Lane log-2 (fork log-2-init).

proofs.title: Every process-death cut of the record-log route is a cut of a model program, at a related state
proofs.statement: books/store-log-route-programs.lisp: the format-9 arms of host/native/io.lisp fnn-advance-frontier, fnn-publish, fnn-mark-committed and fnn-recover call fnn-log-reserve, fnn-log-publish, nothing, and fnn-recover-log, whose durable steps and process-death cuts in source order are exactly fn-lg-reserve-program (frontier-reserved), fn-lg-append-program ++ fn-lg-fence-program ++ fn-lg-order-program (log-written, log-fenced, record-completing; a batch of one), and fn-lg-open-program (P-LOG-RECOVER's log-truncated and log-recovered, then recover-replayed and the three recovery barriers -- journal/, the root, its parent; *fn-sf-recovery-barrier-count* 3 since lane open-barriers -- each followed by recover-barrier): tools/native_program_check.py checks each arm (tests/campaign/native_cuts.py verify_log_route_arms, in make check; teeth in tests/test_native_program_check.py LogRouteArmTests). fn-lg-reserve-program-keeps-the-relation: from R, the state at frontier-reserved (the kernel caught up by fn-olr-consume-to) is R-related; fn-lg-order-program-keeps-the-relation: from R and a record, the state at record-completing (the record taken into the open batch, fn-olr-take) is related; fn-lg-open-suffix-keeps-the-relation: from R (as fn-lg-recover-program-establishes-the-relation leaves it), every state after log-recovered is related (the hypothesis 'nothing in flight' the five-barrier suffix needed for the segment's second fence was removed with that fence, after the weakened theorem was proved). So a process death at any cut is a crash of an R-related state (fn-lgk-crash-of-related-state-is-a-prefix). Teeth: tests/acl2/store-log-route-programs-tests.lisp (reached states of store-log-kernel-tests; R removed; a batch in flight, related at every cut of the three-barrier suffix). Which of the open's fences the byte model needs (books/store-log-open-barriers.lisp, lane log-recovery-2): fn-lgob-duplicate-segment-fence-is-identity: on an R-related state with nothing in flight the second recovery barrier (the segment again) changes neither the byte store nor the kernel, and fn-lgob-recovered-segment-fence-is-identity: at the state fnn-log-recover leaves at log-recovered the second fence is the identity for every store whose segment inode exists (restated by lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G4-7: the weakened theorem was proved, so the six hypotheses R needed, the owner's sole-pending-writer obligation among them, were dropped); fn-lgob-file-fence-keeps-entry-operations: a file fence drains no directory entry operation, so ONE barrier (the segment's) is not sufficient: fn-lgob-one-barrier-loses-a-rotated-segment (a death at rotate-created, the open fencing only the segment, a batch fenced: a crash image holds the batch's octets under no durable name) and fn-lgob-journal-fence-keeps-the-rotated-segment (with journal/ fenced every crash image names it). Teeth: tests/acl2/store-log-open-barriers-tests.lisp. Three barriers, not five (lane open-barriers, 2026-09-27; host subject host/native/io.lisp fnn-store-recovery-barriers, called by fnn-recover-log and the owner's open): fn-lgob-three-barrier-open-is-the-five-at-every-cut (KEYSTONE): from any byte store whose segment and config file have no pending write, the byte states at the process-death cuts of the five-barrier open (config.json, the segment, journal/, the root, the parent) are those of the three-barrier open with the recovered state twice in front, so every cut of either leaves the same states and crash images (fn-lgob-three-and-five-barrier-opens-have-the-same-cut-states); fn-lgob-three-barrier-open-after-recovery-is-the-five: the same composed with P-LOG-RECOVER, from any store whose segment exists and whose config file has no pending write (fn-lgob-recovered-state-meets-the-segment-hypothesis discharges the segment half); fn-lgob-only-a-write-unfences-a-file: of every byte syscall only a write of an inode adds a pending write of it -- with the host fact (argued from the source, not proved) that config.json is written only by its publications, each fencing the file before naming it, this is the config half; none of the three can go, one ground counterexample per omitted barrier: fn-lgob-two-barriers-without-journal-lose-a-rotated-segment (a death at rotate-created, an acknowledged batch in an unnamed segment), fn-lgob-two-barriers-without-root-lose-a-checkpointed-history (a checkpoint renamed but not root-fenced, the open's drop durable, neither the checkpoint nor its covered segment named), fn-lgob-two-barriers-without-parent-lose-an-imported-store (an import at import-published, an acknowledged batch in a store with no durable name), each with its three-barrier control (fn-lgob-three-barriers-keep-the-rotated-segment, -keep-the-checkpoint, -keep-the-imported-store). The per-file fn-bs-recover-program (books/byte-store-programs.lisp; the layout is unreachable) keeps the count with three directory fences. Teeth: tests/acl2/store-log-open-barriers-tests.lisp (a reachable witness, one failing state per hypothesis).

proofs.title: The pipelined group commit: the next batch prepares behind the barrier, and no record is revealed or acknowledged before its own barrier
proofs.statement: Subjects fn-ocp-commit-event and fn-ocp-committer-wake (books/owner-commit-pipeline.lisp), which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-commit-event and fnn-owner-commit-wake call from the committer (fnn-owner-commit-pipeline), and fn-ocp-next / fn-ocp-observe, which fnn-owner-gate-pick / fnn-owner-gate-leave call at every release of the owner. KEYSTONE fn-ocp-next-open-only-in-flight: after any commit event, a next batch is open only while the commit's ocs phase is in flight, so (fn-ocp-next-is-ocs-next, fn-ocs-in-flight-admits-only-inspect-and-commit, restated over the host's pick as fn-ocp-in-flight-admits-only-inspect-commit-and-reader) no reader, poster, transit or mutating control quantum runs while a prepared record of the batch in flight or of the one behind it is not durable. fn-ocp-commit-event-completes-only-after-the-barrier: COMPLETE (the acknowledgements and the replies of the batch in flight) is named only for a staged batch whose syncer returned :fenced; the next batch's members become the staged batch only through COMPLETE's :sync (fn-ocp-sync-only-when-none-in-flight: a batch is handed to the syncer only from an idle owner after a START or by COMPLETE after the batch in flight was fenced), so appends are in the batches' order and at most one is in flight, as the kernel requires (fn-lgk-append refuses a second). fn-ocp-start-next-only-behind-a-sync: START-NEXT runs only while a batch is staged, its barrier not returned, no next batch open, a member queued and (lane durability-bugs, PRF-901) no control, poster or transit request waiting past the pass budget. The crash half is PRF (commit-onto-log) fn-olr-crash-reads-a-prefix-of-the-history, whose link (committed ++ in flight ++ open batch) covers the batch prepared behind the barrier; the host's kernel updates are serialized by the log's lock (host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-with-kernel) and the syncer touches only the log struct. Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-commit-pipeline-tests.lisp (the pipeline reached step by step from fn-ocp-init; hypothesis removal for the keystone and the completion rule); native: tests/test_native_commit_log.py test_the_next_batch_prepares_behind_the_barrier (the operator's batch bound 2, the barrier held 700 ms, 16 POSTs from 8 posters: START-NEXT ran, every POST 240 and served after a restart).

proofs.title: The live configuration completion applies its one record to the owner's carried node and configuration: under the owner invariant it is fn-ocl-publish, and it carries the invariant, so no control quantum replays the Store history
proofs.statement: fn-oclc-publish-is-publish (books/config-owner-carried.lisp; keystone, hypothesis fn-ocl-relation OC, the owner invariant books/config-owner-live.lisp defines): (fn-oclc-publish OC GENERATION MAX-OCTETS) equals (fn-ocl-publish OC GENERATION MAX-OCTETS), verdict and owner, for every record, generation and phase. fn-oclc-publish is the host-called completion (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reconfigure-complete, reached from host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked for every live group create, control grant and the other live configuration verbs); it replaces fn-ocl-complete's fn-cpo-configure-durable (fn-cpo-history-relation's full fn-cpr-replay and fn-sn-statep of the store, a second full replay over the extended configuration history, fn-sn-statep of the candidate) and fn-ocl-store-config (a third replay) by one configuration step from the store's node and the owner's configuration: fn-oclc-configure, whose install is fn-cpo-configure-durable (fn-oclc-configure-is-configure-durable, hypotheses fn-cpo-history-relation ST and CONFIG the replayed configuration) and whose configuration is fn-ocl-store-config of the installed store on success (fn-oclc-configure-config-is-store-config); fn-oclc-complete-is-complete (the staged completion, from fn-cst-relation and fn-ocl-config-historyp); fn-oclc-ready-cst-relation-is-history-relation (fn-cst-relation at the :ready phase is fn-cpo-history-relation). fn-oclc-publish-carries-ocl-relation (keystone, hypothesis fn-ocl-relation OC): the owner fn-oclc-publish answers satisfies fn-ocl-relation again, whatever the verdict (:durable through config-owner-live's fn-ocl-complete-preserves-full-historical-relation; :refused and :recovery-required keep OC). The invariant is established by fn-owner-recover (books/owner-recover-ocl.lisp fn-orec-started-owner-ocl-relation) and preserved by the owner's other transitions (the fn-ocl-*-preserves-historical-relation family of books/config-owner-live.lisp, config-owner-advance-invariants, owner-commit-ocl); fn-oclc-publish tests none of it at run time (guard t), which is the point: its hold no longer grows with the store.

Profiled with sb-sprof on hbox (tools/profile/): at 1,000 articles 85 per cent of a live group create's owner samples were fn-ocl-complete's three replays; at 10,000 the replay is quadratic (fn-retain-pin-id-scanp, fn-acceptedp per event) and one control quantum held the owner 40 to 46 s. proofs.title: The Store kernel holds its history and its success history as snoc-lists: a commit and a success append in O(1), and the prepare, the finish and the refresh read the length, the last and the newest records in O(1)
proofs.statement: books/snoc-list.lisp and books/store-files.lisp (post-alloc-2). The kernel state's RECORDS and SUCCESSES fields hold (:snoc N . REV) (the length-N list whose reverse is the first N of REV); fn-sf-records / fn-sf-successes read the lists back and every accessor lemma of fn-sf-make is unchanged; fn-sf-shapep requires each field to be the representation of its list. KEYSTONES: fn-sl-list-of-fn-sl-of (every value round-trips), fn-sl-list-of-fn-sl-snoc and fn-sl-snoc-of-fn-sl-of (the O(1) snoc is the append, for every value / list), fn-sl-count-is-len, fn-sl-last-is-last, fn-sl-nth-is-nth (no hypothesis); fn-sf-make-fields-is-make, fn-sf-make-fields-snoc-records-is-make, fn-sf-make-fields-snoc-successes-is-make (under fn-sf-shapep: what every transition's mbe executes). The logic of every store-files transition is unchanged (the mbe :logic is the former body). Host subjects: the commit host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-io -> books/records-concrete.lisp fn-rcon-sf-record-dir-result (O(1) append); the prepare fn-owner-prepare-buffer -> books/owner-prepare-carried.lisp fn-pcar-stage-record over fn-pcar-files-candidatep (fn-pcar-files-candidatep-is-candidatep, no hypothesis) and fn-pcar-sbud-prepare over fn-sf-records-count (fn-pcar-records-count-is-sbud-used); the finish fn-owner-finish-submission -> books/owner-commit-carried.lisp fn-ccar-completion-record over fn-ccar-seek-at (fn-ccar-seek-at-is-seek, no hypothesis); books/owner.lisp fn-own-refresh reads the count in O(1) and keeps its withdrawals without reading the history when the acceptance is unchanged (mbe; logic unchanged). Local policy (D27: bound work, not data); no RFC requirement.

proofs.title: Compaction and reclaim off the whole history's octet lists: the compaction verb decides and captures over the history's length and one link's window, and the reclaim decision is a fold over one record at a time; each answers exactly what the whole-history function answers
proofs.statement: books/store-compact-window.lisp (lane compact-arena, PKT-686 item 2). fn-scw-window-count (lens lower), the count of records the next link takes read from the records' lengths, is fn-ccc-fit of the records above LOWER: fn-scw-window-count-is-fit (equal (fn-scw-window-count (fn-scw-lens records) lower) (fn-ccc-fit (nthcdr (nfix lower) records))), no hypothesis. KEYSTONE fn-cverb-decide-window-is-cverb-decide: (implies (and (equal used (len records)) (equal window (fn-scw-window records lower))) (equal (fn-cverb-decide-window profile used lower window names generations selected disk-free) (fn-cverb-decide profile records lower names generations selected disk-free))). proofs.title: Every history the profile admits reopens: the open's recovery input bound is H plus the profile's transaction count times the per-record encoding overhead, which holds every admitted history's encoded records
proofs.statement: books/store-replay-bound.lisp (lane compact-arena, the coordinator's addition to PKT-686). Since the records flip the history budget H counts an article row's payload octets while its transaction file holds the whole encoded record, so a store the budget admitted up to H held more than H octets of records and the open refused it at every heap size ("transaction recovery input exceeds configured bound": a small-preset store of 3,500 x 2 KiB posts, lane reservation-after-flip; post-alloc's capacity-vector store). fn-srb-replay-input-bound PROFILE = H + T x fn-srb-record-overhead, the overhead fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling 0 G (books/records-shape.lisp: 1,083 + 261 G). KEYSTONE fn-srb-admitted-history-is-within-the-bound: (implies (and (fn-bs-profile-admittedp profile) (<= (len encoded) T) (<= (fn-srb-sum stored) H) (fn-srb-pointwise-within encoded stored (fn-srb-record-overhead profile))) (fn-srb-replay-within-boundp profile (fn-srb-sum encoded))): any history of at most T records whose budget octets sum within H, each record encoded within its budget octets plus the overhead, is within the bound. fn-srb-within-h-is-within-the-bound: everything the H bound accepted is accepted. Host: host/store-host.lisp fn-store-profile-replay-within-bound calls fn-srb-replay-within-boundp, from host/native/io.lisp fnn-durable-records and fnn-read-suffix-records. Scope: the per-record hypothesis is records-seam's narrow length bound for the records the POST path produces (fn-sbud-article-figure-bounds-the-record); every other row's budget octets are its whole encoding (fn-sbud-row-octets), overhead 0. The small preset's bound is 94,552,064 octets.
