proofs.title: The paged payload arena: fixed pages, no doubling; the node's arena attachment corresponds to the generic's list of sealed payloads
proofs.statement: books/payload-arena-paged.lisp: fn-arena-paged is an abstract stobj over the concrete fn-arena$p (a resizable table of page stobjs, each a byte array of *fn-arp-page* = 262,144 octets: above SBCL's large-object size, 131,072, so the collector never copies a page allocated when the page is added; an offset and a size per handle; the count, the fill and the page count). Its logical side is fn-arena-bytes's, verbatim (fn-arena$ap, create-fn-arena$a, the eight fn-arena$a-*), so books/payload-arena-attach.lisp's (attach-stobj fn-arena fn-arena-paged) makes the generic fn-arena (PRF-221) execute over pages while every certificate above the generic stays the generic's. The abstraction fn-arena$pcorr is fn-arena$corr's (PRF-118) with the pages' byte lists concatenated (fn-arp-flat over the first npages pages, each full: fn-arp-fullp) in place of the byte array, and the fill within the pages' capacity. The page arithmetic is proved once: fn-arp-nth-flat and fn-arp-flat-of-page-write (page K's octet J is the flat view's position J + 262144 K; a write there is the flat view's update-nth), fn-arp-nth-flat-at / fn-arp-flat-of-write-at (the same at floor and mod of a position), fn-arp-flat-snoc and fn-arp-flat-of-resize-list (adding a page appends its octets; doubling the table of POINTERS keeps the view). Steps: fn-arp-put-step (a page write is the flat view's update), fn-arp-add-page-step (one more page; every octet below the old capacity kept), fn-arp-write-octet-step, fn-arp-write-appends, fn-arp-seal-list-step; reads fn-arp-byte-is-nth and fn-arp-list-pages-is-list-from (the payload reader walks pages). Every {correspondence}, {preserved} and {guard-thm} obligation is proved before the defabsstobj (fn-arena-paged-get{correspondence} ... fn-arena-paged-clear{preserved}); every executable function is guard-verified. What it changes: a sealed octet never moves and a seal never copies an older payload; growth allocates one 256 KiB page and, when the table has no spare slot, doubles the table's pointers (8 octets per page); the arena's footprint is its payload octets plus under one page plus the handle arrays, and no two copies are live (recover-memory-2's packet P1: the byte array's last doubling kept 256 and 512 MiB live together). The clear releases the page table. Host subject: every host call of an fn-arena export (host/native/io.lisp fnn-arena-seal-*, host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-lookup through fn-handle-bytes, host/owner-host.lisp's clears) runs over this attachment; the host names only the generic.

Stage 2 (payloads off the heap: handle -> durable file extent, A-DURABLE-EXTENT) builds on the same generic. proofs.title: The configured Store relation, with its carried companion, survives every Store step of the article commit: the reservation's file steps, the carried prepare of a served article, the record file steps, the publishing directory observation, the refused reservation and the recovery barriers
proofs.statement: books/config-store-steps.lisp. The configured fold over a history extended by one Store event is one event step from the fold without it (fn-cstp-replay-append-event: hypotheses the history recoverable at the event's transaction id, the event's sequence and transaction id, and the event served by the fold's configuration). fn-cst-relation (books/config-store-traces.lisp) is preserved by fn-sn-io for the reservation's and recovery barrier's operations for every result (fn-cstp-reserve-io-preserves-relation), by the record file and link steps and a non-publishing directory observation (fn-cstp-record-io-preserves-relation), by the carried article prepare the host calls (books/store-prepare-correspondence.lisp fn-spc-prepare) when the article's groups are served by the replayed configuration (fn-cstp-spc-prepare-preserves-relation), by the directory observation that publishes an article candidate given the carried companion fn-cstp-carriedp (fn-cstp-held-record-dir-preserves-relation), and with fn-cstp-carriedp by the refused reservation (fn-cstp-refuse-reservation-preserves). fn-cstp-carriedp (the prepare gate's facts about the candidate from staging to the directory observation; at :completing the topic prefix one short of the history; elsewhere the topic prefix at the history's length with status :ok) is preserved by the same steps, by fn-sn-finish (fn-cstp-finish-preserves-carriedp) and by the configuration install (fn-cstp-configure-durable-preserves-carriedp), and established by the configured open (fn-cstp-open-establishes-carriedp). The companion is necessary: fn-cst-relation's :completing arm demands fn-sn-completion-enabledp, which no record-phase arm carries (corrupted-state witness in the teeth).

REPL-admitted on hbox against dev; teeth in tests/acl2/owner-log-ocl-tests.lisp (every keystone's reachable witness on the configured owner and its POST article; hypothesis witnesses: the served hypothesis by a retired group, the companion by a topic counter off the history, fn-cst-relation by a node advanced past the frontier).

proofs.title: The configured owner's invariant is carried across the format-9 commit, the live configuration completion and recovery, so the carried completion's hypothesis holds at every completion
proofs.statement: books/owner-log-ocl.lisp. fn-lgoc-invariantp OC = (fn-ocl-relation OC) and fn-cstp-carriedp of its Store. It is established by the recovery the host calls on either path (fn-lgoc-recover-installs-invariant: fn-ock-recover-extended of a capture extended over the rest of the history, not :fault) and preserved by every host step of an article's life on the log route: fn-olr-ocfg-reserve (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-io :log-reserve; fn-lgoc-log-reserve-preserves-invariant), the prepare below the budget gate (fn-sbud-prepare; fn-lgoc-sbud-prepare-preserves-invariant) and the host's fn-pidx-sbud-prepare under its two carried index premises (fn-lgoc-pidx-sbud-prepare-preserves-invariant), both with the hypothesis that an article's groups are served by the live configuration (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer tests it; the prepare does not), fn-olr-ocfg-order with an article staged (:log-order; fn-lgoc-log-order-preserves-invariant), the finish (fn-owner-finish-submission; fn-lgoc-finish-preserves-invariant), the refused reservation (fn-owner-refuse-reservation; fn-lgoc-refuse-reservation-preserves-invariant), every safe file observation incl. the recovery barriers (fn-lgoc-rcon-io-preserves-invariant), and the live configuration completion fn-oclc-publish (fn-lgoc-publish-preserves-invariant). The step lemma: an owner over a Store related to the same configuration history and a history extending its own satisfies fn-ocl-relation (fn-lgoc-ocl-relation-of-owner-with-store).
proofs.progress_note: Lane control-quanta-2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27; PKT-827 (c)). Proved against the owner-model steps the host calls on dev 92bb10df1 (it contains log-2 and scheduler-2-rebase: their START/BARRIER/COMPLETE and pipelined sync call the same fn-olr-ocfg-reserve/-order, prepare and finish per member). Not covered: the deferred publications (retention, identity, consumer, topic prepares and their order), fn-owner-known-abort, :begin/:take and the served reads (they leave the Store unchanged; their fn-ocl-relation theorems exist).

proofs.title: A live configuration request is authorized from the owner's carried state before publication: an authorized record's completion is durable, and the durable history reopens to the state it installs
proofs.statement: books/config-owner-carried.lisp fn-oclc-live-authorizep (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reconfigure-authorizedp, called by host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked after staging and before fnn-admin-publish): the staged record applies to the owner's carried node and configuration (fn-oclc-configure changes the configuration history). fn-oclc-live-authorizep-is-durable-completion: for a staged record at its generation, the completion fn-oclc-publish answers :durable iff the request was authorized (never :recovery-required for an authorized record). KEYSTONE fn-oclc-authorized-record-reopens (hypotheses fn-ocl-relation OC and the authorization): the Store the completion installs satisfies fn-cpo-history-relation -- the configured fold of the configuration history extended by the record over the Store's history (the log's records the owner carries) succeeds and its node at the frontier, domain and capacity are the installed ones -- with the history extended by exactly the record, the Store history and frontier unchanged, and the live configuration the reopened fold's (fn-ocl-store-config). It reads no record and replays nothing.

proofs.title: While a batch's barrier is in flight readers are served at the durable view and new POSTs are prepared into the next batch: no read reveals a record of the batch in flight or of the next one before its COMPLETE, and no new POST joins the batch in flight
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-ocv-capture (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reader-views-capture, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-reader-capture at the committer's START, START-NEXT, COMPLETE and drop), fn-ocfg-with-view / fn-ocfg-at-reader-view (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-at-reader-view, around fn-owner-chunk-span and fn-owner-open), fn-olr-take (host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-take). KEYSTONE fn-ocvm-reader-view-is-the-completed-prefix (books/owner-reader-view.lisp): in the capture discipline's count model (a view as the record count it is the view of), along every legal run of START (at an idle owner), START-NEXT (behind a batch in flight, no next open), :unnext, COMPLETE and drop events from the idle owner, the reader view fn-ocv-reader-view is C, the count of records whose batch COMPLETED (whose barrier returned fenced: fn-ocp-complete-only-after-the-barrier), while the working view is C + A + B (A the batch in flight, B the next batch): no read counts a record of either batch before its COMPLETE. Hypothesis: the run is legal (fn-ocvm-legal-run-p), which fn-ocp-start-next-only-behind-a-sync and fn-ocp-sync-only-when-none-in-flight give the host's event order; the model counts views, the host captures the view objects at the same points. KEYSTONE fn-ocl-relation-of-a-view-captured-before-appends: the view of a related owner OC0 (fn-ocl-relation), put into a related owner OC whose Store has only appended records since OC0 (the same configuration history and configuration), gives a related owner, and the view's version is at most OC0's record count: every served-read theorem stated under fn-ocl-relation (fn-scar-ocfg-read-span-is-reference-under-ocl-relation among them) holds of the read a reader quantum runs during a barrier, over the replay of at most the records the Store held at the capture. Hypotheses: the append-only Store and the unchanged configuration between capture and read (in flight no control quantum runs: fn-ocs-in-flight-admits-only-inspect-commit-and-reader). Scope: the relation of the owner AFTER the reader's entry, with the working view put back, is PRF-296's (fn-orr-read-span-at-a-captured-view-restores-the-owner). KEYSTONE fn-olr-take-never-joins-the-batch-in-flight: the log's take never changes the kernel's INFLIGHT, and a taken record is appended to the open BATCH; with fn-ocp-sync-only-when-none-in-flight (the open batch is sealed only after the batch in flight is fenced) a POST a reader queued during a barrier never joins the batch in flight.
proofs.progress_note: Lane owner-scheduler-2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27; PKT-688 (4) slice 2, on lane commit-onto-log's :commit class). Host lines: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-gate-pick calls fn-ocs-next at every release of the owner and every arrival at an idle one; fnn-owner-gate-leave calls fn-ocs-observe; fnn-owner-commit-event calls fn-ocs-commit-event inside the committer's :commit quanta (fnn-owner-commit-batch: START = fnn-owner-commit-start-locked, then fnn-owner-commit-barrier with the owner released, then COMPLETE = fnn-owner-commit-complete-locked under a second :commit quantum whose unwind-protect applies :completed); host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status-answer enters as :inspect after ACL2's fn-native-live-status-host-requestp chose that path. Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-commit-steps-tests.lisp (states reached from fn-ocs-init; the keystone tight at 1 in and out of a batch; must-fail with the inspect absent for three picks: delay 3; in flight only readers waiting: nobody admitted, and the same readers admitted after :fenced/:completed (must-fail); the step machine's whole cycle and its faults). Native: tests.test_native_owner_scheduler test_status_is_answered_while_a_batch_barrier_is_in_flight (a developer selector holds the barrier 6 s: status answered inside it, GROUP and the 240 after it).

proofs.title: The owner holds its ledger as a snoc-list: the commit appends one pair in O(1), and the take, the outcome and the host's finish read its length in O(1)
proofs.statement: books/owner.lisp (post-alloc-3). The owner record's ledger field holds a snoc-list (books/snoc-list.lisp; a plain list, nil included, represents itself: fn-sl-list-when-plain); fn-own-ledger reads the list back (fn-sl-list of fn-own-ledger-field) and fn-own-make takes the FIELD, so a transition that keeps the ledger passes the field through and fn-own-ledger-of-fn-own-make reads (fn-sl-list FIELD), which fn-sl-list-of-fn-own-ledger-field names back as the ledger. fn-own-ledger-count (O(1) on a snoc form) is the length for every owner (fn-own-ledger-count-is-len); fn-own-take-submission's mark and fn-own-completion-consumedp read it through mbe (logic unchanged). KEYSTONES (no hypothesis): fn-rix-own-complete-enabled-ledger-field (the completion the host calls puts the pair on the field with fn-sl-snoc: one cons) and fn-rix-own-complete-enabled-ledger (the ledger it represents is the old one with the pair appended); fn-sl-list-of-fn-sl-snoc (PRF-275) for every value. Host subjects: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission -> books/owner-refresh-indexed.lisp fn-rix-own-finish -> fn-rix-own-complete -> fn-rix-own-complete-enabled; fn-owner-finish -> fn-rix-ocfg-complete (the same completion) and compares fn-own-ledger-count before and after. Before: the commit copied the ledger (fn-ag-append), 16 B x POSTs-since-open per POST, and the take and the outcome walked it for its length. Local policy (D27: bound work, not data); no RFC requirement.

proofs.title: A POST's profile admission is decided once per open and carried
proofs.statement: books/store-profile-carried.lisp (post-alloc-3). The carry pairs the Store profile with its admission verdict (fn-pvc-make, written once by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-profile; NIL at the recovery reset); fn-pvc-carryp: the verdict is fn-bs-profile-admittedp of the profile it names (no owner state, so no owner step falsifies it; fn-pvc-carryp-of-make, fn-pvc-carryp-when-atom); a reader uses the verdict only for the profile the carry names and decides afresh otherwise. KEYSTONES fn-pvc-article-budget-carried-is-cvec-article-budget-for (under fn-pvc-carryp, the budget fn-owner-prepare-buffer and fn-owner-prepare hand the prepare is fn-cvec-article-budget-for of the profile in hand), fn-pvc-post-boundary-carried-is-sbud-post-boundary (fn-owner-post-boundary), fn-pvc-verdict-carried-is-cvec-verdict-at (fn-owner-publication-verdict). Local policy; no RFC requirement.

proofs.title: The carried obligation-id set is a path-compressed id trie, updated by the retention delta
proofs.statement: books/post-retain-carried.lisp (post-alloc-3). The carry's set is a path-compressed id trie whose leaves are the ledger's own id strings (fn-rit-put, fn-rit-hasp; fn-rit-hasp-of-put holds for every node). fn-prc-carryp is fn-prc-set-okp: every pin and release id is in the trie and every string stored in it is a known id; fn-prc-set-okp-is-knownp: the trie then answers exactly fn-rii-knownp of the ledger it names. fn-prc-refresh keeps the carry for the same ledger, applies the retention delta (releases consed on the carried ones; pins = new pins over the carried ones less released ones: fn-prc-delta, fn-prc-set-okp-of-delta) and rebuilds only otherwise (fn-prc-set-okp-of-build); fn-prc-carryp-of-refresh. KEYSTONE unchanged: fn-prc-sbud-prepare-is-pidx-sbud-prepare (the prepare host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer installs is PRF-191's fn-pidx-sbud-prepare under fn-prc-carryp), through fn-prc-admissiblep-is-admissiblep. host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-extended builds the carry at every recovery (fn-prc-refresh of nil). Local policy; no RFC requirement.

proofs.title: The open streams the transaction files: the numbered chunk checks each file's sequence in its one decode, and the unframe answers the payload without copying it
proofs.statement: Subjects, called by the host: fn-srs-checked-decode and fn-srs-unframe (books/store-recover-stream.lisp sections 5 and 6). host/native/io.lisp fnn-recover-full-replay (fnn-recover: every full-replay open, the store verbs and the owner start) reads the transaction files a chunk at a time as the replay takes them (fnn-recover-file-chunks): each file unframed by fnn-unframe-list, which sends the file as its protected prefix and its trailer to host/store-host.lisp fn-store-unframe-split (fn-srs-unframe), then the chunk of (FILE-NUMBER . RECORD) pairs to fn-srs-checked-decode, then its value to the guard-verified fn-srs-intern-step unless it answered :sequence (the host faults, as the per-file check did). KEYSTONE fn-srs-checked-decode-is-the-per-file-check: for every numbered chunk, fn-srs-checked-decode is :bad when a record does not decode, otherwise :sequence unless every record's sequence (fn-srs-record-sequence, which host/store-host.lisp fn-store-record-sequence is) is its file's number, and otherwise the decode of the chunk's records. fn-srs-checked-step-is-the-step: the host's two calls over a numbered chunk are fn-srs-step over its records, so PRF-261's fold keystone carries over. KEYSTONE fn-srs-unframe-is-the-frame-decode (no hypothesis, guard-verified subject): fn-srs-unframe of PREFIX and TRAILER is fn-frame-store-decode of their concatenation with fn-frame-trailer of PREFIX, which is what fnn-unframe computed for the whole file and its digest; on a well-formed frame its payload is PREFIX's own tail (no copy). Scope: the full-replay path without a selected pack (with one, the history is fnn-committed-history's and goes over in chunks by PRF-261); the open now answers the record count, and the verbs that need the records read them with fnn-history-records, which on a format-9 store reads the record log (fnn-log-history-records: the log kernel's committed records) and on format 8 the per-file layout (lane rm2-format9).

proofs.title: The owner's prepares decide the served groups themselves, and the carried owner invariant holds across every owner prepare the host calls, the deferred publications' order and the known abort
proofs.statement: books/owner-prepare-served.lisp and books/owner-prepare-served-ocl.lisp. The host's article prepare is fn-psrv-prepare (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer and fn-owner-prepare): fn-prc-sbud-prepare when fn-psrv-event-servedp of the live configuration and the record, the owner unchanged otherwise (fn-psrv-prepare-refuses-unserved, fn-psrv-prepare-when-served); the refusal word is fn-psrv-refusal-kind (:refused for an unserved group). The host makes no served test. fn-psrv-event-servedp equals the configured replay's fn-cpr-event-servedp at the configuration (fn-psrv-event-servedp-is-cpr-event-servedp). KEYSTONES, each with fn-lgoc-invariantp (PRF-286) as the only hypothesis unless named: fn-psrv-prepare-preserves-invariant (plus fn-prc-carryp and the two carried index premises of PRF-191/PRF-242; no served hypothesis), fn-psrv-prepare-identity-preserves-invariant (fn-owner-prepare-identity: fn-psrv-prepare-identity tests a signed composite's article groups), fn-psrv-prepare-retention-preserves-invariant and fn-psrv-prepare-consumer-preserves-invariant ((:store (:prepare-retention/consumer E)) through fn-ocfg-step), fn-psrv-prepare-topic-preserves-invariant (fn-owner-prepare-topic: fn-psrv-prepare-topic, which is (:store (:prepare-topic E)) where the consumer projection admits E, fn-psrv-prepare-topic-is-ocfg-step-when-admitted), fn-psrv-known-abort-preserves-invariant ((:store (:known-abort))), fn-psrv-rcon-io-preserves-invariant (every record file observation of any staged record) and fn-psrv-log-order-preserves-invariant (fn-olr-ocfg-order whatever is staged). Store level: fn-psrv-deferred-stage-preserves (a deferred candidate staged at the reservation keeps fn-cst-relation and fn-cstp-carriedp), fn-psrv-deferred-record-dir-preserves-relation, fn-psrv-known-abort-preserves. The bridge to the budget gate: fn-psrv-prepare-is-sbud-prepare-when-served (under the carry's recognizer and PRF-191/PRF-242's carried view premises, the host's prepare of a served record is fn-sbud-prepare). The standalone Store's POST (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-prepare) calls fn-psrv-store-prepare-next (books/store-prepare-served.lisp), which stages only a record whose groups the configuration serves (fn-psrv-store-prepare-next-cases).
proofs.progress_note: Lane prepare-served (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27; PKT-827 (d)). The retired-group witness (control-quanta-2's *lgt-r-prepared*) is refused by the host's prepare with the invariant kept. Teeth for the identity, consumer and topic prepares (lane host-decisions, 2026-09-27): tests/acl2/owner-prepare-served-events-tests.lisp, reachable positive witnesses on owner-log-ocl-tests' configured owner over the events ACL2 proposes to the host (fn-th-local-propose :install, fn-col-bootstrap, fn-hsig-keyring-event, fn-pa-authorized-event's composite row): each staged, invariant carried, then ordered and finished with the invariant (*pse-topic-staged*, *pse-consumer-staged*, *pse-identity-staged*, *pse-k2-reserved* composite); the topic prepare equals the configured owner's (:store (:prepare-topic E)) at the admitted event; THE UNSERVED-COMPOSITE WITNESS (fn.test retired by a live completion, the author enrolled): refused, owner unchanged, invariant kept, while fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity stages it and breaks the invariant; corrupted-state witnesses labelled separately. The topic prepare's projection-refused branch has no reachable witness (argued, not proved: the proposal's sequence is the carried topic counter, which the invariant keeps at the Store's next). FINDING: the plain signed composite (fn-stxa-p, what fn-owner-prepare-identity admits and fn-pcb-carried-event returns) is never staged: fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity admits only the row (fn-hstxa-p); witnessed in the same book. Certified hbox certify-20260927T145853Z-4012905. The host's identity entry is now fn-oiis-prepare-identity (books/owner-identity-served.lisp: signed-post's interned row, then this target's served test; the plain-composite finding above is fixed by that intern). Its teeth: tests/acl2/owner-identity-served-tests.lisp -- *ois-staged* (reachable: the wire composite of the signed fn.test article at the arena's count, staged as the candidate row, invariant before and after, completed by order and finish), the retired fn.test composite refused by name (owner unchanged, invariant kept; fn-oii-ocfg-prepare-identity alone stages it and breaks the invariant), the WIRE value where the row is expected (not staged; its served test passes whatever the groups), and *ois-bad* (corrupted-state: invariant dropped, row staged, conclusion fails). proofs.title: A configuration request refused before its record is written is un-staged by ACL2, so the configuration lock does not outlive the refusal
proofs.statement: books/owner-prepare-served.lisp fn-psrv-unstage, called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reconfigure-unstage from host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked on the three pre-publication refusals (fn-oclc-live-authorizep refused, fnn-admin-authorize's candidate open refused, the immutable publisher's :refused); an uncertain publication or a fault keeps the stage and fences. KEYSTONE fn-psrv-unstage-preserves-invariant (hypothesis fn-lgoc-invariantp): the result carries the invariant, has the same owner (so the same Store and durable state: a process death on either side of the un-stage recovers the same history), configuration and pins, and nothing staged. Before it, a refused request left the record staged and fn-ocfg-step refused every :begin and :take (every POST) until a restart.

proofs.title: The served ARTICLE reads the article's bytes once and builds its reply in one pass, equal to the specified reply
proofs.statement: Lane gate-regress (2026-09-27): fn-rcompat-article-reply (books/nntp-reader-compat.lisp; reached from the served step through fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned, host/native/io.lisp fnn-reader-chunk's fn-served-step) executes fn-rcompat-article-reply-exec: one read of the article's bytes through the arena, the served reply over the served octets by fn-nntp-article-response-of-bytes, whose ARTICLE arm is the one pass fn-nntp-block-rev (RFC 3977 3.1.1 framing validated and each line dot-stuffed onto a reversed accumulator), and the stored reply's session decided by fn-nntp-response-okp-of-bytes without allocating. Over the live arena the exec is the specified reply (fn-rcompat-article-reply-exec-is-the-reply, hypothesis fn-arena-p); the pass is fn-nntp-crlf-lines then fn-nntp-stuff-lines then .CRLF over octet lists (fn-nntp-block-rev-is-the-block); fn-nntp-article-response is the of-bytes response over fn-nntp-article-bytes (fn-nntp-article-response-is-of-bytes); a response's session moves exactly when okp holds (fn-nntp-response-of-bytes-session).

proofs.title: The owner's identity prepare stages the row the intern makes of a signed composite, and seals its article's payload only when the Store took it
proofs.statement: books/owner-identity-intern.lisp fn-oii-ocfg-prepare-identity (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-identity, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-identity-commit for every signed POST's, signed NNTP transit's and signed BP application's kind-4 composite and every keyring snapshot). Since the records flip the identity prepare's gate (fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity) admits the retained kinds only (fn-stxe-p, fn-stxk-p, fn-hstxa-p); the owner's composite (fn-pa-authorized-event) is a wire fn-stxa-p, so it was refused and every signed POST answered 441. The entry stages fn-oii-identity-row, the row fn-intern-event makes, at the arena's count under the Store's keyring and generation. fn-oii-identity-row-is-the-intern: at h = (fn-arena-count fn-arena) the row is (mv-nth 0 (fn-intern-event w k g fn-arena)); fn-oii-seal-is-the-intern-arena: the intern's arena is the arena with fn-oii-identity-payload sealed when fn-oii-identity-sealsp holds, else unchanged (the host seals exactly that, and only when the Store changed); fn-oii-composite-row-is-held: a composite whose article decodes interns to an fn-hstxa-p row carrying the composite unchanged (D25: the relayed octets, which the test book shows are the poster's post-injection octets). KEYSTONE fn-oii-ocfg-prepare-identity-is-intern-then-step (hypothesis fn-own-relation of the owner): the entry at the arena's count is (fn-ocfg-step oc (list :store (list :prepare-identity ROW)) fn-arena) for ROW the intern's row, by PRF-144's fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity-is-ocfg-step-under-relation.
proofs.progress_note: Lane signed-post (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27). The regression: records-flip c5808cd72 (fn-sn-prepare-identity's gate to fn-hstxa-p) and flip-L3 d689ec388 (the same in fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity) changed the gate; the host entry kept passing the wire composite, and owner-signed-post-tests hand-built its row (ospt-row), so no test crossed the host line. The test book's witness is the reachable served-POST trace of owner-signed-post-tests over a flipped owner: the wire composite is refused by the gate, the interned row is staged, and the completion records the signed verdict.

proofs.title: The store's history is an abstract stobj of columns whose logical value is the history list, and the store node's event index answers what it answers
proofs.statement: books/history-columns.lisp (lane history-columns, stage 1 of 3; the coordinator's decision on PKT-PRS-1's event-index half, PKT-PRS-3, PKT-PRS-4). defabsstobj fn-hist: logical value the true list of retained events (fn-sf-records, oldest first, sequence = position); executable fn-hist$c: a resizable rows column by sequence, the count, and a Message-ID table from a salted 32-bit FNV-1a hash of the Message-ID of an event's article (taken by digest-free shape, fn-hist-key-article) to the sequences carrying it, newest first; a lookup compares every candidate exactly (fn-cei-event-article, fn-held-p, equal), so no answer assumes Message-ID uniqueness or hash separation (PKT-774 worst case: an adversary who learns the salt puts all N articles in one bucket; a lookup is then N exact comparisons, an append stays O(1)). Correspondence fn-hist$corr: the object IS the fold of the history's appends from the empty object with its salt (supporters digest-free; :corr-fn-exists t). Exports refined by defabsstobj: fn-hist-count (len), fn-hist-at (nth), fn-hist-msgid-records (fn-cei-article-records-for), fn-hist-append (append one) and fn-hist-clear, all exec functions guard-verified. KEYSTONE fn-hist-load-is-the-history: the open's load (clear with a salt, one append per event) is the history. Bridges over the store node's index under its correspondence fn-cei-correspondencep (PRF-144): fn-hist-count-serves-cei-count, fn-hist-at-serves-cei-get (every natural sequence, the history within 2^32 events), fn-hist-msgid-records-serve-cei (every Message-ID). Stage 2a (books/history-columns-store.lisp): R(o, fn-hist) := fn-hist = (fn-sf-records (fn-sn-files (fn-own-store o))); fn-hist-sync appends the rows past the stobj's count (fn-sf-records-nth); KEYSTONE fn-hist-sync-after-run-is-the-history: under fn-own-relation, R before any fn-own-run implies the synced stobj is the history after it (by fn-own-run-records-prefix); fn-hist-sync-of-prefix-is-the-history. The store's carried folds from the stobj under R alone, for every cache: fn-hist-count-is-used (fn-sbud-used), fn-hist-bytes-carried-is-bytes-extend, fn-hist-debt-carried-is-debt-extend, fn-hist-usage-carried-is-usage-extend (the EXTEND specifications fn-sbud-bytes-carried, fn-scf-debt-carried, fn-scf-usage-carried meet under the index). Stage 2b path E (lane history-columns-2): host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-extended calls fn-hist-load on the installed store's history (every recovery: fn-owner-recover-from-store-open, -recover-rows, -recover-from-checkpoint), establishing R; fn-owner-record-octets, fn-owner-record-debt and fn-owner-carried-usage call fn-hist-sync on the owner store's files then fn-hist-bytes-carried, fn-hist-debt-carried and fn-hist-usage-carried (guard-verified), preserving R between installs by fn-hist-sync-after-run-is-the-history; the committed count the budget reads is fn-sf-records-count (fn-sf-records-count-is-used-by-definition), no longer the event index. Not yet switched (stage 2b remainder): the Message-ID readers (acceptance payload ref on the store node, the BP receiver's fast lookups), the consumer poll window, the owner completion refresh, the checkpoint tables and the in-book prepares' fn-sbud-count. Local policy; no RFC requirement.
proofs.progress_note: history-columns stage 1 2026-09-27: measured in an hbox ACL2 session over the same held rows, the structure's own live bytes per record: fn-hist 58.6 B (10k, 27-char Message-IDs), 56.8 B (10k, 47-char), 76.4 B (1k); the store node's index fn-cei-build 692 B, 1,429 B, 681 B. Stage 2 (switch the store node's index) and stage 3 (held-row strings into a byte pool) open.

proofs.title: The log kernel the host holds keeps the committed records' count, frames by guard-verified code, and every host transition over it, the pipelined commit's included, is the logical kernel's transition under the abstraction
proofs.statement: Subjects: the concrete kernel transitions host/native/io.lisp calls (fnn-log-open-kernel -> fn-lgc-open, fnn-log-prepare -> fn-lgc-t-prepare, fnn-log-take -> fn-lgc-phase / fn-lgc-take, fnn-log-ensure-extent -> fn-lgc-extension-needed-p / fn-lgc-extension-target, fnn-log-append -> fn-lgc-append-admitsp / fn-lgc-frontier / fn-lgc-append-octets / fn-lgc-append, fnn-log-fence (the syncer's fnn-log-sync-sealed-batch) -> fn-lgc-fence / fn-lgc-fence-failed, fnn-log-finish -> fn-lgc-finish-one, fnn-log-rotate -> fn-lgc-rotate-admitsp / -rotate-needed-p / -rotate, the open's catch-up, fnn-log-reserve and fnn-log-write-history -> fn-lgc-consume-to). The concrete kernel is (:lgc COUNT LAST FRONTIER NEXT-TXID BATCH INFLIGHT ACKED PHASE); fn-lgc-of replaces the logical kernel's COMMITTED by its length. KEYSTONE fn-lgc-run-refines-the-kernel (books/store-log-kernel-concrete.lisp): for every host operation sequence OPS -- prepare, take, consume-to, append, SEAL (the extension to fn-lgc-sealed-extent then the append: lane log-2's pipelined commit), fence, fence-failed, finish-one, rotate -- the concrete kernel reached from fn-lgc-open of the segment string is fn-lgc-of the logical kernel reached by the same OPS from fn-lgt-recover of its octets (the kernel fn-lg-recover-program-establishes-the-relation names), with no hypothesis. The pipelined commit's owner and syncer steps are each one operation under the log's kernel lock (fnn-log-with-kernel), so every interleaving is one OPS (a take behind the batch in flight is a :take between its :seal and :fence). So PRF-264's relation, crash and link theorems over fn-lgk-* are theorems about the kernel the host holds. Per transition: fn-lgc-prepare-refines, -t-prepare-, -append-, -fence-, -fence-failed-, -finish-one-, -consume-to-, -take-, -rotate-refines, fn-lgc-open-refines, and the observers (fn-lgc-observers-of-abstraction, -append-octets-, -append-len-, -fitsp-, -append-admitsp-, -extension-needed-p-, -extension-target-, -sealed-extent-of-abstraction). The extension: fn-lgc-extend-program-keeps-the-relation (fn-lg-extend-program run over the concrete kernel ends on the same kernel, R-related to the logical one, the segment NEXT long; fn-lg-extend-run-keeps-the-kernel), fn-lgc-sealed-extent-fits-the-batch (after the extension the seal's append fits, whole units, never shrinking; hypotheses: a positive unit, an extent of whole units). Execution (input-loop-2 section 6: *1* fn-lg-log recursed per octet and a 3 MiB POST exhausted the owner's stack): the fit and the fence's frontier use fn-lgc-log-len, guard-verified arithmetic over record lengths, equal to (len (fn-lg-log records prev unit)) with no hypothesis (fn-lgc-log-len-is-the-log-length); the append's octets and the fence's chain head use guard-verified twins fn-lgx-* (each equal to its logical function with no hypothesis) through fn-lgc-log-octets / fn-lgc-last-trailer (fn-lgc-log-octets-is-log, fn-lgc-last-trailer-is-last-trailer). Measured (hbox, 1,000 POSTs x 2 KiB, format 9): the kernel's retained COMMITTED was 38.8 KB per record (18 B per history octet) of live heap, and each fence copied it; after, 0 (planning/evidence/per-record-state-2026-09-27.md; lane kernel-concrete-2's re-measure there).

proofs.title: The Store prepares' field checks are ACL2's: the host calls one verdict per prepare, the metadata bound is exactly the record codec's, and every field the node generates for a POST is admitted
proofs.statement: books/post-fields.lisp. Subjects, each the function the host calls: fn-pfld-article-inputsp (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer, fn-owner-prepare; host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-prepare), fn-pfld-retention-inputsp (fn-owner-prepare-retention, fn-store-sn-prepare-retention), fn-pfld-lookup-inputsp (fn-owner-existing-action, fn-owner-existing-action-buffer, fn-store-sn-existing-action), fn-pfld-group-name-requestp (fn-owner-reconfigure, fn-owner-declare-group), fn-pfld-bp-ingress-inputsp (host/bp-ingress-host.lisp fn-bpi-host-inputsp), fn-af-message-idp (fn-store-sn-lookup, -lookup-foundp, -verdict), fn-pfld-post-evidence (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-prov-post). The host predicates fn-store-text-octetsp, fn-store-msgid-octetsp, fn-store-msgid-validp and the host constant *fn-store-max-text* (512) are deleted. KEYSTONE fn-pfld-textp-is-a-record-metadata-field: an admitted field is fn-record-metadata-bytes-p of its string and its octets round-trip. KEYSTONE fn-pfld-textp-is-exactly-the-record-metadata-domain: over printable octets (33..126, hypothesis) the check IS the record's metadata domain, so no ceiling below the codec's (*fn-record-max-metadata* 256) remains; the deleted 512 admitted fields the record refuses. KEYSTONE fn-pfld-identity-text-is-admitted: fn-id-text of a nonempty octet identity of at most 128 octets (a SHA-256 identity is 32) is admitted. KEYSTONE fn-pfld-post-evidence-is-admitted: for a natural generation, the post evidence (wire form when fn-prov-durablep, legacy rendering otherwise; principal 'local' when no path identity) is admitted. fn-pfld-group-name-requestp-is-bounded-by-the-codec: a group-name request is within the group name's codec ceiling. Scope: the three metadata fields are node-generated, so their bound is a codec domain (STO-021's third class), not an admission limit or a profile field; the data a POST carries keeps its bounds where they are (RFC 5536 Message-ID, the profile's payload/group bound fn-sbud-post-boundary, the profile's header limits STO-030).
proofs.progress_note: Lane host-decisions (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27; prepare-served's host-decision list, item 1). Teeth: tests/acl2/post-fields-tests.lisp: REACHABLE witnesses over the identities and evidence the node builds for a POST (fn-id-subject-of-payload, fn-id-obligation-of through the digest attachment; fn-pfld-post-evidence with and without a path identity), each keystone's complete antecedent and conclusion; each conjunct of the article verdict removed refuses; BOUNDARY witnesses at 256/257/512 octets (the old host limit admitted 512, the record refuses it); the printable hypothesis needed (a space is a metadata octet the check refuses); the identity bound needed (129 octets renders 258); must-fail of the exactness keystone without its hypothesis and of the identity keystone without its bound.

proofs.title: A known abort of any staged deferred record (retention, identity, consumer, topic) resolves: the Store lands :ready with the live node advanced over the consumed transaction id, the relations kept
proofs.statement: books/store-node-resolution.lisp fn-sn-known-abort (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-known-abort: (:store (:known-abort)) through fn-owner-step, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-publish-prepared on a StoreError before the link; host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-known-abort for the standalone Store). fn-sn-known-abort-enabledp: a record phase (:record-staged or :record-data-durable) and, for a held article row, fn-sn-record-bindsp; for every other Store event (fn-store-event-p, not fn-held-p), that the event applies to the live node (consp of fn-replay-apply-record). The transition: the file kernel's known abort (fn-sn-known-abort-files, unchanged) and the node's aborted completion for a held row, fn-replay-advance-txid to the frontier for a deferred event. Before this target only the retention event had the deferred arm; a known abort of a staged identity, consumer or topic record was the identity, so the owner answered :fault and the host fenced (indeterminate) where the abort was known. KEYSTONE fn-sn-known-abort-preserves-relation (fn-snt-relation, no other hypothesis), fn-sn-known-abort-is-exact-node-abort (:ready and the node, per arm), fn-sn-known-abort-cannot-acknowledge. Configured level: fn-psrv-known-abort-preserves (fn-cst-relation and fn-cstp-carriedp) and fn-psrv-known-abort-preserves-invariant (fn-lgoc-invariantp of the owner after (:store (:known-abort))), every candidate. Crash points: the abort performs no syscall; its cuts are the record program's cuts before the link (books/byte-store-programs fn-bs-record-program: record-created, record-written, record-staged-durable), which are independent of the record's kind.
proofs.progress_note: Lane host-decisions-abort (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27; lane host-decisions item 2, prepare-served's liveness finding). Teeth, reachable (the real reserve and prepare of each kind, then fn-sn-known-abort; antecedent and conclusion asserted): tests/acl2/store-identity-traces-tests *sit-identity-aborted* (keyring snapshot, :record-staged) and *sit-composite-aborted* (signed composite fn-hstxa-p, :record-data-durable); tests/acl2/consumer-store-node-tests *csnt-ack-aborted* (consumer ack; restaged after at the same sequence); tests/acl2/topic-history-store-node-tests *thsn-install-aborted* (topic admin install). CORRUPTED-STATE witness: *sit-corrupt-staged-identity* (node advanced past the event: gate refuses, abort is the identity, relation false). Owner-level reachable witnesses (lane host-decisions-teeth): tests/acl2/owner-prepare-served-abort-tests.lisp *psa-topic-aborted*, *psa-consumer-aborted*, *psa-keyring-aborted*, *psa-composite-aborted* -- the host's (:store (:known-abort)) on the topic, consumer, keyring and interned-composite-row candidates the host's own prepares staged (owner-prepare-served-events-tests, owner-identity-served-tests): fn-owner-known-abort's word :aborted, :ready, the node's next txid advanced to the frontier, no record published, fn-lgoc-invariantp before and after, and a second prepare (a fresh topic install) admitted and staged with the invariant (the owner is not fenced). Affected roots of store-node-resolution, owner-prepare-served-ocl, post-fields and these test books at 4 jobs on hbox, certify-20260927T153827Z-94348: 308 passed, 9 red, all nine listed in planning/evidence/batch-au-flip-reds-2026-09-27.md (records-flip wire-vs-row assertions: bp-release-authority, bp-request-reference, owner-store-indexed, post-identity-index, reader-open-carried, records-concrete, store-carried-folds, store-events-carried, store-reclaim-holders tests); none reads the known abort. The host needed no change: fn-owner-known-abort already answers :aborted exactly when ACL2 moved the Store to :ready.

proofs.title: A reader entry during a batch's barrier leaves the owner related, with its working view, Store and configuration back, and answers the reference read at the captured view; no configuration publication (an XREDEEM's among them) runs under a capture
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-orr-read-span (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at, called for every served socket region by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk-read through fnn-core-buffer-state) and fn-ocs-publication-class with fn-ocs-next (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-redeem-quantum: an XREDEEM PASS's publication, in a quantum of that class after the reader quantum; fnn-owner-gate-pick calls fn-ocs-next). KEYSTONE fn-orr-read-span-at-a-captured-view-restores-the-owner (books/owner-reader-read.lisp): with a capture held (VIEWS a cons whose first is the view of the owner OC0 at the capture), under fn-ocri-relation of OC0 and of the working owner OC, OC's Store records OC0's with EXTRA appended, the same configuration history and configuration, the span read's catalog premise fn-scr-owner-catalogp at the captured view, and natp i, end: the owner after the entry satisfies fn-ocri-relation (hence fn-ocl-relation), has OC's view, Store, next id, connection bound, pending, ledger, clock, facts, configuration and staged record (the entry changes its connections only), and the reply is the effects of fn-ocfg-read of OC at the captured view over the consumed octets. With no capture it is fn-scr-ocfg-read-span (fn-orr-read-span-without-a-capture-is-the-span-read-by-definition). KEYSTONE fn-ocvp-reader-view-is-at-the-current-generation: in the capture discipline with configuration generations (fn-ocv-capture of the working count tagged with the generation; START, START-NEXT, :unnext, COMPLETE, drop, and :publish legal only with no capture held), along every legal run from the idle owner the reader view carries the current generation: the configuration hypothesis above holds at every read. :publish is legal only with no capture because a publication runs as fn-ocs-publication-class (:control), which fn-ocs-next never picks in flight (fn-ocs-a-publication-waits-for-the-complete, from fn-ocs-in-flight-admits-only-inspect-commit-and-reader), and the committer holds a capture only while a batch is in flight. Scope: the Store-append and the capture-only-in-flight premises are the host discipline (the commit steps append; START captures, COMPLETE releases), not restated from the host code; a redeem waiting in the gate stalls its own I/O loop for up to the barrier, as a transit connection's wait does.
proofs.progress_note: Lane scheduler-3 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27; PKT-828 open items 1 and 2, continuing scheduler-2-rebase). Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-reader-read-tests.lisp: a reached capture (owner-log-ocl-tests' *lgt-oc0*, 2 records) and working owner (*lgt-finished*, the POST committed, 3 records), GROUP fn.letters on connection 0 answers 211 0 1 0 at the reader view and 211 1 1 1 at the working one; one hypothesis-removal witness per hypothesis (a relabelled view; the capture's owner or the working owner carrying it; the roles swapped so the Store is not an append; a publication between capture and read, config-owner-publish-tests' *ocp-closed* / *ocp-new*, where a GROUP repins connection 2 to the new configuration with the old view's archive and the owner leaves the relation), must-fail with the keystone's own hints for the configuration alone and the catalog premise; the generation model's reached run and its illegal publication in flight; the scheduler picks nobody for a waiting control class in flight and picks it outside. proofs.title: The format-9 open reads a segment one entry at a time, and the stream it runs is the recovered kernel's scan
proofs.statement: Subjects: the calls host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-stream-segment makes per entry (fn-lgw-start, fn-lgw-header-len, fn-lgw-entry-len, fn-lgw-step, fn-lgw-stop, fn-lgw-pos, fn-lgw-broken, fn-lgw-kernel), reached from fnn-log-recover, fnn-log-open-read-only and fnn-log-scan-segments (fnn-recover-log, whose full replay takes each record straight into the replay's chunk), and from the history reads fnn-log-read-closed-segment and fnn-log-read-active-segment (the active segment to the concrete kernel's frontier). The host reads the header octets fn-lgw-header-len names at the state's offset, then the entry fn-lgw-entry-len names (or none), and fn-lgw-step decides it from one frame open (fn-lgw-decide-is-okp-and-records): the record (handed to the replay, not kept), the next offset past the padding, the chain's trailer, the count, the next txid, the stop and the splice verdict. KEYSTONE fn-lgw-run-is-the-open (books/store-log-stream.lisp): over the segment's octets C, with no hypothesis, the run from (fn-lgw-start GENESIS FLOOR) emits exactly the committed records (a batch entry's several in order, PKT-749) of (fn-lgt-recover C GENESIS UNIT MAX FLOOR) in order, ends in a state whose kernel is fn-lgc-of that recovered kernel (the kernel fn-lg-recover-program-establishes-the-relation names; PRF-276's refinement starts from it), and whose splice verdict is fn-lgs-chain-broken-p of C. Composed from one window = the scan's slice (fn-lgw-window-is-the-slice), one step = one scan step (fn-lgw-step-when-entry, -when-no-entry), and fn-lgw-run-is-the-scan (the run over the steps with the step closed); fn-lgw-run-is-fn-lgc-open equates it with the whole-segment open. The host's reads are windows of C (A-HOST's read of a regular file, the assumption the whole-segment read made). Measured in planning/evidence/log-open-stream-2026-09-27.md.

proofs.title: A live owner's administrative publication is authorized from its carried state: no Store record read and no history replayed, equal to the replaying authorization under the owner invariant
proofs.statement: books/config-owner-live-authorize.lisp fn-olau-authorize (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-cfg-native-admin-authorize, called by host/native/admin.lisp fnn-admin-authorize-owner from fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked for every live configuration verb): fn-native-admin-publication-authorize under the profile's group-name bound and configuration generations, with the candidate open replaced by fn-olau-candidatep -- the ready phase, the observed configuration history equal to the carried one, the configuration-only fold one step from the observed history's, the record at the frontier with the next sequence, and the one record accepted by and applied to the carried node and configuration (fn-cnode-carried-acceptablep, fn-oclc-apply), its node accepting the frontier. KEYSTONE fn-olau-authorize-is-the-replayed-authorization (hypotheses: fn-ocl-relation OC, the conjunct of fn-lgoc-invariantp it needs; the store at :ready; CONFIG-RECORDS the carried configuration history; the record's txid the frontier; fn-olau-events-reopenp of the Store history, its identity, consumer and topic replays and identity typing): fn-olau-authorize equals fn-cvec-native-admin-authorize over the carried rows and frontier on every arm. fn-olau-candidatep-is-the-replayed-candidate (fn-cpo-history-relation, :ready, the carried configuration, a record at the frontier, the reopen conditions): the carried candidate is fn-native-admin-candidate-openp of the extended history.

proofs.title: The catalog and the owner's view stay joined: established at every open and kept by every host entry (the served chain's catalog premise carried as fn-scj-invp)
proofs.statement: books/served-catalog-join.lisp fn-scj-joinp (the catalog's view at its count is the owner's visible archive; every withdrawal mark below the count; every row's sequence below the view's version) gives fn-sca-join, the served chain's open hypothesis (fn-scj-joinp-gives-sca-join), and is preserved by the host's finish (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission and fn-owner-finish-identity: fn-sca-finish over the refreshed view's index and fn-sca-targets-of the completed Message-ID over its withdrawals) against the refreshed view fn-crf-apply-article, which is fn-own-refresh after an article completion (PRF-202): KEYSTONE fn-scj-joinp-of-article-finish, from the list-level KEYSTONE fn-scj-join-of-finish-lists (books/served-catalog-join-step.lisp). Hypotheses: the join before; the old index corresponds to the old visible list; string Message-IDs in both visible lists; the completed Message-ID new and the old visible Message-IDs distinct (acceptance fn-articles-freshp); the pending row is the completed article's row, not withdrawn, with its sequence below the new version; THE ROW EQUATION: the committed row read as an article (fn-cat-row-article) is the installed article, numbers included (OPEN: catalog numbers are one past each group's high over the rows, the acceptance's its watermarks). The identity finish's owner (fn-rix-ocfg-complete, no staged record, the event index carried) is the article finish's (fn-scj-identity-finish-owner-is-article-finish-owner), so fn-sca-ocl-relation-of-finish holds there (fn-scj-ocl-relation-of-identity-finish). fn-sca-targets-of now scans the whole withdrawal list (it stopped at the first record of another cause, an ordering no invariant carries). THE ROW RELATION (lane sca-join-2, books/served-catalog-join-number.lisp fn-scj-acc-rowsp): the acceptance's articles are the catalog's rows read as articles, newest first, numbers included; every watermark of the domain is one past the rows' high in that group; no row binds a number outside the domain. KEYSTONE fn-scj-acc-rowsp-of-install (and -withdrawn): an acceptance that prepares and installs row H's article stays related to the catalog that commits H (fn-scj-allocate-is-assign-numbers: the allocation at the watermarks IS fn-cat-assign-numbers). KEYSTONE fn-scj-acc-rowsp-of-cpr-loop (books/served-catalog-join-open.lisp): the configured replay fold and the host's load (fn-sca-load-held-rows-from, any view index) keep it event for event (fn-scj-acc-rowsp-of-replay-record: article and composite rows, retention, identity-neutral events; fn-scj-acc-rowsp-of-apply-config: a configuration record grows the domain at watermark 1). KEYSTONE fn-scj-acc-rowsp-at-idle-related-owner (E): for every owner in fn-ocl-relation at an idle store -- what recover, checkpoint open and the full open install (fn-sca-ocl-relation-at-recover, -at-full-open) and what a reclaimed store re-enters by -- the catalog the host loads from its rows (fn-sca-load-held-rows, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-extended) is related to its acceptance. KEYSTONE fn-scj-row-equation-of-acc-rowsp: under the relation the committed row read as an article is the head of the installed acceptance's articles, which discharges fn-scj-joinp-of-article-finish's row-equation hypothesis given the relation after the install. THE JOIN AT THE OPENS (lane sca-join-3, books/served-catalog-join-entry.lisp): KEYSTONE fn-scj-joinp-of-load: the catalog the host loads (fn-sca-load-held-rows) from ROWS under a view's index is joined to that view when it is related to an acceptance (fn-scj-acc-rowsp) whose articles the view filters (the visible list is fn-ctl-visible-articles of them) and indexes (the index is fn-midx-build of the visible list), the rows carry no withdrawal (fn-scj-rows-clearp) and every loaded row's sequence is below the view's version (fn-scj-rows-seqs-below); from the load's invariant fn-scj-load-invp (the view at the count is the rows' articles filtered by the index, fn-scj-shown) and the view side fn-scj-shown-of-build-of-filter (distinct string Message-IDs). KEYSTONE fn-scj-joinp-at-idle-current-owner: for every owner in fn-ocl-relation at an idle store with an indexed, current view (version the history's length, frontier the store's), whose rows carry no withdrawal and satisfy fn-rows-composites-okp, the loaded catalog is joined (the sequences from the replay's own sequence check, fn-scj-seqs-from-of-cpr-replay, and the intern's composite binding, fn-scj-load-h-sequence). KEYSTONES fn-scj-joinp-at-recover and fn-scj-joinp-at-full-open: over the owner the host installs (fn-ock-recover-extended, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-extended) and the catalog it loads under that owner's view index; the full open's intern writes no withdrawal (fn-scj-intern-events-rows-clear); the checkpoint entry takes fn-scj-rows-clearp of its rows as it takes fn-rows-composites-okp. THE FINISH LINK (lane sca-join-3, books/served-catalog-join-finish.lisp): the row relation reads a catalog only through its rows read as articles (fn-scj-acc-rowsp-by-arts); the catalog's invariant fn-scj-rows-invp (its rows as articles are the load's of the store's history) holds of every load (fn-scj-rows-invp-of-load) and KEYSTONE fn-scj-finish-keeps-rows-invp: the host's fn-sca-finish with the token and count it checks keeps it over the history the store appended EVENT to when the pending row is EVENT's loaded row; at an idle store in the live relation it gives the row relation (fn-scj-acc-rowsp-of-rows-invp). KEYSTONE fn-scj-joinp-at-host-finish: over the owner fn-ccar-own-finish installs (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission through fn-apc-own-finish-is-ccar-own-finish) and the catalog fn-sca-finish computes over that owner's view index and targets, the join and the rows invariant are carried, the row equation discharged (fn-scj-finish-row-side); hypotheses: the join and the rows invariant before, the view indexed and at most the old history's length, the store after idle and related with history old ++ EVENT (composites bound, rows clear), the finish link, the host's token and count, PRF-202's acceptance and verdict equations, and both visible lists acceptance filters (fn-ocl-view-historyp). THE CARRIED INVARIANT (lane sca-join-4, books/served-catalog-join-conns.lisp): fn-scj-invp = the join, the rows as the load of the history the view has seen (fn-own-take of its version), VV (the view's raw list and verdicts are the store's acceptance articles and verdicts), the view live over the catalog, every connection record pinned over it; fn-scj-invp-gives-owner-catalogp. KEYSTONE fn-scj-ocfg-read-span-is-reference-under-invp: the chain keystone with fn-scr-owner-catalogp replaced by fn-scj-invp. Established: fn-scj-invp-at-recover, -at-full-open (books/served-catalog-join-inv.lisp; the owner fn-owner-install-extended installs and the catalog it loads). Kept: the host's read entry fn-otm-read-span / fn-orr-read-span (fn-scj-invp-of-otm-read-span, fn-scj-invp-of-orr-read-span; a captured reader view live over the catalog, fn-scj-captured-owner-catalogp, kept across the finish by fn-scj-live-okp-of-finish); the refresh (fn-scj-invp-of-refresh: under VV the refresh takes fn-ctl-refresh-visible's first arm, so a verdict-only refresh cannot move the view -- store verdicts change only with an accepted article, fn-scj-identity-finish-keeps-verdicts); every connection arm (books/served-catalog-join-frame-conns.lisp, fn-scj-invp-of-ocfg-step-conn-event, fn-scj-conn-pinp-of-view-pinned); every store arm that completes no article (books/served-catalog-join-frame-store.lisp, fn-scjs-invp-of-store-frame); pinned readers across the catalog finish (books/served-catalog-join-pinned.lisp, fn-scj-owner-catalogp-at-host-finish: rows sorted by sequence, the bisection's view of an old pin unchanged); the article finish fn-scj-invp-at-host-article-finish-carried with PRF-202's acceptance and verdict equations derived (fn-scj-acceptance-of-article-finish, fn-scj-installed-article-msgid, fn-scj-verdicts-of-article-finish) and the history before the in-flight event read off fn-scjs-seenp; the identity finish fn-scj-invp-at-identity-finish. NAMED HYPOTHESES (not discharged): the view archive's fn-nntp-projectionp; the finished owner's relation facts (fn-own-view-okp, fn-cst-relation, the visible equations); the finish link and the rows' composite/clear facts (witnessed on the T2 owner); the composite's equations at the identity finish; fn-own-reopen and model crash/recover arms not covered; the staged configuration completion's frame fact.
proofs.progress_note: Lane sca-join (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27). PROVED: the join's preservation at the article finish and at the identity finish (over the owner the host installs), and the join's sufficiency for fn-sca-join. OPEN (the chain's fn-scr-catalogp stays a hypothesis of fn-scr-ocfg-read-span-is-reference-under-ocl-relation until these land): (1) the row equation (numbering: fn-cat-assign-numbers over the rows = fn-allocate-memberships at the watermarks, and the pending row's fields = the store's pending); (2) E: fn-sca-load-held-rows establishes fn-scj-joinp at recover / full open / checkpoint open -- PROVED by lane sca-join-3 (fn-scj-joinp-at-recover, fn-scj-joinp-at-full-open; teeth over a replaying two-article full open, tests/acl2/served-catalog-join-entry-tests.lisp); (3) every pinned connection: fn-scr-owner-catalogp needs the join at each connection's version (the catalog keeps every version at or below the count: fn-sca-finish-keeps-pinned-views) plus the pin correspondences and fn-cnx-freshp; (4) steps that touch neither view nor catalog keep fn-scj-joinp by construction (no view change when the acceptance and verdicts are unchanged: fn-ctl-refresh-visible's first arm; config keeps the article list: fn-cnode-apply-config-keeps-watermarks-and-articles) but are not yet stated over fn-ocfg-step. No counterexample found: live E over cancel-after-target, key-declines, cancel-before-target and plain histories joins (REPL, owner-cancel-refresh-tests); verdicts are historical (fn-sn-verdicts is only extended), reclaim is an offline command re-entering by E. Teeth: tests/acl2/served-catalog-join-tests.lisp (reachable cancel-after-target witness, every hypothesis and conclusion; corrupted catalog; pending-row-withdrawn removal; targets mutation). Lane sca-join-2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27): the row relation fn-scj-acc-rowsp, its install keystone, its establishment at every entry over the replay (E), and the row equation from it: items (1)'s numbering half and (2) of the open list. STILL OPEN: E for fn-scj-joinp itself (the visible list = the load's view at its count: a subsequence-with-distinct-ids-is-the-filter lemma over the view index; seqs-below from fn-cpr-loop's event-sequence check and fn-stxa-bindsp for composites); the finish-side link between the store's staged pending and the catalog's pending row (so fn-scj-acc-rowsp-of-install applies at fn-owner-finish-submission); (3) pinned connections; (4) the other owner steps over fn-ocfg-step; the composed invariant and removing fn-scr-owner-catalogp from the chain keystone. Teeth: tests/acl2/served-catalog-join-open-tests.lisp (the conclusion over five owners reached through the real transitions; the renumbering and outside-domain mutations; the fixtures' stores carry no configuration history, so the antecedent's fn-ocl-relation is not witnessed). Lane sca-join-4 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27): steps 3, 4 and 5 -- the carried invariant, its entries and arms, the chain keystone over it; REPL-admitted, not certified; NOT discharged: see planning/evidence/sca-join-2026-09-27.md, 'What remains named'. Lane join-f2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-28): the catalog premise asks fn-statep, not fn-nntp-projectionp (its article-count conjunct no store fact gives); the finishes ask fn-scj-view-indexesp, not the static fn-own-view-okp. The host's protocol is carried: fn-sjh-okp (books/served-catalog-join-host.lisp) = fn-scj-invp + the carried side facts + S (the store rows' composites, handles, no withdrawal) + LINK (the host's pending row is the store's in-flight row's catalog row, with its token and the catalog's count; none when the in-flight row loads none). Established at every open (-host-open: install, recover with the checkpoint's row facts named, full open with none), kept by the POST (-host-post: prepare, seal, catalog prepare), the io steps, the known abort and the refused reservation (the host now clears its pending row there), and the article finish (-host-finish) with no named hypothesis beyond the owner relation and the host's own words. Then (same lane): the identity prepares (signed composite and keyring snapshot), the retention/consumer/topic prepares and the completions the catalog does not see (books/served-catalog-join-host-identity, -complete). Lane join-f2-2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-29): the identity finish with its pending row, every branch (books/served-catalog-join-host-identity-finish: the (I) equations derived from the store); every other configured-owner event and the host's wrappers (-host-arms); the served read over fn-mca-read-span (-host-read; fn-scol-okp and the captured reader view's liveness stay named); executable-twin teeth (-host-exec, tests/acl2/served-catalog-join-host-tests.lisp). Then the log route, the live configuration's completion (fn-oclc-publish; the frame sca-join-4 named holds by definition for the carried configure), the opens with and without a captured reader view, the exposure open and the wire read steps (-host-entries): fn-sjh-okp at every owner-installing host entry but fn-owner-chunk (the retired Python host's). Then the read's column premise carried: fn-sjh-colsp (fn-scol-okp, the rows' handles inside the arena, the pending row's column its bytes') established at the opens and kept by the prepares, the finishes and the commit's reseat (-host-columns, -host-columns-open). And the captured reader views: fn-sjh-viewsp (every captured view live over the catalog, no newer than the working view) established at each capture and kept by every host entry (-host-views); the read and the captured open need no named premise beyond fn-sjh-okp, fn-sjh-colsp and fn-sjh-viewsp. the owner relation fn-ocl-relation at every host entry is row Q3c's (each J theorem takes it before, and the view's fn-statep after).

proofs.title: The owner transitions the host calls answer their own word: every prepare, the reservation refusal, the known abort, :begin and :declare-group return (mv WORD NEXT), and each word is the before/after comparison the host used to make
proofs.statement: books/owner-prepare-outcome.lisp (prefix fn-pout-). Subjects, each the function the host line calls (host/owner-host.lisp): fn-pout-prepare-article (fn-owner-prepare, fn-owner-prepare-buffer), fn-pout-prepare-identity (fn-owner-prepare-identity), fn-pout-prepare-topic (fn-owner-prepare-topic), fn-pout-prepare-retention (fn-owner-prepare-retention), fn-pout-prepare-consumer (fn-owner-prepare-consumer), fn-pout-refuse-reservation (fn-owner-refuse-reservation), fn-pout-known-abort (fn-owner-known-abort), fn-pout-begin (fn-owner-begin), fn-pout-declare-group (fn-owner-declare-group). Each returns NEXT, the configured owner the host installed before (the same term), and WORD: a prepare is :prepared exactly when it staged a record (fn-pout-stagedp: the Store went :reserved -> :record-staged), else :refused (the article: fn-psrv-refusal-kind, :refused or :unaffordable); the reservation refusal :refused exactly when fn-sn-refuse-reservation-enabledp holds, the known abort :aborted exactly when fn-sn-known-abort-enabledp holds, else :fault; :begin :begun and :declare-group :declared exactly when their gates hold (fn-pout-begin-admitsp, fn-pout-declare-group-admitsp; fn-pout-begin-unfolds, fn-pout-declare-group-unfolds name them as the transitions' tests). KEYSTONES fn-pout-prepare-{article,identity,topic,retention,consumer}-answers-the-store-change, fn-pout-refuse-reservation-answers-the-host-test, fn-pout-known-abort-answers-the-host-test, fn-pout-declare-group-answers-the-host-test (no hypothesis) and fn-pout-begin-answers-the-host-test (hypothesis: a non-NIL connection identifier; the host's are naturals): WORD equals the comparison the host line made (Store unchanged -> refusal, owner core unchanged -> :refused, the phase-and-change test of the refusal and the abort), so the served behaviour is unchanged and the ten host comparisons are deleted. The Store lemma fn-pout-sn-prepares-stage-or-keep: every Store prepare (fn-sn-prepare-retention, -consumer, -topic, fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity, fn-prc-spc-prepare) returns its Store or stages from :reserved. No outcome is uncertain: every entry is pure. The topic entry's consumer-projection refusal (books/owner-prepare-outcome-topic.lisp): fn-pout-staged-topic-passes-the-consumer-projection (hypotheses fn-sn-statep and fn-snt-consumerp: whenever fn-sn-prepare-topic would stage E the carried consumer projection admits E at the next sequence; the u32 ceiling is no exception, fn-csi-candidate-sequence-below-max) and fn-pout-topic-entry-is-the-store-prepare-under-the-consumer-relation (the entry's Store is fn-sn-prepare-topic's): the arm is unreachable on every Store the consumer relation holds of (fn-csi-full-relationp is preserved by the Store's normal steps, crash and recovery), and reachable under fn-lgoc-invariantp alone, which does not carry the consumer relation (so the test is what lets fn-psrv-prepare-topic-preserves-invariant hold without it).
proofs.progress_note: Lane host-decisions-2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27; packet A of planning/evidence/host-decisions-2026-09-27.md). Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-prepare-outcome-tests.lisp (prefix pot-): for every entry a REACHABLE witness of each word over owners the log route's host steps reach (owner-log-ocl-tests' *lgt-reserved*/*lgt-oc0*, prepare-served's and host-decisions' staged owners), asserting WORD, that NEXT is the owner the host installed (*pst-prepared*, *ois-staged*, *pse-topic-staged*, *pst-ret-staged*, *pse-consumer-staged*, *psa-topic-aborted*) and that WORD equals the former host comparison: article :prepared/:refused (retired group)/:unaffordable (budget 0)/:refused (already staged); identity :prepared/:refused (retired fn.test); topic, retention, consumer :prepared/:refused; refuse-reservation :refused/:fault; known abort :aborted (topic, article)/:fault; begin :begun/:refused (pending, unknown id); declare-group :declared/:refused (same name, no clock). CORRUPTED-STATE hypothesis-removal witness for the begin keystone: a connection whose identifier is NIL, where the gate admits and the comparison said :refused. proofs.title: The local control socket's launch decision is ACL2's: a worker exactly when the plane is not stopping and the live workers are below ACL2's ceiling, BUSY by name at and past it
proofs.statement: books/native-control-launch.lisp (prefix fn-ncla-). KEYSTONE fn-ncla-launch-exactly-below-the-ceiling: :launch iff not stopping and the count is a natural below fn-native-control-max-active-clients, a launch never takes the live workers past the ceiling, every answer is :stopping, :busy or :launch. fn-ncla-at-the-ceiling-is-busy: at or past the ceiling a live plane answers :busy. proofs.title: A lab host's raw clock reading becomes a clock observation in ACL2: units, the DTN epoch and whether the wall is usable are decided there
proofs.statement: books/clock-reading.lisp (prefix fn-clkr-). Subject fn-clkr-observation-of-ns, called by host/bp-ingress-host.lisp fn-bpi-host-observation (the lab BP ingress, Python bridge; fn-bpi-host-context). KEYSTONE fn-clkr-observation-of-ns-decides-the-wall, no hypothesis: every reading is a fn-clock-observationp; it has a wall exactly when the host claims one, the reading is a natural at or after the DTN epoch (2000-01-01, *fn-clkr-dtn-epoch-unix-ms*, equal to books/nntp-responses' *fn-nntp-unix-dtn-offset-ms*) and the error bound is a natural; then its wall is the reading's milliseconds past the epoch and its error the host's bound, each within the clock's range. The host's ns-to-ms arithmetic, epoch comparison and constant *fn-bpi-host-dtn-epoch-ms* are deleted. Scope: the native owner's own reading (host/native/io.lisp fnn-owner-wall-milliseconds) still converts gettimeofday and decides has-wall by the sign in host code; recorded as the next item of this kind.

proofs.title: The outbound feed sends the stored article's bytes, read through the arena, and a command word reaches the host only with octets: an unsendable offer is refused by name, never an owner stop
proofs.statement: books/owner-feed-article.lisp. Subjects: fn-ofa-feed-article (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-feed-octets passes it to fn-own-feed-port-observe-peer as the article of a 335 or 238; called by fn-owner-feed-reply-chunk, which host/native/feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-reply-step calls through fnn-owner-feed-arena-step) and fn-ofa-publication (the publication fn-owner-feed-octets and fn-owner-feed-tick return; feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-reply-step and fnn-feed-tick). KEYSTONES: fn-ofa-feed-article-is-the-feed-article-over-alpha (under fn-apr-store-at-restp of the owner's Store, the bytes are the payload of the octet-list model's feed article over ALPHA of the acceptance articles, books/store-intern.lisp fn-articles-wire-of: what fn-own-feed-article read before the records flip); fn-ofa-publication-command-words-have-octets (a publication whose word is :send or :offer has a non-empty command; otherwise its word is :unsendable, its sealed record plan is the port's, and it differs from the input only when the input was a command word without octets). fn-ofa-feed-article-is-an-octet-list: over an arena (fn-arena-p) the bytes are an octet list, never the handle. fn-ofa-publication-is-well-formed: the host's recognizer holds of the output. The host flushes an :unsendable publication's records, writes its ACL2 line (the renderer's reason, or no-article) and drops the link, which fn-feed-lost requeues (PRF-047's composition). The defect this closes: after the records flip (c5808cd72) the feed handed the row's handle to the port, the renderer refused it, and the host stopped the owner on the empty command (tests.test_native_peering 12 of 14 red on dev 2026-09-27). Local policy; RFC 3977 section 6.3.2 (IHAVE: after 335 the article is sent) and RFC 4644 section 2.5 (TAKETHIS carries the article).

proofs.title: Payloads off the heap: the arena's extent handles, the open's verified extent seals and the served read's trailer check
proofs.statement: books/payload-arena-extent.lisp, books/payload-arena-extent-logic.lisp, books/payload-extent.lisp, books/payload-arena.lisp: payloads off the heap (arena-offheap stage 2). The generic fn-arena gains the export fn-arena-seal-extent (logic: append of fn-durable-octets FILE POFF PLEN, A-DURABLE-EXTENT); KEYSTONE fn-arena-seal-extent-payload: the new handle is the old count and denotes the extent's durable octets, every older handle keeps its payload, the count grows by one. The attachment fn-arena-extent (books/payload-arena-extent.lisp) nests the paged arena (PRF-281) as a child plus an EXT array; an extent handle holds no octets; its relation fn-arena$xcorr is fn-arx-view of the child's logical value, and every {correspondence}/{guard-thm}/{preserved} obligation is proved (fn-arena-extent-get{correspondence} reads an extent handle through the realizer fn-durable-realize-octet, equal to the durable octet by A-DURABLE-EXTENT; fn-arena-extent-seal-extent{correspondence}). At the open (books/payload-extent.lisp): fn-arx-positions answers each log entry's start, frame length and trailer; fn-arx-extent-of finds the payload's place by the codec's suffix length and VERIFIES it octet for octet; fn-arx-extent-of-denotes-payload: under the faithful read the extent's durable octets are the decoded payload; KEYSTONE fn-arx-intern-step-refines: the host's chunk step with extents (host/native/io.lisp fnn-bridge-recover calls fn-arx-intern-step on each chunk fnn-recover-record-chunks answers with its places) equals fn-srs-intern-step when fn-arx-faithful-p (each placed record's octets are its entry's durable octets: A-HOST's read and A-DURABLE-EXTENT; a record with no place needs nothing, fn-arx-intern-event-without-place); KEYSTONE fn-arx-steps-are-one-step-of-the-concatenation: folding that step over ANY chunking of the history (fn-arx-steps, the host's loop) answers what one resident step over the whole history answers (fn-srs-steps-are-one-step-of-the-concatenation), so every theorem about the open's rows and arena holds. Served reads of an extent handle: the host realizer (host/native/extent.lisp) preads the entry's protected prefix and asks fn-arx-entry-ok (SHA-256 equals the recorded trailer); fn-arx-entry-ok-of-durable: a faithful read passes; a mismatch is refused by name (arena-extent-digest), a store fault. Host subject: host/native/io.lisp fnn-bridge-recover (fn-arx-intern-step), fnn-log-scan-segments (fn-arx-positions via fnn-extent-positions), host/native/extent.lisp fnn-extent-entry (fn-arx-entry-ok, fn-arx-read-cache-entries).

The open of a format-9 store seals extents on its full replay; the state-checkpoint route, the commit and format 8 stay resident (the record's section on what is not done). Lane arena-offheap-3 (2026-09-27): rebased onto dev's chunk stream (rm2-format9 / log-recovery: fnn-bridge-recover folds a next-chunk source); the scan's places ride in the chunks (fnn-recover-record-chunks answers each chunk's places) and the composed keystone is fn-arx-steps-are-one-step-of-the-concatenation.

proofs.title: The frame digest over an octet buffer (P3's obstruction): a buffer digest attached together with fn-frame-digest, and the served read's entry check in the realizer's buffer
proofs.statement: books/frame-digest-buffer.lisp: fn-frame-digest-buffer PREFIX BUF is constrained to be fn-frame-digest of PREFIX followed by the buffer's octets (KEYSTONE fn-frame-digest-buffer-is-the-frame-digest), and one defattach attaches it together with fn-frame-digest (fn-blake3-stobj, as books/crypto-attach.lisp) to the buffer BLAKE3 (fn-blake3-of-prefixed-buffer-any; SHA-256 up to store format 9); the attachment's obligation is books/blake3-stobj.lisp's keystone fn-blake3-of-prefixed-buffer-is-blake3; A-CRYPTO still says only 32 octets. books/payload-extent-read.lisp: the realizer's own buffer fn-octets-rd (congruent to fn-octets) and fn-arx-entry-ok-buffer TRAILER BUF; KEYSTONE fn-arx-entry-ok-buffer-is-the-frame-check: it is (equal (fn-frame-digest BUF) TRAILER), the log's own frame check (fn-lg-frame through fn-frame-seal); fn-arx-entry-ok-buffer-of-durable: a faithful read of an intact entry passes. Host subject: host/native/extent.lisp fnn-extent-entry-ok (called by fnn-extent-entry, the realizer's read) calls fn-arx-entry-ok-buffer over fn-octets-rd. NOT done: the record decode reading the buffer by index (the rest of recover-memory-2's P3); the obstruction it named is removed.

proofs.title: The commit moves a durable payload off the heap: staged buffer seals, the reseat as the log extent after the barrier, and the release
proofs.statement: books/payload-arena-extent.lisp: the extent arena's per-handle STAGE (an array of page stobjs): fn-arena$x-seal-buffer stages the buffer's copy in the handle's own page (:staged); fn-arena$x-reseat-extent re-points a handle at an extent; fn-arena$x-release empties an EXTENT handle's page; every {correspondence}/{guard-thm}/{preserved} obligation proved, the exec functions guard-verified. books/payload-arena.lisp: the generic exports fn-arena-reseat-extent (logic: the handle becomes the extent's durable octets) and fn-arena-release (the identity); KEYSTONE fn-arena-reseat-extent-payload (the handle is the extent's durable octets, every other handle keeps its payload, the count is unchanged) and KEYSTONE fn-arena-reseat-extent-keeps-a-faithful-arena (when the extent's durable octets are the handle's payload the arena is unchanged). books/payload-commit-extent.lisp: fn-arx-commit-extent finds the handle's payload in the record the log wrote (the entry's frame must be the record's; the payload compared octet for octet against the arena's copy, by index, in a window before the record's end); KEYSTONE fn-arx-commit-reseat-keeps-the-arena and fn-arx-commit-reseats-keep-the-arena: under the faithful write (the file holds, at each entry's record position, the record the log wrote there: A-HOST, A-DURABLE-EXTENT) the reseat leaves every handle's payload unchanged -- the extent reads the same bytes the commit wrote. Host subject: host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-reseat-fenced (called by fnn-log-batch-finish, the COMPLETE after the batch's barrier) calls fn-arx-commit-reseats and fn-arena-release; fnn-log-members-in-flight places the batch's members with fn-arx-positions from the append's frontier.
