proofs.title: Every durability report follows the barrier that persisted it: a key statement's commit is fenced before its crash cut and its executor, and the owner's batch quantum tells, logs and cuts only fenced records, for every record kind
proofs.statement: books/owner-ack-after-barrier.lisp. The decision fn-oab-fence-before-change (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-statement-fence, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-statement-committed after every durable kind-4 composite fnn-owner-attempt-transit commits): an event whose authored source carries a key statement is fenced -- fnn-owner-statement-barrier commits the log's open batch, the statement and every member drained before it (fnn-log-commit-open-batch, awaiting a batch in flight first) -- before the statement-committed cut and the executor run. fn-oab-plan-only-after-the-fence (fn-ks-plan non-nil implies the fence), fn-oab-execute-only-after-the-fence, fn-oab-recovered-statement-was-fenced (fn-ks-pending, the open's recovery, acts only on such a record). KEYSTONE fn-oab-quantum-reports-after-its-barrier: over fn-oab-quantum, the host's schedule of one batch quantum (START's drain with the statement fence, cut and key-change take; SYNC's barrier when the word is :fenced; COMPLETE's deferred lines -- each member's outcome line and the executor's line naming the statement and its key change -- and the replies fn-ocs-member-releases names over fn-ocs-commit-step's action), fn-oab-reports-follow-fences-p holds: every cut, line and rendered reply names only records a barrier has fenced since their take. fn-oab-pipeline-reports-after-its-barriers: the same for a batch in flight and the next batch prepared behind its barrier (START-NEXT), a statement among them. fn-oab-every-kind-reports-after-its-barrier: for each of the fourteen record kinds in *fn-oab-record-kinds* (served and relayed articles, statements and their key changes in the quantum; the control post, BP applications, identity events, the key change at open, keys redecide, consumer, topic and retention events as a batch of one; configuration records and XREDEEM's publication through their own immutable publication), its route's trace reports only after its barrier; a kind with no route is unaccounted. The host's order is the model's by tests/campaign/native_cuts.py verify_statement_cut_map (run by tools/native_program_check.py and tests/test_native_cut_map.py): fence, barrier, cut, executor in fnn-owner-statement-committed; the executor's line deferred inside a quantum (fnn-owner-line-after-barrier); every kind-4 commit of fnn-owner-attempt-transit through fnn-owner-statement-committed; *fnn-log-batch* bound only by fnn-owner-commit-start-locked and fnn-log-write-history; COMPLETE's lines after the acknowledgement. The served cut table now names record-completing (absent inside a quantum, present in a batch of one).
proofs.progress_note: Lane ack-before-barrier (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27), from log-recovery-2's diagnosis (planning/evidence/log-recovery-2026-09-27.md section 8): a served statement's cut and executor ran inside the drain, before the batch's barrier, so FN_NATIVE_KEY_STATEMENT_FAULT=statement-committed:kill killed with the statement in memory only and the key-statement line reported an unfenced key change. Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-ack-after-barrier-tests.lisp (reachable: an ordinary article, the acting succession and the declining carried statement in one batch, trace non-vacuous; the pipeline; every kind; hypothesis removal: an ordinary composite is not fenced, an unrouted kind fails; mutations M1 the pre-fix unfenced cut, M2 an undeferred executor line, M3 replies without the barrier, each failing the property).

proofs.title: A batch barrier is a request with a deadline and the disk's mode is ACL2's over recorded time: reads and status never wait on a pending barrier, a deadline never tells a member anything, and a POST arriving while the disk is slow is refused try-later with the reason exactly when health says so; past the stall deadline H every poster of the batch in flight is told uncertain, never accepted or refused, within H plus one committer wake (F4-W)
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-otm-next, fn-otm-observe, fn-otm-commit-event, fn-otm-committer-wake (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-gate-pick, fnn-owner-gate-leave, fnn-owner-commit-event, fnn-owner-commit-wake), fn-otm-disk-event (fnn-owner-disk-event: the committer's :issue at the syncer's start, :clock at each expiry of its timed wait, :return at the completion it observes; :clock on demand before a POST admission and a health/status render), fn-otm-wait-ms (fnn-owner-disk-wait-ms), fn-otm-admit-post (fnn-owner-disk-admit, in the served read quantum that queued a POST), fn-otm-disk-lines / fn-otm-health-lines (host/native-live-status-host.lisp). KEYSTONE fn-otm-barrier-reader-bound (books/owner-time-model.lisp): for S with the pipeline's phase :staged (the barrier pending) and every sequence WS of pick observations (W EVENT) with a reader waiting at every pick and the commit class waiting only when the committer's wake is :start-next (fn-otm-barrier-walk-okp), the quanta picked before the first :reader pick (fn-otm-barrier-walk) contain no control, poster or transit quantum, at most one :commit whose event is :next-started, and at most one more :inspect than :commit; EVENT is unconstrained and the device's latency is not a quantity of the walk. KEYSTONE fn-otm-disk-event-keeps-the-pipeline: every disk event leaves the pipeline's value unchanged (so fn-ocs-members-told-only-after-the-barrier and fn-ocp-complete-only-after-the-barrier hold of every run with deadlines: a deadline never tells a member anything). fn-otm-next-is-ocp-next, fn-otm-commit-event-is-ocp-commit-event, fn-otm-observe-keeps-the-disk: the pipeline's keystones (PRF-248, PRF-267, PRF-272, PRF-288) hold of the host's calls. fn-otm-recorded-time-is-monotone (the recorded time is the max of the readings; a lower reading increments the regression count and moves nothing); fn-otm-shed-only-past-the-deadline and fn-otm-past-the-deadline-sheds (a POST is shed exactly while a barrier is pending D or more at the recorded time); fn-otm-shed-iff-slow (shed iff the health/status disk line says disk slow); fn-otm-return-recovers, fn-otm-clock-event-never-issues (the completion is the recovery; no clock event re-enters slow without a new barrier); fn-otm-return-records-the-latency; fn-otm-wait-reaches-the-deadline (a clock event WAIT-MS after the recorded time finds the barrier past its deadline and enters :slow once); fn-otm-issue-only-when-none-pending, fn-otm-issue-is-pending-and-admits. Hypotheses of the wall-clock reading (stated, not proved): the store commits through the record log (format 9); the quanta admitted during a barrier contain no I/O wait (true of :inspect, :reader and START-NEXT; the inline barrier of :control/:poster/:transit quanta is not admitted in flight, PKT-825 (c)); the served read's octets are in memory; the committer thread is scheduled (its clock events can be late, never early). Slice 2 (lane time-model-2): the limits (D H C) are the live configuration's barrier-deadline-ms, barrier-stall-ms and clock-event-ms rows (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-barrier-limits; fn-otm-limits: defaults 5,000 / 30,000 / 1,000 ms, H read as at least D), carried by the barrier's :issue. fn-otm-disk-mode is :stalled past H; fn-otm-admit-is-the-mode (shed exactly in :slow and :stalled). KEYSTONE fn-otm-stall-tells-no-member-its-outcome: fn-otm-stall-releases (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-stall-release, called by the committer once per barrier when fnn-owner-disk-stalled-p) releases every member :own-uncertain, :uncertain-reply or :close, never :rendered, one per member; with fn-otm-disk-event-keeps-the-pipeline a member is told its own outcome only in a COMPLETE after a fenced barrier, and a member told at the stall is dropped from the COMPLETE's releases (fnn-owner-unreleased). KEYSTONE fn-otm-f4w-stall-within-h: from a pending barrier not past H (since at most the recorded time), committer clock events each at most its wait (fn-otm-wait-ms) plus LATE after the recorded time (fn-otm-clock-run-okp) enter :stalled at a reading at most since + H + LATE, and until one does every reading is before since + H; fn-otm-wait-stays-within-the-stall (the wait never reaches past H). fn-otm-return-after-a-stall-is-named (the completion after a stall answers :recovered-from-stall). Hypotheses stated, not proved: the committer is not blocked on the device (the syncer is); LATE bounds the scheduler's lateness of one timed wait; the committer appends a clock event at every wake while a barrier is pending (host). Not claimed: that the since-at-most-now hypothesis is needed (no counterexample found; the weakened statement is not yet proved).

Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-time-model-tests.lisp (prefix otmt-): a reached run (START, issue at 1,000 ms, clock events, a 30 s stall, the completion), each keystone's complete antecedent and conclusion, and one removal witness per hypothesis of fn-otm-barrier-reader-bound (the barrier not pending: a mutating control quantum runs; a reader not waiting: three :inspect quanta with no :commit; the commit waiting past its wake: a second START-NEXT) and of fn-otm-wait-reaches-the-deadline. proofs.title: QUIT ends the served fold: after the 205 no octet is framed or answered, whatever the read boundaries (RFC 3977 section 5.4)
proofs.statement: fn-served-step-stops-at-quit: for any connection CONN and octets LEFT and RIGHT, when the connection fn-served-step leaves after LEFT is quit (fn-served-quitp: its reader session is no longer open, which QUIT's 205 leaves), fn-served-step over LEFT ++ RIGHT has exactly the effects and the connection of fn-served-step over LEFT (the one hypothesis). fn-served-step-of-quit-connection-is-a-no-op: a read of a quit connection emits nothing and leaves it unchanged; fn-served-feed-of-quit-connection: the byte fold stops there. The fold stops on fn-served-haltedp (the handshake owed after 382, or quit) in fn-served-feed and in every twin the host executes (fn-served-feed-counted, fn-scar-feed-counted, fn-scar-feed-span, fn-scar-scan-span, fn-scr-feed-span, fn-scr-scan-span), each proved equal to the reference as before. Subject: fn-served-step, which books/owner.lisp fn-own-read calls once per socket read; the native owner calls fn-served-step-counted-fast (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span), equal to fn-served-step of its consumed prefix (fn-served-step-counted-fast-is-reference, fn-served-step-counted-result-is-step-of-consumed-prefix). With fn-served-run-is-the-concatenated-step every cut of LEFT ++ RIGHT into reads serves the same, which is the host's stop after the read that carried the close (fuzz-nntp F1).
proofs.progress_note: Covered scope: the host's stop after the read carrying the close (host/native/mux.lisp) is measured by the fuzz reproducers and the differential harness, not proved. host/native/mux.lisp's close-after-handshake case (STARTTLS and a close in one read) is deleted (lane served-leftovers): the host reads books/served-plan.lisp fn-splan-step-handshake-owed, the 382's handshake only when the step neither closes (after QUIT no 382 is emitted) nor meets the exposure's failed-login close, so the loop never holds both.

proofs.title: A transit article is bounded by the operator's profile before its verdict: the transit connection opens at the profile bound, the served run retains at most it, and the cut article is refused by name (437/439) and closed
proofs.statement: fn-tb-open-peer-body-limit-is-the-profile-bound: for an admitted profile and O2 the owner fn-osb-install leaves (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-profile, on every run path), a transit connection fn-own-open-peer opens (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open-peer, at accept) has a wire body limit no larger than the profile's max-article-octets A, whatever the peer record's inbound-max-octets (peer add writes the codec ceiling, 4 GiB, there); fn-own-peer-body-limit-is-within-the-profile-bound: the limit fn-own-open-peer uses is positive and at most fn-own-body-limit. fn-tb-served-run-retains-at-most-the-body-limit: for any connection whose wire is a wire state (fn-wire-statep, which every open establishes) and any reads, the article octets the wire retains after fn-served-run are at most the body limit it opened with and the partial line at most the line ceiling (the opening line limit or the body limit plus one); fn-tb-served-step-keeps-the-body-limit / fn-tb-served-run-keeps-the-body-limit: no read changes the limit. fn-peer-transfer-unreceived-effects (called by fn-peer-step and its carried twin fn-pgc-transfer-step): an article the wire cut at the limit ((:reject :body-overlimit)) is refused 437 with the size's reason text (IHAVE, RFC 3977 section 6.3.2) or 439 echoing the Message-ID (TAKETHIS, RFC 4644 section 2.5.2), then closed; fn-peer-transfer-unreceived-effects-well-formed. Fuzz-nntp F2.
proofs.progress_note: Open (D27): the bound is on octets, not on the representation; the wire retains an article in flight as octet lists, so its heap cost is a constant multiple of A (measured in the record), as for POST. The concrete in-flight representation is input-loop-2's item 2.

proofs.title: Every group membership is charged to the history budget: the budget is the sum of the stored charges, a crosspost the budget cannot pay for is refused by name, and the heap figure's membership term is bounded by H
proofs.statement: ember's decision 2026-09-27 17:30Z (D27: no new crosspost cap). books/store-budget.lisp *fn-sbud-membership-octets* = 320 (the heap model's *fn-heap-membership-octets*: measured 137 octets of live heap a membership plus 45 for the group's name, 182, with the per-group index's doubling slack): fn-sbud-row-octets charges a held row its payload extent plus 320 per group (fn-sbud-row-memberships: a held row's groups, or the held article's inside an accepted-statement composite), so KEYSTONE fn-sbud-record-octets-pays-the-memberships: 320 x (fn-sbud-record-memberships records) <= (fn-sbud-record-octets records). books/store-budget-stored.lisp KEYSTONE fn-sbud-record-octets-is-the-stored-octets (restated): under fn-sbud-rows-extents-okp the budget is the sum of fn-sbud-row-stored-octets (extent + 320 per membership). books/store-budget-article.lisp: fn-sbud-article-figure p k = the record ceiling + 320 k, so every gate (article verdict, capacity vector, carried verdict) charges the memberships and the stored charge is within the figure (fn-cvec-held-row-within-its-figure). books/store-capacity-vector.lisp fn-cvec-article-refusal-word (host: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer, over fn-pout-prepare-article's word): KEYSTONE fn-cvec-article-refusal-word-names-the-memberships: the word is :memberships exactly when the prepare answered :unaffordable, k >= 1, the article budget was 0, and without the membership charge the count gate, the history gate and the vector would have admitted it; 441 posting failed; ... (memberships) (books/nntp-post.lisp), 436 to a feeding peer (books/peer-inbound.lisp). books/heap-store-figure.lisp: the state is arena(USED) + 48 N + 2 x 12,288 N + 2 x 320 M with M the memberships; the figure takes M = fn-heap-membership-bound = floor(H / 320) (KEYSTONE fn-heap-membership-bound-holds-the-charged-memberships; fn-heap-membership-term-is-at-most-twice-h), and fn-heap-store-figure-holds-every-store gains the hypothesis 320 M <= H. Figures (core 200 MB, 64 MiB nursery; full-store heap before -> after): small 1,052 -> 891 MB, development 7,326 -> 2,254, scale 172,841 -> 10,539, default 10,856,110,718 -> 120,789,633 (its T = 2^32 - 1 records at 12 KiB each), gate (scale, T 2^20, A 4096) 41,977,971 -> 37,107. Lane bp-retention-leftovers (membership-budget's two deferrals): the accepted-statement composite's gate charges its figure, fn-cvec-statement-figure k = the kind's publication ceiling 196,608 + 320 k (k the groups its article is filed in): fn-cvec-statement-verdict-at (count gate, history gate and vector at the figure; host: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-identity-publication-verdict through the carried twin fn-pvc-statement-verdict-carried, KEYSTONE fn-pvc-statement-verdict-carried-is-cvec-statement-verdict-at, asked by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-identity-commit over the WIRE event, whose kind the row reading fn-store-event-kind answered NIL, so the preflight charged a composite nothing), and the history arm fn-cvec-record-admittedp admits an :accepted-statement row at that verdict with its stored charge within the figure. KEYSTONE fn-cvec-statement-admission-keeps-the-vector; KEYSTONE fn-cvec-statement-row-within-its-figure: for a retained composite row, its stored charge is within its figure exactly when its encoding is within the ceiling, whatever its group count; fn-cvec-record-keeps-the-vector restated over the new arm. The preflight's count fn-oii-publication-group-count is the interned row's (fn-oii-publication-group-count-is-the-rows). proofs.title: The store's history as an FNADTSN2 image on the page store's pages: the decoder inverts it, the page store's page digest is the image's page-digest leaf, an append changes only O(K + columns) pages while no region doubles, and the open's header check and the row read the host calls (need-verdicts) answer the history over verified pages
proofs.statement: books/history-pages.lisp. The image of a history H (fn-hp-image H SALT) is adt-ser (the FNADTSN2 bytes, books/proto/adt-bytes.lisp) over the schema ((:u64) (:u64) (:octets)): per event MKEY (1 + fn-hist-hash of fn-hist-key-msgid, 0 when none), the length of its fn-scc-encode tree octets, and those octets zero-padded to a multiple of 8. KEYSTONES: fn-hp-decode-image (fn-hp-events-okp H, (len H) and (len (fn-hp-image H SALT)) below 2^64 => (fn-hp-decode (fn-hp-image H SALT) SALT) = (:ok H)); fn-hp-page-digest-is-leaf ((natp K), page K's words LE = page K of the image => (pgs-x-page-digest K ...) = the be-nat of leaf K of adt-page-digests, BLAKE3 of page K's octets: the page store's table-entry digest IS the image's per-page leaf, no second digest table); fn-hp-append-changes-only-dirty ((natp K), K not in (fn-hp-append-dirty H NEW SALT) => page K of (fn-hp-image (append H NEW) SALT) = page K of (fn-hp-image H SALT)); fn-hp-append-dirty-bound ((fn-hp-caps-same ...) => 16384 * |dirty| <= 11 * 16384 + 32 |NEW| + NEW's padded tree octets). Generic lemmas over any in-place region growth: fn-hp-body-page-same, fn-hp-ser-page-same, fn-hp-regs-of-append, fn-hp-body-dirty-in-pages, fn-hp-dirty-pages-bound. Named limit L-HP-DOUBLING: the canonical image places regions contiguously; a region that doubles is the writer's verdict (:grow R). Milestone 2 (books/history-pages-words, -exec, -read): the image as the page store's little-endian words (fn-hp-iw = fn-hp-pack8 of the image; fn-hp-words-le-octets-of-pack8, fn-hp-page-words-of-pack8); its header, cells and pool entries read back (fn-hp-w-header-of-image, fn-hp-w-row-of-image); the host-called reads return need-verdicts and never fill a page. KEYSTONES: fn-hp-x-header-is-image ((fn-hp-okp H SALT), NPAGES = (fn-hp-npages H SALT), (fn-hp-vhold 0 (pgs-v-length pgs-mem) pgs-mem (fn-hp-iw H SALT)): every verified page holds the image's words, and the header's verdict :ok => (fn-hp-x-header NPAGES pgs-mem) answers (:ok (len H) lens starts); another schema digest is refused :schema); fn-hp-x-at-is-nth ((fn-hp-okp H SALT), (natp SEQ), SEQ < (len H), the same fn-hp-vhold, verdict :ok => (fn-hp-x-at SEQ ...) answers (:ok (nth SEQ H))). The open reads page 0 only; the first read of a row pays at most its four cells' pages and its pool entry's pages. Milestone 3a (lane arena-store-3, books/history-pages-write, -write-exec, -write-keys): the writer the host calls, fn-hp-x-append EV SALT N LENS STARTS pgs-mem -> (mv VERDICT N2 LENS2 pgs-mem): six blocks (header words 6-17, one cell per column, the padded tree's words in the pool) written with fn-hp-x-put (each word's page marked dirty) only after every touched page is verified (fn-hp-x-blocks-ready: else the need-verdict, nothing written) and only while no region changes its cap (else (:grow R), nothing written). Model theorem fn-hp-iw-of-append1: (fn-hp-iw (append H (list EV)) SALT) = (fn-hp-wreps (fn-hp-iw H SALT) (fn-hp-blocks H EV SALT)) when no region's cap changes and the new header fields are u64. KEYSTONE fn-hp-x-append-refines: (fn-hp-okp H SALT), N = (len H), LENS = (fn-hp-lens H SALT), STARTS = (fn-hp-starts H SALT), (fn-hp-vhold 0 (pgs-v-length pgs-mem) pgs-mem (fn-hp-iw H SALT)) and the verdict :ok => (fn-hp-okp (append H (list EV)) SALT), N2 = (len (append H (list EV))), LENS2 = (fn-hp-lens (append H (list EV)) SALT), the starts do not move, (fn-hp-vhold 0 ... mem2 (fn-hp-iw (append H (list EV)) SALT)), and every page P it marks dirty is in (fn-hp-append-dirty H (list EV) SALT) and verified in mem2. Milestone 3b (arena-store-3): the image format is FNADTSN2 (books/proto/adt-bytes.lisp: magic FNADTSN2, version 2, the image's page count NPAGES after the region table; adt-decode and the history's open check fn-hp-w-header accept any placement adt-placement-ok (every region after page 0, inside NPAGES, apart from every other) and refuse any other :placement; FNADTSN1 is refused :magic; adt-decode-ser keeps the canonical round trip, adt-placement-ok-of-starts-l the canonical placement); every keystone above re-proved over the FNADTSN2 image; the decoder's acceptance of a moved region is witnessed in tests/acl2/proto-adt-2-tests.lisp. The placed image (books/history-pages-placed): fn-hp-piw H SALT STARTS NP, NP pages of zeros with the header page (naming STARTS and NP) and each region's padded words at its start; fn-hp-piw-canonical: at the canonical starts and page count it IS fn-hp-iw. KEYSTONES over ANY placement (adt-placement-ok STARTS (fn-hp-lens H SALT) NP): fn-hp-x-header-is-placed ((fn-hp-okp H SALT), (fn-hp-starts-okp STARTS), the placement, (fn-hp-vhold 0 (pgs-v-length pgs-mem) pgs-mem (fn-hp-piw H SALT STARTS NP)), verdict :ok => (fn-hp-x-header NP pgs-mem) answers (:ok (len H) (fn-hp-lens H SALT) STARTS)); fn-hp-x-at-is-nth-placed (the same over the placed image, (natp SEQ), SEQ < (len H) => (fn-hp-x-at SEQ ...) answers (:ok (nth SEQ H))); fn-hp-x-append-refines-placed (books/history-pages-append-grown; the writer takes NP and grows a region's cap in place when (adt-placement-ok STARTS LENS2 NP), else answers (:grow R C) and writes nothing: N = (len H), LENS = (fn-hp-lens H SALT), (fn-hp-starts-okp STARTS), the placement, the vhold over the placed image, verdict :ok => the appended history is an image, N2/LENS2 its header, the placement stays valid, every verified page holds the appended history's placed image, and every newly dirty page is in fn-hp-append-pdirty and verified). Model fn-hp-piw-of-append1 from generic facts: block replacements nest (fn-hp-wreps-nest) and commute (fn-hp-wreps-commute), books/history-pages-nest. GROWTH (lane arena-store-4): fn-hp-piw-caps-extend (the placed image viewed with larger caps that still fit the placement is the same image) and fn-hp-piw-of-append1-grown (the append model without cap equality: the new lengths fit the placement, the deltas word-aligned); fn-hp-piw-relocated (books/history-pages-grow: moving region R to page TT >= NP of an image grown to NPN pages is three block writes -- header words 6-18, R's old pages zeroed, R's words at TT); KEYSTONE fn-hp-x-relocate-refines (books/history-pages-relocate: the host's (fn-hp-x-relocate R C N LENS STARTS NP pgs-mem) answering :ok leaves every verified page holding (fn-hp-piw H SALT (update-nth R NP STARTS) (+ NP C)), the placement valid there, and every newly dirty page page 0, one of R's old pages or a new page, each verified; any other answer changes nothing); fn-hp-grow-then-append (books/history-pages-grow-then-append: after (:grow R C) and a relocation answering :ok, the next :grow names a later region, so an event relocates at most five times; -only-r: none when only R outgrew). Old logical pages become zero pages; their physical pages leave every new root at the next commit and are reclaimed (PRF-344); logical page 0 and the reserved physical page never move. RECORDS ON PAGES (m3c P1, ACL2 side; books/history-pages-step, -import, -view): KEYSTONE fn-hp-x-append-step-refines (the one call per committed event, fn-hp-x-append-step: the writer, relocating on (:grow R C) at most five times; never answers :grow; :ok => the vhold of the appended history's placed image at STARTS2 NP2 and its header answer; otherwise the history unchanged at the (possibly relocated) STARTS2 NP2); fn-hp-x-init-refines (the empty history's image on an empty page store); fn-hp-x-append-all-refines (the import fold: the first K2 events appended, all of them on :ok); fn-hp-records-at-is-nth (record I of the image's history followed by an in-memory suffix: an :ok answer is (nth I (append H SUFFIX)); below the end the answer is :ok or a need-verdict). The link from fn-sf-records to image + suffix is not proved yet.
proofs.pending_subject: No host function calls the image yet: the owner's open and snapshot through the page store (fnps-open / fnps-commit over the fn-hist image; fn-hp-x-header, fn-hp-x-at and fn-hp-x-append from the host) are lane arena-store-3's m4.
proofs.progress_note: Milestone 1: the image, its round trip, the one digest theorem and the region plan. Milestone 2: the words, the open's header check and the row read with need-verdicts over verified pages. Milestone 3a (arena-store-3): the writer, refining the append into the words, marking only the proved dirty list. Milestone 3b: the FNADTSN2 format (free placement, NPAGES); the header check, the row read and the writer proved over any placement. Open: the growth path (a region that outgrows its pages moves to new pages; the (:grow R) verdict), the store's E/R records on pages with fn-hist a view, host wiring, measurement at the store open.

proofs.title: The owner's snapshot as a copy-on-write page store with a two-level page table: commit-then-open, crash anywhere, fork isolation, complete fresh allocation, and reclamation that never frees a page a live root keeps
proofs.statement: books/pagestore.lisp (model), books/pagestore-keystones.lisp, books/pagestore-reclaim.lisp, books/pagestore-exec.lisp, books/pagestore-gc.lisp, books/pagestore-words.lisp, books/pagestore-words-blake3.lisp. Model: a commit record names a directory run whose entries name table pages of 341 entries, whose entries name data pages (PHYS TXID BLAKE3-256); growth appends logical pages; allocation from (FREE HWM). KEYSTONES over R-opens, dirty pages in order (pgs-lpages-ok) and the allocator invariant (pgs-alloc-inv): pgs-open-after-commit (the commit opens on the next txid and the state with the dirty pages replaced or appended); pgs-open-after-crash (any subset of the commit's data, table and directory writes with the record old, torn or new opens on the committed or the previous state, the previous one unless the record landed; takes pgs-writes-faithful, A-CRYPTO instantiated); pgs-crash-isolates-other-roots; pgs-fork-denotes; pgs-alloc-fresh (allocation always answers, distinct, fresh) and pgs-plan-commit-complete; pgs-tables-after-plan (rewriting only the touched table pages rebuilds the new table pages). Reclamation: pgs-keeps-after-commit, pgs-alloc-inv-after-commit, pgs-cycle-inv-start/-after-commit, pgs-invariants-after-fork, KEYSTONE pgs-reclaim-never-frees-live (the sweep of a mark-and-sweep cycle that commits may interleave with adds only addresses no valid record of any root keeps), pgs-sweep-split (bounded quanta). Executable: pgs-x-plan-tab-refines/-dir-refines (the O(dirty) plan over the pgs-t words is pgs-plan-ptab on the decoded table), KEYSTONE pgs-x-commit-refines (pgs-x-commit, what the host calls, is pgs-plan-commit's sequence), pgs-x-dir-verdict-is-model, pgs-x-table-verdict-is-model, pgs-decode-encode-table; pgs-g-sweep-all-is, pgs-g-mark-record-covers-encoded, pgs-g-reclaim-sound (the executable cycle keeps pgs-alloc-inv); pgs-x-words-digest-is-blake3 (the word digest the host calls, pgs-x-words-digest over the page store's octet buffer fn-octets-pg, is the big-endian natural of fn-blake3 of the words' little-endian octets, with hypotheses (natp BASE) (natp NB) only; fn-blake3 is fn-digest's attachment's value, fn-blake3-stobj-is-blake3; SHA-256 until 2026-09-28). Whole-disk refinement (books/pagestore-refine.lisp, lane arena-store-5): the abstraction pgs-x-abs-disk of the files (the model pages and each root's slot page) with the handle's slot words pgs-m[0,1024) bound first as the open root. KEYSTONE pgs-x-commit-refines-plan: over a handle holding the table and directory of the record the model's open of that abstraction lands on (the other slot, the next txid, a free list of naturals, the table and directory invariants), the plan pgs-x-commit answers (its data, table-page and directory writes as the words the host writes, decoded; its slot; its record; the allocator after) IS pgs-plan-commit's, when the digests the executable observed are the digest seam's of the same objects (A-PGS-OBSERVE, stated as hypotheses: the dirty pages', the rewritten table pages', the record's check, its directory digest; the teeth attach the seam to BLAKE3 of those words and they hold). pgs-x-commit-refines-crash and pgs-x-commit-refines-commit: the files after the host's writes (any KEEP subset; the record in the handle's slot words) abstract to pgs-crash of that plan and, all kept, to pgs-commit. KEYSTONE pgs-x-fork-refines: the root page pgs-x-fork leaves (the landing slot's record in slot 0, every other word zero), bound as the new root, is pgs-fork's disk when the model's open lands on the slot the host passes. Not yet: the open square (the host's open is a host loop of ACL2 steps and fills, and its lazy open is not the model's, L-PGS-LAZY-SHAPE), so the handle's agreement with the model's open is a hypothesis of both squares; the model pages are not yet derived from the page file through A-PGS-HOST-IO. Host subject: host/native/proto-pagestore.lisp fnps-commit (pgs-x-commit), fnps-cmd-branch (pgs-x-fork), fnps-open (pgs-x-open-dir, pgs-x-open-table-page, pgs-x-open-page), fnps-reclaim (pgs-g-start, pgs-g-sweep-all, pgs-g-install), not yet the owner's path.
proofs.pending_subject: host wiring behind its own driver (host/native/proto-pagestore.lisp) until fn-hist lives in pages (lane arena-store milestone 5); the owner does not call it.
proofs.progress_note: Page 0 (the owner's root slots) is the model's reserved page: pgs-disk-keeps keeps it, pgs-g-start marks it (pgs-g-start-facts), so allocation freshness and both reclamation keystones cover it. Reach: pgs-reclaim-is-g-install ties pgs-reclaim to pgs-g-install, which fnps-reclaim calls. Open: L-PGS-LAZY-SHAPE, the host's lazy open defers the shape check of table pages written by older commits to first touch while the model's lazy open checks them (eager equals the model; record section 5); the per-disk marking composition is a hypothesis of pgs-g-reclaim-sound; A-PGS-HOST-IO names the fill; milestone 5 (fn-hist columns in FNADTSN1 regions on these pages) not started. Reach (arena-store-5, 2026-09-28): pgs-x-commit-refines-commit and pgs-x-commit-refines-crash tie pgs-commit, pgs-crash and pgs-plan-commit to pgs-x-commit (fnps-commit), pgs-x-fork-refines ties pgs-fork to pgs-x-fork (fnps-cmd-branch), through reach_check's square with the abstraction from the concrete state; the five HOST rows of planning/reach-baseline.json are gone.

proofs.title: init refuses by name a profile the machine's budget cannot hold, unless a target budget is named; a store init admitted always reopens on the same machine
proofs.statement: ember's decision 2026-09-27 17:30Z and the coordinator's release blocker (friend-path packet A: a 2 GiB node init said within-budget=yes, reservation 1,234 MB, and after 960 posts every start refused machine-cannot-hold-profile heap=2104 MB machine=2031 MB). books/heap-reservation.lisp: fn-heap-reserve-full-store-decide (was fn-heap-reserve-first-run-decide over the empty store) judges the run of the FULL store the profile admits (heap-figure's :run figure unobserved), and fn-heap-reserve-acceptsp and fn-heap-init-reservation-octets use it. KEYSTONE fn-heap-init-accepted-store-always-reopens: a profile (the admittedness hypothesis was removed after proving the weakened theorem) the full-store decision accepts within OBS is accepted by the launcher's :run decision (fn-heap-reserve-operation-decide) on the same OBS for every OBSERVED store and every owner bound. fn-heap-init-decide, for an operator's request (sizing :requested) this budget does not hold: written only when FN_INIT_BUDGET_MB names a target budget that holds its whole reservation (fn-heap-init-target-holdsp; the decision (:init REQUEST WORD MB BUDGET-MB :requested NIL TARGET-MB), the line `within-budget=no target-budget=N MB'), else refused :init-budget-cannot-hold-profile with the reservation and the budget (KEYSTONE fn-heap-init-decide-refuses-the-operators-request-past-the-budget; exit 1, fn-heap-init-refusal-exits-1), nothing written; unobserved machine memory is :machine-memory-unobserved. fn-heap-init-decide-honors-the-operators-request now holds when the budget or the named target holds the request. Host: host/native/operator.lisp init (fnn-heap-init-decision, host/native/heap.lisp), unchanged: it prints the line and exits with the decision's code. EXTENSION (batch AX fix init-budget, finding R1 of the public-node rehearsal, planning/evidence/public-node-rehearsal-2026-09-27.md): init run outside the service's memory limit sized the store for the whole machine and the service then refused machine-cannot-hold-profile. The named budget is FN_INIT_BUDGET_MB (there is no init option); it already caps the budget init sizes for. books/heap-reservation.lisp fn-heap-init-budget-note (decision physical limits budget-octets), called by host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-init-decision-noted (from host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-execute-init, on the same observation of the machine as the decision), is NIL or (:named-budget-below-machine NAMED-MB MACHINE-MB), MACHINE-MB the budget init observes without the named one (fn-heap-init-machine-octets: the physical memory less the OS's reserve and each limit). Init still writes (a warning, not a refusal: a named budget below the machine is how a store is made for a smaller limit, and the harness names one); the host prints fn-heap-init-budget-note-line on stderr after the init line: `warning init-budget-below-machine named-budget=N MB machine-budget=M MB: ...' telling the operator to run init under the service's memory limit. KEYSTONE fn-heap-init-budget-note-names-the-budget-init-sized-for: (implies (and (equal (car d) :init) (posp named) (< (floor named MiB) machine-mb)) (and (equal (car note) :named-budget-below-machine) (equal (nth 1 note) (nth 4 d)) (equal (nth 2 note) machine-mb) (< (nth 4 d) machine-mb))) with d the fn-heap-init-decide decision and note its fn-heap-init-budget-note: the note names the budget the store was sized for (the decision's) and the larger machine; fn-heap-init-budget-note-only-when-named-below-machine-by-definition: otherwise (no named budget, a named budget at or above the machine, a refusal) there is no note and init is as before; fn-heap-init-budget-is-the-named-below-the-machine. Not addressed: an init with NO named budget outside the service's limit still sizes for the whole machine silently (it cannot observe the unit's limit); the docs say to run init under the limit or name it.

proofs.title: The record log's open refuses damage by name and recovers only the torn tail of the one pending write
proofs.statement: Subjects: the calls host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-stream-segment makes after the stream's stop (fnn-log-probe-tail: fn-lgdm-start, fn-lgdm-done-p, fn-lgdm-q, fn-lgdm-header-len, fn-lgdm-entry-len, fn-lgdm-step; then fn-lgdm-verdict, fn-lgdm-effective, fn-lgdm-refused-p, fn-lgdm-refusal-text, fn-lgdm-report-text, fn-lgdm-repair-text), reached from fnn-log-recover (the writable open of the active segment; fn-lgdm-quarantine-name before a confirmed repair's truncation), fnn-log-open-read-only (status), fnn-log-scan-segments and fnn-log-read-closed-segment (closed segments), and fnn-command-recover's --repair truncate SEGMENT:OFFSET; and fnn-log-check-history-chain (fn-lgdm-chain-continues-p) in the history reads fnn-log-history-each and fnn-log-closed-records. KEYSTONE fn-lgdm-open-verdict-is-the-classification (books/store-log-damage.lisp): over the segment's octets C with no hypothesis, the verdict of the probe run from the stream's stopped state (the state fn-lgw-run-is-the-open names) is fn-lgdm-classify: the stop is the scan's frontier, the splice verdict is fn-lgs-chain-broken-p's, and the damage point is the least unit-aligned offset at or past the stop where an entry validates under the predecessor it claims (fn-lgdm-least-valid). KEYSTONE fn-lgdm-no-silent-prefix: the open's stop is the scan's frontier; when a valid entry starts at any offset P + k*UNIT below the extent the verdict is refused (:broken or :damaged), never a recovered prefix; and a :damaged verdict names a valid entry at or past the stop. KEYSTONE fn-lgdm-damage-lies-in-the-last-write: for C = a well-formed log of admitted records from a digest genesis, then octets Y, then zeros (a crash image of the one pending write at L's end has this shape with Y inside the write's range: fn-bs-crash-of-aligned-append), the stop is at or past L's end, a :damaged or :broken verdict points into Y, and with Y empty the verdict is not refused. fn-lgdm-repair-is-only-the-confirmed-damage: the operator's repair changes nothing but the :damaged verdict of the active segment of a writable open at exactly the confirmed SEGMENT:OFFSET, and keeps the stop. Scope: the torn-tail case is exactly the last incomplete write; damage confined to the LAST entry is indistinguishable from a torn tail and is recovered with a `log torn-tail' line (reported, exit 0); a frame embedded at a unit-aligned offset inside the torn write's own octets is refused (fail-closed). Record: planning/evidence/log-corruption-2026-09-27.md.

proofs.title: A payload handle is not octets: the retained article's and held row's payload is a handle by recognizer, disjoint from octets, and the host's every call into ACL2 refuses a wrong-kind argument or argument count by name before the entry runs
proofs.statement: books/payload-kinds.lisp. fn-payload-handle-p (a compound recognizer for natp) types the retained payload fields (books/acceptance.lisp fn-article-payload, books/held-record.lisp fn-held-payload). KEYSTONES fn-payload-handle-is-not-octets and fn-payload-octets-are-not-a-handle: no value is both a handle and fn-cbor-octet-listp octets, so a guard naming one kind refuses the other. The host entry guard (host/native/io.lisp fnn-entry-guard, run by fnn-call, the dispatcher every fnn-core* wrapper applies) evaluates, on the actual arguments, the entry's arity and exactly the conjuncts (R v) of the entry's own ACL2 guard with R in *fn-entry-guard-kinds* and v a non-stobj formal, and raises fnn-entry-guard-fault naming the entry, the position, the formal and the kind; it never evaluates another conjunct (no whole-state revalidation). tools/harness_check.py entry-guards: every dispatched entry's byte-carrying formal is covered by a kind conjunct (111), a body-first kind test (11) or a named exemption (16); tools/payload_kind_check.py: every definition that reads a retained payload declares its kind (fn-payload-kind :handle, :source or :wire) and the check has no waivers (lane entry-guards-2 closed the fourteen). The consumers it found: KEYSTONE fn-stx-index-of-store-without-a-keyring (books/stx-index.lisp; no hypothesis): with no keyring the statement index of ANY article list is (fn-stx-index-empty), so the keyring-less opens (books/config-observed.lisp, books/store-checkpoint-open.lisp twice, books/replay-identity-index.lisp; host fn-store-open-* through the owner's open) build the empty index and never walk the retained articles' handles. KEYSTONE fn-ofa-feed-article-is-the-owner-step-article (books/owner-feed-article.lisp; hypothesis fn-apr-store-at-restp): the bytes the book owner's feed step hands the feed (books/owner.lisp fn-own-feed-reply, now over fn-arena: fn-handle-bytes of fn-own-feed-article's handle) are the host entry's (fn-ofa-feed-article, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-feed-octets). Reclaim: fn-rcl-verdict and fn-rcl-summary are the octet model (declared :wire), equal over ALPHA to the arena counts the host calls (fn-rcl-store-counts, PRF-088's fn-rcl-store-counts-is-the-model-over-alpha); fn-rcl-reclaimable is the standing verdict (fn-rcl-standing-verdict), which reads no payload: the log reclaim's context (books/store-reclaim-pack.lisp fn-rclp-ctx-reclaimable) tests the tombstone on the record's own octets and the counts through the arena (fn-rcl-verdict-in). Control status and HDR :fn-control read the article through the arena (lane matrix-reds, PRF-084/PRF-228).

The two keystones are proved; the host entry guard is host code, witnessed by tests/test_native_entry_guard.py on the developer image (a handle, an octet vector, a wrong count, a handle in the second position: each the named fault; octets reach the entry). proofs.title: The decision journal: every event the scheduler's disk-and-clock value takes is one journal entry, the journal reads back whole and replays to agreement from the run's start, and every decision the host asks of the value reads only what the journal determines
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-otm-disk-step (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-disk-event: every disk and clock event, the served read's :served reading included, fnn-owner-advance-clock), fn-otm-note-step (fnn-owner-journal-note: the stall's release, members told and queued POSTs shed), fn-otm-start-line (fnn-owner-journal-open), each rendering the entry (SEQ OP READING A B C WORD) with fn-otm-jline; the host offers it to the service-log writer thread (host/native/io.lisp fnn-journal-line), which appends it to STORE/decisions/decisions.fnj, never on the owner and never waited on, bounded by ACL2's sink (books/log-sink.lisp). fn-otm-disk-step-unfolds: the step's word and value are fn-otm-disk-event's. fn-otm-journal-read-of-jlines: a list of entries (naturals) rendered and read back is itself, the reader's status :whole. KEYSTONE fn-otm-journal-determines-the-decisions: for every run STEPS of the host's calls (fn-otm-run: disk events of the four kinds, notes, and the gate's fn-otm-next, fn-otm-observe and fn-otm-commit-event interleaved in any order; hypothesis fn-otm-run-okp: the host appends only :clock, :served, :issue and :return events), the journal it writes reads back :whole and fn-otm-replay from the run's start answers :agrees (every recomputed word equals the journaled one, no gap) at the run's disk and clock. fn-otm-decisions-read-only-the-journal-state: admission, mode, wait, the 441 and 440 reply lines, health's disk lines and the log lines read only the disk and the clock. fn-otm-wall-reading-shape (books/clock-wall-reading.lisp, N3 of lane proto-determinism): the wall reading's validity is ACL2's (host/native/io.lisp fnn-owner-wall-milliseconds). fn-otm-journal-report-of-a-run: the operator's replay (host/native/io.lisp `store ROOT journal' calls fn-otm-journal-report and fn-otm-journal-exit) of the journal of any such run from fn-otm-init reports status=whole replay=agrees. Not claimed: that the file on disk holds every entry (the sink drops by name under its bound: a gap replay reports as (:gap SEQ)); anything about the record log's fold (lane proto-determinism: deterministic); the served machine's own replay from the :served readings (the readings are journaled; the served transcript replay is not built).
proofs.progress_note: Lane time-model-2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27). REPL-admitted on hbox (the book 4.6 s ACL2 time from source). Teeth (tests/acl2/owner-time-model-tests.lisp, prefix t2-): a reached run of nine interleaved host calls whose six entries are exact, read back whole and replayed to agreement; a tampered word (:diverged 3); a dropped entry (:gap 3); a run with an event kind the host never appends (:malformed 1, fn-otm-run-okp removed); two values with equal disk and clock decide alike and a different clock does not.

proofs.title: While the disk sheds a served read runs with posting not permitted and under the disk-slow posture, so a POST command is answered 440 with the disk's reason before its article, a peer's IHAVE 436 and CHECK 431, and the node's configuration is never changed by it
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-otm-read-span (books/owner-time-admission.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at calls with S, the gate's scheduler value at the read's recorded time (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk-read: fnn-owner-advance-clock's :served event, then fnn-owner-gate-sched-value; the admission is fn-otm-admit-post of S). fn-otm-read-span-when-admitted-unfolds: admitted, it is fn-orr-read-span (every reader-read theorem, PRF-288/PRF-296, holds of the host's call). KEYSTONE fn-otm-read-span-while-shedding: while shedding, connection ID's read is fn-orr-read-span over the owner with that connection's injection configuration's posting bit off (the served step reads the connection's snapshot, books/owner.lisp fn-own-served-conn; its effects are that read's), and afterwards the connection, when its record has the owner's shape, has the posting bit it had before; the owner's own configuration is never touched. fn-otm-closed-posting-never-awaits-an-article: under a configuration that does not permit posting, fn-scr-post-step from a session not awaiting an article leaves it not awaiting one (the POST is answered 440, RFC 3977 section 6.3.1, and no article is read). Mutating control (host/native/control.lisp: an operator post, a live configuration change, a moderation decision) is answered BUSY while fn-otm-admit-post sheds, at a clock event appended before it waits for the gate. Not claimed: the chain from fn-orr-read-span to fn-scr-post-step (the served machine calls it with the connection's injection configuration; stated, not proved here); IHAVE/CHECK during slow (PKT-862). EXTENSION (lane log-leftovers, 2026-09-27; the disk's reason on the wire and PKT-858). KEYSTONE fn-otm-read-span-while-shedding (restated): connection ID's read while fn-otm-admit-post S is :shed runs over fn-otm-shed-ocfg (posting bit off; the disk-slow posture's entry *fn-peer-shed-entry* at the front of the owner's refused-offer memory, so every peer session re-pinned with it by books/owner.lisp fn-own-conn-live-session is fn-peer-shed-p); its effects are that read's with each generic 440 and posting-disallowed 441 replaced by ACL2's fn-otm-post-command-reply S / fn-otm-shed-reply S exactly when the connection's posting bit was on before the read (fn-otm-disk-effects), and the read's own when it was off (the configuration refuses, not the disk); afterwards the connection has its posting bit back and the refused-offer memory is the read's with the posture's entries out (fn-otm-strip-shed; fn-otm-strip-shed-leaves-no-posture, fn-otm-strip-shed-of-marked). fn-otm-disk-effects-names-the-disk: with replacement lines that are not the generic ones (true of the host's lines at every reached slow and stalled state, test book), no generic 440 or 441 is left and the count of effects is kept; fn-otm-disk-effects-keeps-the-rest. KEYSTONE fn-peer-shed-offer-is-disk-slow (books/peer-inbound-invariants.lisp; subject fn-peer-decide-offer, called by books/peer-inbound.lisp fn-peer-command's IHAVE and CHECK arms, the served chain of host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at): under fn-peer-shed-p, an offer from an inbound peer with a well-formed Message-ID is :defer :disk-slow whatever the node holds (436 'retry later; the disk is slow' to IHAVE, 431 to CHECK: fn-peer-not-now-is-a-retry-code; RFC 3977 section 6.3.2, RFC 4644 section 2.4), before the history arm, because the live node the peer is re-pinned to holds the batch in flight. The peer read's class (host/native/mux.lisp fnn-mux-step through host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-peer-read-class): fn-otm-peer-read-class-is-reader-exactly-while-shedding; fn-otm-peer-reader-read-only-while-shedding (fn-otm-peer-read-proceeds-p, checked in fnn-owner-handle-chunk-read: a reader-class peer read the disk no longer sheds is deferred and retried as transit). Not claimed: the chain from fn-orr-read-span to fn-peer-decide-offer (stated, as the posting bit's); a transfer (IHAVE's article after a 335 given before the disk went slow, a TAKETHIS) is queued as before and waits for the barrier (fn-peer-decide-transfer is not under the posture: the transfer runs in its own transit quantum).

proofs.title: Catching up from a peer: the XFNCATCHUP batch serves only what ARTICLE would, always progresses within its quantum, and the requester offers only verified batches, only through its own IHAVE verdict, and resumes at the last journaled batch
proofs.statement: Serve (books/peer-catchup-serve.lisp fn-cu-serve-reply, which books/nntp.lisp fn-nntp-command-pinned calls for XFNCATCHUP on the pinned, READ-restricted view; books/nntp-auth.lisp gates it with the archive readers): fn-cu-select-serves-only-retrievable: every article a batch serves is an entry of the view and fn-cu-servedp (a valid Message-ID in the view's trie, not reclaimed, CRLF-framed, held at a number in a group the wildmat admits: what ARTICLE <msgid> on the same view returns); fn-cu-select-makes-progress: a batch from FROM below the view's end answers NEXT > FROM; fn-cu-select-stays-within-the-quantum: for a natural quantum, the batch's article octets are at most the quantum or the batch is exactly one article (served whole, never cut); fn-cu-serve-reply-effects-well-formed (books/peer-catchup-effects.lisp, cited by books/nntp-pinned-effects.lisp): the reply is one well-formed response. Requester (books/peer-catchup.lisp; host/native/pull-service.lisp fnn-pull-round calls fn-cu-session-begin-pair, fn-cu-session-step-pair, fn-cu-session-close; fnn-pull-journal-append calls fn-cu-cursor-envelope; fnn-catchup-journal-open calls fn-cu-journal-scan and fn-cu-records-replay): fn-cu-step-keeps-offers-verified: fn-cu-step preserves fn-cu-verifiedp (while offering, the held batch chains from the committed chain to the peer's claim and what remains is a suffix of it; while waiting, nothing remains), and fn-cu-begin establishes it; fn-cu-on-end-refuses-a-digest-mismatch: a batch whose records do not chain to the claim ends the round :failed with (:close) only and the cursor unmoved; fn-cu-step-installs-only-through-the-verdict: every effect of a step that reaches the local node is the IHAVE of the record the round then waits on, or, only on the local node's 335 in phase :offer, that record's body; every journal record is the round's committed cursor with nothing of its batch left; fn-cu-records-replay-is-the-last-cursor and fn-cu-resume-asks-from-the-journaled-cursor: the open recovers the last journaled cursor of the peer and a round begun from it asks from exactly that position and chain; fn-cu-decode-of-encode: the FNCU record round-trips. The digest chain c' = SHA-256(c || SHA-256(article) || msgid) is a transport and completeness check, not an authentication of the peer. Not proved: positions are stable only while the view grows (a READ-rule change can skip entries on resume); the peer's claim is relative to the chain the requester presents.
proofs.progress_note: Slice 1. Open: an absolute peer digest at a position (needs an ordinal index), position stability across a view reshape, the concrete representation of the batch buffer (D27, as the pull's ARTICLE), the snapshot hook (design only, waits for arena-store).

proofs.title: A compressed record in the log expands to exactly the record it was sealed from; a compressed extent reads back, through the proved LZ decoder, as the record's payload; the replay and the commit with compressed extents are the resident ones
proofs.statement: books/payload-lz-record.lisp (brief C2 of planning/evidence/article-compression-2026-09-27.md section 6; lane compression-extents). The record FRAME sits between the record codec and the log: Z = 'fn-z' head ++ u32 DICT-ID, K, N, |STUB| ++ STUB ++ C, STUB the record R without its payload span [K, K+N), C an LZ4 block (books/payload-lz.lisp) decoding to that span against the dictionary DICT-ID; fn-lzr-expand gives R back or refuses by name (:lz-frame, :lz-dictionary, :lz-decode); a record that is not a frame passes unchanged. fn-lzr-seal (the one producer of a frame) runs the proved decoder over the host's untrusted candidate and frames R only when it decodes to the span, the span reaches the profile's threshold MIN (0 never) and the frame is shorter (fn-lzr-compress-p); a record that begins with the frame head is framed with an empty span. KEYSTONE fn-lzr-expand-of-seal: for a table binding DICT-ID to DICT, a u32 DICT-ID and an octet record of u32 length, (fn-lzr-expand dicts (fn-lzr-seal dict dict-id min r k n candidate)) = (:ok r), whatever the candidate, threshold or span. fn-lzr-replay-reads-the-sealed-record (the D25 decision): for (fn-record-p w) the expansion of the seal of (fn-record-encode w) decodes to (:ok w), so the content identity, Message-ID comparison, signatures and Cancel-Lock -- all over the authored octets, computed before the seal -- are unchanged; the log's frame trailer covers the durable Z. Dictionaries: fn-lzr-dictsp (u32 id, at most 65,536 octets, the LZ4 window), fn-lzr-dicts-add refuses a rebinding (fn-lzr-dicts-add-keeps-bindings). The compressed extent (FILE EOFF ELEN CPOFF CLEN TRAILER N DICT-ID) of a frame at its log place (fn-lzr-extent-of: C is Z's tail and decodes to the record's payload); KEYSTONE fn-lzr-extent-read-denotes: under the faithful read of Z at its place, fn-lzr-read of C's durable octets against the dictionary is (:ok payload). The arena (books/payload-arena.lisp, books/payload-arena-extent.lisp, books/payload-arena-extent-logic.lisp): exports fn-arena-seal-lz-extent / fn-arena-reseat-lz-extent (logic: the handle is fn-lzr-lz-value DICT (durable C) N, books/payload-lz-value.lisp), every {correspondence}/{guard-thm}/{preserved} obligation proved over the reference and the extent attachment (EXT entry an 8-tuple carrying the dictionary's octets); KEYSTONE fn-arena-seal-lz-extent-payload, KEYSTONE fn-arena-reseat-lz-extent-keeps-a-faithful-arena. The replay (books/payload-lz-replay.lisp): fn-lzr-intern-step (a frame whose C decodes to the record's payload sealed as a compressed extent, anything else the plain extent intern); KEYSTONE fn-lzr-intern-step-refines: under fn-arx-faithful-p it is fn-srs-intern-step. The commit: fn-lzr-commit-reseats; KEYSTONE fn-lzr-commit-reseats-keep-the-arena under fn-arx-commit-faithful-p. The served read of a compressed handle is the host realizer fn-durable-realize-lz (A-DURABLE-LZ): the extent realizer's trailer-checked read of C, then ACL2's fn-lzr-lz-read (fn-lzr-lz-read-is-the-lz-value), a failed decode refused by name (arena-extent-lz-decode). Host subject: host/native/extent.lisp fn-durable-realize-lz calls fn-lzr-lz-read; the seal (POST), the replay step and the commit reseat have no host caller yet (the lane's continuation wires them: planning/evidence/compression-extents-2026-09-27.md).

proofs.title: `store reclaim` records its instant before it rewrites, and the rewrite is a function of the pre-reclaim store and that record
proofs.statement: books/reclaim-instant.lisp. The reclaim's instant NOW (the clock's stamp the context reads, host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-reclaim-rule-and-stamp) is the configuration limit row `retention-reclaim-at` (CODE = NOW + 1, 0 for no wall reading), staged as the one delta fn-rci-delta by fn-store-reclaim-instant-record (host/checkpoint-host.lisp, over the configuration record path fn-store-cfg-peer-delta-record) and published, before any rewrite, by host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-reclaim-record-instant (through host/native/admin.lisp fnn-admin-publish-record: authorization, publication, read-back), called by fnn-log-reclaim-steps on the :reclaim decision. fn-rci-recorded-instant-reads-back: for NOW nil or a natural (fn-rci-instantp), the configuration the published record yields (fn-rci-recorded-config: fn-cfg-apply-record, what every open applies) records an instant, reads back NOW, and keeps the retention rule. KEYSTONE fn-rci-recorded-context-is-the-decided-context: the context a replay derives from that configuration (fn-rci-context) is fn-rclp-ctx of the rule and NOW the host decided under. KEYSTONE fn-rci-recorded-decision-is-the-decision: the decision over the recorded configuration (fn-rci-decide-stream; `store reclaim --recorded`, host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-log-reclaim-decide-recorded from fnn-log-reclaim-steps) is fn-lgr-decide-stream at that rule and NOW over the same store and fold, so with PRF-271 the history the host checkpointed is determined by the pre-reclaim history and the record. With no recorded instant `--recorded` is refused :no-recorded-instant (fn-rci-decide-stream's first arm). fn-rci-delta-is-a-delta: for a representable NOW the staged delta passes fn-cfg-delta-listp. The operator keystones: `store reclaim --recorded` is exactly the :reclaim-recorded native action (fn-native-operator-run-store-reclaim-recorded-is-the-reclaim-recorded-action, fn-native-operator-run-reclaim-recorded-action-is-only-store-reclaim-recorded). Not a store-format change: a :set-limit row of a slot no reader names is admitted by every image (books/config.lisp fn-cfg-limit-ceiling) and read by none; a new record-log kind would be (books/store-recover-stream.lisp fn-srs-decode refuses an undecodable record).
proofs.progress_note: Lane log-leftovers (sub-lane log-leftovers-reclaim), 2026-09-27: PKT-857 (N2 of lane proto-determinism; time-model-2's PKT-861). Open: a process death between the instant's record and the checkpoint's install leaves the instant recorded and the history unrewritten; `store reclaim --recorded` completes it, a plain rerun records a later instant (the open does not apply a recorded instant by itself). The hypothesis fn-rci-instantp is shown necessary for the context keystone (tests: :late); for the decision keystone no counterexample is claimed (the decision reads NOW only through fn-rcl-rule-permits' natp test).

proofs.title: A peer's feed queue holds undelivered obligations, never history: a final answer retires the entry, a full queue is the named refusal feed-queue-full, and health holds it
proofs.statement: fn-feed-done (fn-feed-observe on 235/239/435/438/437/439, host: fn-owner-feed-octets -> fn-own-feed-reply; replay at open: fn-own-feed-recover -> fn-feed-replay) removes the entry (fn-feed-queue-retire). fn-feed-queue-length-is-undelivered: for a driven journal (fn-feed-drivenp), the queue after fn-feed-replay has length start + enqueue/commit records - final outcome records. fn-feed-final-outcome-retires-for-good: a final outcome for a Message-ID with no later enqueue leaves it out of the queue after the fold. fn-feed-accepted-outcomes-bounded-by-enqueues: accepted outcomes for (peer, Message-ID) are at most the times it was owed; fn-feed-at-most-one-accepted-outcome: at most one when owed once (fn-feedp is implied by fn-feed-drivenp, fn-feed-drivenp-implies-feedp). fn-own-intent-refusal-word (host: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-drain-one) names a :capacity intent :feed-queue-full: its own 441 line (fn-post-store-refusal-text), and 436 for transit (fn-peer-transit-code; fn-peer-full-feed-queue-is-a-retry-code-by-definition). fn-nh-feed-queue-full-intent-is-held: a :capacity intent (fn-own-submission-intent-result, the reference of fn-icar-submission-intent the host calls) holds unavailable-peer in fn-nh-verdict over the same feed table (fn-nh-saturated-peer-is-held, fn-nh-feed-queue-refusal-is-held). fn-feed-distinct-fast-is-distinctp: fn-feed-distinctp (the fn-feedp conjunct every transition and replayed record checks) executes one pass with a fast alist (mbe); 0.2 ms at 1,024 entries on hbox against 19 ms quadratic.
proofs.progress_note: Open: the owner-level theorem keeps fn-own-feed-tablep, which is probably redundant (no violating value found; the weakened theorem is not proved). The power-loss rig has no feeding workload yet; retirement writes no new record (the :feed-outcome record already was a cut), and the keystones hold over every driven prefix. max-queue is still 1024 from `peer add` (an admission limit on undelivered backlog; no operator verb sets it).

proofs.title: The running owner's report string and obligation lines are built with constant stack: `obligations` at 5,000 answers and the owner keeps running
proofs.statement: fn-nls-octets-string-is-record-octets-string: fn-nls-octets-string, a loop, equals fn-record-octets-string on every value. fn-nls-buffer (called by host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-status-host-answer) builds the report text with fn-record-octets-string, which since PRF-345 executes by a loop itself (books/records-shape.lisp); before, its non-tail recursion exhausted the 1,024 KB control stack past about 50,000 octets. fn-nls-obligation-lines executes fn-nls-obligation-lines-rev (mbe; the equation is its guard).
proofs.progress_note: Closed at the cause by PRF-345 (lane thread-stacks, PKT-693): books/records-shape.lisp fn-record-octets-chars and fn-record-string-octets-aux execute an accumulator loop (mbe), so every caller of the two conversions runs in constant stack; fn-nls-buffer now calls fn-record-octets-string directly and fn-nls-octets-string stays with its equation and tests.

proofs.title: Octet text codecs over the octet buffer: decimal and hexadecimal naturals, hex strings and RFC 4648 base64 round-trip, base64 accepts only canonical text and refuses by name, case-insensitive equality is equality of case folds, and the bounded token split loses nothing
proofs.statement: books/octet-text.lisp. Each codec is a list model over octet lists with an in-place twin over the octet buffer (fn-octets, books/octets-stobj.lisp) and a boundary theorem equating the twin with the model on the buffer's slice; every executable function is guard-verified. fn-ot-nat-parse-of-nat-octets: parsing the printed natural (radix 2..16) under the caller's bound MAX gives it back; fn-ot-nat-parse-bounded: an accepted natural is at most MAX. fn-ot-hex-decode-of-encode and fn-ot-b64-decode-of-encode: decode of encode is the identity (RFC 4648 section 4 for base64). fn-ot-b64-accepted-is-canonical: an accepted base64 text is the encoding of what it decodes to (padding bits zero, the pad only in the last quantum); fn-ot-b64-refuses-outside-alphabet and the refusal kinds :b64-quantum, :b64-alphabet, :b64-padding-bits are named. fn-ot-ci-equal-is-downcase-equal: ASCII case-insensitive equality is equality of the case folds. fn-ot-split-wsp-loses-nothing: the tokens are the input's non-whitespace octets in order, at most LIMIT of them; more is the refusal :too-many-tokens, never a truncation. No function caps data: bounds are the caller's (D27).
proofs.pending_subject: No host function calls these codecs yet (lane shared-books built them as the shared library the wire books re-derived); each wire book that adopts one names its host caller then.
proofs.progress_note: Lane shared-books (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-28), id assigned at the batch AY merge. Certified on persvati: certify-20260928T025149Z-846867 (under 10 s). Teeth: tests/acl2/octet-text-tests.lisp with the RFC 4648 section 10 vectors. Proof-style findings in docs/proof-style.md.

proofs.title: The compressed append: ACL2 plans the payload span, decides the frame over the untrusted LZ4 candidate with named outcomes, and every record the log hands out is read back through the proved decoder; the switch is a configuration row
proofs.statement: books/payload-lz-append.lisp (lane compression-extents-2, the host wiring of C2 over PRF-326). fn-lzr-append-plan MIN R: the payload span (K . N) of the article record R (the codec decodes R; the payload's place checked) when MIN (the `compress-min-octets' :set-limit configuration row, fn-lzr-config-min; no row is 0, off: fn-lzr-config-min-without-a-row-is-off, fn-lzr-append-plan-off) wants it and N is within the encoder's LZ4_MAX_INPUT_SIZE. fn-lzr-append-decide DICT DICT-ID MIN R K N CANDIDATE runs the proved decoder over the host's candidate (liblz4-HC 1.10.0, vendored, untrusted) and answers (:framed Z), (:kept :lz-no-gain) (the named policy: no block within the cap, or the frame not shorter), (:kept :lz-span), or (:refused :lz-candidate). KEYSTONE fn-lzr-append-decide-framed-expands: a framed decision's octets expand, under any table binding DICT-ID to DICT, to R; fn-lzr-append-decide-framed-is-the-seal; fn-lzr-append-decide-refuses-exactly-a-bad-candidate (iff the candidate does not decode to the span); fn-lzr-append-decide-keeps-only-without-gain; fn-lzr-append-decide-framed-is-shorter (the frame fits every bound R fits); fn-lzr-record-is-not-a-frame (a record passes the read unchanged); fn-lzr-append-replay-reads-the-record (the octets the log takes, whatever the decision, read back as R and decode as R decodes: the digests stay over the original octets, D25). Host subjects: host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-compress (from fnn-log-publish, before the fence; and fnn-log-write-history under a developer selector) calls fn-lzr-append-plan, fn-lzr-candidate-cap and fn-lzr-append-decide; fnn-log-read-record (from fnn-log-stream-segment, the one place records leave the log) calls fn-lzr-read-step (fn-lzr-read-step-expands-by-definition: its record is fn-lzr-expand's); the replay calls fn-lzr-intern-step for a chunk holding frames; fnn-log-reseat-fenced calls fn-lzr-commit-reseats once the log has taken a frame; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-compress-min-octets and host/store-host.lisp fn-store-compress-min-octets read the row. The archive reader (proposed D38): books/store-export.lisp fn-sxp-config-decode-archive reads the profile layout before batch AS (thirteen u64 fields) with that release's header limits (fn-sxp-config-decode-archive-is-valid, -of-a-current-frame).

proofs.title: The NNTP protocol table is the reader dispatcher's reply codes and framing: every reply code fn-nntp-command-pinned emits for a command is in that command's table row, and only :article-framed rows (POST) hand the connection to article mode
proofs.statement: books/protocol-table.lisp (lane defprotocol, G4 of planning/extrapolation-2026-09-27.md section 3): `defprotocol` holds one row per NNTP command (RFC 3977, 4642, 4643, 4644, 6048, RFC 2980's legacy spellings, fn's XREDEEM and XFNCATCHUP) and three pseudo-rows (syntax, unrecognized, connection): the RFC section, the dispatch layer, the existing parser functions, the reference / -cat / Xref model functions, the framing (:command or :article), every reply (code, class accepted/refused/uncertain, layer, key, text; :computed and :unreachable flags), the fuzzer's argument grammar and the FAQ line; it checks the rows (a 2xx/3xx reply is accepted, a 4xx/5xx never is; a text begins with its code). KEYSTONE fn-proto-command-pinned-replies-are-in-the-row (books/protocol-codes.lisp), no hypothesis: every :reply effect of (fn-nntp-command-pinned session archive index verdicts env tokens fn-arena) carries a status code in (fn-proto-reader-codes (car tokens)) -- the syntax pseudo-row's for a non-keyword token, the matching row's :reader codes, else the unrecognized pseudo-row's. Subject: fn-nntp-command-pinned; the host path is host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk-read -> fn-owner-chunk-span -> fn-scr-step -> fn-scr-command, which fn-scr-command-is-command-pinned equates with it under fn-scr-catalogp. Proof: one lemma per response builder (fn-proto-codes-of-*, parametric in the retrieval kind and the legacy HDR flag), one generated theorem per row (fn-proto-row-NAME-codes, fn-proto-row-NAME-lookup) and the keystone as their generated case split. KEYSTONE fn-proto-command-pinned-offers-only-article-framing (books/protocol-framing.lisp): a first token no :article row names yields no begin-article effect; the case split is generated from the :framing column (fn-proto-row-NAME-framing), and fn-proto-offers-only-post-by-table derives nntp-auth-fold's fn-auth-fold-command-pinned-offers-only-post from it without that theorem. Not claimed: the auth, peer, post and owner layers' replies (listed in the rows, layer-tagged, unproved), which situation earns which code (tested), and codes of branches marked :unreachable.

proofs.title: F2: every served lookup the host reaches is constant or logarithmic in the store: the Xref ARTICLE/HEAD/HDR arms, the by-number withdrawn test, GROUP/LISTGROUP's summary and the re-pin read the catalog, equal to the archive walks they replace
proofs.statement: Lane sca-join-5. (1) books/served-catalog.lisp fn-rcompat-reply-cat (called by fn-nntp-archive-command-cat, the -cat dispatcher of the host's served read, books/served-catalog-chain.lisp fn-scr-command) answers ARTICLE/HEAD by number and of the current article with fn-scat-number-article / fn-scat-available-article (one number-table probe) and HDR/XHDR Xref with fn-scat-range-numbers, where books/nntp-reader-compat.lisp fn-rcompat-retrieval and fn-rcompat-hdr walk the pinned archive; KEYSTONES fn-rcompat-reply-cat-is-rcompat-reply, fn-rcompat-retrieval-cat-is-retrieval, fn-rcompat-hdr-cat-is-hdr (hypotheses: the archive is the catalog's view at V, fn-cnx-freshp). fn-nntp-number-withdrawn-p-cat probes the number table before walking the pinned withdrawn list W (fn-nntp-number-withdrawn-p-cat-is-archive). proofs.title: BLAKE3 in ACL2: the definition over octet lists and its executable twin over the octet buffer
proofs.statement: books/blake3.lisp defines BLAKE3 (the compression function over 64-octet blocks with seven rounds as a chain of multiple-value functions over declared 32-bit words, chunks of up to 1024 octets with CHUNK_START and CHUNK_END, the tree whose left subtree holds the largest power-of-two number of whole chunks shorter than the input, parents, and the root's first 32 output octets) in the hash, keyed_hash and derive_key modes, every function guard-verified, with the shape proved (fn-blake3-shape, fn-blake3-keyed-shape, fn-blake3-derive-key-shape: 32 octets for every object). Agreement with BLAKE3 is evidence, not proof: tests/acl2/blake3-tests.lisp evaluates all 35 official vectors (third_party/blake3/test_vectors, tag 1.8.7) in all three modes. books/blake3-stobj.lisp is the executable twin over a list prefix and a window of the octet buffer, conses nothing per block, and is proved equal to the definition level by level: fn-b3x-byte-is-nthx, fn-b3x-words-is-words, fn-b3x-chunk-is-chunk, fn-b3x-node-is-node, and the keystone fn-b3x-hash-is-hash (the buffer hash of PREFIX then the window [A, A+WN) is fn-b3-hash of the octets of their concatenation, for a window inside the buffer); its three entries fn-blake3-stobj (any object, copied once into a local buffer), fn-blake3-of-prefixed-buffer and fn-blake3-of-prefixed-range are equal to fn-blake3 (fn-blake3-stobj-is-blake3, fn-blake3-of-prefixed-buffer-is-blake3, fn-blake3-of-prefixed-range-is-blake3). books/crypto-attach.lisp and books/frame-digest-buffer.lisp attach them to fn-digest, fn-frame-digest, fn-frame-digest-buffer and fn-frame-digest-range. In the saved images host/native/digest.lisp replaces the three entries with the vendored C (lib/libfn-blake3) after checking it against the official vectors and fn-b3x-hash (A-CRYPTO-NATIVE). Collision resistance is A-CRYPTO: about 2^-128 per chosen pair (the birthday bound over 256 bits), not proved.
proofs.progress_note: Lane blake3-digest (2026-09-28): ember, BLAKE3 wherever fn chooses the algorithm; store format 10 with lane format-bump-10.

proofs.title: A POST the store refuses at its drain for capacity or input wrote nothing: it is told its named refusal at once and never waits for, or is told uncertain because of, another member's barrier; a START of only such refusals issues no sync
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-ocs-told-at-drain-p (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-commit-start-locked, per drained member of a START, START-NEXT or the inline quantum), fn-ocs-start-event (fnn-owner-commit-start-event), fn-ocs-commit-step (the inline quantum, fnn-owner-commit-queued-locked) and fn-ocp-commit-step (the committer, through fn-otm-commit-event). KEYSTONE fn-ocs-unstaged-start-tells-its-refusals (books/owner-commit-steps.lisp): for every list WORDS of drained members' outcome words observed certain, if every word is told at its drain (fn-ocs-all-told-at-drain-p: :unaffordable, :memberships or :malformed, the refusals whose prepare staged no record) then the batch keeps no member (fn-ocs-kept-count 0), the START's event is :started-none, and the step from an idle owner is :none with the owner idle: no barrier. fn-ocs-kept-member-starts-the-barrier: a START whose first member is not told at its drain names the barrier. fn-ocs-told-at-drain-p-by-definition: a told word is never :durable, :durable-key-change-refused, :uncertain, :duplicate, :conflict or :refused. fn-ocp-unstaged-start-issues-no-sync (books/owner-commit-pipeline.lisp): the committer's step names :none, leaves the phase :idle and opens no next batch. books/owner-ack-after-barrier.lisp: the drain model tells such a member at once with a report naming no record and the batch completes the members it kept; fn-oab-quantum-reports-after-its-barrier and fn-oab-pipeline-reports-after-its-barriers (PRF-267's reply keystones in the ack model) hold unchanged in statement over it. Scope: the words are ACL2's outcome words, which the host takes from the attempt (fnn-owner-attempt: the prepare's refusal after the refused reservation was consumed); that a refusal word means no record was staged is the prepare's property (books/owner-prepare-outcome.lisp), cited, not re-proved here. A capacity refusal reads the capacity unfenced members use: its reason may not hold after a failed barrier, its outcome (nothing stored) does. A refusal that names another record waits for the barrier as before (fn-ocs-member-release).
proofs.progress_note: Lane full-vs-uncertain (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-28), coordinator decision after the openbsd-datasize finding (a 441 uncertain at a full store under 2G, not reproduced in over 70 runs). REPL-admitted on persvati: the three books and both test books. Teeth: owner-commit-steps-tests (reached idle state *ocst-s-done*: positive witness with all conjuncts; hypothesis removal with an accepted member: kept 1, :started, :barrier, staged; a duplicate kept; labelled mutations) and owner-ack-after-barrier-tests (a full-store refusal beside an article in a failed batch is reported and the property holds; mutation: a told reply naming a record). Native: tests/test_native_slow_disk.py test_a_full_store_refusal_is_told_while_another_barrier_stalls.

proofs.title: RETIRED (no migrations: fresh deploys at 6.6.0; D38 withdrawn, lane one-format): Format 9 to 10: every record kind a format-9 node writes translates, keeping what it asserts, or is refused by name
proofs.statement: books/store-format-9-records.lisp, the import's record translation (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-store-import via books/store-export.lisp fn-sxp-import-plan's fn-f9r-records, a guard-verified loop fn-f9r-loop over fn-f9r-step). Accepted composites (fn-e kind 4: schema 0, schema 1 verified, schema 1 carried): fn-f9r-composite-keeps-what-it-binds -- sequence, txid, generation, keyring generation, profile, schema, the exact verdict bytes and the exact authored source are the archive's and the embedded article is the translated archive article (fn-f9r-article: payload with both signatures, Message-ID, groups, evidence, charge and stamp kept); fn-f9r-composite-identities-are-format-10s -- its content subject is its translated article's and its authored-source identity is fn-hsig-authored-source-id of the carried source (the derivation replay checks; schema 0 keeps none); fn-f9r-step-of-a-composite -- the step admits a composite only as that translation and only when it binds (fn-stxa-bindsp, the check replay runs), otherwise (:refused :composite-binding). No signature is re-made: the D09 signed preimage is the domain tag, principal, keys and source (books/hybrid-signature.lisp fn-hsig-signed-preimage), none of which the translation changes. fn-f9r-step-carries-identity-free-kinds-verbatim: statement verdicts (kind 2), keyring snapshots (kind 3: enrollment, succession, revocation, a key statement's key change), consumer events (fnce) and the topic administrator's install (fnto 2) import as exactly their archive octets. Topic anchors and admissions (fnto 0/1) are refused (:signed-format-9-identity) with their sequence: replay re-prepares them from the root's or report's SIGNED source, which names the controller key set, topic, policy and parents by format-9 identities that format 10 neither parses (fn-id-labelledp requires algorithm 2) nor could re-sign. fn-f9r-loop-keeps-sequences: the translated records are the archive's sequences in order. Teeth: tests/acl2/store-format-9-records-tests.lisp (each kind's format-9 twin translates to the format-10 fixture itself; the verified composite binds the enrolled snapshot again, fn-hsig-article-event-snapshot-bindsp-v1; an unbound composite and a format-9 anchor are refused by name). Native: tests/test_native_format_9_every_kind.py. Not claimed: that a local account's credential, invitation or posting-account value survives (they are derived under the old digest or keyed MAC; specs/storage.md, the migration); that a principal derived from a login under SHA-256 is still that login's (the snapshot keeps the format-9 principal verbatim).

proofs.title: store digest streams: the executable digest is the block chain of the canonical octets, one block of memory, and a value within one block is unchanged
proofs.statement: books/state-digest.lisp fn-sdg-digest (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-store-digest via host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-replay-digest-report) is (mbe :logic (fn-sdg-chain (fn-sdg-canon x)) :exec the streamed sink). KEYSTONE fn-sdg-canon-rev-sink-is-the-chain-of-the-canon: the sink the executable pushes every canonical octet into, in the order fn-sdg-canon produces them, finishes as fn-sdg-chain of fn-sdg-canon (the D27 boundary: the served path never materializes the canonical list). KEYSTONE fn-sdg-chain-of-one-block: a true list of at most *fn-sdg-block-octets* (65,536) octets chains to fn-digest of it, the value before this change. fn-sdg-rows-history and fn-sdg-arena-pool stream the same way. And `store status' counts retention classes by loops (books/store-reclaim-holders.lisp fn-rcl-summary-in, fn-rcl-held-count-in, fn-rcl-class-count-in: mbe forward loops, logic unchanged; host fn-native-live-status-host-offline via io.lisp fnn-command-live-report). Measured on hbox (syn1m-2k copy): store status exit 4 (control stack) -> exit 0, 3:11, 7.55 GB; store digest exit 1 (heap exhausted at 32.9 GB) -> exit 0, 7:46, 5.93 GB; syn100k digest 0:43/4.62 GB -> 0:58/1.41 GB. Not claimed: anything of the digest beyond A-CRYPTO; that the lines whose stream exceeds one block keep their pre-change values (they do not; no reader compares them across images).
