proofs.title: The served owner's records are the history image's followed by the log suffix: the owner the host installs from a checkpoint holds exactly the checkpoint's records then the suffix, the image of the checkpoint's records answers them through the record view, and the publication's append of its canonical rows leaves the image of the next checkpoint's records
proofs.statement: books/history-pages-owner.lisp. KEYSTONES: fn-hpo-installed-records-are-checkpoint-then-suffix (no hypothesis beyond the install's success: with PAIR = (fn-rii-sco-extend-open C CONFIGS SUFFIX FRONTIER) and OC = (fn-ock-install (car (cadr PAIR)) (cadr (cadr PAIR)) MAX-CONNS) not :fault, (fn-sf-records (fn-sn-files (fn-own-store (fn-ocfg-owner OC)))) = (append (true-list-fix (fn-sco-records C)) SUFFIX)); fn-hpo-records-at-is-installed-nth (the same OC not :fault, H = (fn-sco-records C) with fn-hp-okp, N = (len H), LENS = (fn-hp-lens H SALT), STARTS placed (fn-hp-starts-okp, adt-placement-ok STARTS LENS NP), the page store's verified pages holding (fn-hp-piw H SALT STARTS NP), I natural: (fn-hp-records-at I N SUFFIX SALT LENS STARTS PGS-MEM) answers (:ok (nth I RECORDS)) whenever its verdict is :ok below (len RECORDS), is :ok or a need-verdict there, and (:refused :seq) at and past it, RECORDS the installed owner's); fn-hpo-records-at-is-nth-of-extension (the same over any R with (fn-sf-prefixp H R) and the suffix (nthcdr (len H) R): the served owner's records only extend, owner-invariants-served fn-own-run-records-prefix); fn-hpo-snapshot-image-is-next-checkpoint (the owner's publication: H = (fn-sco-records BASE) imaged as above, CANON = (fn-scka-canon-rows (nthcdr (len H) RECORDS) FN-ARENA H0) not :bad, (fn-hp-x-append-all CANON 0 SALT (len H) LENS STARTS NP PGS-MEM) answering :ok => (fn-sco-records (fn-scka-next-checkpoint BASE H0 CONFIGS RECORDS FN-ARENA)) = (append H CANON), and the answer's header (N2 LENS2 STARTS2 NP2) and store hold that history's image: fn-hp-okp, N2 its length, LENS2 its fn-hp-lens, (fn-hp-vhold ... (fn-hp-piw (append H CANON) SALT STARTS2 NP2))). Scope: the image and the checkpoint are two durable writes; that the pair an open reads belongs to one snapshot is the host's to establish and is the hypothesis H = (fn-sco-records C).

proofs.title: The collector's trigger while a store opens is sized to the history it reads: at least 8 MiB, at most 4 x the history on disk, never more than the figure's trigger, and the figure holds every store at it
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-heap-open-nursery-trigger (books/heap-open-nursery.lisp), which host/native/io.lisp fnn-open-nursery calls at the start of every open (fnn-recover: the owner's recovery and every offline verb that opens), over the launcher's own history observation (host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-history-octets: the log's segments, checkpoints/ and the state checkpoint; NIL when unreadable). KEYSTONE fn-heap-open-nursery-trigger-bounds: for every D, NURSERY and HISTORY, 8 MiB <= trigger <= (fn-heap-nursery-trigger D NURSERY), and for a natural HISTORY trigger <= max(8 MiB, 4 x HISTORY). fn-heap-store-figure-holds-every-store-at-the-open-trigger: under PRF-198's keystone's hypotheses the store's need at this trigger is within D (the figure's keystone at the figure's trigger, and fn-heap-store-need monotone in the trigger). Why (F1, lane f1-bisect): an open conses in proportion to its history (81.5 MB for a 1,000 x 2 KiB store of 4,388,380 octets on d5ab87aec, two thirds in the checkpoint's decode), so at the figure's trigger (a sixteenth of the dynamic space, 48.75 MiB at the small profile's 780 MB) the open's garbage reached the whole trigger before the first collection: the reopen's peak was the live heap plus the profile's trigger, whatever the store's size.

proofs.title: The free space is a recorded observation and a write is admitted only above ACL2's need: below it every POST is refused try-later by name before its article (440, or 441 for an article already sent), nothing stored, the owner stays up, and the next observation with room recovers
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-otm-admit-post (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk-read after fnn-owner-advance-clock's :served and, when fn-otm-space-due-p, :space event; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at feeds S to fn-otm-read-span, PRF-323), fn-otm-disk-event with kind :space (fnn-owner-space-event: the committer before every barrier's syncer, fnn-owner-sched-snapshot before every health/status render, fnn-owner-space-observe-if-due before a served read's admission; ARG (FREE NEED), FREE the statvfs observation of the store's filesystem or nil), fn-otm-space-need (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-space-need: PRF-129's fn-smr-reserve-octets + 2 x fn-olr-omax + the `disk-reserve-octets' row, default 64 MiB), fn-otm-shed-reply / fn-otm-post-command-reply (the reason), fn-otm-disk-step (journal op 6). KEYSTONE fn-otm-admit-keeps-the-space-need: admitted with the space observed, free >= need. fn-otm-full-sheds: observed below the need, every write is shed whatever the barrier. fn-otm-space-need-covers-two-batches: from an observation F >= need, two batches of at most OMAX octets leave the reserve and the extra (hypothesis: nothing else writes to the filesystem between the observation and the appends; the observation at every barrier's issue keeps that window to two batches). fn-otm-space-recovers: an observation with room admits unless the barrier is past D. fn-otm-space-of-event / fn-otm-full-p-of-other-event / fn-otm-space-event-keeps-the-disk: only a :space event moves the space and it moves nothing else (so fn-otm-disk-event-keeps-the-pipeline and the durability keystones hold). fn-otm-admit-is-the-mode: shed exactly in :slow, :stalled, :full. fn-otm-shed-iff-slow restated: shed exactly when the disk line says slow/stalled or the space line says `disk full:'. PRF-311's fn-otm-shed-only-past-the-deadline, fn-otm-return-recovers, fn-otm-clock-event-never-issues and fn-otm-issue-is-pending-and-admits carry the hypothesis (not (fn-otm-full-p s)). fn-otm-journal-determines-the-decisions holds with the fifth kind. Scope: statvfs unobserved is never :full (an append that then meets ENOSPC stays the recovery event it was); the space consumed between observations by another writer is outside the model.

proofs.title: The decision journal never keeps a torn line: a failed append is truncated back to the last whole entry, the next entry after a loss carries a mark the replay reads as a gap naming the first sequence number missing, a run's start cuts a torn tail, and so at every process-death and ENOSPC cut the journal reads whole or torn, never malformed, and replays to agreement or a named gap
proofs.statement: Subjects (books/owner-time-journal-writer.lisp): fn-otm-jw-init, fn-otm-jw-open-first, fn-otm-jw-open-step and fn-otm-jw-cut-line (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-journal-open, fnn-owner-journal-cut: the file read backwards in chunks of *fn-otm-jw-open-chunk* octets and cut to its last whole entry before the run's start entry); fn-otm-jw-drop, fn-otm-jw-plan, fn-otm-jw-after, fn-otm-jw-truncated and fn-otm-jw-closed-line (host/native/io.lisp fnn-journal-write, called by fnn-log-writer-loop through fnn-log-write-item; a :journal-gap item is the first journal entry queued after the sink dropped one, host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-offer). The writer carries (OFFSET OWE CLOSED); its plan is the entry's line, the mark line (0 7 0 0 0 0 0, *fn-otm-mark-entry*) first when an entry was lost since the last whole one, nil when closed; a non-written outcome asks for a truncation to OFFSET, and a truncation that fails closes the journal for the run. fn-otm-replay (books/owner-time-journal.lisp) reads the mark as (:gap N) and a sequence jump likewise, N one past the last entry replayed. fn-otm-jw-sim composes the host calls over ANY fates of the offered entries (written; dropped by the sink; failed after K octets landed, the truncation holding or not -- a process death mid-append is the last such fate). fn-otm-jw-sim-file: the file is the starting file, the lines of fn-otm-jw-whole, then fn-otm-jw-frag, a fragment with no LF (fn-otm-jw-frag-is-a-fragment). KEYSTONE fn-otm-jw-file-reads-agrees-or-gap: from a file of whole lines E0 that replays to agreement from R, and entries ES that replay to agreement after it, the file the writer leaves reads back with a status other than :malformed, as E0 followed by the entries that landed whole, and replays from R to :agrees when no entry was written after a loss, else to (:gap N), N one past the entries replayed before the first loss. fn-otm-jw-gap-is-the-first-lost: when the first entry lost is not a start entry, N is its sequence number (fn-otm-jw-gap-names-the-first-missing). fn-otm-jw-segment-agrees: a segment as the host offers it (fn-otm-start-line's entry, fn-otm-jw-start-line-is-the-start-entry, then any run of fn-otm-run-okp host calls from fn-otm-init) replays to agreement from any state, so the keystone applies to every segment. fn-otm-jw-open-step-is-the-cut: under the backward read's invariant (the octets after the chunk hold no LF), a :cut is the whole file's cut fn-otm-jw-open-cut and a :more keeps the invariant; fn-otm-jw-open-step-cuts-a-written-file: over a file the writer left (whole lines then a fragment), every :cut under that invariant is the length of the whole lines. Not claimed: that every entry is on the disk (a loss is named, and the tail lost by a death or by a journal closed until the run ends is not marked: the reader's status says torn when octets of it remain); anything about the record log.

proofs.title: A graceful stop drains the POSTs in flight: the fence comes only when every member was told its reply (240 after a fenced barrier) or, past the drain deadline H, told uncertain by the stall's rule, and the drain ends within H plus the send grace
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-osd-drain-next (books/owner-stop-drain.lisp: the step fn-osd-drain-step, fn-osd-drain-next-step-unfolds, and whether the release was made), which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-drain-service calls once per observation after a SIGTERM (fnn-owner-run: the drain, then fnn-owner-stop-service), with S0 and S the gate's scheduler values after a clock event (fnn-owner-sched-snapshot) at the drain's start and at the observation, LIMITS the configuration's (D H C) (fn-owner-barrier-limits), AWAITING the connections registered for a completion plus the queued submissions, UNSENT the connections holding a completion's reply not yet written (host/native/mux.lisp fnn-mux-unsent), RELEASED whether its :release was acted on. KEYSTONE fn-osd-stops-only-when-nothing-is-owed: :stop only when fn-osd-quiet-p (no member awaits, no reply unsent, and no batch in flight unless released by this drain or by the stall, fn-otm-disk-stalled) or released and H + 10,000 ms have passed since S0. KEYSTONE fn-osd-releases-only-at-the-deadline: :release only unreleased, at or past H, and not quiet; the committer then answers every member of the batches in flight by fn-otm-stall-releases (fn-otm-stall-tells-no-member-its-outcome: uncertain, never accepted or refused) and sheds the queued POSTs (refused try-later, nothing stored). KEYSTONE fn-osd-drain-ends-by-the-deadline: unreleased, at or past H and not quiet is :release; released and past H + grace is :stop. KEYSTONE fn-osd-drain-stops-by-the-deadline (lane sigterm-hang): the host's composition of fn-osd-drain-next over two consecutive observations S1, S2 (the second call takes the RELEASED the first returned) at or past H + grace since S0, with ANY AWAITING and UNSENT at each (any number of connections mid-article, mid-commit or holding an unread reply) and any RELEASED carried in: the first answers :stop or the second does; with the host's 100 ms cadence on a clock that never goes back, the stop comes within H + grace + one poll. A connection mid-article is in neither count and never holds the drain; the fence closes it (nothing stored). The host reaches the drain at the SIGTERM in every accept mode (host/native/mux.lisp fnn-mux-serve-once returns at the SIGTERM; batch AZ's once-mode hang). fn-osd-deadline-is-past-the-slow-deadline: H is at least D. With fn-ocs-members-told-only-after-the-barrier (PRF-267) a member is told 240 only in the COMPLETE after its fenced barrier, which the drain lets run before the fence. Not covered: the fence (fnn-owner-stop-service, a :control quantum) waits for a barrier that does not return; a command read but not yet stepped at the SIGTERM is not answered (nothing stored).

proofs.title: HDR :fn-verified reads the catalog and resolves a reply's recorded verdicts in one pass: O(R + V), where the pinned reference was O(R x (N + V))
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-nntp-verdict-hdr-response-cat (books/served-catalog.lisp), which fn-nntp-archive-command-cat calls for HDR :fn-verified; the host reaches it through fn-scr-command (books/served-catalog-chain.lisp, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span). The range arm takes the numbers from fn-scat-range-numbers and each article from fn-scat-available-article (catalog probes), builds a fast alist of the reply's Message-IDs (fn-scat-vh-want) and walks the view's verdict list ONCE keeping each wanted Message-ID's first pair (fn-scat-vh-fill; fn-scat-vh-fill-lookup: its lookup is the list's first pair for a wanted key), and renders every line from that table (fn-scat-vh-lines, exec a loop); both tables are freed on exit. The current and Message-ID arms probe the catalog (fn-scat-available-article, fn-scat-msgid-article). KEYSTONE fn-nntp-verdict-hdr-response-cat-is-archive: under fn-cnx-freshp and the view equation (the archive's articles are fn-cat-view-articles v), it equals fn-nntp-verdict-hdr-response (books/nntp-verdict.lisp), so fn-nntp-archive-command-cat-is-pinned is unchanged. The verdict is the RECORDED evidence (SUB-006), not the catalog row's context (decided under the keyring at intern and replaced by :redecide); a constant-time verdict column needs that equation carried and is not claimed. Scope: work is O(R + V) per request for R lines and V recorded verdicts, one step (not quantum-bounded), like every served range read.

proofs.title: The running owner's status reads each article's tombstone flag from the catalog column in one walk, and the status client joins its pages linearly (lane scale-reads: status and obligations at 1,000,000 articles)
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/native-status-columns.lisp fn-nsc-answer-report, which host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-status-host-answer calls for every FNLS report the running owner renders (host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status-answer, with the live catalog fnn-live-cat), and fn-nsc-client-step, which host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status folds pages through (fn-native-live-status-host-client-step-chunks). fn-nsc-verdict-is-verdict-in: under the column relation F (books/served-columns.lisp fn-scol-okp), an article's verdict with its tombstone flag read from the column (fn-scol-tombstonep) is fn-rcl-verdict-in's, which reads the payload through the arena. KEYSTONE fn-nsc-store-tally-is-counts-and-classes: under F, the one walk fn-nsc-store-tally (a guard-verified loop, fn-nsc-tally-loop) is (append (fn-rcl-store-counts rule now s fn-arena) (fn-rcl-store-classes rule now s fn-arena)): the seven reclaim figures of the four walks before. fn-nsc-reclaim-words-is-reclaim-words and fn-nsc-report-is-report lift it; KEYSTONE fn-nsc-answer-report-is-answer-report: under F, (fn-nsc-answer-report kind profile oc cache obs min disk fn-arena fn-cat) = (fn-nh-answer-report kind profile oc cache obs min disk fn-arena) for every kind, so PRF-089's, PRF-361's and the health verdict's theorems speak of the words the owner sends. KEYSTONE fn-nsc-client-step-is-client-step: with N the length of the joined pages (fn-nsc-join, pages newest first), (fn-nsc-client-view (fn-nsc-client-step chunks n total digest reply)) = (fn-nls-client-step (fn-nsc-join chunks) total digest reply); fn-nsc-client-step-carries-its-length: a :next's length is its pages' joined length, so the hypothesis holds from (nil, 0) at every page. The cost measured: the reclaim line realized and digest-checked every payload four times under the owner mutex (sb-sprof: 98% under fn-durable-realize-octet); in a raw Lisp over the production core the reclaim words took 66 s at syn100k-2k and 518 s at syn1m-2k; the client's (append acc chunk) per page took 69.2 s to join the 24,400,035-octet obligations report of syn100k-2k against 3.4 s for the owner's pages (planning/evidence/scale-reads-status-2026-09-28.md). proofs.title: store export a chunk at a time: the streamed archive is the whole-list export's, byte for byte
proofs.statement: books/store-export-stream.lisp fn-sxp-stream-is-the-export (no hypotheses): for every chunking CHUNKS of the history, the entries host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-store-export writes (fn-sxp-export-head, then fn-sxp-export-chunk per chunk of at most +fnn-export-chunk+ records read by fnn-log-history-each), in order, are fn-sxp-entries of PROFILE, FRONTIER, CONFIGS and the concatenated records, and the MANIFEST octets it writes (the steps' lines appended in order, renamed onto MANIFEST after every entry is fenced) are fn-sxp-manifest of those entries. So PRF-205's round trip holds of the streamed archive. The export's work and allocation per ACL2 call are one chunk's; the MANIFEST is a transport check under the abstract digest seam.

proofs.title: store import a chunk at a time: the streamed plan is the whole-archive import plan
proofs.statement: books/store-import-stream.lisp fn-sxi-stream-plan-is-the-import-plan (no hypotheses): for every chunking CHUNKS of the archive's records and every MANIFEST octet string M, the host's loop (host/native/io.lisp fnn-import-pass: fn-sxi-head and fn-sxi-start over the profile, frontier and configuration records, then per chunk of at most +fnn-export-chunk+ records fn-sxi-want and fn-sxi-step over the MANIFEST octets read at the chunk's place, then fn-sxi-final over what follows the last chunk's lines) decides exactly what fn-sxp-import-plan decides over the whole archive: the same refusal by the same name, or the same profile, configuration records and records (the steps' records joined in order). So PRF-205's round trip holds of the streamed import. The import's work and allocation per ACL2 call are one chunk's; the MANIFEST is never held whole. Pass two (the records appended to the stage's log) re-runs the same steps and is refused by name (archive-changed) when it does not decide what pass one decided.

proofs.title: export durability: the data share one sync, the MANIFEST is durable last, a crash leaves an archive refused by name or the complete archive
proofs.statement: books/store-export-durability.lisp fn-sxd-crash-is-incomplete-or-complete: over the byte model (books/byte-store.lisp, crash images with torn writes and unordered entry operations), from a well-formed state whose archive directory has no MANIFEST durable or pending, a crash at any state of any run of fn-sxd-program (entries created and written with no per-file fence, the MANIFEST's lines into MANIFEST.partial, ONE :sync-all, then MANIFEST.partial, records/ and config/ fenced, the rename onto MANIFEST, the directory fenced), under any syscall outcome, leaves either no MANIFEST or the MANIFEST bound to the file the lines were written to, holding them, with every entry bound to a file holding its octets. fn-sxd-import-verdict-is-incomplete-or-complete: the import's verdict (fn-sxd-archive-verdict, which host/native/io.lisp fnn-import-pass asks first) over every such image is :archive-incomplete (refused by name) or :read over the complete archive. The host (fnn-command-store-export) runs the program step for step with its cuts (tests/campaign/native_cuts.py EXPORT_CUTS); :sync-all is Linux syncfs(2), elsewhere a fence of every file under the archive. The model writes the MANIFEST's lines in one write; the host appends them per chunk, all before the sync.

proofs.title: The owner's records as an abstract stobj over the history image: the read with its one need-page retry loop answers the history's record, keeps the history, its faithfulness and the page file's relation, and never stops for fuel; append, load and the flush into the image keep the history faithful
proofs.statement: books/history-records.lisp. The abstract stobj fn-hrecs (defabsstobj: value (H . C), H the history as a ghost, C the concrete: the FNADTSN2 image of H's first N events on a nested page store then a suffix array; correspondence C itself). fn-hrecs-faithful ST: (fn-hrs-rel H C), H the image's events then the suffix's and every verified page of the nested store holding H's placed image (fn-hp-vhold of fn-hp-piw). KEYSTONES: fn-hrecs-at-is-nth ((fn-hrecs-p ST), faithful, SEQ natural: an :ok answer of (fn-hrecs-at SEQ ST) is (:ok (nth SEQ H)) below (len H) and (:refused :seq) past it; any other verdict is a need-verdict and SEQ < (len H)); fn-hrecs-read-is-nth (ST faithful and (fn-hrecs-disk-faithful FILE ST): the page file FILE holds, at the address the table names, the image's page for every page not verified; then (fn-hrecs-read SEQ FILE ST) keeps fn-hrecs-p, H, faithfulness and the page file's relation, answers :ok only with record SEQ as above, and never (:refused :fuel)); fn-hrecs-get-is-nth and fn-hrecs-get-fuel-enough (the loop with any fuel; fuel at least the number of pages not verified suffices); fn-hrecs-serve-keeps (one fill from fn-pgs-fill-realize, A-PGS-HOST-IO, keeps all three, whatever it answers); fn-hrecs-fill-keeps (a fill that writes the image's page when the page is not verified keeps H faithful, whatever it answers); fn-hrecs-flush-keeps (the oldest suffix event into the image, fn-hp-x-append-step, the empty image first: keeps H faithful, whatever it answers; over fn-hrs-loop-placement: a step's answer other than :ok leaves a valid placement); fn-hrecs-append-appends, fn-hrecs-load-is-events, fn-hrecs-count-is-len. Scope: not yet host-called; the store's readers still read the record list (fn-sf-records); the open's adopt of a committed image, the flush's retry over pages not verified and the commit are not stated.
proofs.progress_note: Lane arena-store-6 milestone (a), 2026-09-28: history-columns' stage 3 as the coordinator decided it (one abstract stobj, not a twin per consumer). Not yet host-called: milestone (b) migrates the served readers of fn-sf-records onto fn-hrecs-read, (c) wires the served open (adopt, no E decode) and the snapshot (commit of the dirty pages). Teeth: ground witnesses for fn-hrc-at-is-nth (positive, and removal of the relation, the shape and (natp seq)), the fill's page-store step (positive; removal of the words hypothesis: a table matching other words is accepted and faithfulness fails), and live executions of load/flush/read (40 events, relocations) and of the need path (need, fill, read; a wrong fill refused :page-damaged and the page asked again). The stobj-level keystones over updating exports have no ground witness: ACL2 does not evaluate stobj-let updaters on ground lists in a proof.

proofs.title: The operator's obligations report is sent page by page with a version token: the owner renders one page per request from a cursor, and the pages a client joins at one version are the whole report (lane obligations-paged)
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/native-live-pages.lisp fn-nlp-answer, which host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-pages-host-answer calls under the owner mutex (host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-pages-answer, FNLS request frame kind 4) with the owner's retention (fn-nlp-live-retention) and width *fn-nls-chunk-octets*; fn-nlp-client-step, which host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-pages folds every reply through (fn-native-live-pages-host-client-step); fn-nlp-offline-start and fn-nlp-offline-step, which host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-live-pages calls with no owner running. The report is fn-nlp-report (the header line and one line per obligation); fn-nlp-live-report-is-the-report: with no hypothesis it is fn-nls-live-report of kind :obligations, the whole report the owner rendered before. fn-nlp-take-cuts-the-stream: a page from a cursor (the unsent rest of a line and the obligations not yet rendered) is the next min(W, |rest|) octets of the rest, and the cursor it leaves is what follows. KEYSTONE fn-nlp-pages-join-to-the-report: for any owner cursors CACHE, retention RET, width W and fuel, if the composition of owner answers and client steps from version 0 page 0 (fn-nlp-run) reaches :done, the joined pages are (fn-nlp-report RET), the ledger the owner held at the first page. KEYSTONE fn-nlp-pages-reach-the-report: with 0 < W <= *fn-nls-chunk-octets* and L <= W * FUEL (L the report's length), the run reaches (:done (fn-nlp-report RET)). KEYSTONE fn-nlp-answer-keeps-other-versions: a request that neither names version V nor starts it leaves V's rest at PAGE unchanged or drops it (:none, answered version-gone, the client restarts). KEYSTONE fn-nlp-offline-pages-join-to-the-report: the offline pages from fn-nlp-offline-start, joined, are the report. Work and allocation per request: one page of at most W octets and at most W obligation lines, plus the ledger's length on the first page; the page and version counters wrap modulo 2^32, so no report length is refused. The whole-report exchange (FNLS kind 1) refuses :obligations by the name report-is-paged (host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-status-host-answer).
proofs.progress_note: Lane obligations-paged (2026-09-28). The frame decoders (fn-nlp-request-decode, fn-nlp-reply-decode, fn-nlp-client-step, fn-nlp-answer) are not guard-verified, like every FNLS decoder (fn-record-read-uint is not); the page path (fn-nlp-header, -fill, -take, -serve, -offline-step) is. The pages are octet lists of at most 128 KiB; their string twin is open. control log and control evidence (books/control-evidence.lisp) still render whole: they grow with withdrawal records, not articles.

proofs.title: The heap figure holds a pool of article credits and every served read admits a connection into article mode only within them, refusing the rest by name, and an admitted upload is never blocked (reserve-to-finish): concurrent large POSTs no longer exhaust the heap
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-oas-read-span (books/owner-article-slots.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at calls for every served read with the slots host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-connection-budget installs from the store's profile (fn-heap-article-slots; one before any run: fn-owner-article-slots). THE POOL (books/heap-store-figure.lisp): the heap figure's base and need hold fn-heap-articles-octets = max(r, min(32 r, 64 MiB)), r = fn-heap-article-reserve-octets = 2 x 16 x (512 + A + HDR), what one admitted article retains at most (the body as wire lists within the body limit and a line; then its submission, the injected article within A and its groups within HDR, as lists; the collector's copy); fn-heap-article-slots = floor(pool / r) in [1, 32] (fn-heap-article-slots-bounds). KEYSTONE fn-heap-article-slots-are-held: k credits, k <= the slots, are within the pool. fn-heap-articles-octets-monotone: the pool grows with A and HDR (so fn-heap-store-base-octets-grows-with-the-profile and heap-reservation's fn-heap-figure-octets-grows-with-history-and-record gained the A hypothesis; its removal witness is in tests/acl2/heap-reservation-tests.lisp). THE ADMISSION: fn-oas-held counts the owner's connections in article mode, its queued submissions and the batch in flight (the credit moves with the request and is released when the commit answers). A read is OVER (fn-oas-over-p) when the owner then holds more than the slots and more than before the read, or connection ID entered article mode in it; past the slots the host's call takes the first of three tiers the slots hold (fn-oas-tiers): (a) the read with ID's posting bit off and restored (a POST 440 at the command with the memory reason, as PRF-323's shed read), (b) that read with ID's wire closed, 400 and close (the article it entered dropped, what it completed kept), (c) the whole read refused, 400 and close, nothing taken; an admitted connection skips (a). fn-oas-read-span-held-step: after the host's read the owner holds at most the slots or at most what it held. KEYSTONE fn-oas-read-span-admits-within-the-slots (no hypothesis): a connection that is in article mode after the host's read and was not before leaves the owner holding at most the slots. fn-oas-read-span-when-held-unfolds: a read the slots hold is fn-otm-read-span exactly (PRF-323's theorems hold of the host's call). fn-oas-refusals-are-not-article: tiers (b) and (c) leave ID out of article mode. THE GAP CLOSED (lane admission-gap): the entry test alone let a read that enters article mode AND completes the article (a TAKETHIS, RFC 4644 section 2.5; a pipelined IHAVE or POST; a small article in one socket read) raise what the owner holds past the slots with ID back in command mode. books/owner-article-held.lisp, from the shape of every layer under the host's read (fn-scar-finish-read replaces or removes ID's record and enqueues at most one decision; the view, pin, posting-bit and memory exchanges touch nothing else): KEYSTONE fn-oah-read-span-keeps-held-within-the-slots (held <= slots before the read implies held <= slots after, for a read of any connection carrying anything); KEYSTONE fn-oah-read-span-leaves-the-others-article-mode (the frame: for id2 /= id the read leaves connection id2's record and article mode as they were; fn-oah-read-span-keeps-the-other-records: the connection list less ID is unchanged); KEYSTONE fn-oas-read-span-never-blocks-an-admitted-article (RESERVE-TO-FINISH, restated: a connection in article mode whose read completes its article or only continues it -- ID out of article mode after it, or the queue's length unchanged -- reads exactly as fn-otm-read-span, whatever the slots, so an admitted upload completes, or is refused by name past the body limit, 441, without waiting for any other); fn-oah-admitted-read-keeps-what-it-completed (for an admitted connection the host's call is that read or that read with the article it began closed: the whole-read refusal is unreachable for it). Not claimed: that the octet-list heap of a retained body is 16 octets an octet (a measurement, planning/evidence/rep-wave-d-2026-09-25.md); the queue's growth by the control channel and BP deliveries, which enter no article mode; the body in bounded pooled chunks (the credit's representation step, open); that the served fold yields after one submission (PKT-600) -- the theorems hold without it, and the never-blocks keystone's second hypothesis is therefore stated, not removed.

proofs.title: A configuration record's stamp is the owner clock's milliseconds, so an expired invitation's redeem is refused at admission and faults the replay
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-cfg-account-livep inside fn-cfg-delta-reason (books/config.lisp), reached by fn-cfg-record-acceptablep (host-called through fn-cnode-record-acceptablep: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-cfg-peer-delta-record, the stopped node's records; books/owner-config.lisp the live owner's) and by fn-config-replay-loop (every open's configuration replay). A configuration record's stamp is the owner's clock observation in milliseconds (books/owner-config.lisp fn-ocfg-config-stamp; the stopped node's host/native/admin.lisp fnn-admin-clock-plan through books/native-admin.lisp fn-native-admin-clock-observation), each time a u64 codec item (fn-cfg-uitemp; fn-cfg-stampp is fn-clock-observationp); books/clock-unit.lisp *fn-clock-record-stamp-unit* is :milliseconds and fn-cfg-account-livep reads the stamp through fn-clock-reading-latest-milliseconds. KEYSTONE fn-cfg-record-redeeming-an-expired-code-is-refused-and-faults-replay: a record whose first delta is a well-formed :account-redeem of a pending row, stamped with no wall claim or with wall + error (ms) at or past the row's expiry (ms), has admissible-reason :account-expired, is not acceptable, and a replay reaching it faults. fn-cfg-account-livep-unfolds states livep in milliseconds. Before this, stamps were the seconds projection (uint32) and the check compared seconds with a millisecond expiry, so it never fired (LANEDUMP invite-clock). Also: fn-oag-group-fact-of dates a group by its stamp's wall directly (ms). Not claimed: stores written before this change (their seconds stamps read as milliseconds); every node redeploys fresh at 6.6.0, no migration (ember 2026-09-28). Not claimed: redeem records whose redeem delta is not the first of the record.

proofs.title: A dropped outbound feed link is named in one ACL2 line, and consecutive link failures wait ACL2's doubling redial delay (defect M3)
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/feed-link-backoff.lisp fn-flb-lost, which host/native/feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-drop-link calls with the peer record's backoff base (fn-owner-feed-backoff-ms) and the streak the link carries, for every drop (the dial's, the pump's I/O conditions, EOF, the reply machine's ending words, :unsendable); fn-flb-ready, which fnn-feed-link-became-ready calls on :ready; fn-flb-drop-line, the line fnn-feed-drop-link logs. KEYSTONE fn-flb-lost-advances-the-backoff: for any base and streak, the delay of a second consecutive failure (from the streak the first answered) is at least the first's, and strictly greater when the first is positive and below *fn-flb-max-delay* (300000 ms, local policy). fn-flb-lost-doubles-below-the-ceiling: when twice the first delay is at most the ceiling, the second is exactly twice the first. fn-flb-first-loss-after-ready-waits-the-base: after fn-flb-ready the delay is min(base, ceiling). fn-flb-delay-is-bounded. The streak is per process (not journaled): a restart waits the base. The TLS half of the defect (host/native/tls.lisp fnn-tls-read: WANT_READ/WANT_WRITE at the deadline answers :timeout, never fnn-tls-io-error) is host I/O and is witnessed by tests/test_native_tls_transport.py (session tickets before a greeting) and tests/test_native_feed_tls_read.py, not by a theorem.
proofs.progress_note: Lane feed-tls-read (2026-09-28), defect M3 from lane node-migrate.

proofs.title: An operator pauses and resumes one peer's outbound feed without removing the peer: the configuration deltas set exactly the requested pause, and the outbound worker links exactly the unpaused feeds
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/feed-pause.lisp fn-fps-deltas, which books/native-admin.lisp fn-native-admin-plan-deltas-over builds for a `peer feed NAME pause|resume' plan (books/native-admin-peer.lisp fn-native-admin-peer-extend-plan; host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-native-admin-host-owner-reconfigure, live, and fn-native-admin-host-apply, replayed); fn-fps-live-names, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-feed-peers answers and host/native/feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-refresh-links follows. KEYSTONE fn-fps-deltas-set-the-pause: for a configuration value V whose peer table holds NAME, applying (fn-cfg-apply) the deltas leaves (fn-fps-pausedp NAME) equal to PAUSEP; the deltas add the one (NAME "outbound-paused" "" 1|0) row and remove every other row of that slot. KEYSTONE fn-fps-live-names-are-the-unpaused-feeds: N is a live name exactly when it is a feed-table name and not paused. fn-fps-deltas-of-an-absent-peer (an arm of the definition, not cited): nothing is published for a peer the table does not hold. Scope: the pause gates the dial (the link is closed and not redialled); the owner still enqueues for a paused peer within its max-queue; health still reports a paused peer with pending work as unavailable-peer.
proofs.progress_note: Lane feed-tls-read (2026-09-28), the coordinator's containment ask from lane node-migrate (PKT-882).

proofs.title: The heap reservation itemised: every term of the model named, and the terms add up to exactly the reservation the host is handed
proofs.statement: books/heap-breakdown.lisp fn-heap-breakdown (action profile core nursery observed connections) lists the reservation's terms as the model computes them: the image's dynamic content, the state (the history: payload and memberships sharing H; handles; records), the open's transient (chunk lists, suffix vectors, per-record build), the request in flight (lists, octet buffers), the collector's room, the megabyte rounding, the image outside the dynamic space, and the threads' stacks and runtime. KEYSTONE fn-heap-breakdown-sums-to-the-reservation: for every action but the offline list verbs (:recover :compact :reclaim, whose figure is the larger of two), (equal (fn-heap-breakdown-sum (fn-heap-breakdown action ...)) (fn-heap-reservation-octets (fn-heap-mb-of (fn-heap-operation-figure-octets action ...)) core (fn-heap-stack-kib profile) (fn-heap-thread-count connections))); fn-heap-breakdown-is-inits-reservation: the :run action unobserved at init's connections is fn-heap-init-reservation-octets, the number `init' prints (host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-init-decision). tools/f8_breakdown.py evaluates it: the itemisation is generated, never hand arithmetic.

proofs.title: Memory admission by credits: an operation acquires its credit before it allocates, the credit follows the buffer (connection body, queued submission, the committer's take, the batch in flight), and the ledger M_base + M_cache + sum(credits) + E_completion + E_runtime <= B holds across every transition of the served path; the launcher's reservation is B
proofs.statement: books/memory-credits.lisp: the ledger (BUDGET BASE CACHE COMPLETION RUNTIME DRAWN OPS) and its transitions; fn-mcr-transitions-keep-funded (acquire, grow, retain, release, evict, overdraw: certified, not cited, since no host line calls those transitions; reach_check) and KEYSTONE fn-mcr-resize-and-move-keep-funded (lane credits, the transitions the host calls): fn-mcr-resize sets an operation's credit, never refused when it shrinks (reserve to finish) and admitted to grow exactly within the budget, refused :memory-budget-exhausted by name with the ledger unchanged (fn-mcr-resize-refuses-exactly-past-the-budget); fn-mcr-move moves credit between operations with the funded total unchanged (fn-mcr-total-of-move). THE SERVED PATH (books/owner-credits.lisp; lane credits, B5): the host keeps one ledger a run (host/owner-host.lisp global fn-owner-credits). Subject: fn-mca-read-span, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at calls for every served read over fn-oas-read-span (PRF-377): connection ID's credit (key (:conn . ID)) is resized to fn-mca-need, one reserve fn-heap-article-reserve-octets while it is mid-article and one per queued submission of it; past the budget the read is refused by name (a POST 440 at the command by fn-oas-refused-read, else fn-mca-shut-read: 400 and close, the read not run). KEYSTONE fn-mca-read-span-keeps-funded (hypothesis: a funded ledger only): the host's read never over-commits. KEYSTONE fn-mca-read-span-covers-the-connection: if ID's credit covered its buffers before the read it is exactly their need after. fn-mca-read-span-within-the-credit-unfolds / fn-mca-read-span-never-blocks-what-is-held: a read the credit holds, in particular one that needs no more than ID holds (an admitted article read on and completed into its queued submission), is fn-oas-read-span exactly. THE COMMIT: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-take calls fn-mca-take (one reserve from (:conn . ID) to :open), fn-owner-shed-outcome fn-mca-untake, and host/native/owner.lisp calls fn-owner-credits-seal after fnn-log-seal-open-batch (fn-mca-seal: :open to :sealed), fn-owner-credits-batch-done in COMPLETE after the barrier (fn-mca-batch-done), fn-owner-credits-settle after a synchronous write or a START that kept no member, fn-owner-credits-stop at the stop. KEYSTONE fn-mca-commit-steps-keep-funded; fn-mca-take-and-seal-keep-the-total (the same credit follows the buffer); fn-mca-seal-and-batch-done-move-the-batch. THE CLOSE: fn-owner-close and fn-owner-fault call fn-mca-close. KEYSTONE fn-mca-close-keeps-what-the-commit-owns: a close (client gone, idle timeout, a stall's uncertain answer, a fault) releases only the connection's own credit; the committer's :open and the batch in flight's :sealed keep theirs until COMPLETE, since the native pipeline feeds each member's outcome before the barrier and the syncer's fdatasync still owns the batch (GPT-6 2026-09-28: a timeout does not release memory a worker or submitted syscall owns). THE BUDGET: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-connection-budget installs fn-mca-initial of the store's profile, core and nursery. KEYSTONE fn-mca-initial-funds-exactly-the-articles: the budget is fn-heap-figure-octets (the reservation the launcher sized the dynamic space from), the open's terms are the completion reserve (funded, never admitted against), the collector's room the runtime reserve, and exactly fn-heap-articles-octets is free. Not claimed: that a read of one connection leaves every other connection's buffers as they were (a frame theorem; lane admission-gap), which would make per-connection coverage an invariant of the whole served machine; a served-state witness of the shut-read tier (a peer article completed within one read; needs an owner fixture with a peer connection); M_cache and eviction on the served path (no cache charges yet: a committed article is held by the base's state term at the profile's bounds, fn-heap-store-history-holds-payload-and-memberships; P1/P2 of planning/evidence/f8-reservation-2026-09-28.md); overdraw has no host caller; the accountable-memory figures (measure at convergence).

proofs.title: Configuration admission refuses a record the codec cannot carry: an accepted record encodes within the decoder's whole-record limits (65,535 items, 65,538 octets)
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-cfg-record-fitsp inside fn-cfg-record-acceptablep (books/config.lisp) and inside the carried check the replay folds execute, fn-cnode-carried-acceptablep (books/node-config.lisp; PRF-186's fn-cnode-record-acceptablep-is-the-carried-check equates the two under fn-cfgp), host-called through fn-cnode-record-acceptablep (books/node-config.lisp; host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-cfg-peer-delta-record for the stopped node, books/owner-config.lisp for the live owner) and folded by fn-config-replay-loop. KEYSTONE fn-cfg-record-fitsp-is-the-decoder-limits: fn-cfg-record-fitsp r is exactly (len (fn-cfg-record-items r)) <= *fn-cfg-max-items* and (len (fn-cfg-encode r)) <= *fn-cfg-max-octets*, the two whole-record refusals of fn-cfg-decode-exact (:item-count, :limit), with no hypothesis; so no accepted record is one fn-cfg-decode-exact refuses for size. The check counts item by item (fn-cfg-record-item-count, fn-cfg-record-octet-count: each item encoded alone and only its length kept, every walk a tail loop), never building the record's octets, and each count equals the encoder's by fn-cfg-record-item-count-is-len-of-items and fn-cfg-record-octet-count-is-len-of-encode. The limits are codec widths (STO-021 (iii)), not data caps: fn-cfg-recordp alone admits records up to 64 deltas of 1,024 rows of 256-octet labels, which encode past them. Not claimed: that a record within the limits decodes (fn-cfg-decode-exact's round trip is witnessed on ground records, tests/acl2/config-field-max-tests.lisp, not proved for all records).
proofs.progress_note: Lane config-and-legacy (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-28): closes clock-units-2's labelled GAP. REPL-admitted on persvati/hbox. Teeth in tests/acl2/config-field-max-tests.lisp: a :set-peers record over the replayed default configuration at exactly 65,538 octets satisfies every conjunct of acceptance and round-trips (positive witness); the same record one octet longer keeps recordp, generation and admissibility, fails fitsp, is not acceptable, and fn-cfg-decode-exact refuses its octets :limit (removal witness); the former GAP record is now refused at admission. proofs.title: The owner's queue is fair under sustained POST load: a waiting control request is admitted within 22 counted quanta and six sealed batches
proofs.statement: Subjects fn-otm-next (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-gate-pick), fn-otm-commit-event (fnn-owner-commit-event) and fn-otm-committer-wake (fnn-owner-commit-wake, which passes the gate's six waiting counts, and its recheck inside the START-NEXT quantum of fnn-owner-commit-pipeline). The rule: fn-ocp-wake answers :start-next only while no control, poster or transit request waits past the pass budget (*fn-ocp-pass-bound* = 4 :commit quanta in flight, counted by fn-ocp-next while one waits and reset at a pick where none does; fn-ocp-no-start-next-while-a-shut-out-class-waits, fn-ocf-start-next-while-control-waits-is-within-the-budget). KEYSTONE fn-ocf-control-waits-at-most-the-bound: from ANY scheduler value, for every sequence of picks ITEMS (each the gate's waiting counts and, for a :commit pick, the events its quantum reports) satisfying fn-ocf-okp -- a control request waits at every pick, and each :commit quantum takes one of the host's shapes (outside flight a START; in flight a START-NEXT, :next-started only at a :start-next wake with that pick's counts, or a COMPLETE: the barrier's word then :completed) -- before the first control pick or the owner's stop at most 22 quanta run that are not :inspect, not a :reader in flight and not a START-NEXT that took nobody (fn-ocf-delay-at-most-the-potential with fn-ocf-potential-at-most-twenty-two), and at most 6 batches are sealed (fn-ocf-seals-at-most-the-seal-potential, fn-ocf-seal-potential-at-most-six). Proof by a potential: the four classes' distance to the control slot (PRF-248's measure) + 3 x whether a START can still be due + the batches left to complete + 3 x the passes the budget still allows. Not counted and bounded elsewhere: :inspect alternates (PRF-267); readers during a barrier run while the fdatasync runs and a waiting COMPLETE goes first (fn-ocs-in-flight-commit-before-reader); an empty START-NEXT is an owner quantum without I/O. The wall-clock reading takes the disk's barrier time, which books/owner-time-model.lisp bounds by H before the stall answers. Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-commit-fairness-tests.lisp (a reached walk from fn-otm-init: next batch open, control arrives, two COMPLETEs, control admitted, delay 2, seals 1; the starvation counterexample under the pre-lane wake: 12 batches sealed, 24 counted quanta, control never admitted; the budget spent: one START-NEXT allowed, then the wake stops the pipeline and control is admitted; hypothesis removal: no control waiting, a :commit quantum outside the host's shapes). Native: tests/test_native_owner_scheduler.py test_a_control_request_is_admitted_under_sustained_post_load (SCN-195).
